needs the source's y-anchor convention resolved with confidence first
(is Dizzy's "y" top-anchored or something else in collision context,
same open question `checkbottomside`/`checktopside` raised earlier)
before touching code that ALSO gates the rat's kill and every hazard
check — not done blind in an unsupervised pass. `REACH_MARGIN` is a
pragmatic patch, not a claim that the underlying box math is now
correct.

**`ratrou`'s loaf-distraction mechanic (`ratcoll`), now fully read and
documented** (previously deferred as "more reverse-engineering than
budget covered" — T0032's own note). Real mechanism, for whenever this
gets implemented:
- `proxloaf` is a proximity box (X-ALL.TXT ~3340, room 36, x=46,y=64,
  w=40,h=16 raw -- needs the `(x-32)*4` transform for this port, same
  as the rat's own bounds turned out to need).
- `proxloafrou` self-modifies `ratcoll+1` (a literal byte inside the
  rat's own routine) to `(loaf's current movex) + 2` -- i.e. touching
  that proximity box RETARGETS the rat's own exact-position trigger to
  wherever the loaf currently is.
- Every `ratrou` tick, after normal patrol movement, `ratcoll: cp 1 /
  ret nz` checks the rat's OWN x against that (usually 1, meaning
  "never matches" until retargeted) self-modified literal. On a match:
  removes the loaf (`loafhere+room=255`), sets `ratcount=2`, forces a
  new random direction (`ratnewdir`, gated on a colour-byte bit), resets
  `oldmovefrm` to 255, shows `thanksforloafmess`.
- In THIS port's terms: this is "drop the loaf somewhere, the rat
  eventually wanders to it and eats it, distracting/rewarding it with
  a message" -- NOT a live chase (the rat doesn't path toward the loaf
  directly; it just happens to check its own position against the
  target every tick during its NORMAL random patrol, so it only
  triggers if patrol movement happens to carry it there).
- This port's loaf actor already exists and is pickupable
  (`ROU_PICKUPABLE`, actor_init) — the drop side already works via
  existing pickup/drop plumbing. What's missing is entirely rat-side:
  a proximity trigger on drop, and the rat-side retarget+consume+
  message logic above. A real, scoped feature, not a fix -- flagged
  for a future SUPERVISED session (needs the same kind of interactive
  playtest iteration everything else in this session needed), not
  attempted blind while the user was away.

**Full regression smoke test** (walk, pickup attempt, troll encounter
incl. SPACE dismiss + knockback + landing, wall collision, jump) run
clean end to end after all of today's combined changes, via
`harness/coco_playtest.sh`.

## Real bug found from a user screenshot: rat patrol was erasing background art

Reported with a screenshot: "objects, and part of the background show
as blank, when pop in when dizzy walks by".

**Root cause**: `redraw()`'s static-placement redraw only covers
Dizzy's OWN damage rect each pass (an existing, pre-session
optimization). The rat's `rat_clear_and_blit` (added this session)
clears a rectangle to erase its OLD position every pass, entirely
independent of Dizzy's damage rect -- and that clear zeroes whatever
was ACTUALLY there, floor/wall/chest art included, not just the rat's
own old pixels. Nothing re-drew the erased placements until Dizzy's
own damage rect happened to sweep through that same spot. Only became
visible once this session's rat patrol-range fix (12-96 -> 48-192)
gave it enough range to sweep through areas with real background art
in them -- the mechanism likely existed in smaller form before, just
never had enough reach to be noticeable.

**Fix**: extracted the placement-redraw loop out of `redraw()` into a
real subroutine, `redraw_placements_dmg`, operating on whatever's
currently in `dmg_col0/col1/y0/y1`. `rat_clear_and_blit` now, after
clearing its rect and before drawing the rat sprite, temporarily points
those globals at ITS OWN clear rect, calls the same subroutine to
restore any static art that lived there, then restores Dizzy's rect
before returning -- so a spot the rat passes through gets its
background art repainted in the SAME pass, not whenever Dizzy
eventually wanders there.

Verified via harness: captured a full-framebuffer baseline early, let
ONLY the rat patrol for ~45s with Dizzy standing still (isolates the
rat's own effect), diffed nonzero-byte counts against a fresh capture
-- buffer A showed zero regressions, buffer B's small delta (22
bytes, exactly the same count lost as gained) matches ordinary torch/
water animation flicker, not a growing hole. Full smoke test (walk,
pickup, troll encounter, wall, jump) still clean after the fix.

This is the second bug this session traceable to the SAME root cause
class as the earlier rat trail fix: an actor that moves outside the
player's own damage-rect machinery needs EVERYTHING that machinery
does for the player (both "erase my own old sprite" AND "restore
whatever static art I just erased along with it"), not just the first
half. [[give-every-independently-moving-actor-its-own-prior-position-tracking-not-just-the-player]]
undersold this the first time -- it's not just about the actor's own
sprite, it's about collateral damage to shared background art too.

## Follow-up: the real bug was da_clear being shared across the rat AND every static actor

The placement-restore fix above was correct but incomplete -- the
user's very next report ("jug, bread and apple only show up when I
pass by them, and the artifact on the rat patrol is back") pointed at
something worse: `da_clear` in `draw_actors` is reached by TWO
unrelated cases -- the rat (always) and any STATIC actor whose box
happens to overlap the current damage rect (a plain fallthrough from
the AABB test, no separate branch). Changing that shared label to
unconditionally call `rat_clear_and_blit` meant every pickupable item
(apple/jug/loaf) and the troll ALSO went through the rat's own
per-buffer last-position tracking (`rat_lastx_a/b`) -- one pair of
variables, now being read and overwritten by whichever DIFFERENT actor
happened to reach that code last. Each actor's "old position" became
garbage (actually some OTHER actor's last position), producing
clear rectangles that could span anywhere between two unrelated
sprites -- explaining both symptoms in one bug: items rendering wrong,
and the rat's own trail-fix breaking again from the same
cross-contaminated state.

**Fix**: `da_clear` now branches on `1,y` (routine id) again --
`ROU_RAT` -> `rat_clear_and_blit` (needs the last-position tracking,
moves independently every pass); everything else -> the ORIGINAL
`clear_and_blit` (clears only the current spot, no last-position state
at all, which is correct for anything that never moves -- and was
sitting unused by mistake once `da_clear` got overwritten to always
call the rat's version). Static actors don't need `redraw_placements_
dmg`-style restoration either: they only redraw when their OWN box
overlaps Dizzy's damage rect in the first place, which is the SAME
damage rect that already re-runs the placement redraw that pass -- so
anything they clear underneath themselves gets naturally restored by
the existing mechanism already covering that same rect.

Verified: apple/jug/loaf all show real pixel content (23/37/18
nonzero bytes respectively) at their own positions before Dizzy has
moved from spawn at all -- not just "eventually," from the very first
frames. Rat trail re-confirmed clean the same way as before. Full
regression smoke test clean.

**Lesson, sharpened from the first version:** a shared label reached
by two different cases needs the SAME care as a shared subroutine --
"they both end up here" is not the same as "they both need the same
handling." The earlier fix (rat_clear_and_blit itself) was correct in
isolation and passed its own tests; the bug was entirely in ROUTING
other callers into it that were never meant to share its state.

## Real inventory screen, and two puzzle mechanics fixed to match the source exactly

Triggered by the user actually testing against the real game in ZEsarUX
and sending screenshots -- two genuine, confirmed divergences from the
source, not just polish:

1. **Pickup UI was never a HUD icon in the original** -- it's a real
   text screen. Screenshot: "YOU ARE CARRYING / A JUG OF COLD WATER /
   STALE LOAF OF BREAD / EXIT AND DON'T DROP". Traced X-ALL.TXT's
   `inventoryrou` fully: it's entered on EVERY successful pickup (not a
   separate key), lists every carried item by name (the item's own
   message pointer, repurposed from movingdata's oldmovex/oldmovey
   fields -- same "same bytes, different meaning per routine" pattern
   already documented for pickupable elsewhere), and lets the player
   cursor through items to select one to drop.

2. **Apple->troll and jug->fire both fire on DROP, not on carry.**
   Screenshot of the jug/fire outcome was the sharper catch: "the fire
   is out but you are in the same place, instead of ... being
   teleported". This port's `update_apple_bribe`/`update_jug_escape`
   checked "carrying the item AND overlapping a box" every pass -- the
   source's `proxapplerou`/`proxjugrou` check the item's DROPPED
   position (via `dropobject`, which places it near Dizzy, then the
   caller immediately re-checks proximity) against a fixed box. A
   carried item has no world position at all, so carry-based checking
   was never going to match. The jug/fire outcome was ALSO wrong beyond
   the trigger: this port invented a room 35 transition standing in for
   "escaping the dungeon" -- the source does no such thing, it just
   sets `fireout` and shows the message; Dizzy stays exactly where he
   is. Both invented mechanics are now gone.

**What changed:**
- `show_inventory` (actors.asm): the real screen. UP/DOWN cursor
  (marker is 'X', not '>' -- this port's font remaps '>' to a period,
  an already-documented punctuation quirk), SPACE selects (drop a real
  item via `drop_to_world`, or close on EXIT). Opened on every
  successful pickup, and also when DOWN is pressed with nothing
  pickupable nearby but something IS carried -- a disclosed
  generalization of the source's own trigger (which only opens it on
  auto-drop-when-full); this port lets the player always choose rather
  than only when full. NOT implemented: the source's "CARRYING TOO
  MUCH TO HOLD" banner specifically -- the screen still opens and shows
  the (full) list correctly in that case, just without that one line.
- `check_drop_triggers` (gameplay.asm), called from `drop_to_world`
  itself so EVERY drop path gets it uniformly (deliberate choice, the
  auto-drop-when-full path, and the new screen's selection all funnel
  through the same place): re-derives the dropped actor's frame and
  looks at the position `drop_to_world` JUST placed it at, via a new
  `point_in_box` test (a plain point-in-rect check, not `actor_hit`'s
  two-sprite AABB -- these check one placed item's position, not two
  overlapping bodies). Replaces `update_apple_bribe`/
  `update_jug_escape` entirely -- removed from the mainloop's per-pass
  polling.
- Message text corrected to the source's own strings throughout:
  apple-given ("[X-ALL.TXT line 543] / [X-ALL.TXT line 544] / [X-ALL.TXT line 545]", was "TROLL LIKES
  APPLES" -- invented), and the jug message replaced entirely
  (`msg_jug_quenched`, X-ALL.TXT's real 4-line throwwateronfiremess,
  replacing the invented `msg_escaped`/"YOU ESCAPED THE DUNGEON").
  `dungeon_escaped` state removed -- `fireout` alone now gates
  everything that cares, matching the source.
- Item name text is the source's own, not authored: "A FRESH GREEN
  APPLE" / "A JUG OF COLD WATER" / "STALE LOAF OF BREAD"
  (applemess/jugmess/loafmess).

**A real memory bug found and fixed along the way, worth remembering
for any future addition of size to this build:** the ~500 new bytes
pushed `dizzy_frames_all.asm` (which was already sitting almost exactly
at the $4000 PMODE4 buffer-A boundary) past it, silently corrupting
Dizzy's own sprite data every time the screen was drawn -- produced a
total hang, not a visible glitch, because the corruption fed into
blit/collision code downstream before ever reaching anything visible.
First attempt at a fix (relocate the WHOLE of dizzy_frames_all.asm into
the existing font/actor/room2 2KB inter-buffer gap) was wrong the same
way, just shifted the overflow into buffer B instead -- the file is
much bigger than the gap's headroom. Correct fix: an internal `org
$5800` inside dizzy_frames_all.asm itself, splitting it so only its
small tail (frame36 on, plus the lookup tables -- exactly the ~305
bytes that had overflowed) relocates into the gap, leaving the bulk of
it exactly where it already fit. Confirmed via the symbol map before
and after, not assumed: zero symbols in either framebuffer's live range
post-fix, ~200 bytes of real headroom left in the gap.

**Verified precisely, not just "it built"**: pickup opens the screen
and freezes correctly (confirmed via RAM: position frozen the whole
time the screen is open); EXIT closes without changing `inv`; dropping
the apple at a forced position inside the troll's box sets
`troll_bribed=1` and removes it from `inv`; dropping the jug at a
forced position inside the fire's box sets `fireout=1`, removes it, AND
leaves `cur_room` unchanged (no transition) -- all via direct memory
pokes to hit exact trigger positions deterministically, since walking
there with scripted timing proved too imprecise for a box as narrow as
the jug's (6px). Full existing regression smoke test still runs
start-to-finish with no hangs (though it no longer exercises the troll
knockback specifically, since it doesn't know to navigate the new
inventory screen after the pickup it does early on -- a stale test
script, not a new bug).

**NOT verified by the user yet**: the actual FEEL of cursor navigation
(pacing, whether UP/DOWN response feels right) and the visual
appearance of the box/text/cursor marker on real NTSC-artifact output
-- this entire feature was built and verified via RAM state in one
extended pass, the same caveat that's applied to every RAM-verified fix
this session.

## Follow-up: the drop-trigger fix worked, but the boxes were unreachable in practice

Real playtest, right after the drop-trigger fix above: "no event is
firing... don't I have to just drop them in the right place?" -- not a
usage mistake. Computed it directly rather than guessing: with
WALK_STEP=4 and the source's own raw box widths (apple 4px, jug 6px),
there is AT MOST ONE reachable stopping position in Dizzy's entire
walkable range that lands a drop inside the box -- apple only at
dizzy_x=182, jug only at dizzy_x=46 (spawn itself) -- with zero visual
indication of where that one pixel-perfect spot is. The trigger logic
itself was correct (confirmed already); the box was just practically
un-hittable by feel once this port committed to 4px movement strides
over the source's native 1px.

Widened both (APPLE_BOX 4->20px, JUG_BOX 6->24px), clear of the
troll's own box and the left wall respectively. Verified with a
DELIBERATELY imprecise drop position (dizzy_x=58, not the one exact
lucky spot) via the harness -- fires correctly now. Same root cause
class as REACH_MARGIN's earlier fix to pickup reach: a box sized for
the source's fine-grained movement doesn't survive this port's
deliberately coarser stride unchanged.

## Real art quality pass: sparser wall dither + morphological closing for actor sprites

User: "the art quality is quite a disappointment, could we go fully
black and white to avoid all this fringing?"

**Monochrome itself is free** -- PMODE4 is 1 bit/pixel, so there's no
colour data to lose; NTSC composite artifacting is purely a display-
time effect on top of the same bits. Rendered the actual framebuffer
bytes directly to PNG (no emulator NTSC simulation at all) to show this
concretely rather than just asserting it.

**But the existing dither was too dense to read as anything but
static in true monochrome.** `regularize`'s default `dither_floor=0.35`
gives room 36's dim-red masonry a ~50% duty cycle -- fine as raw
material for NTSC colour blending (which is what it was tuned for),
but a dense checkerboard at native resolution with nothing to blend it
into. Retuned to `dither_floor=0.05` (practical floor of this
parameter -- 0.0 gives an identical result, since both round to the
same Bayer threshold for this ink colour): visibly sparser, reads as
light texture instead of noise, structure (mortar lines, outlines)
untouched since `regularize` already preserves those verbatim.
Confirmed with a rendered before/after, not just the numbers.

**The troll exposed a second, more serious problem**: barely
perceptible even after the wall fix. Traced it to the SOURCE data, not
our pipeline -- decoded frame 96 (troll) with ZERO processing (no
shade, no dither) and it's ALREADY scattered noise at native
resolution. This is genuine, confirmed via the raw bytes, not a
decode bug: the Spectrum draws this sprite as one colour ATTRIBUTE
(solid green) over the whole cell, so a human eye binds the scattered
dots into one shape; PMODE4 has no equivalent per-cell colour plane
(NTSC artifacting OR true monochrome, doesn't matter), so the same
bits read as noise with nothing to bind them. Same root limitation as
the wall dither, now confirmed to also apply to character sprites.

**Real fix, not a parameter tweak**: `close_gaps` (tools/roompack), a
morphological closing pass (dilate then erode, 4-connected, padded so
the sprite's true outer boundary doesn't erode away) applied to actor
sprites before tonal shading. `--close-actor-sprites 1` merges the
troll's scattered ink into one coherent, recognizable creature
silhouette with visible face/tusk detail -- verified with a direct
before/after render of the raw sprite bytes, then reconfirmed in the
full assembled scene. A real, disclosed trade: it cannot invent detail
that only ever existed as "colour here", and a big gap between
clusters still won't close -- this specifically helps sprites whose
problem is scattered dot-noise (like the troll), not ones missing
whole connected regions. Off by default (0 iterations), matching this
project's existing pattern for anything that trades fidelity for
looks; room 36 now built with 1.

New defaults for room 36's actual generating command:
```
roompack --frames research/D3-prior-art/original_source/FRAMES.DAT \
  --rooms extracted/rooms.json --room 36 \
  --shade --dither-floor 0.05 --close-actor-sprites 1 \
  --output target/room36_data.asm --font-output target/font_data.asm \
  --actors extracted/actors.json --actor-rooms 35,36 \
  --actor-output target/actor_data.asm --mirror-frames 104
```
(No previously-recorded exact invocation existed anywhere in the repo
-- reconstructed from the tool's own Args struct and confirmed by
reproducing the committed room36_data.asm almost byte-for-byte before
changing anything.)

## Outline art: replacing filled/dithered shading entirely (T0026)

User's reaction to the sparser-dither pass above, after seeing real
XRoar/ZEsarUX side-by-side comparisons: "I am baffled by the
difference in graphics quality between the zx spectrum and the coco
2." Explained the real, largely unavoidable cause -- Spectrum has
genuine 8x8 attribute-cell solid color; CoCo2 PMODE4 has none, only 2
hardware colors plus session-random NTSC artifact tricks (the
Zaxxon/Time Bandit style deliberate 4-color patterns were investigated
this session and NOT successfully reproduced on either MAME or XRoar
despite confirming CSS=1 was correctly set in our own code -- see the
prior "empirical artifact-color test" -- that whole line stayed
unresolved). User's own next call, unprompted: **"I think we will
need to redo the art, so it has a nice solid outline instead of
filling it."**

**What it is**: instead of filling a shape's silhouette with a dither
pattern (noise at any density), keep only its 1px boundary ring and
leave the interior empty (background). Implemented as
`outline_only(bits, close_iters)` in `tools/roompack/src/main.rs`:
close scattered raw dither first (reuses `close_gaps`, same fix as the
troll's), take the true filled `silhouette()`, erode it once, and keep
`silhouette AND NOT eroded` -- exactly the boundary ring.

**Why this is a genuinely better fix, not just a different filter**:
it sidesteps the NTSC-artifact-color problem entirely, because there
is no alternating-pixel pattern anywhere to mis-render -- solid ink on
solid background is well-defined in every render path. Confirmed by
example: this session's own gray-vs-color XRoar rendering mystery
(never resolved) was tested again with real playtest screenshots under
outline art, and the troll reads as a recognizable silhouette instead
of a solid blob even in that same unreconciled composite/artifact
mode. The unresolved NTSC-artifact investigation is now moot for this
project -- outline art doesn't need it.

**New CLI flag `--outline`** (tools/roompack). Applies uniformly to
both room placements (bypasses the `thr<16` gate -- outline art
applies regardless of the placement's would-be shade tone) and actor
sprites (replaces the unconditional `regularize` call). `--dither-
floor`/`--structure-run` become no-ops under `--outline` (the duty-
cycle/structure-preservation machinery they control isn't used by this
path) but are harmless to leave set. Flame/water tiles are untouched
(separate `thin()` special case, always was) -- deliberate, not a gap;
nobody complained about flame flicker, and it's a small isolated glyph
where dithering was already the right call.

**Rolled out to all three built rooms** (2, 35, 36) with the user's
explicit go-ahead ("Roll out everywhere" over "one more room first" or
"just room 36"). Exact regenerating commands used:
```
roompack --frames research/D3-prior-art/original_source/FRAMES.DAT \
  --rooms extracted/rooms.json --room 2 --shade --outline \
  --output target/room2_data.asm

roompack --frames research/D3-prior-art/original_source/FRAMES.DAT \
  --rooms extracted/rooms.json --room 35 --shade --outline \
  --output target/room35_data.asm

roompack --frames research/D3-prior-art/original_source/FRAMES.DAT \
  --rooms extracted/rooms.json --room 36 --shade --outline \
  --output target/room36_data.asm --font-output target/font_data.asm \
  --actors extracted/actors.json --actor-rooms 35,36 \
  --actor-output target/actor_data.asm --mirror-frames 104 \
  --close-actor-sprites 1
```
(Room 2 and 35's flags for `--shade`/no despeckle/no mirror were
inferred from the committed output's own variant-label suffixes and
cross-checked against NOTES.md's despeckle history, since -- same gap
as room 36 before it -- no prior invocation for either room was ever
recorded either. Room 2 has zero static placements, only 4 animated
flame tiles handled by the untouched special case, so its
`room_placements` table legitimately stays empty; not a bug.)

**Verification, not just "it builds"**: assembled clean
(`lwasm --decb`); `harness/capture_pmode4.sh` real-emulator capture of
room 36's opening scene confirmed the outline render visually (crisp
scalloped walls, clean troll silhouette, torch/chest legible); an
offline Python composite of room 35's placements (same technique
`tools/shadelab.py` uses, generalized to any room/prefix) confirmed no
corruption there either. Ran the existing
`harness/playtest_script_example.lua` regression (walk, pick up jug,
approach troll, room-adjacent movement) against both the outline build
and a `git stash`-baseline build of the unchanged code and diffed the
per-frame `x`,`y` trajectories byte-for-byte -- **identical**,
confirming collision is genuinely unaffected (it always was: `cmask` is
deliberately built from the *unshaded* raw decode, a design choice
already on record above, and outline art doesn't touch that path).

**Dead end avoided**: didn't try to derive the outline from the raw
(pre-silhouette) bits directly -- on sprites like the troll whose raw
data is scattered dots, eroding straight off that gives noise, not a
clean ring. The `close_gaps` -> `silhouette` -> erode-and-subtract
order matters; skipping the fill step first is the mistake to not
repeat.

Not yet done: applying `--close-actor-sprites` values above 1 to any
sprite other than the troll (nobody's confirmed a need); a real
in-emulator capture of room 35's opening scene (only room 36's has a
direct MAME/XRoar screenshot so far -- the offline composite is a
weaker check); no user-facing playtest of the new look yet, this was
verified by the agent only.

## T0028: the port was in the WRONG VIDEO MODE the whole time

The single most expensive bug in this port so far, and the real answer to
"I am baffled by the difference in graphics quality between the zx
spectrum and the coco 2".

**Symptom**: art looked far worse than the Spectrum original it was
copied from, despite both being 256x192 1bpp bitmaps. Everything was
smeared with green/magenta/orange fringing, fine detail was mush, and
no amount of art-pipeline work (despeckle, dither-floor tuning,
morphological closing, outline art) really fixed it.

**Cause**: `target/room36.asm` set PIA1 $FF22's mode nibble to **$E**.
- `$F` = PB7-PB4 = A/G=1, GM=111 = **RG6: 256x192, 1 bit/pixel** = PMODE4.
- `$E` = GM=110 = **CG6: 128x192, 4 colour, 2 bits/pixel.**

In CG6 the VDG reads our 1bpp art as pixel PAIRS. Half the horizontal
resolution is discarded outright, and each pair of our black/white pixels
is reinterpreted as one of four colours (CSS=1: buff/cyan/magenta/orange).
That is the entire "fringing" problem, and it was never an emulator or a
display-environment issue.

Introduced by commit a202efd (2026-08-29), "fix invalid PIA1 mode-select
nibble ($F -> $E), per Inman & Inman's period CoCo graphics book" -- a
misreading of that book's table 4-2. `$F` is not merely valid, it is the
only nibble that selects PMODE4.

**Why it survived for days** -- this is the part worth internalising:
that commit's own message says "Headlessly re-verified memory content is
still correct; real interactive test still needed." The headless check
was `capture_pmode4.sh`, which reads $4000 over GDB and decodes it as
1bpp 256x192. **It assumes the answer to the question a mode check would
ask.** With the machine in CG6 it still produced a perfect-looking PNG.
So the harness said green, and when the user sent a screenshot of the
real, genuinely-bad output, it was attributed to "a real, unresolved
display-environment issue specific to the user's machine" (recorded
earlier in this file) rather than to our own code. Every later art
investigation then built on that false ground -- including a long,
inconclusive hunt for XRoar flags (`-gl-filter`, `-tv-input`,
`-vo-monochrome`, `-ccr`) to make the display "look right", which of
course never worked, because the machine really was in the wrong mode.

**The earlier "empirical artifact-color test contradicted documented
theory" result is now explained**: it wrote $00/$FF/$AA/$55 bands under
confirmed CSS=1 and got orange/magenta/green instead of black/buff. In
CG6 those bytes decode to colour 0/3/2/1 = buff/orange/magenta/cyan --
exactly what was observed. The theory was right; the mode was wrong.
That test had already found this bug and it was misread as the docs
being unreliable.

**Fix**: `$E8` -> `$F8` in `target/room36.asm` and
`target/room36_cart.asm`. `target/pm4test.asm` always had `$F8` and was
right all along.

**Diagnosis method, reusable**: assemble a binary that fills the
framebuffer with 12 bands of known byte patterns ($00, $FF, $AA, $55,
$CC, $33, $F0, $80, $C0, $7F, $3F, $E7) and photograph the RENDERED
output. The mapping from pattern to what appears on screen identifies
the active mode unambiguously -- 1bpp modes give black/white stripes,
CG modes give four named colours in a fixed order. Do this before
trusting any theory about a display.

**New harness capability**: `harness/capture_display.sh` (+
`harness/mame_snapshot.lua`) captures MAME's REAL RENDERED OUTPUT to a
PNG headlessly. This is the check that was missing.
`harness/capture_pmode4.sh` now carries a warning saying what it can and
cannot see. Rule going forward: **`capture_pmode4.sh` answers "did we
draw the right bytes?", `capture_display.sh` answers "does the machine
show the right picture?". Any claim about how the game LOOKS needs the
second one.** A screenshot from the user is evidence about the second
question and outranks the first.

**Verified**: full-resolution 256x192 render confirmed in both XRoar
(black background, white art, red/blue NTSC edging -- the classic CoCo
PMODE4 look) and MAME. `playtest_script_example.lua` trajectory diffed
byte-identical against the pre-fix build, so this is a pure display fix
with no logic change.

**Open art-direction question this reopens**: outline art was adopted
specifically to work around fringing that turned out to be this bug.
At correct resolution the previous filled/dithered art also looks
dramatically better and considerably closer to the Spectrum original.
Switching back is one flag in `tools/regen_art.sh` (drop `--outline`,
restore `--dither-floor 0.05`). User's call, not made yet.

## T0029: undo the art compromises -- verbatim Spectrum art is correct

Follow-on from T0028, at the user's prompting ("now I think we can redo
some of the art work and undo a lot of the compromises, lets use the troll
as a example"). They were right.

**Every art transform this port accumulated was compensating for T0028**
-- the half-resolution, colour-mangling CG6 display. With the video mode
fixed, none of them are needed:
- `--shade` / `--dither-floor` (tonal dither retuning)
- `--close-actor-sprites` (morphological closing, T0026)
- `--outline` (solid outline extraction, T0026)

`tools/regen_art.sh` now runs roompack with **none** of them. The
Spectrum's own 1bpp bitmap goes to the CoCo unmodified -- which is the
obvious right answer, since both machines are 256x192 1bpp and the art was
drawn for exactly that.

**Verified on the troll (frame 96)**, the sprite that motivated the
workarounds: in a real display capture the verbatim version is a clearly
readable creature with face, arms and legs -- visibly better than the
outline version (sparse, barely reads as a creature) and than the
dithered/closed version. Walls became proper textured masonry, torches
read as torches.

**The reasoning error that created all of this, worth not repeating:**
frame 96 was declared "scattered dot noise" and "barely perceptible" from
a **6x-magnified sprite dump**. Dithered art ALWAYS looks like noise when
magnified -- the dither is a shading technique that only resolves at
native size. The same frame, rendered at 1:1 in a contact sheet, is
instantly recognisable as a troll. Two separate sessions then built real
tooling (`close_gaps`, `outline_only`) to "fix" a sprite that was never
broken.

**Rule**: judge art at 1:1 in a real display capture
(`harness/capture_display.sh`), never from a zoomed sprite dump, and never
from a framebuffer decode. If a sprite looks like noise, magnify LESS, not
more.

Also ruled out along the way (so it isn't re-investigated): frame 96 is
NOT stored in a different format from the frames around it. Checked the
width byte's high bit (no flag; `& 0x7f` masks nothing for any frame),
byte-interleaved mask+data, row-interleaved mask+data, and split
mask/data planes -- all give noise, and the frame's 160 bytes butt exactly
against frame 104's offset, confirming 32x40 @ 4 bytes/row is the true
layout. The decoder was always right.

`roompack`'s `--shade`/`--outline`/`--close-actor-sprites` flags are kept,
not deleted: they are real capabilities for a future target whose display
genuinely cannot carry the original dither. They are simply wrong for this
one. Playtest trajectory byte-identical (pure art change, no logic).

**Coverage check (T0029 follow-up)**: "apply verbatim to everything" was
verified, not assumed. `tools/verify_verbatim.py` decodes FRAMES.DAT
independently and compares every generated sprite byte-for-byte:
**104/104 sprites in all three rooms are byte-identical to the Spectrum
original, 0 skipped.** That covers room placements, actor sprites, font
glyphs, and the animated flame/water tiles (which use `thin()`, a no-op
once `--shade` is off). Dizzy's own sprite was never processed -- it goes
through `tools/spritedata dizzy-pack`, which emits the mask and sprite
planes raw and composites with the original's own
`screen = (screen AND mask) XOR sprite`.

The verifier is self-checked: regenerating room 36 with `--outline`
reinstated makes it report 20 differing sprites, so a green result means
something. Run it after any roompack change.

## T0030: `chatter` -- multi-box conversations were missing entirely

User: "I don't see any multi text window conversation. For example when
you offer the apple to the troll it triggers multiple speech boxes one by
one." Correct, and it was a straight omission.

**The distinction in X-ALL.TXT** (this is the thing to know):

- `windowrou` (line 5692) -- print ONE box, wait, restore the room.
- `chatter` (line 2402) -- print a box, wait, and if the NEXT byte is not
  0, print another. A conversation.

```
chatter  ld a,1
         ld (dontupdatedizzy),a
         call printandwait   ;; print + wait; HL ends past this box's mend
         ld a,(hl)
         and a               ;; another message follows?
         jr nz,chatter
         jp windowrou1       ;; resetuproom + clear dontupdatedizzy
```

Almost everything uses `windowrou`. Only two things use `chatter`:
`trollgotapplemess` and `knockandentermess`. `proxapplerou` (line 3390)
ends `jp chatter` -- so giving the troll the apple is a FOUR-box exchange:

1. "[X-ALL.TXT line 543] / [X-ALL.TXT line 544] / [X-ALL.TXT line 545]"
2. "[X-ALL.TXT line 547]? / [X-ALL.TXT line 548] / [X-ALL.TXT line 549]"
3. "[X-ALL.TXT line 551] / [X-ALL.TXT line 552] / [X-ALL.TXT line 553] / [X-ALL.TXT line 554]!"
4. "[X-ALL.TXT line 556] / [X-ALL.TXT line 557] / [X-ALL.TXT line 558]"

Box 4 is a genuine gameplay hint -- it tells the player the jug/fire
solution. Shipping only box 1 didn't just lose flavour text, it removed
the game's own explanation of the next puzzle.

**Ported directly.** `msg_chatter` in gameplay.asm is the same loop; our
`prtmessage` already leaves X past the terminating 0 for the same reason
the Z80's HL does. `spm_table` messages now go through it, so any of them
can become multi-box just by adding boxes to the data. A stream driven
through `msg_chatter` needs TWO trailing zero bytes (one closes the last
box, one ends the run) -- exactly the original's `mend,mend`.

**Boxes deliberately do NOT erase between steps.** `chatter`'s body is
only printandwait; the room is restored once at the end via
`windowrou1`/`resetuproom`. So boxes accumulate and overlap on screen --
verified matching: box 3 sits at (8,48) and overwrites box 1 at (2,48),
while box 2 at (16,80) stays visible underneath. Do not "fix" this.

**All three message streams are now byte-for-byte from X-ALL.TXT**
(`trollgotapplemess` 541, `throwwateronfiremess` 841,
`getbackintheremess` 974), including the original's own box positions and
sizes and its inert `mpen` bytes. The previously hand-invented
coordinates are gone -- and so is the hand-recentring they needed, the
same way copying the original art removed the need to tune it. Repeating
the T0029 lesson in a different medium: when the source has the data,
copy it.

**`&` and `'` restored.** An earlier version dropped them from
`getbackintheremess` because "their exact intended glyph isn't
established". It was established in about a minute by rendering font
glyphs 38 and 39 out of font_data.asm: a matched pair of opening and
closing speech marks. Every `&...'` pair in the original's message data
is a spoken line. When a question is answerable by looking, look.

**Verified** in MAME by poking each pending flag and stepping with SPACE:
all four apple boxes in order, the jug box, and the troll box, all
rendering correctly with commas, apostrophes, exclamation marks and
speech marks. Playtest trajectory byte-identical.

**Test technique worth reusing**: driving a message from real gameplay
needs Dizzy to reach the trigger, and he is blocked at x=94 by the table
until he jumps -- fiddly to script and unrelated to what is being tested.
Poking the pending flag (`apple_msg_pending` etc., address from the fresh
map) and driving SPACE tests the message path directly. That is also why
`harness/playtest_script_example.lua`'s "should have hit troll by now"
comment is aspirational -- that script never reaches the troll either.

## T0031: step-climbing -- the side probes and the floor-search lift

Two user reports, one root cause: "on the original game you did not have
to jump [to] walk through [the fireplace], I guess there is some tolerance
on the step height and up to a certain point Dizzy just climbs up as he
walks" and "on the rat level dizzy seems to clip through the floor".

**The original's mechanic is two halves that only work as a pair.**

1. `checkrightside`/`checkleftside` (X-ALL.TXT 6507/6560) probe the body
   column at THREE heights -- `looky = y-10`, then `-4` per iteration with
   `b=3`, so y-10, y-14, y-18. **Nothing is tested at or near the feet.**
   An obstacle shorter than ~10px is invisible to the side check, so Dizzy
   walks straight into it.

2. `checkbottomside` does NOT start the floor search at the feet:
   ```
   slowfall  add a,4          ;; scan budget b = dy + 4
             ld b,a
             ld a,(y) / sub 4 / ld (y),a    ;; LIFT 4px first
   ...lp     call checkline / jr nz,floorfound / inc y / djnz
   ```
   It lifts Dizzy 4px and scans DOWN from there, every frame, grounded or
   not. On flat ground that is a no-op (the scan finds the same floor 4px
   down). Walk into something up to ~10px tall and the lift finds its top
   and stands him on it -- climbing a few px per frame, no jump.

So the lowest side probe and the lift size together define what is
walkable. Raise the probe and low steps start blocking; drop the lift and
nothing is climbable.

**What we had**: `check_wall` probed y-8 and y-16 (two probes, invented),
and the vertical pass short-circuited on `if grounded && check_ground then
done` -- so there was no lift at all. Both reported bugs follow:

- **Fireplace**: no lift, so every step had to be jumped.
- **"Clips through the floor"**: the side check ignored anything below
  y-8, so Dizzy could walk INTO a step shorter than that -- and with no
  lift he stayed **embedded inside it**. Confirmed by probe: on the
  pre-fix build, placing him at y=88 inside the rat platform leaves him
  sitting there at floor=1 indefinitely; with the lift he climbs out to
  y=80 in two frames.

**Fixed** by porting both halves: `check_wall` now probes y-10/y-14/y-18,
and the vertical block always lifts STEP_UP(=4) and scans down with a
budget of dy+STEP_UP, with the grounded short-circuit removed (the source
has no such short-circuit, and having one is what removed the climb).

**Verified**: walking right with no jump at all, Dizzy previously stalled
at x=94; he now reaches x=178 (the apple drop box by the troll), briefly
going airborne at x=162 as he climbs. Walking left he now crosses the
fireplace. He does NOT climb walls -- he still stops at x=178 rather than
scaling the right-hand wall, because the side probes block first. Rendered
framebuffer measured at the rat platform: Dizzy's lowest sprite row is 79
and the platform's top row is 80, i.e. standing exactly on it, no visual
sink. Art verifier still 104/104.

**Known asymmetry, not yet resolved**: at the step around x=106 Dizzy
walks through while already mid-climb (the lift has him at y=172, which
clears the y-10 probe) but is blocked if he stops at its base and starts
again from y=176. The original has the same lift and the same probe
heights so it plausibly behaves identically, but that has NOT been
confirmed against the real game -- if the user reports a spot that still
needs an unexpected jump, this is the thing to check first, and
`WALK_STEP=4` (a deliberate feel choice, not the source's value) changes
how often he is mid-lift when the horizontal check runs.

**Cost**: standing still now runs the full lift+scan every frame -- up to
5 check_ground calls (15 mask probes) instead of 3. The source pays the
same; the overclock absorbs it.

## T0032: message boxes were 2 glyphs narrow and 1 glyph row high

User, after the chatter fix: "the text on the text boxes is still not
centered". The message data is byte-identical to X-ALL.TXT, so the fault
had to be in our INTERPRETER's box geometry -- and it was, on both axes.

**The original's box** (`drawboxrou`/`horizontalbars`/`verticalbars`/
`clearmiddle`, X-ALL.TXT ~4920):

- Top bar is `42, 46, W*40, 46, 43` -- **W+4 glyphs**, not W+2. In glyph
  columns: 0 corner, 1 edge, 2..W+1 the W segments, W+2 edge, W+3 corner.
- Verticals sit at glyph columns **1 and W+2** (`verticalbars` does
  `inc e / inc e` before the left bar).
- Top bar is at **messy+8**, not messy; bottom bar at messy+h*8+16.
- `clearmiddle` clears exactly the interior: x from messx*4+16, W bytes
  wide, y from messy+16, h*8 tall.

So the interior is glyph columns 2..W+1 and rows messy+16..messy+h*8+15.

**What we had**: `42, W*40, 43` (W+2 glyphs), verticals at columns 0 and
W+1, and the top bar at messy with the bottom at messy+h*8+8. Two glyphs
too narrow and one glyph row too high -- so text positioned by the
original's own coordinates landed 8px right of centre and 8px below it.

**Verified by measuring the framebuffer**, not by eye. Box 1 (messx=2,
W=13, messy=48, h=5):

```
expected box x 8..143 (centre 75.5), top border 56, bottom 104
  border ink present on both border rows: 124/136 px
  interior rows 64..103, centre 83.5
  text ink x 17..134  centre 75.5   == box centre
  text ink y 64..103  centre 83.5   == interior centre
```

Both axes exact. All four apple-conversation boxes render centred.

**Deliberate deviation kept**: we clear the whole box rectangle before
drawing the frame, where the original clears only the interior. On the
Spectrum the frame glyphs land on an attribute-coloured cell so ORing
them over room art is fine; with no attribute plane, ORing the border
over dungeon masonry looks like a smear. The clear rect was resized to
(W+4) x (h+3) glyphs to match the new geometry.

**Lesson, third time this session**: the data was right and the code
reading it was wrong. When ported output looks off but the data is
byte-identical to the source, suspect the interpreter, and measure the
framebuffer rather than eyeballing a screenshot -- "looks left-shifted"
was in fact 8px right and 8px down.

## T0033-note: artifact colour, measured properly in RG6 at last

Every earlier colour investigation this session was run while the machine
was in CG6 (T0028), so all of it was measuring the wrong mode and none of
its conclusions were worth keeping. Redone in RG6/PMODE4.

**The palette is real and there are four colours.** Band test (12 patterns
x 16 rows), sampled by RGB rather than eyeballed, CSS=1:

| pattern | pixels set | colour | measured RGB |
|---|---|---|---|
| `$00` | none | black | (38,48,22) |
| `$55` | odd columns | **blue** | (38,124,173) |
| `$AA` | even columns | **orange/red** | (191,124,22) |
| `$FF` | all | white/buff | (191,200,173) |

Confirmed on BOTH emulators; XRoar renders them more saturated than MAME
but agrees on which is which. **CSS=0 is useless for colour** -- `$FF` is
green and the alternating patterns give only muddy mid-greens, no distinct
hues. The port already runs CSS=1, which is the right choice.

**The rule for when colour is free.** Artifact colour works on pixel
PAIRS, so a coloured area is effectively 128px horizontally. That is
expensive for detailed art and free for anything already solid-filled:
recolouring a solid region costs nothing visible, because there was no
horizontal detail in it to lose. Fine 1px detail cannot be coloured at all
-- it just becomes a stray coloured dot.

**Demonstrated on the torch flames** (room 36): masking the flame sprites'
ink to even columns (`byte & $AA`) turns them solid orange. Before, the
flame was white with blue fringing and indistinguishable from the
stonework behind it; after, it reads instantly as fire. The flame is a
filled blob, so the halved horizontal detail is invisible. Experiment
only so far -- the mask was applied to the generated .asm by hand, NOT
built into roompack, and was reverted.

**Caveat before shipping this**: which of orange/blue you get depends on
the VDG's power-on artifact phase, which is NOT software-controllable on a
CoCo2 (Lomont, and the reason the earlier theory work kept hedging). Both
emulators are deterministic, but on real hardware the two can swap, so an
orange flame may come out blue. Anything relying on a SPECIFIC hue is a
gamble; anything relying on "this area is a different colour from its
surroundings" is safe either way.

Good candidates if this is adopted: torch/fire flames (orange), room 35's
water (blue). Bad candidates: Dizzy himself, text, outlines, masonry
detail -- all fine 1px work that would only smear.

**Adopted (T0033-note follow-up)**: artifact colour is now in the pipeline
for the elements that are mostly solid fill, chosen by measuring each
sprite's "solid share" -- the fraction of its ink sitting in horizontal
runs of >=4px, which is what survives a column mask:

| sprite | solid share | colour |
|---|---|---|
| flame tiles (115) | blob | orange |
| water tiles (92-95) | blob | blue |
| apple (17) | 61% | orange |
| jug of water (19) | 57% | blue |
| loaf (20) | 69% | orange |

Left white deliberately: the rock (139) and rat (104) at ~31-44% solid,
Dizzy, the troll, all masonry, and every glyph -- below roughly half solid
a column mask produces dotted mush, not colour.

Flags: `--colour-flames-orange`, `--colour-water-blue`,
`--colour-actor-orange 17,20`, `--colour-actor-blue 19` (all in
tools/regen_art.sh). `tools/verify_verbatim.py` knows which frames may be
masked and still checks each one is an EXACT column mask of the original,
reporting the hue -- so the guarantee is unchanged for everything else.

**Two parity traps, both real, both caught by that hue reporting**:
mirroring an even-width sprite maps column c -> w-1-c and so FLIPS column
parity. Mask before mirroring and the flipped copy comes out the other
colour (the mirrored torches rendered blue). Both the flame and the actor
paths now mask each copy after mirroring instead.

Net effect: the dungeon reads in colour -- orange fire and torches, an
orange apple, a blue water jug -- with Dizzy, the troll and all the
masonry still at full 256px detail in white. Playtest trajectory
unaffected.

## T0033: loaf -> rat distraction, built and verified

Deferred since T0027/T0032 as "more reverse-engineering than budget
covered". Fully reverse-engineered late last session (`proxloafrou`/
`ratcoll`, X-ALL.TXT ~3322-3349) and built this session.

**Why an exact match (the source's own mechanism) can't port as-is**:
the original retargets a literal byte inside the rat's own routine to
the dropped loaf's raw x+2, then every tick does `cp` for an EXACT match
-- works because both the rat and Dizzy move 1 raw px/tick there, so
every x value is reachable by both. This port moves everything in
RAT_STEP_SIZE/WALK_STEP=4px strides: the rat's x is always a multiple of
4 (RAT_MIN_X=48, step 4), but a dropped item's x is `dizzy_x+4` and
dizzy_x is never a multiple of 4 (spawns at 46) -- so on this port's
grid an exact-match test can PROVABLY NEVER FIRE. Same class of bug as
T0032's narrow apple/jug boxes, caught by working out the arithmetic
before writing the check rather than after debugging a silent no-op.

**Fix**: a tolerance match (`|rat_x - rat_target_x| < RAT_STEP_SIZE`) in
`update_rat`. Because the rat's distance to the target changes by
exactly RAT_STEP_SIZE per tick, this is guaranteed to fire exactly once
per pass through the target regardless of grid alignment -- proven by
construction (a sequence decreasing by a fixed step through zero always
has at least one term with |value| less than the step), not just tested.

**Ported faithfully**: `proxloaf`'s box ((46-32)*4=56, y=64, w=40, h=16
-- w/h carry across unscaled, same formula already confirmed via
TROLL_BOX_W/_H matching their raw values exactly). The loaf is NOT
consumed when dropped in the box (unlike the apple/jug) -- matches the
source exactly: `loafhere+room=255` only happens inside `ratcoll`, once
the rat actually reaches it, so the loaf stays a real, visible,
still-pickupable actor until then. `ratcoll`'s own
`bit 7,(ix+colour) / call z,ratnewdir` ported via `rat_dir`, which
already mirrors that same bit (ratnewdir XORs both the same way) --
`if rat_dir==0, force a new direction` after eating.

**Verified three ways**:
1. Poked `rat_target_active`/`rat_target_x` directly and watched the
   rat cross a synthetic target: consumed the loaf, cleared the target,
   showed "[X-ALL.TXT line 915] / [X-ALL.TXT line 916] / [X-ALL.TXT line 917]" (X-ALL.TXT's
   own `thanksforloafmess`, byte-for-byte), dismissed cleanly on SPACE.
2. Drove the REAL drop path end to end through the actual inventory UI
   (carry the loaf, open inventory, select, drop) with Dizzy positioned
   inside the box: armed correctly, `rat_target_x` matched the loaf's
   real placed x (64), loaf stayed in the room at `room=36`, not
   consumed. Rendered screenshot confirms the loaf sits visibly on the
   rat's own platform.
3. Same drop, positioned OUTSIDE the box: correctly does nothing.

Playtest trajectory byte-identical; art verifier still 104/104.

## T0035: vertical room transitions + room 52 (THE ENTRANCE HALL)

User: "let's carry on to the next rooms, the one above the rat path."
Room 36's up-neighbor is room 52 (roomno+16, X-ALL.TXT `goneup`/
`gonedown`), named "THE ENTRANCE HALL" in rooms.json.

**Ran into a real capacity wall first, not a bug.** Adding room 52's raw
data (91 placements, 15 sprite variants, 1451 compiled bytes) to the
build corrupted framebuffer A and froze the game -- traced precisely (a
band-pattern probe, then measuring every symbol's address in the map)
to this: the build was ALREADY only 9 bytes short of the $4000
framebuffer boundary before room 52 was added at all. There is no
assembler safety net for this -- lwasm has no idea $4000/$6000 are
special, it just assembles sequentially, so an overflow doesn't error,
it silently corrupts the framebuffer at runtime. Reverted cleanly,
verified byte-identical to the last known-good trajectory, and brought
the real numbers to the user rather than force a workaround -- they
chose "investigate freeing memory first" over trimming room 52's
content or pursuing bank-switching (a bigger architecture change,
consistent with this port's existing choice to avoid all-RAM mode).

**Real fix, not a compromise: cross-room sprite deduplication.**
Checked whether the "trim content" framing was even the right one
first -- it wasn't. Room 35 and room 36 already duplicate 10 wall/door
sprite frames between them (each room emitted its own private copy
under a room-prefixed label, e.g. `r35_spr_134` and `r36_spr_134` were
byte-IDENTICAL), because `--shade` off collapses every placement of a
frame to exactly one variant, yet the label was still room-prefixed.
Room 52 itself reuses 7 of its 15 sprites from that same set. This is
pure waste, zero cost to fidelity, and specific to this project's own
now-verbatim pipeline (a `--shade`-on pipeline could still need
per-room tonal variants of the same frame, so this isn't universal).

Added `--shared-sprites PATH` to roompack: a frame's plain, unshaded
sprite bitmap is emitted ONCE, under a global label (`spr_134`, no room
prefix), into a shared file the first time any room in a
`regen_art.sh` run needs it; every later room just references that
existing label. `tools/verify_verbatim.py` updated to check the shared
file's frames too (same byte-for-byte guarantee, no exception).

**Caught a real bug in the dedup itself, before it shipped**: the
cache-loading parser checked `line.strip_suffix("_w")` against the
WHOLE line (`"spr_115_w\tfcb 16"`), which never matches because the
line doesn't END in `_w` -- it has the `fcb` payload after it. Every
room therefore thought it was first and wrote its own copy anyway,
which lwasm's own "multiply defined symbol" error caught immediately
on the very next build. Fixed by matching only the first
whitespace-delimited token (the actual label). A reminder that a
silent no-op in a text-parsing loop won't announce itself the way a
wrong physics value does -- it just quietly fails to do anything, and
the ONLY reason this was caught is that the failure mode (duplicate
labels) happens to be one the assembler already checks for.

**Result**: 51-55 bytes of headroom in the low region, 213 in the gap
-- both now positive, both fragile (any future room needs the same
treatment or more freeing). Full regression trajectory byte-identical.
Art verifier unaffected (0 differ either way).

**Vertical transition mechanic** (`ml_uplp`/`ml_downlp` in room36.asm,
`room_transition_up`/`_down`, `load_room`'s new `lr_room52` branch):
same shape as T0031's step-climb (both are the source's own
checktopside/checkbottomside), extended with a room-gated threshold
check. `TOP_TRANSITION_Y`/`BOT_TRANSITION_Y` are this port's own feel-
based choices (the source's raw y=66/182 use a different anchor and a
fixed eggheight this port already avoids reusing, same reasoning as
REACH_MARGIN). Confirmed the real gap geometrically first, from the
COMPILED cmask, not the source placement rows -- a naive single-row
check at room 36's y=48 wall row found several apparent "gaps" that
turned out to be blocked by other geometry (a shelf at y=80) once
actually probed; only x~192-232 (next to the rope decoration, frame
130) is genuinely open from the main floor all the way up.

**Verified with real jump physics** (dy=-8, matching `JUMP_DY`, not an
artificial forced value): placed Dizzy rising through x=208 in room
36, watched `cur_room` flip 36->52 exactly when y crossed
`TOP_TRANSITION_Y`, arriving in room 52 and settling naturally onto its
stairs. Screenshot confirms room 52 renders correctly: the picture,
crossed swords, railings, and the stair pyramid, torches in artifact
orange.

**Known gap, disclosed rather than hidden**: the down-transition
(`room_transition_down`) is code-correct and symmetric, but a full scan
of room 52's ACTUAL compiled cmask found no x position where all
THREE of Dizzy's foot probes (FOOT_L/M/R, spanning 11px) are
simultaneously clear -- the pyramid's stairs cover every reachable
column too solidly for `check_ground` to ever report "no floor" within
this room alone. `RESPAWN_ROOM=36` means dying always returns you to
the dungeon, so this isn't a permanent trap, but there is currently no
hazard in room 52 either, so a player who climbs up has no way back
down except by finding some other means to trigger death, or a future
session building one. Likely reflects the real game's own room 52
having OTHER neighbors (left/right) not part of this vertical slice
that provide the real return route -- not something to force-fit into
this one gap.

**Not yet built**: `proxpicture`'s look-at-picture message
(X-ALL.TXT `lookatpicturemess`, single box, "[X-ALL.TXT line 850]
PICTURE..."). Deliberately deferred -- the memory budget is razor-thin
again (51-55 bytes) after this session's work, and a proximity check
plus its message text was judged not worth risking another overflow
for a flavor-only interaction. The railing pickup (frame 192) needed
NO new code at all: pickup/inventory is frame-agnostic, and unknown
item names already fall back to `msg_name_generic` via `item_name_msg`.

## T0033 follow-up: the fed rat needs to actually clear the path

User, after playing: "the mouse needs to walk away after eating the
bread, to clear the path for dizzy." Correct -- X-ALL.TXT's `ratcoll`
only picks a new random direction within the SAME [RAT_MIN_X,
RAT_MAX_X] patrol band it always had; it doesn't leave. That's a loose
reading of the [X-ALL.TXT line 917] message text at best.

**Fix**: once fed, the rat ignores its normal patrol/boundary logic
entirely and walks left at the usual RAT_STEP_SIZE toward
`RAT_FLED_X` (new `ur_flee` branch in `update_rat`, gated on a new
`rat_fled` flag). Checked the real compiled cmask before picking the
value, not RAT_MIN_X/MAX_X blindly -- turns out those were never a
physical platform edge either (the floor at the rat's own height is
solid from x=8 to past x=244; RAT_MIN_X=48 was just a chosen patrol
band, per the original's own repurposed-field bound). `RAT_FLED_X=8`
is the room's real left wall, so this is a genuine walk to a safe
corner, not an arbitrary teleport. Stays lethal on contact throughout
(the source doesn't say it becomes safe) -- only the patrol behaviour
changes. No despawn/clear-rect special-casing needed: `draw_actors`
already redraws every actor every frame regardless of motion, so a
parked rat keeps rendering correctly for free.

**A real debugging trap, worth recording**: the first version of this
looked completely broken in testing -- `rat_fled` read back as 1, but
the rat's x never moved, across hundreds of sampled ticks. Chased it
through: checked the assembled branch target byte-for-byte against the
listing (correct), added a temporary counter instruction at the top of
the new code path and rebuilt (it read 0, proving the branch never
executed), then checked whether the mainloop was running AT ALL by
watching an unrelated global (`rng_ctr`) -- also frozen. **The real
cause: eating the loaf arms `ratloaf_msg_pending`, which blocks the
ENTIRE mainloop inside `msg_chatter`'s wait-for-SPACE loop.** My first
test never pressed SPACE, so nothing in the game was progressing --
not just the rat. A second test with a correctly-timed SPACE press
showed it working immediately. Lesson: when a change appears totally
inert in a poke-based test, check whether the WHOLE mainloop is
actually advancing (any unrelated counter) before concluding the new
code itself is unreached -- a blocked message box looks identical to a
plain bug from outside.

Verified: rat walks 116->108->...->16->8 and parks exactly at
RAT_FLED_X, screenshot confirms it visibly out of the loaf/rope
corridor. Playtest trajectory byte-identical, art verifier unaffected.

Memory note: this cost ~42 net bytes. Low-region headroom is now only
13 bytes -- the next change of any kind needs a headroom check first
(map file, highest symbol address below $4000) before writing any code.

## T0033 follow-up #2: "exit through the hole on the right", and a real memory audit that found a live bug

User: "The rat has to exit and disapeer through the hole in the wall on
the right side of the screen." Direct correction to the just-shipped
left-and-park version.

**There really is a hole**, confirmed against the compiled cmask, not
guessed: x=248/252 are the only fully-open columns (no collision at any
row) anywhere in room 36, right at the screen's own right edge, near the
rope decoration (frame 130) Dizzy climbs through to room 52. `ur_flee`
rewritten to walk RIGHT (mirrored sprite) toward `RAT_FLED_X=224` --
deliberately short of the true 248 opening, because the rat's sprite is
32px wide and `blit` has no edge clamp (confirmed: it will happily write
past column 32 of a row into the START of the next row, silent visual
corruption, not a crash) -- and DESPAWN (`room=255`, the same "gone"
convention consumed items already use) there rather than park, since
"disappear" was explicit. Disclosed trade-off: no explicit erase-on-
despawn (would cost bytes this build didn't have); its last position
sits inside dense existing wall/rope texture, not open background, so
residual pixels are hard to notice in practice.

### The real memory ceiling, and a live corruption bug found while investigating it

User asked directly: "how much are we missing? Keep in mind the original
game ran on 48kb and this one is 64kb." Investigating that question
found something worse than a tight budget.

**The headroom-checking method used since T0035 was wrong.** It found
"the highest symbol address still below $4000" and called that number
free space. That is blind to a REAL failure mode: content defined AFTER
that symbol in file order can independently land ABOVE $4000 (inside
live framebuffer A) while something else, earlier in the same region,
still happens to sit under the boundary. Checked properly (does ANY
symbol fall in $4000-$57FF, $6000-$77FF, or >=$8000, except the BUFA/BUFB
markers themselves) against the CURRENTLY COMMITTED, PUSHED build from
before this session even started: **dizzy_frame24 through frame35 (24
symbols, the back half of the walk-right animation) were already sitting
inside live framebuffer A.** This has been true since room 52 (T0035)
pushed the existing `org $5800` split point too late to save it -- by
the time the assembler reaches the `org` line before frame36, frames
24-35 had already been assigned addresses past $4000 by ordinary
sequential growth, and the org only rescues frame36 onward. Not
something today's session introduced; today's session is what finally
measured it correctly. Confirmed the failure mode empirically too: a
mid-session attempt to redistribute more content into the gaps produced
exactly this signature (dizzy frames past $4000, `aspr_104` past $8000)
before being caught and reverted.

**The 64K question, answered with real numbers.** $0E00-$4000 (12800
bytes) plus the inter-framebuffer gap $5800-$5FFF (2048 bytes) is the
"safe, no-reconfiguration" budget this port has used since T0023 --
14848 bytes total. A SECOND, previously entirely unused 2KB block sits
at $7800-$7FFF (right after framebuffer B, before $8000 where ROM
starts) -- ordinary, always-mapped RAM on the base 32K address range
every CoCo2 has, 64K or not; no SAM all-RAM/banking reconfiguration
needed. Confirmed genuinely free by checking the runtime stack pointer
(~$03D3 at boot, nowhere near either block) before relying on it.
Between the two, real headroom right now: 694 bytes low region, 259
bytes gap1 ($5800), 1340 bytes gap2 ($7800) -- roughly 2300 bytes total,
a large improvement over the single-digit-to-13-byte margins this build
had been running on.

That said: **the true 64K ceiling is NOT reached by these two gaps
alone.** They total 4096 bytes; the full $8000-$FEFF ROM-shadow region
on a genuine 64K board would add ~32512 more if the SAM's all-RAM/
banking mode were engaged -- NOT attempted this session (a real
architecture change, needs its own careful, dedicated pass: the CPU
can't fetch further instructions from ROM once it's banked out, so
every remaining call into BASIC/ROM has to be accounted for first).
Comparable in scale to what the original 48K Spectrum has after its own
screen+system overhead. This is the honest, complete answer to "how
much are we missing": not memory itself -- the target genuinely has
room comparable to the source -- but this port currently only accesses
the always-safe ~15KB slice of it.

**Room 52 pulled from the build, disclosed not hidden.** Exhaustively
verified (not estimated) that room 52's addition makes total demand for
shared_sprites_data.asm + font_data.asm + actor_data.asm + room2_data.asm
(2797 bytes) exceed the two gaps' combined free space (~2285 bytes) by
about 512 bytes, regardless of how the four files are distributed
between them (checked every subset). Removing room 52 (its own
placement/cmask data, its 8 exclusive shared sprites, the railing actor,
and disabling -- not deleting -- the vertical-transition trigger and
`load_room`'s r52 branch) closes the gap with real margin to spare, and
every check (art verifier, playtest trajectory, and a direct capture of
Dizzy walking through the exact frame range that was corrupted) confirms
a clean, working build. Re-enabling room 52 needs either a real further
content reduction (the flame/water tiles are NOT yet deduplicated the
way sprites are, since --shade being uniformly off makes their tonal
variants collapse too -- a real, available saving not yet taken) or the
64K all-RAM work above; `tools/regen_art.sh` documents exactly what to
restore and where.

**roompack gained `--shared-sprites-budget`/`--shared-sprites-overflow`**
(splits the shared-sprite file across two destinations once a size
budget is hit) while chasing this -- built, verified against the primary
file working correctly, but NOT currently exercising the split (the
final fix was removing room 52, not needing the overflow path). Kept
for whenever room 52 or a future room needs it.

**Process lesson, the important one**: "does it assemble" and "does the
playtest trajectory match" are NOT sufficient to prove a build isn't
corrupted when relocating data across memory regions -- both of those
passed on the broken committed build too, because the corruption
happened to sit in animation frames (24-35) that weren't exercised by
the specific playtest script in use. Only a real address-range audit
(every symbol's location, checked against every protected region, not
just "the boundary I was watching") catches this. `tools/regen_art.sh`
now states the correct check explicitly.

### T0041: the SAM's all-RAM mode, implemented and verified -- room 52 re-enabled

User's explicit call, made with the risk disclosed up front: the CoCo2
Technical Reference Manual says SAM register TY (`$FFDE`/`$FFDF`) "should
be cleared at all times", an unqualified warning against ever setting
all-RAM mode. User chose to implement it anyway, targeting real 64K
hardware. Built in stages, each verified before trusting the next:

**1. Mechanism, verified in MAME before touching real game code.** A
standalone diagnostic (`/tmp/allram_test.asm`) confirmed: `sta $ffdf`
makes `$8000+` genuinely writable RAM (write/read-back round-trip, vs.
ROM content beforehand); `$0000-$7FFF` is completely untouched (no bank
swap -- sentinels planted there stayed put); `sta $ffde` correctly
switches back (`$8000+` reads ROM content again), proving the SAM's own
control-register decode stays live even while all-RAM mode is engaged.
A second diagnostic (`/tmp/allram_pia.asm`) sampled `$FF03` (PIA0 side
B, the vsync flag `wait_vsync` depends on every frame) 40 times across
real elapsed time while all-RAM mode was active: the value changed on
its own partway through the run, which plain RAM cannot do (it would
just echo back whatever was last written) -- confirming the PIA stays
live too, not frozen.

**2. The real complication: BASIC's own CLOADM loader runs BEFORE this
code, in normal ROM mode.** A DECB block targeted directly at `$8000+`
would silently fail to write -- the loader has already finished and
handed off to `start:` by the time any of our own code could flip the
SAM bit; flipping it here is too late to help data that needed to
already be there. Fix: stage the data at an ordinary low-memory CLOADM
destination instead (loads normally, same as everything else in this
file), then relocate it up to its real address once all-RAM mode is
live. `lwasm` has exactly the primitive this needs: `PHASE`/`DEPHASE`
lets code be assembled as if living at one address (labels resolve
there, so every reference elsewhere in the file compiles correctly)
while the actual output bytes land at a completely different physical
location in the file. Confirmed with a throwaway test
(`/tmp/phase_test.asm`) before relying on it for real: `org $0500` /
`phase $8000` / data / `dephase` puts the bytes at file offset $0500
but resolves labels to $8000+, exactly as needed.

**3. Implementation** (`room36.asm`): room 52's data (the piece pulled
in T0035/the memory audit above) is staged at `org $0500` -- comfortably
below `start:`'s own `$0E00` and well clear of the ~$03D3 stack (which
only grows further DOWN, toward $0000, away from $0500) -- wrapped in
`phase $8000`/`dephase`. `start:` engages all-RAM mode (`sta $ffdf`,
right after the existing SAM/PIA/video-mode setup, before anything else
touches memory) and immediately copies `r52_staged_start..r52_staged_end`
up to `$8000` with a tight `lda ,x+ / sta ,y+` loop before Dizzy's own
spawn/`load_room` runs. `load_room` gained back its `lr_room52` branch
(labels already resolve to $8000+ thanks to PHASE, no different from
referencing r35_/r36_ symbols), and the vertical-transition trigger in
`ml_uplp` is unconditional again. Room 52 is regenerated standalone (no
`--shared-sprites`) -- with ~32KB free above $8000, the cross-room dedup
the two old 2KB gaps needed to survive at all buys nothing up here and
just adds an ordering dependency.

**4. Verified for real, not just assembled clean:**
- Full address-range audit on the actual build (not the diagnostic):
  zero symbols in framebuffer A/B, zero above `$FEFF`; 87 room-52
  symbols land in `$8000-$842B`, exactly where expected.
- GDB memory read of `$8000` on a running instance: `10 0d 02 01 00 02
  20 07...` -- byte-identical to `r52_spr_115`'s source data
  (`fcb $01,$00,$02,...` after its w/h/bpr header), proving the staged
  copy actually executed correctly at runtime, not just in theory.
- Forced the real jump physics (`dizzy_x=208, dizzy_y=45, dizzy_dy=-8,
  dizzy_floor=0`, same geometry as the original T0035 verification) and
  ran for real time: `cur_room` flipped 36->52, Dizzy settled at
  `dizzy_y=168`, `dizzy_x` unchanged at 208 -- matching
  `room_transition_up`'s own design exactly.
- Room 36's own boot capture (`harness/capture_display.sh`) is pixel-
  unchanged from before this work -- all-RAM mode and the relocation
  copy add zero visible disruption to the base game.
- `tools/verify_verbatim.py`: 112 sprites checked, 0 differ.
- `harness/coco_playtest.sh` regression script: runs clean, no crash,
  no corruption.

**Scope deliberately NOT touched**: room 52's two actor-table entries
(a pickupable "railingmess" prop, a "proxpicture" proximity trigger) --
that's T0040's job, `--actor-rooms` stays at `35,36`. The down-
transition's "no way back down within room 52 alone" gap (T0035's own
note, still true) is unaffected by any of this.

**Reusable pattern for future rooms**: the same `org <low addr>` /
`phase $8000+offset` / `dephase` staging trick, plus a copy loop in
`start:`, generalizes to anything future work wants to put above
`$8000` -- ~32KB of genuinely free space (`$8000-$FEFF`) now exists,
vastly more than the two old 2KB gaps combined. Keep the staging
address low (well under `$0E00`) and keep phase blocks non-overlapping
in their target range; the copy loop is cheap and can be repeated per
block, or generalized to a table of (src_start, src_end, dst) triples
if several blocks need staging in one build.

### T0034: game-over state -- real death message + a genuine end state

Real playtest premise: "lives currently wraps 3->0->3 with no end state".
Root cause was actually TWO gaps, not one: this port had never shown
anything on death at all (the original always does), and there was no
distinct behaviour at 0 lives either.

**The original's real flow** (X-ALL.TXT `nextlife`/`subfromlives`, line
1177 / the death handler at ~1370): every death shows `deadwindow`
([X-ALL.TXT line 991] + a hazard-specific quip like `killedbyflame`/
`ratgotyoumess`) and blocks on `waitforkey`, unconditionally. Only
AFTER that does it check lives: nonzero loops back to `nextlife`
(keep playing), zero falls through to `quitted` (flips back to the
title screen). This port has no title screen to fall back to -- a
vertical slice, not the full game -- so there's nothing faithful to
port for that specific fallthrough.

**Fix, in two pieces**:
- `msg_deadwindow`: the original's own `deadwindow` text, byte-for-byte
  (box position/size included), shown+dismissed on EVERY death now,
  same as the source. The hazard-specific second line the original
  also shows is deliberately NOT wired up -- `kill_dizzy`'s callers
  (rat contact, flame contact) don't currently pass which hazard killed
  Dizzy through to `update_death`, and threading that through is a
  separate, larger change than this task asked for.
- `msg_gameover`: NOT from X-ALL.TXT -- disclosed as this port's own
  invention, since the state it covers (0 lives, nothing to flip back
  to) doesn't have a real equivalent in a 3-room slice. Same box
  footprint as `msg_deadwindow` so it fully overdraws with no stray
  fragments, shown+dismissed only when lives==0, immediately before the
  same refill-to-3-and-respawn this always did.

**Verified with a scripted MAME test** (`/tmp/t0034_test.lua`, poke
`lives`/`killed` directly, drive SPACE via the real ioport field, read
state back): at lives=0, exactly two boxes appear in sequence (deadwindow,
then GAME OVER/PRESS SPACE) and lives only refills to 3 after BOTH are
dismissed -- screenshots confirm both render correctly, text centred,
readable. At lives=2 (the normal case), exactly ONE box appears and
lives decrements+respawns immediately after it's dismissed, same as
before this fix -- confirming the new gameover path is genuinely gated
on lives==0 and doesn't change the ordinary-death behaviour at all.
Full regression clean: `verify_verbatim.py` 112/112, playtest script
runs clean, full address-range audit still 0 in every protected region.

### T0036: room 53 (SNAP HAPPY GATOR) added, room 52's east neighbor

First room added since the vertical slice was declared done -- picked
room 53 specifically because it reuses the horizontal transition
mechanism (35<->36) rather than the vertical one (36<->52): X-ALL.TXT's
`goneleft`/`goneright` never consult the collision mask at all (just set
a fixed x and carry y through unchanged), so unlike a vertical neighbor
there was no real gap to find or verify geometrically -- much lower risk
for a first "add more rooms" pass.

**Explored and abandoned room 35's up-neighbor (51, MOAT AND
PORTCULLIS) first**: `goneup` is unconditional roomno+16 in X-ALL.TXT,
so 51 IS room 35's real neighbor by the game's own arithmetic. But
`checktopside`/`checkbottomside` both require `checkline` to report
CLEAR before a vertical transition can fire (X-ALL.TXT ~6497/~6524) --
i.e. an actual gap in the wall -- and decoding room 35's real compiled
cmask found its y=48 wall row 100% solid across the whole room, no gap
anywhere. Room 52's own up-neighbor (68, BANQUET HALL) was checked too:
room 52's ceiling IS wide open, but room 68's own floor is 100% solid
except the 2-column screen-edge padding every room has. Neither pair
has a real connection in the compiled data -- this port has no title
screen to reach any other way, and inventing a gap that isn't really
there would be exactly the kind of guessing this project's geometry
work has consistently avoided elsewhere (T0035's own room 36/52 gap was
found the same way, not assumed). Left unbuilt, not wired -- a genuine
dead end, recorded so a future session doesn't re-attempt it blind.

**roompack crashed on room 51** (`pixel_x -4 out of byte range`) before
any of the above was even reachable -- a real, previously-unhit bug:
4 of its placements have `x<32` in the original's own coordinate space,
which the `(x-32)*4` transform sends negative, and pixel_x is a single
`fcb` byte (0-255) that cannot encode a negative value at all, not just
clamp one. Fixed in `roompack` (not room-51-specific): any placement
whose transformed pixel_x falls outside 0..255 is now skipped with a
loud stderr warning instead of panicking or being silently clamped to a
guessed position. Room 51's own 4 skipped placements (frames
178/179/180/210) are off its left edge -- plausibly part of the
portcullis mechanism the room is named for, not ordinary background --
worth a real look if room 51 ever gets built for its own sake, not
something to paper over.

**Room 53 build**: straight `roompack --room 53` (no `--shared-sprites`
-- see room 52's own note on why that's not worth it above $8000), same
staging+PHASE treatment as room 52. Combined room 52+53 staged data
(2873 bytes) no longer fit the old `$0500-$0E00` gap room 52 alone used
(2304 bytes available there) -- fixed by giving `start:` an explicit
`lds #$0100` (previously relied on BASIC's own leftover stack pointer,
observed ~$03D3 but never actually guaranteed) and moving the staging
org down to `$0100`, freeing the full `$0100-$0DFF` window (3584 bytes)
for both rooms' combined 2873-byte payload with real margin (455
bytes). One phase block now covers both rooms' data contiguously,
copied to `$8000+` by the same relocate loop from T0041.

**A real hazard-placement bug found by testing the transition, not
guessed**: room 53 has a torch flame at pixel_x 20-36 (`r53_room_flames`
in room53_data.asm). The obvious "arrive near the left edge" convention
(x=8, same as every other transition in this file) put a fresh arrival
close enough to that flame's box that falling/settling through it could
burn Dizzy immediately on entry -- caught with a scripted MAME test
forcing the transition and watching `killed` (it went from 0 to
counting down within a few frames of arrival). Fixed by entering at
x=48 instead -- confirmed against room 53's own compiled cmask to still
be solid floor there, and comfortably clear of the flame's box with
margin on both sides. Re-tested the same scenario after the fix:
`killed` stays 0 throughout, Dizzy settles cleanly.

**Verified**: full address-range audit (0 in framebuffers/ROM, 186
symbols correctly in `$8000-$89B9`), scripted MAME tests confirm both
transition directions (52->53 arriving at x=48/no death, 53->52 arriving
at x=216) work correctly with real key input (not just poked state),
room 53 screenshot confirms correct art (verified against the compiled
cmask, not eyeballed blind), room 36's own boot is pixel-unchanged,
`verify_verbatim.py` 134/134 (up from 112 -- room 53's own sprites),
playtest regression runs clean.

**Left for a later session, not this one**: room 53's own actor (a
crocodile, `extracted/actors.json` room 53 slot 16) and its two
pickupables (a rock, a whiskey bottle) aren't wired -- `--actor-rooms`
stays at `35,36`, matching how room 52's actors were deferred to T0040.
Room 51/68 (the abandoned pair above) and any other neighbor worth
trying next should start from a real compiled-cmask gap check, not
from the roomno±16/±1 arithmetic alone -- that arithmetic says what
room COULD be adjacent, not whether the level design actually connects
it walkably.

### T0037: attempted, blocked by a real harness bug -- deferred, not answered

Set out to confirm the T0031 step-climb asymmetry at x=106 against the
real Spectrum via `harness/zx_orig.sh`. Found and fixed one real bug on
the way (below), then hit a second, more fundamental one that stopped
this task short of an actual answer.

**Fixed**: `zx_orig.sh`'s general-purpose run path used `-nothrottle`,
which (combined with `-video none`) silently stops `emu.register_periodic`
from firing more than a handful of times on the `spectrum` MAME driver --
confirmed with a bare tick counter: it reached ~f=20 and then nothing,
no error, regardless of `-seconds_to_run`. Removed `-nothrottle` from
that path (kept on the separate `--from-tape` path, which was already
proven working and isn't worth the risk of re-running -- see its own
comment). Runs now cost roughly 1 real second per emulated second, fine
for a few seconds of scripted movement.

**Blocked by**: with that fixed, `manager.machine:load()` (restoring the
`room36.sta` savestate mid-script, which is how the whole "fast, 5-second
run instead of a 7-minute tape load" trick works) turns out to ALSO stop
`register_periodic` from firing anything further -- confirmed the same
way, with a minimal script that prints every tick: ticks stop dead the
frame after `load()` returns (which itself reports success, no error).
