**It's a screen-flip trick on ONE room boundary, not a gameplay
mechanic.** `upsidedown` is a single global flag. It is read in exactly
three places: `flipscreenrou` (flips the DISPLAY), the gravity-tumble
code (`cp 8 / ld a,-6 / jr z,aroundgravity` -- while `sequence==8`, dy
is pinned to a constant -6 instead of accumulating normally, for the
duration of one scripted animation), and nowhere else. There is no
"walk around with inverted controls" state anywhere in the source --
once the one scripted tumble finishes and you land, physics are
completely normal again.

**The four "rooms" are really: one well shaft, its two real endpoints,
and a redirect that isn't a room at all.**
- Room 7 is empty in the extraction (0 things) -- it never gets
  DRAWN. Walking off room 23's bottom edge lands you there by ordinary
  grid arithmetic (23-16=7), and `fallenoutof23`
  (X-ALL.TXT ~1247) immediately redirects to room 39 with an ordinary
  downward tumble. Room 7 needs no art, ever.
- Room 39 (GOING DOWN THE WELL!) is the shaft itself, and it has TWO
  special-cased exits, neither of which is the ordinary grid
  transition: leaving toward 23 triggers `flipandsettumble`
  (y=180, sequence=8, dy pinned to -6, `upsidedown` toggled, `jp
  gotoenterroom` straight to room 39... which reads oddly until you
  realize this is the "climb back UP the well" traversal -- the flip
  makes falling code look like climbing) (~1296); leaving the OTHER
  way checks `lastroom` (~1310) and redirects to EITHER 23 or 55
  depending which end you last came from -- a one-way-feeling shaft
  that remembers your direction, not a fixed pair of exits.
- Rooms 23 (A STRANGE NEW WORLD!) and 55 (THE BOTTOMLESS WELL) are the
  real endpoints, drawn and played completely normally once you're in
  them.

**Room 55 is already at the built slice's own frontier, and needs
nothing new at all.** `55 = 54+1` (T0067's own grid arithmetic) --
THE WIDE-EYED DRAGON's east neighbour, already listed in
games/dizzy/recipe/MAP.md's frontier. It could be added today with the
existing --actor-rooms/room_desc_table pipeline, no new engine work,
exactly like T0067's four rooms. Rooms 39/23/7 hang off it in a strict
chain (55->39->23->7, each reachable only through the last), so they'd
have to come in that order.

**The one real new capability needed is the screen flip, and this
port's own architecture makes it CHEAPER than the original's, not
harder.** The source's trick is startlingly clever for a memory-
constrained target: `screentable` is a lookup of the SPECTRUM's
notoriously interleaved row addresses, and `flipscreenrou` swaps PAIRS
OF ENTRIES IN THAT TABLE (not pixel data) -- so every subsequent
ordinary draw call, which already goes through `screentable[row]` to
find its target address, transparently lands upside-down for free,
with no separate "flip the picture" pass and no per-draw cost. This
port's `blit`/`clear_and_blit` don't have that indirection -- T0064
deliberately removed table lookups from the hot path for speed
(`draw_base + row*32 + col`, direct arithmetic) -- so replicating the
trick AS WRITTEN would mean reintroducing exactly the indirection that
work removed. The straightforward alternative fits this port much
better: a plain post-render pass that swaps row N with row (191-N)
across the same range the source uses (`6*8` to `183` -- i.e.
excluding the status bar, which should never flip), run once whenever
`upsidedown` changes state, not on every draw. Cheap, because it would
only ever run during the one scripted well traversal, never during
ordinary play.

**What building the whole chain would actually take, in order:**
1. Room 55 -- ordinary T0067-shaped work, no blockers, could start now.
2. Room 39 -- ordinary room content, PLUS: the screen-flip pass
   described above; wiring seq6/seq8 into dizzy_seqtab's existing
   ANIMATION dispatch (the table entries are already recovered and
   sitting there unused, per T0059's own note); and replacing the
   generic grid transition with the two special-cased ones above for
   BOTH of 39's edges (neither is ordinary).
3. Room 23 -- ordinary content, plus the SAME special-casing on its
   OWN downward exit (its ordinary down-neighbour is room 7, which
   redirects rather than existing).
4. Room 7 -- nothing to build; the redirect logic lives in room 23's
   own transition, not in a room 7 that exists.

No code changed for this entry -- scoping only, so the next session (or
this one, if asked) has a real decision to make instead of a guess.

### T0073: OVERCLOCK off, and why draw_water doesn't get the flame treatment

Turned the SAM 2x speed-up off by default (`OVERCLOCK equ 0`). T0064's
profiling already showed the port comfortable at 1x -- room 36, fire
lit, the heaviest steady state -- at 47.6ms of a 66.7ms frame, still
15.0 passes/sec. The speed-up was bought when the budget was
genuinely tight; it no longer is, and it's the one setting in this
codebase whose safety margin MAME can't verify (double-speed operation
is documented as marginal on some real CoCo2s depending on RAM chip
speed -- an analog concern, invisible to emulation).

**But room 35 measured 14.0 passes/sec at 1x, not the expected flat
15.0** -- reproduced twice with `harness/rate.lua`, confirmed with
`harness/profile.lua`'s `PROF_ROOM=35`. This wasn't a new bug from the
OVERCLOCK edit itself: T0064's own note on room 35 already says it
"went from 14.3 to a flat 15.0 passes/sec [at 2x], because the extra
room absorbs the room-transition spike it used to lose a pass to."
Same mechanism, reappearing now that 1x halves the spare headroom that
used to swallow the spike.

**Checked whether `draw_water` could get T0064's flame fix (a
`cb_needed`-style damage-rect gate) -- it can't, and here's why, so
nobody retries this:** `draw_flames`' saving came specifically from a
duplication BUG in the source data -- the flame table's 4 entries are
really only 2 distinct bitmaps (0/1 and 2/3 byte-identical), so masking
the variant to `flame_ctr & 2` makes the "did the picture actually
change" check true only every 2nd pass, and `cb_needed` skips the
other half. Checked room35_data.asm's 4 water bitmaps the same way:
all four are genuinely distinct (confirmed by dumping the raw `fcb`
tables, not by inspection of the source disassembly), and `water_ctr`
advances every pass (`ANIM_DIVIDER equ 1`, room36.asm ~L275). A
variant-changed check on water would read true on every single pass --
identical to what `draw_water` already does, at the cost of an extra
compare. There's no free lunch hiding here; water's frame cost is
real, animated content, not redundant redraws like the flames were.

**Decision: shipped anyway.** A 14.0-vs-15.0 dip in one room (~7%,
still well above anything that reads as stutter) is a smaller risk than
leaving an unverifiable real-hardware margin in place for a benefit the
profiling says the port no longer needs. Documented in room36.asm's own
OVERCLOCK comment rather than left as a silent regression. Revisit only
if room 35 gets its own reported "feels sluggish" -- at that point the
honest fix is cutting water's animation to a 2-step cycle (a visual
fidelity call, not a free optimization, so it needs sign-off) or
re-enabling OVERCLOCK for that room specifically.

`memaudit.py` clean, `verify_verbatim.py` clean (art unaffected --
this is a pacing-only change). Framedump byte-diff not re-run: room
content per logical pass doesn't depend on wall-clock speed, only on
pass count, so it isn't the right check for this class of change.

### T0074: room 55 (THE BOTTOMLESS WELL) -- built, and a harness dead end worth recording

Added exactly per T0038's own scoping note: room 55 is 54+1, needs no
new engine work, buildable the same self-contained way as T0067's four
rooms. `tools/regen_art.sh` gained one more roompack invocation;
`room36.asm` gained one `include "room55_data.asm"` in the r9800
staging block (alongside 51/54/68) and one `fdb r55_room_desc` in
`room_desc_table`. That's the whole change -- the grid-arithmetic
transition code (`room_transition_left/right`, T0067) needs no edits
per room, by design; room 55's own west<->54 link and its blocked
north/east/south edges (39/56/71, all unbuilt) all fall out of the
existing mechanism for free.

`memaudit.py`: clean, but tight -- the r9800 staging block (framebuffer
B's 6KB window, carrying rooms 51/54/68/55) now reports **0 bytes
free**, not overflowing but with zero slack. The NEXT room added to
this specific block will need to move to a new third staging window
(same computed-destination pattern as r9800 itself, `org` from a fresh
low address, `phase` continuing from `r9800_staged_end`). `verify_verbatim.py`
clean. Rendered via `harness/framedump.lua DUMP_ROOM=55` and inspected
as a PNG -- the well shaft, trees and grass all present and correct.

**Dead end, recorded so it isn't rediscovered at real cost:** tried to
verify the 54<->55 transition by actually WALKING Dizzy there in MAME
(hold RIGHT after `respawn_room`/`killed=1` teleports him next to the
edge). Every variant froze -- `keyflags` reads back correctly for
SPACE but RIGHT/UP never register (confirmed with a `write_u8` tap on
`dizzy_x`: after the respawn's own write, nothing writes it again for
250+ held-key frames), while the EXACT SAME key-press technique against
a room reached WITHOUT the respawn/killed path (raw `cur_room` poke, or
`harness/topclimb.lua`'s real walk into room 53) works perfectly.
**Confirmed NOT a T0074 regression**: reproduces identically on the
pre-T0074 build, and targets room 54 specifically (already-shipped,
untouched by this task). Likely candidate, not chased further: the
respawn/death sequence leaves something (a message-wait state?) that
only reads SPACE, and 40+ seconds of alternating SPACE presses never
satisfied whatever dismiss condition it wants. Resolved enough to stop worrying about it: re-ran
`harness/topclimb.lua` (a REAL death, walking into room 53's
crocodile pit, no manual `killed` poke) and it falls, respawns, and
keeps responding to RIGHT every single cycle, dozens of times over.
So a genuine in-game death doesn't lock input -- only forcing
`killed=1` directly, skipping whatever else a real hazard trigger sets
alongside it, does. Not a player-facing bug; a test-harness gotcha:
when a future session needs to teleport-and-then-drive-keys for a
room this task's chain didn't reach naturally, walk Dizzy into a real
hazard for the death (or use `harness/framedump.lua`'s pattern, which
only ever needs a STATIC pose after teleporting, never a held key
afterward) rather than poking `killed` directly.

Confidence in the transition itself rests on construction, not this
failed runtime test: `room_exists`/`load_room` read the same
`room_desc_table` this entry appends to, and the identical mechanism
is what 51/54/68/69 already ship on.

### T0075: the well lid, and a real memory-corruption bug T0074 shipped without noticing

**The feature itself is small.** X-ALL.TXT's `proxcrowbarrou` (~3443)
is a one-shot proximity trigger, not an actor with a per-frame update
-- same shape as the dragon's own `proxsleep`: `aabb_hit` against a
fixed box (raw `(46,144,8,16)` -> pixel `(56,144,32,16)`, the same
`(x-32)*4` / y,h-unscaled conversion the dragon's own constants already
use), and on the first hit it hides `welllidhere`'s actor slot
(`room=255`, which also doubles as the one-shot latch -- a hidden slot
never matches `uw_find` again) and shows `usecrowbarmess`
(`msg_crowbar`). No inventory/held-item check: the source doesn't have
one despite the trigger's name, and `crowbarhere` (the actual pickup
item, room 88) isn't built in this slice -- the mechanic is wired and
correct, just unreachable by the "hold the crowbar" route until some
future session builds room 88. `update_welllid` added to mainloop
alongside the other per-room hazard updates; room 55 added to
`--actor-rooms` so roompack emits its four actor slots + two coins.

**What actually cost the whole session: a real, already-shipped
memory-corruption bug, not a bug in this feature.** Adding room 55's
actors grew `actor_data.asm` by ~150 bytes, and the game started
hanging on the very FIRST mainloop pass -- before any respawn, before
any test of the well lid itself, in room 36, doing nothing new.
`update_welllid` itself was confirmed innocent early (`cur_room!=55`
is an instant `rts`, and disabling the mainloop call entirely didn't
fix the hang) -- the actual cause took a full binary-search-by-symbol
investigation to find:

- A live PC trace (`cpu.state["PC"]`) against a known-good build showed
  execution stuck looping inside `blit`'s row-copy loop
  (`blit_alignedlp`), never reaching `wait_vsync` even once.
- Reading `blit_ptr` live during the loop showed a sprite header of
  `w=255 h=255 bpr=252` -- pure garbage, the exact "T0058 nibswap"
  class of bug this project's own `regen_art.sh` header already warns
  about, this time hitting `aspr_0` (the coin sprite, which room 36's
  own `coin_init` entry at (200,160) draws on literally the first
  pass).
- Dumping the DECB block list directly (`memaudit.py`'s own technique,
  by hand) found the real cause: the r9800 staging block (`room36.asm`,
  framebuffer B's 6KB window, carrying rooms 51/54/68/55) needed 7489
  bytes SOURCE-SIDE against a 6144-byte window -- **1345 bytes over**,
  silently. Its block loads AFTER gap2 (`actor_data.asm`, `org $7800`)
  in the file, and DECB/CLOADM applies blocks in file order, so the
  overflowing tail of the staging block was silently overwriting the
  tail of actor_data.asm at LOAD TIME, every single boot.
- Confirmed by reading the raw bytes at the same address from both
  blocks in the `.bin`: block 10 (actor_data.asm, correct) had `$10`
  where block 12 (staging, applied after) had `$ff` -- direct proof of
  which one "wins".

**This bug did not start with T0075 -- it started with T0074.** The
r9800 block's own needed size (`r9800_staged_end`) was IDENTICAL
(`$7d41`) whether or not room 55 had any actors at all, because it's
governed by the four rooms' STATIC content, not by `--actor-rooms`.
Room 55 alone (T0074) already pushed this block 1345 bytes over its
window; `memaudit.py` said "0 bytes free... every loaded byte is in a
region that allows loading" at the time and was simply wrong, because
it had never been asked to check whether two *different* DECB blocks
overlap EACH OTHER -- only whether each one individually lands
somewhere "allowed". T0074 "worked" by pure luck: whatever garbage
byte pattern the overlap produced at the time happened to not trigger
an infinite loop in `blit`. T0075's own actor growth shifted
`actor_data.asm`'s layout enough that the SAME overlap now clobbers a
different, load-bearing address (`aspr_0`), and this time the specific
garbage values (`$ff`×3) do hang.

**The fix, in two parts:**

1. `tools/memaudit.py` now also checks every pair of DECB blocks for
   address overlap, not just each block against the fixed region list
   -- this exact bug (individually-valid, mutually-overlapping blocks)
   was invisible to it before. Fails loudly now, naming both blocks and
   which one wins.
2. Closed the actual overflow by deduplicating repeated wall/floor/door
   tiles across ALL nine art-generating rooms (2/35/52/53/69/51/54/68/
   55/36), not just 2/35/36 as before -- `tools/roompack`'s existing
   `--shared-sprites-budget`/`--shared-sprites-overflow` pair (already
   built for "two separate small unused RAM blocks", just never asked
   for until now) splits the combined dedup pool: a small
   (`SHARED_BUDGET=6200`-char) primary file lands in r8000 (which had
   almost no spare margin to begin with), and everything past that
   budget overflows into a second file landed in r9800 (which has real
   room once its own four rooms shrink from the same dedup). Both
   files accumulate into ONE `shared_known` label set internally
   (roompack's own code, unchanged), so a tile used by rooms on both
   sides of the split still isn't emitted twice.

Tuning the budget was empirical, not derived: tried 600 (left r9800
866 bytes over), 4200 (237 over), 5600 (2 bytes over), landed on 6200
for real margin on both sides. **Final state, `memaudit.py`:** r8000
1939 free, r9800 167 free, gap2 162 free, no overlaps. Re-ran
`verify_verbatim.py` (clean -- this is all a layout/dedup change, no
pixel content changed) and the PC-trace/rng_ctr check (settles into
`wait_vsync` on pass 1, same as a known-good build) to confirm the
hang is actually gone, not just the symptom moved. The well-lid trigger
itself then verified via a state-scan test (teleport into room 55,
watch the actor slot's own room byte flip from 55 to 255 the instant
Dizzy enters the box) -- the direct-`killed=1`-poke-then-hold-a-key
technique from T0074's own dead-end entry was avoided entirely.

**Two numbers worth remembering if a tenth room ever needs a home:**
r8000 (framebuffer A) and r9800 (framebuffer B) are each a hard 6144
bytes, no exceptions, and NEITHER `memaudit.py`'s per-block region
check NOR a passing `lwasm` assembly says anything about whether two
blocks' ADDRESSES collide -- only the new overlap check does. Trust
that one over "it assembled and memaudit was clean" from now on.

**Two dead ends on the way to the fix above, so a future session
doesn't retry them:**
- Two INDEPENDENT `--shared-sprites` files (one for room2/35/36's
  existing pool, a second hand-rolled one for 51/54/68/55, each with
  its own `--shared-sprites` flag and no `--shared-sprites-overflow`
  link between them) fails to assemble: roompack tracks "already
  emitted" labels in a set that's local to ONE invocation's primary+
  overflow pair, so two unrelated pools both choosing the same frame
  number (51/54/68/55 and room2/35/36 both happened to use frame 192
  as an ordinary wall tile) emit the same global label twice --
  `lwasm`'s own duplicate-symbol error, not a silent corruption, but
  wasted a round trip discovering it. The fix is `--shared-sprites-
  budget`/`--shared-sprites-overflow` on ONE shared pool, not two
  separate ones.
- Routing the overflow file into r8000 (alongside the small primary)
  instead of r9800 fails differently: r8000 had almost no spare margin
  to begin with (its own four rooms + room2 already used nearly all
  6144 bytes before any of this), so ANY meaningful overflow content
  landing there overflows it instead, just relocating the exact same
  bug one staging block over. The overflow file has to go where the
  real headroom actually is (r9800, once 51/54/68/55's OWN dedup
  shrinks them) -- check the CURRENT free-byte numbers per block before
  picking a destination, don't assume the smaller-numbered block has
  room just because it usually has in the past.

### T0076: room 51's ceiling -- a denied vertical transition never reset dizzy_dy

Playtest: "I can manage to jump over the edge of the top wall and out
the door, I also cannot reach the room above in any way" (room 51,
MOAT AND PORTCULLIS). Also reported the portcullis gate and its lever
looking dead -- turned out to be a symptom of this same bug, not a
separate one (see below).

**Room 51's own collision mask (`room51_data.asm`) has no ceiling at
all above y=48** -- rows 0-11 of `r51_room_cmask` are entirely `$00`,
open sky, because that's genuinely correct: the staircase visible in
the room's own art climbs to a top step around (x=80-95, y=48), and
the space above it is meant to be a TRANSITION zone (up to room 67,
`R51 -- N/S --- R67` in MAP.md), not a walled ceiling. Room 67 isn't
built in this slice, so the transition is denied every time -- correct,
same as any other unbuilt edge -- but here's what "denied" actually did:

`rt_vertical` (`room_transition_up`/`_down`'s shared tail) checked
`room_exists` and, on failure, jumped straight to `ml_vertdone` --
**without clearing `dizzy_dy`**. Contrast `ml_bonk`, the code path for
hitting a REAL ceiling elsewhere in the room: `clr dizzy_dy` then fall
through to the same `ml_vertdone`. Horizontally this class of bug can't
happen -- `check_wall` physically stops `dizzy_x` from ever changing
BEFORE `room_transition_left/right` is even called, so a denied
transition there really does look and feel like a wall. Vertically
there is no equivalent: `check_ceiling`/`check_ground` pass Dizzy
through a REAL gap in the room's own collision mask (that gap is what
makes the transition reachable in a room where the neighbour IS built),
so by the time `rt_vertical` runs, his `dizzy_dy` is whatever the
jump/fall left it as, and leaving it alone was the bug.

**Confirmed both the break and the fix live, not just reasoned about.**
Forcing `dizzy_y=30` (well above the y=48 step, unambiguously open
sky) with `dizzy_dy=-8` (mid-jump) on the pre-fix build: gravity
reasserts as expected (dy climbs 0->1->2...) and he falls back down to
the step at y=48 -- but `dizzy_dy` keeps climbing to `+7` (FALL_CAP)
and STAYS there forever, frozen at y=48, because `check_ground` finds
the step solid every pass (correctly) but the denied up-transition
never got a chance to zero the velocity the way a real landing would.
Real symptom: standing there, at rest, with residual "fall speed" that
never resolves into anything -- which is what let X-ALL.TXT's own
`checktopside`-adjacent geometry look "bugged out" to a player, not
merely "denied and static." Post-fix, the identical forced state
settles cleanly at y=48, dy=0 -- and walking away (LEFT off the step's
edge) falls normally and lands properly elsewhere in the room
(dy 0->4->7 through the fall, then 0 again on a real landing). The
mechanism now behaves exactly like hitting a wall, both directions,
because `rt_vertical`'s denied branch now does what `ml_bonk` already
does: `clr dizzy_dy` before falling into `ml_vertdone`.

**The gate and lever were never actually broken.** Verified directly:
teleported Dizzy onto the switch's own position (136,78) and pressed
DOWN -- `portswitch`'s v1 flips to thrown, `porthere` (the gate)
correctly rises toward `PORT_OPEN_Y` and reverses at both limits,
oscillating exactly as T0069 built it. The switch sits partway up the
same broken stairwell this bug lives in; the most likely explanation
for "the lever is dead" is that this ceiling bug made reaching it
properly (rather than getting stuck mid-climb) impractical before now.
Not re-tested via a full walk-in after the fix (that needs a real
playtest, not another synthetic-state check) -- flagged as the first
thing to re-verify next.

Fix: `target/room36.asm`, `rt_vertical` -- `bne rt_exists` /
`clr dizzy_dy` / `lbra ml_vertdone` in place of the old `lbeq
ml_vertdone`. No data change, no memaudit/verify_verbatim impact
(pure logic).

### T0077: a status-bar icon, in the strip's existing 8px budget

User's ask: the Spectrum original (`research/D3-prior-art/info/
dizzy3_game.png`) has real art up top -- egg-face life icons, a
score/title bar, a room-name banner -- and a decorative border framing
the whole play area, versus this port's plain "L3 C000" text on black.
Asked the user how much to mimic: a full four-side border shrinks the
interior play area on every side, which means re-deriving extracted
geometry/collision for all 9 already-built rooms -- a large, invasive
change for a cosmetic ask. They picked the smallest-blast-radius
option: upgrade the EXISTING 8-pixel-tall top strip's art, same
budget, zero changes to any room's play-area geometry.

**The mechanism:** this port's font (`font_data.asm`) is every glyph
`FONT_FIRST..FONT_LAST` (38-90) decoded VERBATIM from the Spectrum ROM
font, glyph index == ASCII code, no per-glyph opt-out (`ui.asm`'s own
header note: ordinary `frmtable` frames, drawn through the same `blit`
every other sprite uses). A custom icon therefore needs a code this
game NEVER prints in real dialogue -- checked against every string in
`gap_messages.asm` and `actors.json` (`grep`'d every `fcc` and folded
to a unique-character set): J, M, Q, X, Z are unused. Picked 'Q' (81).

Added `--glyph-override CODE:b0,...,b7` to `tools/roompack` (hex bytes,
one row each, same MSB-first convention as every other packed sprite)
-- substitutes a hand-drawn 8x8 bitmap for that one glyph slot instead
of the extracted ROM character, keeping `regen_art.sh` as the single
source of truth (a hand-edit to the generated `font_data.asm` would be
silently wiped by the next regen, same trap this whole file already
warns about for every other generated asset). `ui.asm`'s status text
changed from `"L0:C000"` to `"Q0:C000"` -- `refresh_ui_text`'s digit
patching is unchanged (same offsets), only the leading literal differs.

`tools/verify_verbatim.py` would otherwise flag `glyph_81` as
corrupted art (it IS different from FRAMES.DAT, deliberately) -- added
a `CUSTOM_GLYPHS` set reported separately from both "skipped: not
frame-derived" and the artifact-colour transform check, so a genuinely
corrupted glyph elsewhere in the font still fails loudly.

Verified with a natural boot (no `killed=1` teleport trick -- see
below) dumped at t=600: renders as "Q3 C000", the icon a distinct
rounded/segmented shape, clearly not a stray letter, in the exact same
8-row strip. `memaudit.py`/`verify_verbatim.py` both clean.

**Found, not fixed, while verifying (pre-existing, not from this
change):** `harness/framedump.lua`'s own `killed=1` teleport trick
(used to jump straight to a target room for a snapshot) shows the
lives digit as garbage (`'Z'`, i.e. `lives=42`) instead of the real
post-respawn value -- reproduced byte-identically on the pre-T0077
build with the same test, so this is a framedump-harness-specific
artifact of forcing a death outside normal play, not a real player-
facing bug: a genuine natural boot shows `lives=3` correctly, and nothing
here touches `lives` itself. Worth a look if a future session leans on
framedump for anything UI-text-related, but out of scope here.

### T0078: a two-row status banner -- DIZZY title + per-room name

Follow-up to T0077, same session: the user asked specifically about the
Spectrum original's title/room-name banner and a border. Before
committing to anything, checked the actual headroom: every built room's
OWN topmost placement y, straight from `extracted/rooms.json` (Python
one-liner, not eyeballed) --

    35:40 36:48 51:32 52:48 53:32 54:50 55:41 68:40 69:40

The tightest are 51/53 at y=32, comfortably clear of a 16px (two-row)
banner. Gave the user three concrete options (grow to 16px with a
second row; keep 8px and just add "DIZZY" to the existing row; push
toward the full 28-32px with an actual divider line) rather than
picking one -- they took the two-row middle option.

**What changed:**
- `draw_ui`'s clear grew from 8 rows/256 bytes (two 128-byte passes) to
  16 rows/512 bytes (four passes) -- same technique, just twice as long.
- Row 0 keeps lives-icon/count + coins + the carried-item icons
  (x=72-148px), and now also prints "DIZZY" right-aligned at x=216px --
  checked against the icon row's own max extent first so the two never
  overlap.
- Row 1 (y=8) is the current room's name, from a new hand-maintained
  `target/ui_room_names.asm`: one prtmessage stream per built room,
  verbatim from `rooms.json`'s own `name` field, already padded to a
  fixed 20 characters with the existing ':'=space/';'=apostrophe/
  '='=hyphen convention (matches the original design sketch's own "need
  20 chrs for room name" note, `research/D3-prior-art/info/
  dizzy3_hudplan.jpg`). `find_room_name` scans a (room, pointer) table
  by `cur_room`, same linear-scan shape as `room_exists`/`load_room` --
  each stream carries its own leading room-number byte (skipped before
  handing the pointer to `prtmessage`, since 35-90 all fall inside the
  literal-character range and would otherwise print garbage first).
- `ui_last_room` added alongside `ui_last_lives`/`ui_last_coins` in the
  "does anything need to redraw" check -- without it, walking into a
  new room with unchanged lives/coins would leave the OLD room's name
  on screen indefinitely.

Hand-maintained, not generated: nine short strings that regen_art.sh
never touches, same reasoning as `gap_messages.asm`'s one-off dialogue
text -- a new roompack codegen path for nine lines wasn't worth it.

**Verified, not assumed:** dumped all 9 rooms via `harness/framedump.lua`
and built a contact sheet. Every room shows its correct name, "DIZZY"
top-right, no clipping of any room's own art against the taller strip.
(Room 51 needed a different `DUMP_X` -- 100 landed Dizzy over a gap and
threw the respawn into an unrelated room; 176 is solid ground there.
Not a bug, just a bad test coordinate.) `memaudit.py` clean (low data
988 free, code+data 269 free, both staging blocks and gap2 unchanged
from T0075-T0077's own numbers, no overlaps). `verify_verbatim.py`
clean (this is layout/code, no art changed beyond T0077's own glyph).

Still open: the full four-side border from the reference screenshot --
not asked for on this pass (the user picked the two-row banner, not the
option that included a border), and remains a bigger job (shrinks the
interior play area, needs re-deriving every built room's geometry) if
ever wanted later.

### T0079: the play-area frame -- and why it turned out to be free

Playtest, on the T0078 banner: "Was the divider supposed to be
bordering the play area? Because it's not." Exactly right -- T0078 put
a solid rule under the banner; the reference screenshot
(`research/D3-prior-art/info/dizzy3_game.png`) has a checkered frame on
ALL FOUR sides of the room.

**I had told the user twice that a border meant re-deriving every
built room's geometry. That was wrong, and checking beat guessing.**
Parsed the generated placement lists (pointer label + x,y) together
with each sprite's OWN w/h, so the extents are real edges, not anchors:

    room  xmin xmax  ymin ymax        touching an 8px margin
      35     8  248    40  192        2  (floor tiles reaching y>=184)
      36     8  248    48  184        0  -- completely free
      51     0  264    32  193       12  (bushes at x=0-4, bottom pillars)
      52     8  248    48  184        0  -- completely free
      53     8  248    32  200        3  (floor tiles)
      54     0  284    50  184        5
      55     8  256    41  184        3
      68     0  264    40  184        2
      69     8  192    40  184        0  -- completely free

Room 36 and 52 sit at x=8..248, y=48..184 -- an 8px margin on every
side, which is the frame's own footprint. The clincher: `DIZZY_MINX`=8
and `DIZZY_MAXX`=224 (+24px sprite = 248) put the PLAYER's reachable
span at exactly x=8..248 too. The original authored its rooms inside
an 8px frame, and this port inherited that inset without anyone
noticing it was there. So the frame costs no geometry change at all --
only the outer 8px of a handful of decorative tiles in 51/54/55/68,
which is what the original's own border covers as well.

**Implementation** (`draw_border`, target/ui.asm): 8px bands at y=16-23
and y=184-191, plus byte column 0 and byte column 31 for the sides --
in PMODE4 8px is exactly one byte, so the side columns are a single
`stb` each per row. Pattern is a 4x4 checkerboard, `$f0` for four rows
then `COMB` for `$0f` -- the nearest a 1bpp buffer gets to the
original's checkered border, and sharing it between bands and columns
makes the corners line up for free. Called LAST in the redraw pass,
after placements/actors/Dizzy/banner: same "drawn last is what
always-on-top means in a serial pass" reasoning T0062 used for Dizzy,
which also means it needs no clear of its own and a placement redrawn
near an edge can never punch a hole in it.

**Cost: none measurable.** `harness/rate.lua`, same build with and
without the border:

    with     15.0 / 15.0 / 13.7 passes/sec  (r36 fire lit, fire out, r35)
    without  15.0 / 15.0 / 13.7

Identical -- the pacing quantises to whole 60Hz fields and the frame's
~850 byte-writes still fit inside the same field count. (The band's 16
`STD`s are unrolled deliberately; a counted inner loop measured a bit
over twice the cycles for the same 32 bytes, and this runs every pass.)
`memaudit.py` clean, no block overlaps -- though code+data is now down
to 136 bytes free, the tightest region in the build. `verify_verbatim`
clean.

Verified visually in rooms 36, 51, 53 and 54 (51 being the worst case
at 12 touching placements): the frame reads as deliberate, and the
covered bush edges in 51 look intentional rather than clipped.

### T0080: the play area was too tall -- the original has a WINDOW, and we never had one

Playtest, with a side-by-side against the Spectrum: "the play area is
too tall compare to the zxspectrum, this is why Dizzy can walk on top
of the room ceiling". The screenshot showed a wide band of empty black
between T0079's frame and room 36's own brick ceiling, where the
Spectrum has the room art sitting flush under its border.

**The answer was two constants in X-ALL.TXT, and they had been sitting
there the whole time:**

    windowtop     defb 6*8      ;0    alter these directly
    windowbottom  defb 192-8    ;192  to change window

The original does NOT draw a room into the whole screen. It clips every
sprite it plots to y=48..184, in the routine at ~3995: a sprite
starting above `windowtop` has its leading rows dropped AND its source
pointer walked forward by the same number of whole rows
(`movestartdown`), and one running past `windowbottom` has its row
count truncated. This port had a bottom clip (T0067, added because a
sprite was running off the framebuffer into other data) but no top
clip and no notion of a window at all.

That single omission explains what the playtest saw. **Room 36's art
starts at y=48 precisely BECAUSE 48 is the original's window top** --
the extracted data is authored against a window it assumes will be
applied. Drawing it into a play area that started at y=24 put 24px of
nothing above every room's ceiling. Checked across all 52 rooms with
content, not just the built nine: topmost placement y is 48 in 12
rooms, 40 in 8, 32 in 4, with a global minimum of 22 -- data that runs
above the window is normal, because the original cuts it off.

**Changes:**
- `WINDOW_TOP`/`WINDOW_BOTTOM` constants, straight from the source.
- `blit` gained the top clip, a direct port of `movestartdown`: rows
  above the window come off the count and the source pointer advances
  by `skipped * bytes_per_row` (one `MUL`), so the slice that lands at
  the window edge is the right part of the bitmap.
- The clip edge is a VARIABLE, `win_top`, not the constant: `draw_ui`
  drops it to 0 while painting the banner and restores it on the way
  out. The banner lives above the window by definition and would
  otherwise clip itself out of existence.
- Layout moved onto the original's geometry: banner rows at y=8 and
  y=24, frame top band y=40-47, window y=48-183, frame bottom band
  y=184-191 (which is what `192-8` was measuring all along).
- `draw_ui`'s clear is now y=8..31 via `STD` -- 768 bytes for about
  what the old 512-byte `STA` clear cost. y=0-7 and y=32-39 need no
  clear now that the window keeps room art out of them.

Gotcha for next time: inserting the clip pushed `blit_offscreen` past
the 8-bit branch range and lwasm reported it as "Byte overflow" on the
PRE-EXISTING `bhs` two dozen lines earlier, not on any new line. Both
are `lbhs` now.

**Cost: none measurable.** `harness/rate.lua` before and after the
clip: 15.0 / 15.0 / 13.7 passes/sec (r36 fire lit, fire out, r35),
identical. `memaudit` clean, no overlaps -- but code+data is down to
**80 bytes free**, now comfortably the tightest region in the build.
The next thing added there needs something relocated first (T0072 and
T0075 are the precedents). `verify_verbatim` clean.

Verified in rooms 36, 51 and 53: art sits flush under the frame, and
51/53's above-window scenery is cut off at y=48 exactly as the original
cuts it.

### T0081: Dizzy went beyond the frame -- his draw path never saw T0080's clip

Playtest, room 51: "the border is in the right place, but dizzy can
still go beyond it" -- with a screenshot of him standing on the
staircase top with his whole sprite ABOVE the play window, drawn across
the room-name banner ("PORTCULLIS" half covered by his head).

Two separate faults, one visible symptom.

**1. `blitdizzy` is not `blit`.** T0080 put the window clip in `blit`,
and Dizzy has his OWN masked compositor (`blitdizzy` -- mask AND, sprite
EOR, 3 source bytes per row in both the aligned and shifted loops)
which never calls `blit` at all. So the clip missed the one sprite most
likely to reach the window edge. Ported the same clip into it: rows
above `win_top` come off `bd_height`, the top row moves to the window
edge, and BOTH source pointers (mask and sprite) advance by
`skipped * 3`. A frame entirely above the window draws nothing.

**2. He could stand there in the first place.** X-ALL.TXT's
`floorfound` always LEAVES the room when the feet land above y=66, so
the original never has Dizzy standing that high. When the room above
isn't in this build the transition is denied, and T0076 only stopped
him RISING -- which is right for a jump (he stops at y=65 and falls
back) but does nothing for the grounded step-climb, which had already
walked him up there. Now the grounded path checks `room_exists` for the
room above BEFORE transitioning, and if it isn't built, restores the
feet y from before this pass's step-up (`pre_y`) and lands him there.
Same rule `check_wall` already gives horizontal edges: an unbuilt
neighbour is an edge you can't walk through.

**memaudit's cross-block overlap check (T0075) earned its keep.** These
two changes pushed the $0E00-$4000 code region 15 bytes past $4000 into
framebuffer A's staging block -- `0x4000-0x400e: block 0x2bea+5157 vs
0x4000+4205`. lwasm was perfectly happy; without that check it would
have been another silent load-time corruption exactly like T0074's.
Fixed by moving `ui.asm` into the $0100 low-data region alongside
gap_messages/ui_room_names (pure code+data reached by absolute jsr, so
its address is arbitrary -- the same relocation T0072 and T0075 did).
code+data is back to 435 bytes free, low data to 538.

**Verified:** placed him at x=88 y=52 in room 51 (feet 4px inside the
window, body well above it) and dumped the frame -- "MOAT AND
PORTCULLIS" renders completely intact with only his clipped feet
showing at the window's top edge, against the playtest screenshot where
his head covered it. Rooms 36/52/55 unchanged at normal floor level.
`rate.lua` still 15.0 / 15.0 / 13.7. `verify_verbatim` clean.

**Not verified, be honest about it:** the climb REFUSAL itself hasn't
been caught firing in a real walk -- the test walk-up in room 51 went
left along the floor to x=8 and never reached the staircase (its steps
are ~24px, too tall for STEP_UP=4, so getting onto them needs a jump
that now stops at y=65 anyway). The refusal is reasoned from the code
path, not observed. If Dizzy is ever seen standing above the window
again, that path is the first place to look.

### T0081 follow-up: the climb refusal DOES fire -- verified, and it exposed a real check_wall gap

T0081 shipped with the climb refusal reasoned from the code path but
never observed firing; the handoff and commit both said so. Closing
that gap turned up both the confirmation and a genuine pre-existing
bug, so it was worth doing.

**Why the first test missed it.** Rendering room 51's collision mask as
ASCII (4x4 cells) shows the route immediately:

    y 48 ....................####....
    y 56 ....................##########..
    y 72 ........................##########..
    y 88 ............................######################..
    y104 ..............................................##################

It is a staircase of **16px steps** climbing up-LEFT (surfaces at
y=104, 88, 72, 56, 48). STEP_UP is 4, so none of it can be walked up --
every step needs a jump. My earlier "walk left and hold jump" test
started on the bottom floor and just hit the left wall at x=8, nowhere
near it. Starting on the y=104 ledge (x=200) and holding LEFT with a
jump cycle drives the real route.

**Result: the refusal fires, every pass, exactly as intended.** He gets
as far as x=96 y=65 and stays there -- `floor=1`, never ascending, for
2700+ ticks. Each pass the step-climb lifts him to y=61, `check_ground`
finds the block solid there, `ml_floorfound` sees 61 < 66, `room_exists`
says room 67 isn't built, and `pre_y` puts him back at 65. Without the
refusal he would land on that block's top surface at y=56 and stand
above the play window, which is the bug the playtest reported.

**But the state he ends in is wrong, and the cause is older than any of
this.** At x=96 y=65 he is 9px INSIDE the block (its top is y=56). He
got there by drifting LEFT while airborne at y=65: `check_wall` probes
only `dizzy_y-10`, `dizzy_y-14` and `dizzy_y-18` -- the upper body --
and never the feet. All three probes sit ABOVE a block whose top edge
is y=56 when he is at y=65, so the wall test says "clear" while his
feet are inside it. **Any** airborne Dizzy can side-step into a
platform whose top lies between y-10 and his feet; this route just
makes it easy to hit. Filed as T0082.

Not fixed here on purpose: adding a foot probe to `check_wall` changes
core collision for every room, every actor and every ledge in the
build, and this file already records what that class of change costs
when it goes in unmeasured (T0031's step-climb, T0055's probe
columns, T0061's foot columns). It wants its own task, its own
before/after framedumps and its own playtest -- not a drive-by.

Also worth stating plainly: none of this can happen once room 67 is
built. The original never has Dizzy above y=66 because `floorfound`
always transitions him out; the refusal only exists to make an UNBUILT
neighbour behave like a wall, and the wedge is reachable only by
deliberately jumping at a boundary that is temporarily a dead end. He
can always walk back out to the right and fall normally -- verified,
not assumed: moving right from x=96 clears `check_wall` and he drops
off the block's edge at x=120.

### tools/roomview.py -- read the collision mask instead of guessing at it

Track 2. Two bugs this session were chased with blind MAME walk tests
that never reached the geometry in question (T0079/T0080's "can a
border fit", T0081's staircase), and both collapsed into something
obvious the moment the mask was rendered as one screen of ASCII. That
happened three times ad-hoc before it earned being a tool.

    tools/roomview.py 51 --surfaces   # mask + every walkable top edge
    tools/roomview.py --above-line    # the T0081 bug class, all rooms

It reads the GENERATED `target/roomNN_data.asm`, not `rooms.json`, so
it shows what the target actually collides against -- past roompack's
clipping and off-screen drops, not before them.

`--surfaces` lists top edges (a solid cell with nothing solid above it),
which is what "can Dizzy stand here" actually means. That is what
finally explained room 51: a staircase of 16px steps climbing up-LEFT
(y=104, 88, 72, 56, 48) when STEP_UP is only 4, so every step needs a
jump -- which is why walking left along the floor never found it.

**`--above-line` found that T0081's stranding is NOT just room 51.**
It cross-references every built room's above-the-line surfaces against
whether the room ABOVE is built:

    room 51:  2 surfaces above the line.  up = 67, NOT BUILT
    room 68:  3 surfaces above the line.  up = 84, NOT BUILT
    room 69: 12 surfaces above the line.  up = 85, NOT BUILT
    rooms 35/36/53 have them too, but their up-neighbour IS built,
    so the transition fires and they behave correctly.

Room 69's twelve are a symmetric pair converging as y falls
(136-140/148-152, 132-136/152-156, ...) -- that is the pitched roof of
the house in THE EAST WING. Dizzy can climb a roof into a room that
doesn't exist yet.

So the T0081 refusal is load-bearing in three rooms, not one, and the
T0082 wedge is reachable in three rooms too. All of it evaporates as
soon as 67/84/85 are built -- worth knowing before anyone spends
effort making the refusal prettier.

### T0076 follow-up: the portcullis lever, verified by actually walking to it

The last claim in the handoff that rested on a placement rather than a
playthrough. T0076 said the gate and lever "work", but that was checked
by writing Dizzy's coordinates onto the switch. Now checked properly,
using `tools/roomview.py` to find the route first instead of guessing:

The switch (actor 122) sits at x=136..152, y=78..88. The surface list
puts a platform top at **y=88, x=136..200** -- so the switch stands ON
that platform, and the platform is one 16px hop up-left from the y=104
ledge at x=200..256. Route: be on the y=104 ledge, hold LEFT with a
jump to clear the step, then walk left along y=88.

End to end, all in normal play: lever throws at x=140
(`switch_v1` 0 -> 1), the "[X-ALL.TXT line 879] LEVER" box appears, and the
gate then runs 136 -> 96 (PORT_CLOSED_Y -> PORT_OPEN_Y) and oscillates,
exactly as T0069 built it.

**Two things the placement test could never have found:**

* **The lever has a narrow approach from the right.** Stopped at x=152
  it does NOT fire; at x=140 it does. `actor_hit` tests Dizzy's
  BODY_L..BODY_R box, which starts at his own x, so at x=152 his box is
  152..172 against a switch ending at 152 -- no overlap. Walking in from
  the right you must get well onto it, not merely touch its edge.
* **Jump discipline matters on the approach.** Holding a jump cycle the
  whole way makes him climb straight PAST the platform and up the
  staircase into the T0082 wedge. The test only works if jumping stops
  once he is on y=88. A player mashing jump would sail past the switch
  the same way.

Also, for the record, I walked into the exact trap this file already
documents in T0061: SPACE has to be toggled for the WHOLE run, not just
through the boot messages. The lever fired, `msg_wait_dismiss` put the
box up, and with SPACE toggling stopped at t=300 the whole main loop
sat frozen -- the gate read as "not moving" for a thousand ticks and
looked like a bug in T0069. It was the harness. The note was right;
I still had to relearn it.

### T0082: check_wall never probed the feet -- fixed for the AIRBORNE case only

Found while verifying T0081 (NOTES above): jumping up room 51's
staircase left Dizzy standing at x=96 y=65, **9px inside** the block
whose top is y=56. `check_wall` probes `dizzy_y-10`, `-14` and `-18` --
the upper body -- and never the feet, so all three probes sat ABOVE
that block's top edge while his feet were buried in it.

**The 10px of slack is not a mistake, which is why this needed care.**
It is what lets the GROUNDED step-climb walk into a step before the
vertical pass lifts him onto it. Removing it globally would have
changed every ledge, step and doorway in the build -- exactly the class
of change this file already records going wrong when done unmeasured
(T0031's step-climb, T0055's probe columns, T0061's foot columns).

So the fix is gated: **when airborne, and only then, probe at
`dizzy_y - STEP_UP` as well.** Airborne there IS no step-climb, so the
slack buys nothing and costs the wedge. STEP_UP (4) rather than an
invented number: 4px is this engine's own idea of how much vertical
slop still counts as walkable, so anything deeper is a wall by the
game's own standard.

**Verification, in the order that made it safe:**

* **Grounded path is provably untouched.** `harness/framedump.lua` over
  all 9 built rooms, before vs after: **byte-identical in all 9**.
  (framedump pins `dizzy_floor=1`, so it exercises exactly the path
  that must not change.)
* **The wedge is gone.** Same staircase drive as T0081. Before: ends at
  x=96 y=65, inside the block. After: ends at **x=120 y=72 floor=1** --
  a real surface (`roomview` lists y=72 x=120..136). He still touches
  y=65 at the jump apex, which is correct and is T0076 stopping the
  rise.
* **Airborne traversal still works.** The portcullis walk-in still
  jumps from the y=104 ledge onto the y=88 platform and throws the
  lever -- so the tighter probe does not block legitimate landings.
* **Costs nothing:** 15.0 passes/sec in rooms 36/35/51/53, before and
  after, identical.

### harness/rate.lua promoted out of scratch -- and two ways it lied first

Measuring "did that cost anything" has come up in T0073, T0079, T0080,
T0081 and T0082. The script lived in a scratch dir and was deleted
between sessions **twice**, so it is committed now, with the per-room
warp table it needs. Two bugs it had on the way in are worth keeping:

* **`rng_ctr` is an LFSR, not a counter.** It was a plain `inc`-per-pass
  counter once, and gameplay.asm's own note records the change to an
  8-bit Galois LFSR. Summing its deltas therefore measures a
  pseudo-random walk averaging ~128 per step -- it reported **2082
  passes/sec** for a build genuinely running at 15. Count how often it
  CHANGES; an LFSR step never repeats the previous value, so one change
  is exactly one pass.
* **One warp position for every room measures the wrong rooms.**
  (100,176) is room 51's MOAT: Dizzy drops through it into room 35, and
  the "room 51" figure was really room 35 measured twice. The table is
  now per-room, taken from `roomview --surfaces` -- but widest surface
  is only a starting point, because room 36's widest is the y=80 slab,
  which is the rat's patrol line. Parking there gets him killed on a
  loop and reads as "8.2 passes/sec" of performance. Check the room's
  actors before trusting a spot.

Both of those produced confident, plausible-looking numbers. The tool
now prints a `!!` when a warp lands in a room other than the one asked
for, which is what caught the moat.

### T0083/T0084: room 67 built -- and the staging ceiling, measured rather than assumed

T0083 was filed as "memory headroom -- framebuffer B staging is at 167
bytes free, blocking any new room". **That framing was wrong, and
measuring took two minutes.** There are two staging windows, not one:

    framebuffer A (r8000, $4000-$5800)   4204 used, 1940 free
    framebuffer B (r9800, $6000-$7800)   5976 used,  167 free

I had been reading only B's number because that is where the last few
rooms went. Room 67 compiles to **1574 bytes** (measured by assembling
it standalone with an `equ _end-_start`, not estimated from the .asm
text, which is 10985 bytes of hex digits and means nothing). 1574 fits
A's 1940 with 365 to spare, so T0084 needed no restructuring at all.

Room 67 is generated **self-contained** (no `--shared-sprites`) on
purpose: the shared pool's overflow half lives in the r9800 block,
which has 167 bytes, so feeding room 67 through the pool would push
tiles into that file and blow B. Self-contained keeps the cost entirely
inside A, where the room actually is.

**The ceiling is real, though, and now close.** After room 67:

    A: 365 free    B: 167 free    total 532

Rooms 84 (51 things) and 85 (36 things) will each be in the same
1300-1600 byte range, so **neither fits**. Staging is hard-capped at
12288 bytes -- the two framebuffers are the only windows BASIC's CLOADM
can write that are also free at boot -- and 11756 of that is now spent.
The next room needs one of: deeper cross-room dedup, compression with a
boot-time unpack, or a genuinely different staging strategy. Filing
that honestly rather than discovering it mid-task.

**What building room 67 bought:** room 51's up-transition now SUCCEEDS
instead of being refused, so T0081's stranding and T0082's wedge are
both simply unreachable there. Verified in-emulator: the same staircase
drive that used to end wedged at x=96 y=65 now climbs to y=66 at x=132
and **transitions into room 67**, arriving at y=160 on its floor.
`roomview --above-line` confirms room 51 flipped to "up = 67, built".

Building a room moves the frontier rather than removing it, and the
tool says so plainly -- room 67 itself has 11 above-line surfaces with
up=83 unbuilt. The pitched roof in THE WEST WING is climbable into
nothing, exactly as room 69's was. That is inherent to a partial map,
not a bug to fix.

Also added: room 67's name to `ui_room_names.asm` (the banner shows
nothing for an unlisted room -- `find_room_name` returns 0 and
`draw_ui` skips it, silently), and its standing spot to
`harness/rate.lua`'s table. 15.0 passes/sec in 36/51/67.

### T0087: the frame is a string of egg beads, not a chessboard

Playtest: "the frame with the checkered pattern isn't very on theme,
make a string of oval beads shaped like dizzy?" Fair -- T0079 picked a
4x4 checkerboard because it was the cheapest thing that read as a
deliberate texture, not because it belonged in this game.

`draw_border` now tiles an 8x8 bead instead:

    fcb $18,$3c,$7e,$7e,$ff,$ff,$7e,$3c

Narrow at the top, wide at the bottom -- an egg. A run of them reads as
a string of beads shaped like Dizzy himself. The tile drives the bands
AND the side columns from the same table, which is what keeps the
corners meeting; the old version got that from a `COMB` trick that only
works for a two-phase pattern and could not have expressed this.

Structurally the routine changed from "4 rows, COMB, 4 rows" to a
proper 8-byte tile table walked with `cmpy #bd_pat_end`, so any 8x8
tile can be dropped in now without touching the code. Cost unchanged:
15.0 passes/sec in rooms 36 and 51, `verify_verbatim` clean.

### T0086 filed: collision above the play window is live but INVISIBLE

Found while chasing the room 35 -> 36 jump report (see below). T0080
made this port clip DRAWING to the original's window (y=48..184), but
this port's collision is a precomputed mask built from every placement,
including the ones above the window. Room 35 has solid cells at y=40-47
(x=40..56) that are now unreachable to the eye and still perfectly
solid to `check_ceiling`.

**The original does not have this problem, and the reason is
structural.** Its collision reads SCREEN ATTRIBUTES (`checkattri`, per
T0022's own note) -- so a sprite clipped out of the window writes no
attributes and therefore does not collide. Drawing and collision come
from the same act. This port split them: roompack bakes a mask from the
placement list, `blit` clips at draw time, and nothing reconciles the
two above y=48.

Filed rather than fixed -- the fix is either to clip the MASK at
generation time (roompack knows the window) or to stop generating
above-window cells at all, and either one changes collision in every
room, so it wants its own before/after framedumps and a playtest.

### T0088/T0089: audio -- and the premise correction that "the Spectrum music" is not in the 48K game

Asked to mimic the Spectrum's sound and music. Prior-art sweep first, per
the rule that has paid off all session, and it immediately changed the
question.

**The 48K Spectrum build -- which is THIS PORT'S SOURCE -- has no music
or sound effects at all.** X-ALL.TXT ~120-190:

    check128   ld e,a
               ld a,(ifmem128)
               and a
               ld a,e
               ret nz
               pop hl          ; <-- not 128K: discard the caller's
               ret             ;     return address and do nothing

`starttune`, `finishmusic`, `dosndfx`, `musicoff` and
`updatemusicingame` ALL begin with `call check128`, so on a 48K machine
every one of them pops its own caller and returns. The 48K player exists
as a file (`MUSIC48.SPC`) but its include is commented out:

    ;	org &f989
    ;	include MUSIC48.SPC

The tunes anyone remembers are the **128K AY** ones -- `MUSIC128.SPC`,
banked into &C000, and its own header says `;;;DIZZY2 MUSIC SPECTRUM
128`, i.e. the Dizzy 2 player reused. So "mimic the Spectrum" cannot
mean "port what the source does": faithfully, the source is silent.
This is an ADDITION, like the status bar was (T0028's own note: "this
is new, not a port").

**The factory already says so on its own axis table** --
`gpf transfer zxspectrum48 coco2`:

    re-derive  audio   beeper -> dac6bit
               music arrangement, sfx design

and `factory/platforms/coco2.toml` spells out why: the CoCo's 6-bit DAC
is "volume-modulated tone/noise, not an on/off beeper edge... this axis
should NOT read as transferring from Spectrum even though most others
do."

**Neither player has readable note data.** Both `MUSIC48.SPC` and
`MUSIC128.SPC` are assembled Z80 delivered as `HEX` statements -- the
beeper writes (`D3FE` = `OUT (&FE),A`) are visible in the blob, but the
tune tables are not separable by reading. Getting the actual tunes means
running a player and logging its output. That route is viable: the
original tapes ARE here (`source/Dizzy III - Fantasy World
Dizzy (1989)(Codemasters).tzx`), and a previous session already left
`research/D3-prior-art/info/music/{checkym6.c,ym6.h}` -- a YM6 (AY
register dump) parser that extracts per-channel notes. Nothing has been
captured yet.

**What IS established, empirically (T0088):** the CoCo2 DAC recipe.

    lda $ff23 / ora #8 / sta $ff23     ; PIA1 CB2 = sound enable
    lda #$fc  / sta $ff20              ; 6-bit DAC value in bits 7-2

A square wave built on a counted delay loop (8 cycles/iteration) at
DELAY=127 predicts ~440Hz; MAME's `-wavwrite` capture measures
**435.5Hz, 1.0% error**. That confirms the register recipe AND the
cycle-timing model in one shot, which is what makes note tables
computable rather than guessed.

`harness/audiocheck.py` does the measuring -- peak amplitude to catch
SILENCE (a mute build and a working one look identical otherwise) and
zero-crossings for pitch. Zero-crossing rather than an FFT on purpose:
the DAC's square-wave output is a clean two-level signal, so
crossings/2 IS the fundamental, and it needs no numpy.

**The budget shape is the good news.** Every DAC sample costs CPU, and
room 36 already spends ~47ms of a 66.7ms frame -- continuous music
under gameplay is not affordable. But the original's own structure is
title song, start tune, then effects only, and the expensive part
happens when the game ISN'T running. In-game effects should be SHORT
and BLOCKING, which is also how the beeper original behaves.

### T0090/T0091: the opening knockback without its text box, and how close the banner can get

Playtest sent screenshots of the real 48K game (ZEsarUX) — note the
status line says **48k**, so all of that banner art IS in the 48K
build. The T0088 finding stands but is narrower than it sounded: the
MUSIC is 128K-only, the GRAPHICS are not.

**T0090 -- skip the troll's greeting at game start.** Dizzy spawns at
x=184, inside the troll's own proximity box (T0050), so the game opened
with "[X-ALL.TXT line 976] [X-ALL.TXT line 977]?" blocking the main loop
before the player had done anything. Asked to keep the knockback and
drop the box. Suppressing the message while KEEPING the state setup is
a shape the ORIGINAL already has -- `proxtrollrou` writes dy/sequence/
the forced-left flag, then `ld a,(ff) / cp 25 / ret z` returns before
ever reaching `windowrou` -- it just keys on the animation frame rather
than on first contact. Here it is keyed on a `troll_greeted` byte, so
later encounters still get the line.

Verified with a boot and **zero key presses**: `troll_greeted` flips,
`troll_launching` fires, Dizzy is thrown from x=184 to x=108, and
rng_ctr keeps advancing at ~15 passes/sec throughout. Previously that
same run sat frozen in `msg_wait_dismiss` forever.

**T0091 -- the banner, and why it is a composition rather than a copy.**
`DIZ3SPEC.SCR` turns out to be a real Spectrum SCREEN$ -- exactly 6912
bytes (6144 bitmap + 768 attributes) in HEX statements -- and
`clearplayarea` starts at `screentable+6*16`, i.e. character row 6 =
**pixel row 48 = WINDOW_TOP**, clearing `17*8` = 136 rows down to
**184 = WINDOW_BOTTOM**. So the original loads ONE screen, wipes only
the play window out of it, and what is left standing IS the banner and
border. The title screen and the in-game frame are the same asset. That
is the third independent confirmation of the window constants.

**It does not fit, and it does not compress.** Measured rather than
assumed:

    banner rows 0..47   raw 1536 bytes   RLE 1696   (RLE makes it WORSE)
    full title screen   raw 6144 bytes   RLE 7806   (worse again)
    banner ink coverage 40%

Dithered art at 40% ink has almost no byte runs, so run-length coding
inflates it. And the largest single free region in the build is 527
bytes (low data), with the whole staging pipe down to 532 -- see T0085.
A 1536-byte banner bitmap has nowhere to live, let alone a 6144-byte
title screen.

So the banner is now COMPOSED from assets already resident -- font
glyphs, the T0077 egg glyph, the T0087 bead tile -- laid out to echo
the original: lives far left, "DIZZY III" centred, score right, room
name centred below, bead border under that. What is still missing
versus the reference is the two large drawn egg characters flanking the
slab, which are bitmap, not text, and therefore land squarely on the
T0085 memory problem.

Bug caught in my own change by looking at the render: the coin digits
are patched by byte offset from `ui_lives_digit`, and splitting the
string into three positioned runs moved them. Off by one wrote the
hundreds digit over the 'C' and the score rendered "0000" instead of
"C000". Counting it out in the comment now.

## T0093 -- T0082 REVERTED: check_wall's 10px slack is load-bearing

T0082 added an airborne foot probe at the head of `check_wall` (when
`dizzy_floor==0`, probe `dizzy_y-STEP_UP` as well). It fixed a cosmetic
wedge. It also made room 35 unfinishable, and that was reported from a
playtest twice before it was believed.

**What the 10px slack is actually for.** The original probes only
`dizzy_y-10/-14/-18` -- upper body, never the feet. That is not an
oversight to be tidied up. Those 10px are the window in which Dizzy may
move sideways while his feet are still level with a platform's side, and
they are what makes a step-climb work *in mid-air*, not just grounded.
Room 35's route to room 36 is an up-right staircase of 8px risers that
is climbed exactly that way. Probing the feet closes the window, and the
staircase stops at its third step.

Measured, same input from the same start, `harness/sweep.lua`:

|                         | apex reached | ends at |
|-------------------------|--------------|---------|
| with T0082              | y=113        | x=168   |
| T0082 reverted          | y=92         | x=188   |

Every other differing trial in the 42-point sweep runs the same way --
the reverted build gets higher or further, never worse.

**Room 35's right side, for the record** (`tools/roomview.py 35 --surfaces`):
the "top ledge" is the pillar top at y=80 x=232..248, with a one-cell
step at y=112 x=224..232 under it. Nothing is within jump range below
that step -- the next surface down is y=168, 56px away, against a 32px
rise. It is not reached by jumping at all: standing at x=224 his 20px
body overlaps the pillar face, `check_wall` fires, and the step-climb
lifts him 4px per pass all the way up. An elevator. It is how you get to
the rat path in room 36 and it runs entirely on those same probes.

**The dead end that cost the most here was methodological.** Three
hand-written jump tests all passed on both builds and cleared T0082
wrongly, because each held a direction and re-jumped on a cycle: they
measured "possible in unlimited attempts" rather than "reachable". A
cycling input test cannot show a regression in reachability. Diff the
two builds across every start position instead -- `harness/sweep.lua`,
which found this in one run.

## T0085 -- staging ceiling lifted: the $8000 image is stored LZSS-packed

Staging is hard-capped at **12288 bytes**: everything bound for $8000+
must arrive through a window BASIC's CLOADM can write, the two 6144-byte
framebuffers are the only ones free at boot, and the raw $8000 image had
reached 11756. 532 bytes left, against rooms of ~1300-1600. Nothing more
fitted.

Packed, the same image is 7628 bytes. **Staging free went 532 -> 4660**,
which at the measured ratio is room for roughly 7000 more raw bytes --
rooms 84 and 85 both, with headroom.

    block A (rooms 52,53,69,2,67 + shared sprites)   5779 -> 3197  (55%)
    block B (rooms 51,54,68,55 + sprite overflow)    5977 -> 4431  (74%)

Costs, both one-time and both measured: **98 bytes** of code+data for the
unpacker (422 -> 324 free), and **+0.33s of boot** (0.284s -> 0.617s from
exec to first live frame).

**Why LZSS and not RLE.** RLE *inflates* this art to 145% -- 40%-ink
dithered 1bpp has almost no byte runs. Same result as the SCREEN$
measurement in T0091. Measure before choosing; the intuition is wrong
here.

**The decoder's window IS the destination buffer** -- a match copies
from `Y-dist`, not from a ring buffer -- so it needs no decode RAM at
all, which mattered more than the last few percent of ratio.
`coma/comb` on `dist-1` yields `-dist`, so `leax d,y` gets the copy
source in one instruction. Overlapping copies are intentional and must
run forwards a byte at a time: `dist=1` is how a run is encoded.

**The two blocks are packed SEPARATELY, one per window.** A single
stream is 86 bytes smaller and cannot be decoded: the windows are not
contiguous ($5800-$5FFF between them holds the dizzy frame tail, the
message VM and the font), so a source pointer walking off the end of A
would read resident data as compressed bytes.

**Why the symbol trick is sound.** Pass 2 contains no room data, so the
685 labels the resident code references come from pass 1's map as
absolute equs (`target/staged_syms.asm`). That only works because the
blocks are `phase`d to absolute $8000 and therefore do not move when
resident code changes size -- and because the staged image is
self-contained: every symbolic operand inside the room data resolves to
another staged label, so there are no baked pointers into resident code
that adding the unpacker could invalidate. Both were checked, not
assumed. If either ever stops holding, this scheme breaks silently.

**Build it with `tools/stage_pack.sh`, never `lwasm` by hand.** The raw
pass generates what the packed pass consumes, so a hand build with
`-DSTAGE_LZ=1` uses stale blobs -- and stale blobs still assemble, still
load, and quietly draw the PREVIOUS art. `regen_art.sh` now `exec`s
stage_pack.sh for exactly that reason rather than printing a reminder.

**Verify with `harness/lzverify.lua`.** The Rust packer's round-trip
assert proves nothing about the 6809 half; a codec wrong in the same
direction on both sides round-trips happily. lzverify compares all
11756 bytes at $8000 in the emulator against the raw image. It passes,
and `harness/sweep.lua` shows the packed build behaving identically to
the raw one across all 42 trials.

## T0094 -- rooms 84 and 85 built, spending T0085's headroom

84 THE CASTLE STAIRCASE (above 68) and 85 THE EAST TOWER (above 69).
Measured standalone first, the T0083 way: **1309 and 1331 bytes**.
Self-contained, no `--shared-sprites`, for the same reason room 67 is --
they go in the r8000 block and the shared pool's overflow half lives in
r9800.

**The raw $8000 image is now 14396 bytes.** That is 2108 bytes past the
old 12288 staging cap: this build could not have existed before T0085.
Packed it is 8793, leaving 3495 bytes of window free (A 1783, B 1712).

That has a consequence worth knowing: the RAW pass now deliberately
overflows, so raw block A runs past $6000 and overlaps block B's address
space in the pass-1 file. Harmless, because stage_pack.sh takes each
window as a WHOLE DECB block by its load address and never by address
range -- and it now asserts exactly that against the map rather than
relying on it. If that assert ever fires, this is why.

**Verified on the target**, not just assembled: lzverify confirms all
14396 bytes at $8000 decode exactly; both rooms collide and are walkable
with nobody falling out; 68 -> 84 transitions from both of room 68's
above-line ledges and 69 -> 85 from room 69's x=56..72 ledge, all
landing on the destination floor at y=176.

**Room 69's other ledge (y=48, x=8..16) does not transition, and that is
correct.** It is 8px wide against a 20px body, so the floor probes at
BODY_L/BODY_R never both find it: he falls off before he can land on it,
and drops straight to y=128 at the same x. Not a bug, and not worth
"fixing" -- checked before filing anything.

**The frontier moved, it did not close.** roomview --above-line now
flags 84 (up=100), 85 (up=101) and still 67 (up=83). Inherent to a
partial map; T0081's refusal is what keeps it graceful.

### harness/sweep.lua: dedupe the clamped start points

A surface running past DIZZY_MAXX yielded the same start point several
times. That point is at the room edge, where holding a direction
transitions immediately, so its trials disagreed with EACH OTHER inside
a single run -- and showed up in the build diff as three "differences"
that were pure noise. Deduped, and two runs of the same binary are now
byte-identical, which is the property that makes a diff mean anything.

## T0095 -- the raw build became a loadable, broken binary. Guarded.

**The bug I shipped in T0085/T0094.** Once packing existed, the raw
$8000 image was allowed to outgrow the 12288-byte staging window -- that
is the point of T0085. But a raw build is still a loadable DECB file,
and lwasm happily emits blocks that OVERLAP. With rooms 84/85 in, plain
`lwasm --decb -o target/room36.bin target/room36.asm` produced:

    $4000..$60e2   8419 bytes   staging block A
    $5800..$5ed7   1752         *** A overruns it by 2275 bytes
    $6000..$7758   5977         *** A overruns it by 227

CLOADM applies blocks in FILE ORDER and the later one wins, so block A's
tail was overwritten and, worse, A had already been written over the
$5800 gap that holds the dizzy frame tail, the message VM and the font.
It assembled clean, it loaded, and it died on boot.

This is the exact T0058 room2 failure this file already carried a
warning about. I reintroduced it and then wrote in NOTES that the
overflow was "harmless" -- true only of stage_pack.sh's own extractor,
which takes whole DECB blocks, and not of the binary anybody would
actually load. `target/room36.bin` is gitignored, so a user who pulls
and builds gets it with whatever command they last used.

**The guard**: room36.asm now refuses to assemble if either staged block
exceeds its window, with a message naming stage_pack.sh. stage_pack.sh's
pass 1 is exempt via `-DSTAGE_GEN=1` -- it is meant to overflow and is
never loaded. Pass 2 is checked, where the labels bracket the packed
blobs, so the check covers the build that ships.

**lwasm trap, and it nearly buried the guard**: lwasm's plain `if` is
only "expression is non-zero" and does NOT implement `>` as a
comparison. **`if 1 > 2` is TRUE.** The first guard used `if a > b` and
fired on every build including good ones -- a guard that cries wolf gets
deleted rather than believed. Use `ifgt <expr>`, which is a real signed
test against zero. Verified: `ifgt 1-2` does not fire, `ifgt 5-2` does.

**Two harnesses lied during this diagnosis; do not trust either.**
`harness/capture_pmode4.sh` reads $4000, which is BOTH framebuffer A and
staging window A, so a healthy build that happens to be displaying
framebuffer B renders as garbage -- it looked like a reproduction and
was not. A GDB-stub liveness probe read cur_room=255 for the known-good
build too. What actually settled it needed no emulator at all: dump the
DECB block table from the .bin and look for overlaps.

### T0095 addendum: find EVERY build path, not the ones you remember

The guard fired on the user's own `./play.sh`, which had been tracked
since the port's first commit and built with a bare lwasm. Two harness
scripts (`pacetest.sh`, `coco_playtest.sh`) had the same line. All three
now go through stage_pack.sh.

I had grepped for `lwasm` before shipping T0095 and missed all three,
because the grep ended in `| head -10` and the matches were past it.
A truncated search that finds SOMETHING reads as a completed search.
When the question is "is there another caller of this", count the
matches before reading them.

`pacetest.sh` needed more than a swap: its variants assemble modified
copies of room36.asm, so they now run stage_pack.sh first (to refresh
the blobs against current room data) and then assemble with
`-DSTAGE_LZ=1`.


## T0092 sizing -- the title screen and banner DO fit, measured

Asked whether there is room now for the intro screen and the top banner
art. Measured against the real asset, not estimated.

**The asset already exists**: `research/D3-prior-art/original_source/
DIZ3SPEC.SCR` is the Spectrum title screen -- not a raw SCREEN$ but an
assembler source of `HEX ...` lines, which decode to exactly 6912 bytes
(6144 bitmap + 768 attributes). The ZX bitmap is the same 256x192 1bpp
as PMODE4, so conversion is a pure de-interleave
(`off = ((y&0xC0)<<5) | ((y&0x07)<<8) | ((y&0x38)<<2) | col`); drop the
attributes and it is a straight black-and-white CoCo screen. It converts
well -- logo, dithered mountains, Code Masters roundel all legible.

**The banner art is the top 48 rows of that same screen** ("DIZZY III /
THE OLIVER TWINS 89" with an egg character either side). So store the
title ONCE and copy its top 48 rows into a resident banner buffer at
boot: the banner then costs ZERO extra staging.

    title, linear order, packed            4345
    title, COLUMN-MAJOR order, packed      3788   <- store it this way
    banner alone, if stored separately      979   (not needed)

Column-major (all 192 bytes of column 0, then column 1...) is worth 557
bytes here and is the single best transform found. Everything else was
measured and was WORSE: XOR-with-previous-row 4664, XOR-with-row-2 4712,
ZX-native interleave 4375. Row XOR filters LOSE on dithered art -- the
dither is already the high-frequency content, and XOR destroys the byte
repeats LZ was living on. Do not re-try them.

A bigger match window is not worth a format change either: dist 8192
with len 3..10 is 3892 (worse), and dist 8192 with len 3..18 needs a
3-byte token and would land near 3701 -- under 100 bytes for a format
break. Entropy coding is where the rest is (zlib 3714, lzma 3604,
column-major zlib 3279) and that needs a Huffman decoder on the 6809.

**Half vertical resolution was tried and rejected on looks, not size.**
3072 raw -> 2210 packed, which fits the windows alone, but dropping
alternate rows destroys the dithering that carries the whole image and
the lettering goes mushy. Rendered and eyeballed before rejecting.

**Where it goes.** 3788 does NOT fit the framebuffer windows alone
(3495 free, 293 short). It fits comfortably in the total loadable-free
space below $8000, which is 4796:

    $0bf6..$0dff   522  low data spare
    $3ebf..$3fff   321  code+data spare
    $5109..$57ff  1783  framebuffer A spare
    $5ed8..$5fff   296  gap1 spare
    $7150..$77ff  1712  framebuffer B spare
    $7d5e..$7dff   162  gap2 spare
                  4796  TOTAL          -> 1008 spare after the title

($7E00-$8000 is NOT loadable -- nibswap + rat save-under, built at boot.
memaudit.py's REGIONS table is the authority on this, not arithmetic.)

**Mechanism, which is why the split is cheap**: the fragments do not
need to be decoded in place. At boot, after `sta $ffdf`, gather the six
fragments into one contiguous scratch buffer above the room image
($8000+ has ~16KB free past $bd9b), then run the existing lz_unpack once
from there into the framebuffer. Display, wait for a key, copy the top
48 rows to a resident banner buffer, then unpack the rooms and start. A
six-entry (src,len) table and one copy loop -- no change to the stream
format and no second decoder.

## T0096 FIXED -- the real title screen (was the tape loading screen)

The title now comes from `research/D3-prior-art/info/dizzy3_title.png`,
a 256x192 grab of the REAL title screen (Yolkfolk cast, "SPC OR FIRE TO
START"), which was vendored in the repo the whole time. tools/title_image.py
thresholds it to linear PMODE4; mktitle takes a raw 6144-byte file as
well as a .SCR now.

**Threshold 64, picked by rendering the alternatives and looking.** 128
and 96 both throw away "STARRING THE YOLKFOLK" and the DIZZY-heart-DAISY
heart, because red luminance is ~76. Bayer dithering makes the lettering
mushy. Red is a big part of this design -- do not raise the threshold
without re-rendering.

It also packs BETTER than the loading screen did: 6144 -> 3081 (50%) vs
3788, leaving 875 bytes of hole space spare instead of 165. Verified
byte-exact against the source image after unpacking on the target.

## T0092 built -- title screen + banner art (image since corrected, see above)

The machinery works and is verified end to end: mktitle converts the
Spectrum screen, splits it across the load-time holes, the target
gathers and unpacks it, de-column-majors it into both framebuffers,
keeps the top 48 rows as the banner, and holds until SPACE. lzverify
confirms the room image is still byte-exact and the frame rate is still
15.0 passes/sec in rooms 36/35/51.

**But the image is wrong.** DIZ3SPEC.SCR is the TAPE LOADING screen, not
the title/menu screen. The real one says "DIZZY III / SPC OR FIRE TO
START" and shows the Yolkfolk cast (Dizzy, Daisy, Denzil, Dylan, Dozy,
Grand Dizzy). It is NOT in the original source as a bitmap -- the only
Spectrum-sized .SCR there is DIZ3SPEC (6912); DIZ3AMS1/2 and
EDITOR/DIZAMS1/2 are 8192-byte Amstrad screens and NEWTREAS.SCR is 3024.
The game draws the title from sprites at runtime, so it has to be
captured from the running original (harness/zx_orig.sh already boots the
tape) rather than extracted. Expect the conversion to be harder than the
loading screen was: the loading screen is dithered near-monochrome and
survives 1bpp well, while the title screen leans on colour (green tree,
coloured text) that 1bpp will flatten.

### harness/sweep.lua measures DRAWING TIME as well as physics

Input is driven on a real-time clock, so anything that changes how long
draw_ui takes moves the trials. T0092 shifted 20 of 36 with the physics
untouched, the room image byte-identical and the rate still 15.0/sec.

A pass clock would fix it and was tried: **rng_ctr is not usable as
one** -- it only steps when something consumes randomness, so in a quiet
room it never ticks and the sweep stalls with zero trials (which is also
why rate.lua warps to rooms that have actors). A real pass counter would
mean changing the binary under test. Documented in the harness header
instead: after a RENDERING change, corroborate with rate.lua and
lzverify rather than reading the diff as a regression.

The boot-wait fix in the same file IS a real improvement and stays: the
sweep now waits for the game to be live rather than for a fixed frame
count, so changing boot time (as the title screen does) no longer shifts
every trial.

## Green is one bit -- VDG_CSS (PIA1 $FF22 bit 3)

In RG6 (PMODE4) the colour-set select decides what an "on" pixel is:
CSS=0 green on black, CSS=1 buff/white on black. Same mode, same
256x192 1bpp resolution, same art, same cycles -- it costs nothing.
It also shifts which artifact hues composite NTSC pulls out of fine
detail, so the red/blue fringing changes with it.

Build it either way: `VDG_CSS=1 ./play.sh` for buff, default 0 for
green. The port shipped `ora #$f8` (mode $F + CSS set); it is now
`ora #$f0+(VDG_CSS*8)`.

**Do not confuse this with the mode nibble.** Changing CSS (bit 3) is
safe. Changing GM (bits 7-4) is the T0028 disaster -- $E is CG6, a
128x192 2bpp mode that reads this port's 1bpp art as pixel pairs.

**Verify it at $FF22, never from a framebuffer capture.** Reading $4000
back decodes as 1bpp whatever the VDG is really doing, so it cannot see
a mode OR a colour-set error -- that blindness is exactly how T0028's
wrong nibble survived for days. harness/vidmode-style check: read $FF22
