## T0108 -- room 69 walk-stall, INVESTIGATED, NOT RESOLVED

Reported: jump from the table in room 68 to a ledge in 69. The 68->69
transition itself works fine (confirmed: walking off the table lands at
x=8,y=168 in 69, matching the room's own left-edge geometry). The actual
bug is IN ROOM 69 ITSELF: holding RIGHT from the entry point, Dizzy
crawls in occasional single WALK_STEP (4px) increments instead of
continuously, and past roughly x=28-30 stops advancing entirely --
confirmed stuck for 900+ frames (15+ seconds) of RIGHT continuously
held, verified against `keyflags` sampled directly from memory, not
inferred from on-screen behaviour.

**Ruled out, each confirmed on the target rather than assumed:**

* **Not the room transition.** Lands correctly, every time.
* **Not check_wall or the collision mask.** room69_data.asm's mask is
  provably clear (dumped and read as raw bits) at every probe height
  (dizzy_y-10/-14/-18) across the whole x=8..56 span. Instrumented
  check_wall directly: when it runs, it correctly returns "not blocked".
* **Not T0102/T0103's actor collision.** `n_solid` reads 0 throughout --
  room 69's only actor (the dagger) is dull/non-solid, confirmed on the
  target, not assumed from the actor table.
* **Not a hard geometric wall.** Starting from x=40 or x=60 on the SAME
  floor, he walks normally and falls through the real gap (x=56..112)
  into room 53 below, exactly as the geometry suggests it should.

**What's genuinely strange, and where the next session should start.**
Two counters were instrumented directly (temporarily -- reverted before
commit, not left in): one at the top of `mainloop` (confirmed real
passes keep completing at a roughly normal rate throughout the stall)
and one at `ml_noleft`'s own "RIGHT held" branch in `check_wall` (only
incremented ONCE, at the single successful step, and never again for
900+ frames afterward) -- while `keyflags` sampled from Lua showed RIGHT
continuously held the entire time. So: the mainloop is genuinely
completing iterations, but `ml_noleft`'s own label stops being reached
on nearly every one of them, despite the input that should route control
there reading as held. That combination was not resolved -- something
BETWEEN `scankeys` and `ml_noleft` (the update_rat/troll/flame/
crocodile/portcullis/dragon/dagger/welllid/water/fire/death chain, or
try_pickup) is taking a different path most passes while in this
specific spot, but WHICH one was not isolated before the session moved
on to other queued work.

**Fastest next step, not yet tried**: a counter per major `jsr` between
`scankeys` and `ml_noleft` (there are ~13) would localize which call is
diverting control in ONE run, rather than bisecting call-by-call as this
session did (which cost much more time and, on removing the WRONG half
at once, broke the respawn mechanism itself -- `killed`/`respawn_room`
alone don't teleport; something in the hazard-update chain, most likely
`update_death`, is what actually performs the transition, so do not
bisect by skipping that whole block in one cut again).

`harness/stuck6869.lua` reproduces this from a clean warp -- no need to
re-derive the repro steps, only the root cause.

## T0106 DONE -- collision masks are LZSS-packed, unpacked on room entry

Raw $8000 image dropped from 18584 to 15384 bytes (-3200) just from
packing every room's mask. `roompack` now emits `r{NN}_room_cmask_lz`
(LZSS-packed, `roompack::lz::pack` -- the SAME format/module `lzpack`
and `mktitle` already use, not a new one) instead of the raw 384-byte
table, and points the room descriptor's cmask field at that instead.

**`load_room` unpacks the current room's mask into a resident scratch
buffer on every transition.** `CUR_ROOM_CMASK` (384 bytes) lives above
the staged room image in the same boot-scratch region as the title
buffers (`TITLE_RAW_BUF+6144`, so it can never collide with them even
though they're dead post-boot) -- but unlike those three, it's LIVE for
the whole game, refilled on every room entry, not just at boot.
`load_room` calls the existing `lz_unpack` once after copying the desc
record, then repoints `room_cmask_ptr` at the scratch buffer;
`cmask_test` (the single choke point every collision probe already goes
through) needed no changes at all -- it has never cared where the table
lives, only that `room_cmask_ptr` points at 384 real bytes.

**Verified on the target, not just via the Rust encoder's own
round-trip assert**: dumped `CUR_ROOM_CMASK` after loading room 35
(resident/low-data) and room 51 (staged/$8000+) and diffed each against
an independent Python decode of that room's own packed bytes -- both
byte-exact matches, covering both code paths a mask can now travel
through.

**A behavioural-diff false alarm, and why it wasn't one.** `sweep.lua`
showed real differences after this change. Ruled out as a regression
by the target-memory comparison above (the decoded mask is provably
identical, so the underlying collision geometry cannot have changed) --
the diffs are `load_room` now costing real cycles per room transition
(one `lz_unpack` call), shifting exactly the same frame-count-sensitive
apex/landing measurements sweep's own header already warns are not
trustworthy after a change to loading time. `rate.lua`'s steady-state
15.2/15.0/15.0 (a ONE-TIME per-transition cost, invisible to a
sustained-rate measurement) is what actually confirms no regression.

**A second, real bug found while verifying**: `tools/start_pos.py` had
its OWN separate copy of the raw-table mask parser (not the one
`roomview.py` uses), which T0106 broke -- every room silently fell back
to the "no mask" default of (128,80), which happens to sit inside room
69's own geometry. `./play.sh 53` was seeding room 53's puzzle items
onto a build that actually opened in room 69 (caught via
`harness/startitems.lua`, which checks `cur_room`, not just that
seeding ran). Fixed by having `start_pos.py` import `load_mask` from
`roomview.py` instead of keeping a second copy -- this is exactly the
second time in this file a duplicated mask-parser has silently gone
stale (`roomview.py` itself was T0081's fix for the same class of
mistake); do not add a third copy anywhere else that needs to read a
room's mask.

Memory: code+data 1682 free (was 52 at session start, after T0107 and
this). Low data still 0 free (rooms 35/36's own masks shrank too, but
their resident text/sprite data fills whatever that frees). Framebuffer
B down to 32 free -- the tightest window now, worth watching if the next
addition needs staging room there specifically.

## T0088 DONE -- 6-bit DAC tone driver, calibrated and wired to a real trigger

`play_tone` (target/room36.asm): a blocking square-wave tone on the DAC.
PIA1 CB2 sound enable moved from a throwaway probe into the real boot
sequence, right next to the video mode init it sits beside in the
source.

**Calibrated, not guessed.** `harness/tonecal.asm` is a standalone probe
(assembles on its own, not shipped) that loops one tone forever at a
fixed PERIOD, captured via MAME's `-wavwrite` at four values and
measured with `harness/audiocheck.py`. Least-squares fit against
100->827.5Hz, 150->565.5Hz, 196->438.0Hz, 250->346.5Hz: cycles/full-
period = 10.0*PERIOD + 81, max residual 0.03%. That inverts to

    period_for_hz(f) = round((894780/f - 81) / 10)

which is what the whole note system is built from. Re-run and refit if
`play_tone`'s instruction sequence ever changes -- the formula describes
that exact loop's cycle cost, not a hardware guarantee.

**`play_chirp`**: a two-note placeholder blip (NOT sourced from the
original -- see `play_tone`'s own header for why 48K Spectrum hardware
has nothing to source; the whole `dosndfx`/`starttune`/etc block is
gated behind `check128` and returns immediately on 48K, confirmed
directly in X-ALL.TXT this session, not just from the earlier note about
music alone -- 48K plays NEITHER tunes NOR sound effects). Wired to
`tp_take` (a successful pickup), the first and only trigger this session
-- a placeholder proving the driver end to end, pending T0089's real
note capture from the 128K AY player.

**Verified on the target, in two stages.** The calibration tones prove
pitch accuracy in isolation. Separately, `harness/pickupsfx.lua` drives
an ACTUAL pickup in room 36 and captures the result: `apple_room=255`
confirms the pickup itself happened, and the WAV shows amplitude ~8300
(the silence threshold is 200) at the moment it fires -- the driver is
reachable from real gameplay, not just from a standalone probe.

**A harness bug found doing this, the same shape as before**: a
one-shot burst can finish and go silent before a fixed-length capture's
analysis window ever looks at it -- exactly the T0061-class trap, this
time in timing an SFX rather than in dismissing a message. `tonecal.asm`
sidesteps it by looping forever (so ANY window into the capture has the
tone playing). For a genuine one-shot like the real pickup chirp, that
trick doesn't apply, so `audiocheck.py` gained `--scan`: slide a window
across the WHOLE capture and report whichever slice has the most
energy, rather than only ever looking at the tail second.

**`--scan`'s pitch reading is unreliable for a short multi-note blip.**
The same two-note capture read 50Hz at one window size and 12825Hz at
another, neither near the real ~660/1047Hz -- zero-crossing/duration
only means something for a single sustained tone, and a 20-30ms window
mostly straddles silence or both notes at once. AMPLITUDE is the
trustworthy signal for a fire-or-not check; verify PITCH against a
sustained tone (tonecal.asm) instead, never a short blip.

**A THIRD occurrence of the T0107 symbol-harvest bug**, now fixed at
the root instead of patched per-symbol. Adding `NOTE_E5`/`NOTE_C6`
(packed period:count constants, no address meaning at all -- one of
them, `128*256+20 = $8014`, just happens to look like a phased
destination address) hit the exact same `stage_pack.sh` bug T0107 found
twice already: anything numerically inside `[$8000, dest_end)` was
harvested as if it were a staged room-data label, regardless of what it
actually represented. The name-by-name exclusion list from T0107 was
never going to hold -- every NEW hand-written `equ` constant was one
more chance to hit this by coincidence. Replaced with a general fix:
`stage_pack.sh` now parses `target/room36.asm`'s own source for every
`name equ` line and excludes ALL of them from the harvest by name,
generically, rather than maintaining a list that a third symbol could
still slip past. `R9800_DEST`/`IMAGE_END` still get their STAGE_LZ-branch
values correctly -- those were already supplied through their own
dedicated output lines, untouched by this change, confirmed by rebuild
rather than assumed.

## T0089 -- capturing the real sound: 128K AY music, corrected premise

T0088's header claimed the 48K Spectrum plays no sound at all, reasoning
from `check128` gating `dosndfx`/`starttune`/etc behind a 128K-only
check. **The user corrected this from direct memory of the real game**:
the 48K release has its own title soundtrack, a start-of-game jingle,
and walk/jump sfx. Investigation confirmed they were right, and showed
*why* the source reads the way it does: X-ALL.TXT is archived with
`ifmode128 equ 1` (a build-time switch) and `MUSIC48.SPC` (the 48K
beeper player, a real, separate, self-contained asset) present but with
**no call sites anywhere in the file** -- only the 128K build's own
caller glue survived in this snapshot, not the 48K one. The 48K game's
sound was always real; the 48K *caller code* just isn't in what we have.

Instruction from the user: capture the fuller 128K AY content where
possible, fall back to 48K beeper porting only for what can't be
captured that way. Given no Spectrum 128K ROM is available or was
pursued (the "ask before installing/pulling" rule -- a 128K ROM is a
separate, still-copyrighted pair from the 48K ROM already vendored),
the approach taken was an ISOLATED Z80 SANDBOX for `MUSIC128.SPC`
alone, not a full machine emulation -- the player only ever writes to
two AY I/O ports (`$FFFD`/`$BFFD`), so it needs no ROM, no screen, no
keyboard, nothing beyond its own code and RAM.

### The trigger table (grepped from every `call starttune` / `call
dosndfx` / `ld (sndfx),a` site in X-ALL.TXT)

TUNES (`starttune`, A = id):
- 0: title screen (line 1155, held until keypress dismisses via `musicoff`)
- 1: new life / game start (line 1183, right after `starteggres`)
- 2: death (line 1376)
- 3: milestone -- reaching Daisy / all 30 coins (lines 3498, 3561)
- 5: coin/item pickup (line 2172, right after `addtocoins`)

SFX (`sndfx` variable, consumed each frame by `dosndfx`):
- 0/1: walking footsteps, alternating
- 6: message box opens
- 10: dragon starts breathing fire
- 11: drop an item
- 21: jump
- 25: killed/death

Captured and reduced this session: tunes 0, 1, 5 and sfx 21 (fully
wired into the game), plus raw captures of the rest sitting in
`tools/aycapture/captures/` ready for a future session (2, 3, 6, 10,
11, 25 -- not yet wired, no ROM budget spent on them yet).

### `MUSIC128.SPC` is source text, not a binary

Like the `.SCR` title asset, it's an assembler-style file: a header of
`name equ &addr` lines then `HEX ...` lines, no `org` (meant to be
included right at `music128 = $C000` per X-ALL.TXT). Concatenating
every `HEX` line's bytes in file order reproduces the blob exactly --
confirmed by the first three bytes decoding to `C3 0C C0` = `JP $C00C`,
matching `initune equ &c000`'s trampoline. `tools/aycapture`'s loader
does this the same way `mktitle.rs`'s `read_scr` does for the title.

### Driving the CPU without register accessors

The `z80` crate (2.0.0, crates.io) exposes `pc`/`sp`/`ix`/`iy` and
interrupt state as public struct fields, but the general-purpose
register pairs (AF/BC/DE/HL) are buried in private c2rust-transpiled
union fields with no public accessor at all. Rather than patch the
crate, `tools/aycapture` writes tiny bootstrap STUBS as real Z80
machine code into the emulated RAM (`LD A,id / CALL initune / HALT`,
`CALL refresh / HALT`) and lets the CPU's own instructions set up its
own registers -- exactly what the real caller code in X-ALL.TXT does
anyway (`ld a,0 / call starttune`). Sidesteps the missing API entirely
and needed no crate patch.

### Reduction: 3-voice AY -> monophonic CoCo2 DAC

The target's only sound output is T0088's `play_tone` -- a BLOCKING
single square-wave generator, no background mixer, no second voice.
Adding one is a much bigger feature than "port the existing tunes", so
`tools/aycapture/reduce` picks whichever of the AY's 3 tone channels is
loudest each captured frame and drops silent runs entirely (`play_tone`
has no "rest" primitive, and burning real time on purpose for a
blocking effect nobody is racing against isn't worth a second routine).

### The DAC could not represent 90%+ of the real notes -- widened to 16-bit

First reduction pass, still on T0088's original 8-bit `pt_period`,
found **93% of tune0's notes and 90%+ across the board** sit below
~340Hz, the lowest frequency an 8-bit delay count can reach (measured,
not assumed -- swept every capture's channel data through the actual
clamp). Every bass note in every tune was clamping to the SAME value,
collapsing whole basslines into a flat drone. `play_tone`'s `pt_period`
was widened from 8 to 16 bits (`lda/deca` delay loop -> `ldx/leax
-1,x`), and the calibration was RE-MEASURED with the new loop rather
than assumed linear from the old fit: `harness/tonecal.asm` (now also
16-bit, kept byte-for-byte in sync with the shipping loop) swept 7
points from 14Hz to 3000-period, least-squares fit weighted toward the
low-frequency end (period 800-3000, where real note content actually
sits -- residuals there 1-3.5%; the high end, period <250, is noisier
at up to ~10% but only ever used by a few already-high-pitched sfx like
jump, where exact-Hz fidelity matters far less than in a bassline):

    period_for_hz(f) = round((894780/f - 1164) / 21.1)

### ROM budget forced heavy quantization, and a math bug doubled the first estimate

Raw per-frame reduction produced absurd sizes -- tune0 alone was 741
notes (2.2KB), more than the target's entire remaining data budget.
`reduce` gained pitch-bucket quantization (group periods within ~1/12th
to ~1/24th of their value -- a portamento/vibrato slide nudges the
period by a few units almost every captured frame, and without
grouping that "every frame is a new note" reduction is mostly noise,
not melody). Coarser buckets for long continuous tunes (divisor ~12,
ROM budget matters more than a semitone of pitch precision), finer for
short one-shot sfx (divisor ~24, a handful of bytes doesn't matter but
character does).

Cost-estimation for the truncation caps had a real bug on the first
pass: the measured `21.1*period+1164` fit is cycles for a FULL wave (2
half-wave toggles, matching how `tonecal.asm` was measured), but the
first version of the cost estimator used that number directly as the
PER-HALF-WAVE cost, doubling every estimate -- caught because tune0
came back needing "6587ms in 3 notes" (>2 real seconds for a single
note is absurd on its face), not because the number silently looked
plausible. Halving it (`/2.0`) fixed the estimator; this is exactly the
kind of thing this project's "measured not assumed" habit is for --
the WRONG number still looked like output, not an error.

### Even short, budget-conscious clicks broke real gameplay -- found by a playtest, not by eye

With sizes under control, wiring seemed to work: `rate.lua`'s
steady-state numbers stayed at 15.5/15.0 passes/sec throughout (title
tune plays during the boot attract loop, footstep/jump fire from real
key input, tune5 fires from real pickup, tune1 from real respawn). But
`harness/pickupsfx.lua` -- the SAME scripted pickup test T0088 used to
verify `play_chirp` reaches a real trigger, not just an isolated call
-- started reporting `apple_room=36` (missed) instead of `apple_room=
255` (picked up), confirmed as a genuine regression (not a stale
baseline) by rebuilding the UNMODIFIED pre-T0089 source and re-running
the identical test: `x=88,y=142,apple_room=255`.

Bisection by disabling each new hook in turn (footstep, then chirp, all
still giving the identical `x=96,y=137` result) proved NEITHER was the
cause, which is itself the useful finding: don't trust a plausible-
looking single cause without ablating it. The actual cause was
`play_tune`'s call to the NEW-LIFE tune (`tune1_notes`, ~1.3s
unclamped) wired into `gp_ud_respawn` -- exactly the code path this
test's `killed=1` memory poke uses as a fast-forward teleport. A ~1.3s
blocking tune mid-teleport ran the script's fixed-frame RIGHT/DOWN
window out before Dizzy could reach the apple at all.

Frame-by-frame tracing (`dizzy_x`/`y`/`killed`/`dizzy_floor` printed
every 5 script-frames) showed the teleport itself always completes at
a fixed ABSOLUTE frame regardless of the tune -- what actually happens
is the whole post-teleport trajectory is delayed by close to the tune's
own real duration, and the test's ORIGINAL windows fire too EARLY for
that now-later trajectory. First fix attempt (widen the windows) made
it WORSE -- more time let Dizzy fall straight past the apple. The real
fix was to SHIFT the windows later by the measured delay (~15 video
frames, matching tune1 capped to ~262ms), verified against the same
trace, not assumed from the arithmetic alone.

**Net result: every sound that can fire DURING active gameplay (walk,
jump, item pickup) is now hard-capped**, using two different knobs in
`tools/aycapture/reduce` depending on what the sound needs to preserve:

- `max_halfwaves_per_run`: shortens every held note while keeping the
  FULL pitch contour -- used for jump (a 10-step rising sweep stays a
  full sweep, just quicker) and tune5/pickup (same idea).
- `max_ms`: a total-time backstop that truncates trailing notes if
  still over budget after the per-run cap -- fine for tunes played only
  during a genuine pause (title, which loops so truncation doesn't
  matter; new-life, capped to ~262ms, still eating into but not
  breaking the tight window a scripted respawn needs).

Footstep additionally only fires every OTHER step (not every step) --
even the cheapest affordable click (~7ms, using captured sndfx 1's
~365Hz instead of sndfx 0's ~68Hz, since a single half-wave at 68Hz
alone costs ~9ms on this delay-loop DAC) was enough to measurably slow
movement at full rate.

### The `play_tone` DAC's real cost model, useful for future sounds

Because the delay loop's cost is `~21.1*period + 1164` cycles per full
wave, and the `+1164` is a FIXED cost that does not shrink at low
period, there is no such thing as a cheap LOW-pitched click on this
hardware -- unlike a real AY chip, where every channel is a free-
running hardware counter regardless of pitch. Any sound meant to fire
during active gameplay (not a dedicated pause) needs either a high
pitch (cheap) or a hard per-run half-wave cap (short regardless of
pitch), and any new tune-during-a-pause still needs SOME cap if a test
or a real player's expectations depend on that pause being short --
"it's not literally realtime, it's a pause" is not a blank check.

### What's still open

- Death (tune2), milestone (tune3), box-open (fx6), dragon-breath
  (fx10), drop-item (fx11), death-sfx (fx25) are captured
  (`tools/aycapture/captures/*.csv`) and reducible with the same tool,
  but not yet wired into the game or budgeted for ROM space.
- The 48K fallback (`MUSIC48.SPC`) was never needed this session --
  everything in the mapped trigger table had a usable 128K capture.
  Worth revisiting only if a future capture attempt genuinely can't
  produce usable content from the 128K side.
- `tools/aycapture` and `tools/aycapture/reduce` are ports/dizzy-coco2-
  local tools (`ports/dizzy-coco2/tools/aycapture/`), not yet promoted
  to `factory/tools/` -- this is the first port needing an AY capture,
  so per the project's own "promote on the second port" rule, that's
  correct as-is for now.

## T0089 follow-up -- the title music was wrong three different ways

Shipped T0089, and the playtest came back immediately: "the title screen
music is not right, and the sound effects seem delayed." All three
causes below were real, and NOT ONE of them was caught by anything
automated in this repo -- amplitude was healthy, `rate.lua` was clean at
15.5/15.0, and `pickupsfx.lua` passed. The checks proved sound was
*firing*, never that it was the *right sound*. That gap is the lesson.

### 1. The calibration was derived with a tool this repo already knew lies

`period_for_hz` was re-derived for the widened 16-bit loop using
`audiocheck.py --scan`. NOTES.md *already recorded*, one section up, that
--scan's pitch reading is untrustworthy -- that warning was written about
short blips and got applied to a sustained calibration tone anyway.

Re-analysing THE SAME WAV FILES in audiocheck.py's default tail-window
mode gives completely different numbers:

    period    --scan      default    hand-derived from the 6809
       100   356.5 Hz    531.5 Hz    537.1 Hz
       800    48.0 Hz     69.5 Hz     69.5 Hz
      3000    14.0 Hz     18.5 Hz     18.6 Hz

--scan was 25-34% low, and by a *frequency-dependent* amount. The
resulting shipped constant (`(894780/f - 1164)/21.1`) put every note
6-40 semitones sharp with every melodic interval stretched, and -- since
half-wave counts are computed for the intended frequency -- every note
too short as well.

**The check that would have caught it instantly: count the cycles.**
The loop is nine instructions; adding them up gives 66 + 16*period per
full wave, which matches the default-mode measurement to 1% across a
29x frequency range and disagrees with the --scan fit by 32% on the
slope and 18x on the intercept. A measurement that disagrees with the
instruction timings is a broken measurement. New rule, in play_tone's
header and tonecal.asm's: any re-derivation gets cross-checked against
the cycle count, and tonecal.asm's documented recipe no longer contains
the string `--scan`.

    period_for_hz(f) = round((894780/f - 66) / 16)

### 2. "Loudest channel per frame" is not a melody -- it is a coin flip

The monophonic reduction picked whichever of the AY's 3 channels was
loudest EACH FRAME. The AY's volume envelopes ramp continuously, so
whenever two channels crossed, the selection flipped -- and the two
loudest are typically the bass and the melody, two octaves apart. The
output zigzagged between them every few frames. Not a melody with wrong
notes in it: an unrecognisable jitter.

Scoring the channels over the whole capture shows how obvious the right
answer is, and that no fixed channel works either:

    tune0 (title)  chA   8 distinct pitches   58-220 Hz   <- bass drone
                   chB  35 distinct pitches   77-176 Hz
                   chC  57 distinct pitches  154-887 Hz   <- MELODY
    fx21  (jump)   chA  11 distinct pitches  385-866 Hz   <- only channel
                   chB, chC silent              that sounds at all

So: commit to ONE lead channel per capture, chosen as the voice that
MOVES (most distinct pitches), higher register breaking ties. Picks C
for the tunes and A for the jump sfx. `reduce` PRINTS the channel it
chose so the call is checkable rather than silently trusted.

### 3. Rests are music, and a 255 cap is not a "no extra cap"

Two smaller data bugs, both of which shortened the tune:
- T0089 dropped silent runs, reasoning a gap is cosmetic. The title
  melody rests in 27% of its frames; dropping those runs every note
  together and destroys the rhythm. Rests are now emitted (period
  `$FFFF`, count in ~1ms units) and `pt_rest` burns the time with the
  DAC parked at 0.
- `max_halfwaves_per_run` was passed 255 for tunes as "no extra cap",
  but 255 is the *count byte's* ceiling, so it silently CLAMPED every
  held note instead of letting it split across entries. 20s of captured
  title music was playing back as 4.2s.

Net: the shipped title tune is now 194 entries / 582 bytes covering 16s
of the real melody. Decoded back out of the table, every pitch is within
**0.06 semitones** of a pitch the original AY actually played, and a
10s capture off the running build puts 146 of 149 pitched windows within
1 semitone of the table (median 0.18), with 50 silent windows proving
the rests are real.

### On "sound effects seem delayed" -- what is measurable from here

Mainloop order is: `scankeys` (line ~717) -> hazard updates -> movement
AND SOUND (~823-865) -> all drawing (~1287-1361) -> flip. So:

- **Input is sampled once per pass, at ~15Hz.** A keypress waits up to
  67ms before the game even looks. That is inherent to the frame rate
  (the original Spectrum sampled at 50Hz), not to the audio.
- **A sound fires ~47ms of drawing BEFORE the frame depicting it
  appears** -- audio LEADS video by roughly a frame.
- **A sound long enough to overrun the ~20ms of frame spare stretches
  the frame it lands on**, which reads as a hitch. Measured and trimmed
  this pass: jump 41 -> 21ms, pickup capped to 62ms, new-life to 560ms,
  footstep 7ms (every other step).

The first two pull in OPPOSITE directions -- moving the sound later
aligns it with the picture but adds to the keypress lag. Which one to
chase depends on which the player is actually hearing, so that is a
question for the next playtest, not a guess to make from here.

### Test fragility, fixed properly this time

`pickupsfx.lua` had its magic frame numbers re-tuned TWICE for audio
duration changes (it triggers a scripted respawn, and the new-life tune
now plays there). It now waits for Dizzy to actually ARRIVE at the
respawn coordinates before starting its input sequence, which makes it
indifferent to how long the audio takes -- the property it always
wanted.

## T0089 follow-up 2 -- "sound effects seem delayed" was INPUT LATENCY

Asked the player to characterise it; answer was "lag after I press the
key", which rules out the audio/video alignment theory and points at
input. Measured it properly with a new tool, `harness/inputlag.lua`:
press UP only when Dizzy is grounded and idle, time it to `dizzy_dy`
going negative (the instant the jump is processed, and exactly where
play_jump fires), 14 samples.

    before:  min 33ms  median 50ms  max 67ms
    after:   min 33ms  median 33ms  max 67ms

**The sounds were never the problem.** The lag is the mainloop sampling
input once per pass at 15Hz, and it has always been there -- adding
audio is simply the first time it became *audible*, because a sharp
transient pins down the exact moment the game notices a key far more
precisely than watching Dizzy start to move does. Worth remembering as a
class: adding feedback to a system can expose latency that was always
present, and the new feature gets blamed for it.

**What was actually fixable.** The pass polled the keyboard at the top
(line ~717) but did not consume it until the movement block, with
`try_pickup` and eleven hazard updates in between. A key pressed during
that stretch had missed its poll and waited a whole further pass. Now
re-sampled immediately before the movement block -- carrying the
`killed` gate with it, since the top-of-pass poll zeroes keyflags while
dead (X-ALL.TXT's `checkkeys` does the same) and re-reading the hardware
without re-applying that would let a dead Dizzy walk.

**What is NOT fixable, and must not be "fixed".** 33-67ms is now the
floor: a press arrives uniformly inside a 66.7ms pass, so it waits a
mean 33ms for the next simulation step. Going lower means stepping the
simulation faster, and `FRAME_FIELDS=4` is deliberate -- at 3 fields
Dizzy walked 80px/sec against the original's 50, and *that* was its own
playtest complaint ("this is harder than the original"). Do not reach
for FRAME_FIELDS=3 to chase input lag; it trades a real speed bug for a
perceptual one.

`OVERCLOCK=1` does NOT help here either, and should not be switched on
for this: it makes the *work* finish sooner, but the pacing loop still
holds the pass to 4 fields for correct game speed, so the sampling
interval -- and the latency -- is unchanged. It would only buy idle
time, at the cost of the one real-hardware risk in this codebase
(T0073: double-speed is marginal on some real CoCo2s depending on RAM
chip speed, which MAME cannot reproduce).

**For perspective, the port is now more responsive than the original**:
X-ALL.TXT paces Dizzy's own logic at 4 ticks of a 50Hz clock = 12.5Hz =
up to 80ms, against this port's 15Hz = up to 67ms.

## T0089 follow-up 3 -- the title tune now comes from the 48K BEEPER

The corrected AY capture put every note within 0.06 semitones of the
original and the playtest still said "doesn't sound great". That is not
a contradiction: **the notes were right and the arrangement was wrong.**
MUSIC128.SPC is a THREE-channel piece, and the CoCo2 has one blocking
square-wave DAC, so reducing it keeps a bare melody line and discards
the harmony and bass that make it recognisable. No amount of accuracy
on the remaining voice fixes that.

MUSIC48.SPC was composed for a one-bit speaker. It is *already*
monophonic, so it survives the trip to a monophonic target intact --
monophonic source, monophonic target. Player's suggestion, and the
right call.

### Capturing a beeper is a different problem from capturing an AY

The AY player writes symbolic values (channel, period, volume) and
`aycapture` reads them straight off. The beeper has no registers at
all: the tune exists ONLY as the timing of speaker-bit flips on port
$FE. So `tools/aycapture/src/bin/beepcapture.rs` runs the same isolated
Z80 sandbox but timestamps every ULA write in T-states.

Two things differ from the AY player and both had to be discovered, not
assumed:

- **It is interrupt driven.** `initune48` does `DI`, installs an IM2
  handler and RETURNS; the music comes from the 50Hz interrupt
  thereafter. Rather than disassemble to find out, the sandbox just ran
  it and printed the CPU state: `I=$FE IM=2 iff1=true`. So the driver
  runs 69888-T-state frames (the real 48K frame) and pulses IRQ at each
  boundary. Port decoding matches `A0 == 0`, not a literal $FE compare,
  because beeper routines reach the ULA through `OUT (C),A` with all
  sorts of values in B.

- **The pitch is NOT the flip interval.** This engine does not emit a
  square wave. Each cycle is a repeating GROUP of edges -- measured:
  484 high, 127 low, 964 high, then a long gap -- a pulse shape chosen
  for timbre. Reading pitch from the flip interval therefore reports
  the pulse width and lands an octave or two high (first attempt gave
  1352-4434Hz "melody", which is nonsense on its face). An FFT is
  closer but still octave-errors, because a narrow pulse train has
  harmonics stronger than its fundamental. **Autocorrelation** on the
  reconstructed 1-bit waveform locks onto the true repeat period.

The result self-checks: tune 0 comes out as 79 / 236 / 118 / 148 Hz
held ~220ms each and repeating -- ratios 1 : 3 : 3/2 : 15/8, i.e.
**D#2, A#3, A#2, D3**. Exact musical intervals falling out of the
arithmetic is not something a mis-detection produces. Whole tune spans
B1-C4 (62-261Hz), which also sits far more comfortably in the DAC's
range than the AY melody line did (155-886Hz).

### It reuses the entire existing pipeline

`beepcapture` emits the SAME CSV shape as the AY captures, writing the
detected pitch back out as though it were AY channel A. So `reduce`
consumes it unchanged, and the pitch bucketing, rests, note splitting,
DAC calibration and gameplay duration caps all apply identically to
both sources. Adding a second, wholly different sound source cost zero
changes downstream.

### tools/mksounds.sh

The capture->reduce->concatenate sequence had been retyped by hand five
times across these sessions, which is how the reduction parameters kept
drifting. It is now one script, with the source and parameters for each
sound recorded in it, and a header explaining WHY the title uses the
beeper and the sfx use the AY. Regenerate with `tools/mksounds.sh`,
then `tools/stage_pack.sh`.

Verified on the running build: 177/195 pitched windows within 1
semitone of the shipped table (median 0.22), 41 silent windows for the
rests. 681 bytes for the title table, 724 bytes still free.

The AY title capture is kept at `captures/tune0.asm` -- switching back
is one line in mksounds.sh. The remaining sounds (new life, pickup,
footstep, jump) are still AY; the same monophonic argument says they
would likely improve on the beeper too, and all six 48K tunes (ids 0-5)
capture cleanly.

## T0089 follow-up 4 -- title back on the AY melody, now with its envelope

Decision chain, for whoever reads this cold:
- 48K beeper title (follow-up 3) -> "sounds nothing like the original".
- Ground truth, finally: loaded the user's own tape in MAME's 48K
  `spectrum` driver and sat on the title screen with the cassette stopped.
  70s of DIGITAL SILENCE, while the same driver DID record beeper output
  from a running game (room-36 savestate) -- though NOT walking sfx as
  first written: that control held `p`, which is not a game key (X-ALL.TXT
  keyboardkeys: left Z, right X, jump SPACE, pickup ENTER). This release plays no title music on a 48K machine at all --
  consistent with X-ALL.TXT gating starttune behind check128 and the
  MUSIC48.SPC include being commented out. The remembered title tune is
  the 128K AY one. (Two traps on the way: the first capture showed a
  constant 1159 peak that was just the cassette never being stopped, and a
  savestate made under `-sound none` would not load into a sound-enabled
  run -- the WAV came out 0.1s long.)
- Player: "back to the AY melody, but fine tune it -- I can recognise the
  song but it sounds terrible".

### Diagnosis before changing anything

Time-aligned comparison of the shipped table against the original melody
channel first read as a disaster (median 5.19 semitones off) -- because
`reduce` trims the melody's 3.78s leading rest, shifting everything. With
the offset searched for, the error is 0.08 semitones median and FLAT
across all 16 seconds: notes and rhythm were right. "Terrible" was timbre.
The measurable difference: the original melody moves through 7 AY volume
levels (9-15) as notes attack and decay; the port played every note at one
fixed amplitude.

### What changed

- **Per-note amplitude.** play_tone toggles `eora pt_amp` instead of
  `eora #$40`. The amplitude index (0-15) is packed into the top nibble of
  each entry's period word -- every real period fits 12 bits -- so entries
  stay 3 bytes. AY volume is mapped through the AY's LOGARITHMIC level
  table, not linearly, or the melody's 9-15 range collapses into a barely
  varying loud band. pt_step also resyncs pt_level to the new amplitude
  when the wave is in its high phase: XOR against a level left by a
  different amplitude does not toggle between 0 and the new value.
- **vol_step** (new reduce arg): split a held note when its amplitude
  moves; 1 follows every envelope step. Title table 199 -> 306 entries.
- **Median pitch and level per run**, not the first frame's -- a run often
  opens on the tail of a slide from the previous note.
- **Calibration** moved with the loop: `eora pt_amp` is extended mode, +3
  cycles, so 72 + 16*period per full wave. Measured (default mode, never
  --scan): 69.5Hz at period 800, exactly as predicted.
- **reduce honours the MIXER register.** It ignored reg 7, so a channel
  with tone disabled was still reduced from its period register. fx10
  (dragon breath) is pure noise with tone off everywhere, and its period
  register held 65533 -- it "reduced" to a 1.7Hz note, caught only by the
  new 12-bit period assert. Mixer survey of every capture: tunes are tone
  only; fx6/fx11/fx21 tone only; fx0/fx1/fx25 tone+noise (only the tone
  half is ported); fx10 noise only (not ported -- needs a noise
  generator).

Verified off the running build (MAME -wavwrite of the title): 7 distinct
loudness bands, 100% of pitched windows within a semitone of the table,
median 0.02 semitones. rate.lua 15.2/15.5, inputlag.lua unchanged
(33/33/67ms).

### Listening references -- harness/ayrender.py

Every check on this music has compared the CoCo against the port's OWN
tables, which proves the last step and says nothing about whether it
sounds like the game; the player's ear has caught that three times now.
`harness/ayrender.py CAPTURE.csv OUT.wav --channels abc|c` synthesises the
captured AY registers back to audio (tone channels only, which is all the
tunes use), so there is an original to compare against without a 128K ROM.
`--channels c` is the ceiling for the one-voice DAC; `abc` is the real
arrangement. If the port matches `c` and still disappoints, the remaining
gap is voices, and the fix is a software mixer on the title screen.

## T0109 -- the rest of the trigger table, wired

| sound | source | hook | cap |
|---|---|---|---|
| box open (sndfx 6) | fx6 | top of msg_begin -- every message box | 35ms |
| drop item (sndfx 11) | fx11 | inventory drop, before drop_to_world | 14ms |
| killed (sndfx 25) | fx25 tone part | kill_dizzy_msg, right after `sta killed` | 55ms |
| death (tune 2) | tune2 | update_death, after the message is printed, before msg_wait_dismiss | 1.1s |

Each goes through a wrapper (play_boxopen/play_drop/play_killed/
play_deathtune) that preserves D and X, because the call sites were never
written expecting a subroutine there: msg_begin's callers load X straight
after it, and kill_dizzy_msg holds its message pointer in X.

NOT wired: milestone (tune 3) -- 1.2KB, and this port has no 30-coin or
reached-Daisy trigger to hang it on yet. Dragon breath (fx10) -- noise.
201 bytes left in code+data after this.

### The pickup test broke three more times, and the game was fine each time

`harness/pickupsfx.lua` teleports Dizzy via a scripted respawn, then walks
him onto the apple. Every audio change that lengthened the respawn path
moved his trajectory out from under its fixed frame windows. Fixes, in
order, each of which exposed the next:

1. "Wait until he arrives at the respawn point" -- but gp_ud_respawn sets
   dizzy_x/y BEFORE playing the new-life tune, so arrival reads true while
   the game is still frozen in play_tune.
2. "...and the CPU is outside play_tone..play_chirp" -- but by then gravity
   has moved him off the exact respawn y, so the combined test never fires.
   Two stages: arrival, THEN three consecutive frames out of audio.
3. Correctly gated, the old DOWN window was now too LATE: it had silently
   been tuned around the tune eating ~34 frames. A single-press sweep on
   the same build settled it -- presses at frames 5,10,15,25,30 after
   resume pick the apple up; 0 and 20 do not (try_pickup starts
   PICKUP_COOLDOWN on the first poll that sees DOWN, hit or miss); 40+ is
   past it. The test now TAPS DOWN while x is within 88-96.

The general lesson is the one the sweep gave in two minutes: when a
scripted test fails after an unrelated change, sweep the input timing
before believing the game regressed.

### tiecroc.lua is broken, but not by this

It reports "never reached proxcroc's box". Built the committed HEAD in a
git worktree (symlinking the gitignored research/ and source/ media, and
copying the gitignored generated target/*_data.asm) and it fails there
identically, x=80 y=176. A trace shows its teleport spot drops Dizzy into
a real kill (killed=10 by the hazard code at ~f=340), after which it never
presses SPACE in room 53 and sits in the death box. Filed as T0110.

### T0109 verified on a REAL kill -- harness/killsfx.lua

The other death tests poke killed=1, which bypasses kill_dizzy_msg, which
is exactly where the killed sfx is hooked. killsfx.lua instead reads room
36's flame boxes out of r2_room_flames, steps Dizzy through candidate
spots until the hazard code itself kills him, and follows through:

    KILLSFX killed_by_hazard=yes at spot 16,163  in_audio_when_killed=yes
    KILLSFX respawned=yes after 169 frames  room=36 lives=2  mainloop_running=yes

i.e. sndfx 25 ran on the genuine path, then the box-open sfx, the death
tune, dismissal, the new-life tune, and the game came back out running
with a life gone. Its first version missed the respawn for the same
reason pickupsfx.lua did (position matches while the tune still blocks;
by the time it lets go, room 36's troll has knocked him off it) -- fixed
with the same two-stage detection.

## T0108 RE-DIAGNOSIS -- there is no walk-stall; the reproduction walked into a fire

The previous investigation's repro (harness/stuck6869.lua) warps Dizzy to
room 69 at (8,168) and holds RIGHT. Traced frame by frame this session:

- keyflags is NOT continuously RIGHT: it sits at $00 for ~100-frame
  stretches -- because `killed` is non-zero and the mainloop zeroes it.
- x goes 8 -> 12 -> back to 8, lives tick down 2 -> 1: a death loop.
- A write tap on `killed` that reads the caller's return address off the
  6809 stack (kill_dizzy_msg pushes X, so S+2) names the killer:
  **hazard_scan+39**, the shared torch-flame scan, through kill_dizzy (no
  message -- death_msg stays $0000, so the box says only [X-ALL.TXT line 991]).
- Room 69's four flames are at (16,155),(4,155),(4,144),(12,147): a tight
  cluster sitting ON the raised block at x=8..32, y=168 -- a hearth. The
  warp point is inside it. The checkpoint is the room entry, so every
  respawn lands back in the fire.

The original agrees on every piece of that: `updateflames` kills on
contact via collidewithdizzy3 (a full AABB, eggwidth 6 units / eggheight
18 -- the same box the port uses); `enterroom` copies x/y into
startx/starty on every entry, exactly like the port's checkpoint; and
rooms.json holds the SAME four-flame cluster mirrored at room 68's right
edge (x=224..252) -- one fireplace straddling the 68|69 boundary. Room 2
is that cluster on its own (4 things, no name), so the duplication is in
the source data, not an extraction bug.

So the old "stall" was the port faithfully burning Dizzy. The SPACE taps
in the harness dismissed each death box before anyone saw it.

**The actual user report** was "jump from the table in room 68 to a ledge
in 69", which the old repro never tried. A route test from 68's table
(y=128, the frame-133 shelf at x=208) shows: from the legitimate standing
spots x=200/204, a rightward jump lands straight back on the table -- the
column of frame-132 blocks at x=224 (y=40,64,88,112) is in the way; starts
at x=208/212 are half-embedded in that column and climb into the high
torch at (204,58). The column's effective attribute is 2 (inherited from
the table, bit 6 clear), i.e. SOLID by the rule roompack implements.
Whether that rule, and therefore the blocked jump, matches the real game
is being checked by running the ORIGINAL -- see the next section.

## The ORIGINAL game's RAM map (48K tape build, running in MAME `spectrum`)

Found by diffing RAM dumps of the real game (loaded from the user's tape
in the same MAME run -- the room-36 savestate cold-resets, see
harness/zx_orig.sh's header) while walking right and jumping, then pinned
exactly by X-ALL.TXT's own declaration order: `colourtable defb
2,3,4,5,6,5,4,3` is a unique 8-byte signature in RAM at $F938, and the
variable block is laid out byte-for-byte from `x` 46 bytes before it.
Verified live, not inferred: x climbed 21->30->38->40 while X was held, y
went 175 -> 145 mid-jump with dy=252 (-4), roomno read 36 in the dungeon.

| var | addr | | var | addr |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| x | $F90A | | startx | $F91D |
| ox | $F90B | | starty | $F91E |
| y | $F90C | | startroom | $F91F |
| oy | $F90D | | roomno | $F925 |
| dy | $F90E | | newroomno | $F926 |
| floor | $F911 | | killed | $F92A |
| animation | $F916 | | coins | $F92D |
| sequence | $F917 | | lives | $F92E |

**Units match the port exactly.** The original's x is the port's
dizzy_x / 4 (startx 46 * 4 = the port's room-36 spawn x of 184); y is in
pixels in both. Keys (X-ALL.TXT `keyboardkeys`, row*32+bit): left Z,
right X, jump SPACE, pickup/fire ENTER.

Gotchas from getting here, so nobody pays for them twice:
- Four MAME instances in parallel and a script that took its RAM dump at
  frame 60 both produced "all zero" dumps -- the real cause was the
  savestate cold-resetting, not either of those. Count nonzero bytes in
  every dump; a loaded game is ~38000 in $5C00-$FFFF, a BASIC boot ~250.
- Screen RAM is a separate `:video_ram` share, so $4000-$57FF reads as
  zeros through the CPU address space. That is expected, not a failure.
- `natkeyboard:post` taps a key; posting every frame is enough to walk.

## T0108 CLOSED -- the port matches the original; verified by running the original

`harness/zx_warp.lua` loads the user's tape in MAME, starts the game, and
pokes the original's own x/y/newroomno so ITS enterroom draws the room and
sets the checkpoint. Same moves as the port's route test:

    ZXWARP t68x50jump | arrived room=68 x=50 y=127 floor=1 start=(50,128,r68) | final room=68 x=50 y=127
    ZXWARP t68x51jump | arrived ... x=51 y=127 ; a=62 LAND r68 x=51 y=127    | final room=68 x=51 y=127
    ZXWARP t68x50run  | arrived ... x=50 y=127 ; a=69 LAND r68 x=50 y=127    | final room=68 x=50 y=127
    ZXWARP fire69     | arrived room=69 x=2 y=167 ; a=1 KILLED r69 x=2 y=167

(x here is original units = port dizzy_x / 4: 50/51 are the port's 200/204.)

- From room 68's table, jumping right in the ORIGINAL lands straight back
  on the table -- the LAND events prove he was airborne -- and never
  reaches room 69. Exactly the port's behaviour. The column beside the
  table is solid in the real game, so roompack's dull-bit rule and its
  colour inheritance are right here.
- At room 69's hearth the ORIGINAL kills Dizzy on the first frame, exactly
  as the port does. The old "walk-stall" repro was the port being faithful.

So the reported "jump from the table in 68 to a ledge in 69" is not a route
that exists in the original either. Nothing to fix. If the user remembers
it differently, the next step is to ask which table/ledge they mean and
check THAT spot with zx_warp.lua -- not to change the port's geometry.

The meta-lesson: two sessions and several hours went into a "bug" whose
repro walked into a fire. The trace that cracked it cost minutes once it
recorded the right variables (`killed`, not just x/keyflags), and the
question "does the original do this too?" is now one script away.

### ...and the other "table": both games, same routes, same pixels

The screenshots showed the port's x=200 spot is a small red SHELF beside
room 68's right-hand column; the Banquet Hall's real table is the grey
one at y=148, x=48..168. So both were tested, in the original
(zx_warp.lua, x in original units) and in the port (same warp-and-act
script shape), side by side:

| route | original | port |
|---|---|---|
| banquet table's right end, jump right | lands x=48(=192) y=175, walks on, BURNT at x=51(=204) y=167 | lands x=192 y=176, BURNT at x=204 y=168 |
| floor from x=192, walk right | BURNT at x=51(=204) y=167 | BURNT at x=204 y=168 |
| shelf by the column (200/204), jump right | lands back on the shelf | lands back on the shelf |
| room 69 hearth (8,168) | burnt on frame 1 | burnt immediately |

Identical to the pixel on every route: the fireplace spans both rooms and
kills from room 68's side at x=204 before Dizzy can ever reach the edge.
There is no way from either table into room 69 in the real game.

## Title tune as full 3-voice AY -- feasibility numbers (NOT built; waiting on the user)

The single-voice title now carries the melody's envelope, and three WAVs
went to the user: the port as it stands, the original melody alone, and
the original full arrangement (harness/ayrender.py). If the verdict is "it
still needs the bass and harmony", this is what a 3-voice title costs,
measured rather than guessed:

**Data.** A change-event stream of the 9 relevant AY registers for tune 0
(frame delta, 2-byte changed-register mask, changed values):

| variant | raw | LZSS (tools/roompack lzpack) | zlib-9, for scale |
|---|---|---|---|
| exact register values | 5985 | 3034 | 2454 |
| periods snapped to the nearest semitone | 3266 | **693** | 459 |

Snapping to semitones throws away the AY engine's per-frame vibrato
wobble, which is most of the entropy -- and the port's single voice
already quantises pitch far more than that. ~700 packed bytes fits the
title image's load-time holes, which reported ~2.7KB spare at the last
build; unpacked (3.3KB) it can reuse TITLE_RAW_BUF once the title image
has been blitted, since nothing else needs that buffer until the game
starts.

**CPU.** A phase-accumulator mixer -- per voice a 16-bit add and a carry
test, then sum the three levels into $FF20 -- is roughly 20-25 cycles per
voice plus ~12 for the output, so ~75 cycles a sample, i.e. ~12kHz at
0.89MHz. That is enough for the title tune's top note (887Hz) with
correct AVERAGE pitch; accumulator jitter at the high end will add some
roughness. The title screen is a dedicated wait loop, so nothing competes.

**The honest constraint is ROM for the code**, not data: code+data has
201 bytes free after T0109, and a mixer plus its event decoder is likely
120-200 bytes. It could run from a load-time hole too (title-only code,
executed before gameplay draws into the framebuffer windows), but that
needs care. None of this is started: the user's last explicit choice was
the single AY melody.

    TIECROC standing on the gator at x=148 y=152 (inside proxcroc)
    TIECROC tie registered (gator var1=255)
    TIECROC PASS croc_var1=255 (255=tied) croc_frame=123 rope_still_carried=false mainloop_back=yes dizzy x=148 y=152 killed=0

T0105 built the tie and noted its harness "never managed to drive the
drop". It had two real bugs, found by instrumenting rather than bending
it again -- plus one false lead of my own, recorded so nobody repeats it:

1. **Bad start spot.** (140,140) is only half over the gator, so Dizzy slid
   off into the pool and drowned, then sat in the death box. A settle sweep
   (drop from x=144..172, record where he comes to rest) found that only
   x=168..172 land him standing ON the gator, at (144..148, 152) -- inside
   the proxcroc box (x 144..184, y 140..160).
2. **Its "hold the mouth shut" poke opened the mouth.** update_crocodile
   does var1+=1 and THEN picks the frame from var1 within one pass; the
   mouth is open on 3/5/7. Forcing var1=2 every frame makes it 3 on every
   animate tick. Write taps on pickup_timer/inv_cursor never fired; the
   death tune played; the game sat in the death box. Now var1=0 (->1,
   shut) and frame 123, and only until var1 reads 255 -- which is also the
   tied state the old poke used to clobber.
3. **False lead: pressing UP in the inventory is CORRECT.** show_inventory
   deliberately opens on EXIT (playtest feedback: dropping should be a
   choice). The rewrite first "fixed" the UP away, and a tap on inv_cursor
   showed it opening at 1 = EXIT and SPACE just closing the inventory.

Harness technique worth reusing: a once-per-frame PC sample almost never
lands inside a blocking UI loop, because those loops live in wait_vsync
and scankeys. Look for the loop's return address on the 6809 stack
(S..S+20) instead -- see in_inventory()/in_msgwait() in tiecroc.lua.

## T0111 -- the dragon's breath: AY noise gets its own note-table entry type

fx10 (sndfx 10, X-ALL.TXT `startbreath`) is PURE noise: the mixer reads
%00110111, every tone bit off, noise on channel A, a 1s swell with volume
6->14->1 and the noise period zig-zagging through reg 6's low five bits.
There was no tone to reduce -- the reducer used to turn its disabled tone
register (65533) into a 1.7Hz "note" until the mixer fix in follow-up 4.

**Format.** A table word whose period field is $0Fxx is NOISE: xx = step
delay (0..254 -- 255 excluded, so amplitude 15 can never spell the $FFFF
rest), count = LFSR steps, top nibble = amplitude as for tones. Tone
periods must stay below $0F00; reduce asserts it (the lowest real note is
period ~900). pt_step checks the high byte once per entry, not per wave, so
tone timing is untouched -- re-verified on the title: 100% of pitched
windows within a semitone, median 0.02, 7 loudness bands.

**play_noise** (room36.asm) steps its OWN 8-bit Galois LFSR ($B8 taps) and
writes 0 or the entry's amplitude to the DAC per step: 46 + 8*delay cycles
on the high path, 38 + 8*delay on the low, budgeted at the average. Not
rng_step, deliberately: that one paces the rat, and harness/rate.lua counts
mainloop passes by watching rng_ctr change -- sharing it would have
corrupted both the game's randomness and the frame-rate measurement.

**reduce** leads a no-tone capture by its busiest noise channel, groups
noise rows into runs split on the volume swell (vol_step), and takes each
run's median noise period for the rate. mksounds.sh caps it like the other
mid-gameplay sfx: 12 steps per run (keeps all 7 steps of the swell), ~15ms
total, since the breath can start at any moment while Dizzy is in room 54.

**Verified** by new harness/breathsfx.lua, which drives the REAL start path
instead of poking dragon_fire: it keeps the dragon awake and seeds rng_ctr
with 0 (rng_step turns that into 1, which is under update_dragon's 5/256
threshold), and counts play_noise's work with a write tap on pn_lfsr:

    BREATHSFX PASS breath_started=yes noise_steps=84 killed=0 mainloop_running=yes

84 = 7 entries x 12 steps, i.e. the whole table played exactly once. 99
bytes left in code+data after this.

Still not ported: the milestone tune (tune 3, 1.2KB) -- it needs both ROM
space and a trigger the port does not have yet (30 coins / reaching Daisy).
Split out as its own task. The noise HALF of the killed and footstep sfx
(tone+noise mixes) could now use this entry type too, but each costs blocking
time mid-action for a subtle gain; left as is unless a playtest asks.

Before changing every room, the question that matters: can any hidden
cell actually be touched? New `tools/roomview.py --hidden` answers it for
every built room, and exits 1 if one can (so it can gate a build when rooms
are added):

    room 35: 8 hidden cell(s) at x=40..56, all capped by solid at y=48 -- unreachable
    room 67: 16 hidden cell(s) at x=168..184, all capped by solid at y=48 -- unreachable
    room 68: 8 hidden cell(s) at x=224..240, all capped by solid at y=48 -- unreachable
    room 69: 8 hidden cell(s) at x=72..88, all capped by solid at y=48 -- unreachable

## 3-voice title mixer -- PROTOTYPE built and heard (standalone, not in the game)

To turn "is the bass and harmony worth it?" into something the user can
listen to, a standalone CoCo2 program now plays the full three-channel AY
title tune on the DAC. Nothing in the game build changed.

- `tools/aycapture/src/bin/mix3stream.rs` turns an aycapture CSV into an
  event stream: per record a delay (50Hz ticks), a mask, then new 16-bit
  phase increments and amplitudes for the voices that changed. `--semitone`
  snaps periods to the nearest semitone; `--cal HZ` emits one steady tone.
- `harness/mixer3.asm` runs three 16-bit phase accumulators on the direct
  page; the three top bits index an 8-entry table of summed amplitudes
  (rebuilt only when a volume changes) that goes straight to $FF20.

**Measured, not assumed:** increment 3604 played 469.0Hz, so the sample
rate is 8529Hz (cycle counting predicted ~8060) and SPT = 171 samples per
tick. Tempo was checked from inside the program -- a Lua script timestamps
each wrap of the stream pointer: 20.41s per loop against 20.05s nominal, ~2%
slow from per-record event processing (SPT=168 would absorb it).
Envelope-autocorrelation of the audio gave 17.4s and then 27.2s on the same
signal, so it is useless for tempo here; the pointer is the truth.

**Size (tools/roompack lzpack):** exact periods 6061 raw -> 2936 packed;
semitone-quantised 2683 raw -> **617 packed**. The mixer itself is ~150
bytes of code.

**Spectral similarity to the original 3-channel render** (log-magnitude,
60-2000Hz, 200ms windows, envelope-aligned -- indicative only, the
alignment correlation is weak): 3-voice prototype 0.33 (exact and semitone
alike), shipping single-voice title 0.12.

**Bug worth remembering:** the first build put the mixer's variables at
$1000, inside the event stream assembled straight after the code. Every
variable write corrupted the stream, the pointer jumped every few seconds,
and two WAVs were captured from that before the wrap timer caught it. The
6-byte calibration stream never reached $1000, so calibration looked fine.
Variables now live on page $06, below the program. The corrupted WAVs were
never sent.

Both WAVs (mix3_exact, mix3_semi) went to the user. Putting it in the game
would need: the ~620-byte stream in a load-time hole gathered like the title
image, the ~150-byte mixer run from a scratch buffer (code+data has 99 bytes
free), and the title loop polling SPACE between tick records.

## 3-voice title IN THE GAME -- behind TITLE_MIX3=1 (default build byte-identical)

Built so that if the user likes mix3_semi.wav, it is one flag, not a project.
`TITLE_MIX3=1 tools/stage_pack.sh` builds it; plain `tools/stage_pack.sh`
produces a binary that `cmp`s identical to the shipped one (checked before
and after, with the stashed tree as the baseline).

**How it rides along without touching the full regions:**

- `target/title_mix3.asm` is the mixer plus `mix3_stream.asm`, assembled
  SEPARATELY with `lwasm --format=raw` into a position-independent blob
  (2898 bytes). Nothing in it depends on IMAGE_END, which moves with every
  room change. PIC tricks: variables are direct-page offsets (the caller sets
  DP), the stream start comes from `leau stream,pcr`, and the amplitude-table
  address comes from `tfr dp,a / ldb #sumtab / tfr d,x`.
- `mktitle --music BLOB` packs it on its own (832 bytes) and appends it after
  the title image's packed stream in the same hole chain. It emits
  `TITLE_LZ_LEN` (image only) and `TITLE_MUSIC_LEN`, and exits if
  image+music exceeds 4096 (the gather gap before TITLE_RAW_BUF).
- boot (`show_title`, `if TITLE_MIX3`): after the blit and the banner copy,
  unpack from `TITLE_LZ_BUF+TITLE_LZ_LEN` into TITLE_RAW_BUF (now dead), set
  DP=MIX3_DP ($DC, about 4KB in, past the blob), JSR it, restore DP=0.
  That's 20 bytes against the single-voice loop's 25, and low data has 0
  free. The explicit offset matters because lz_unpack can read one flags
  byte past its end.
- The mixer polls SPACE (PIA0 column 7, as scankeys does) once per tick
  record, parks the DAC low and returns. ti_release then waits for the key
  to come up, as before.
- mksounds wraps the tune0 table in `ifeq TITLE_MIX3`, so this build frees
  it: code+data goes from 99 to 192 bytes free.
- IRQ/FIRQ are masked for the whole game, so the non-zero DP during the
  title cannot be seen by a handler.

**Verified** (`harness/mix3title.lua`, state-driven):
- PC reaches the blob at 2.27s and stays with no key held.
- The stream pointer wraps every 20.03s.
- SPACE leaves the blob with DP=$00, and the game reaches room 36 with
  Dizzy placed.
- killsfx and pickupsfx pass on the MIX3 build (the sfx tables moved).

**Audio checked against the stream itself, not by ear:** a Python
simulation of the mixer decoding mix3_stream.asm (at 8529Hz) was compared
against the MAME WAVs in 120ms chunks. Normalised cross-correlation was
0.67-0.92 for both the in-game WAV and the standalone WAV the user heard,
with the same per-chunk pattern. The odd-offset hits are the tune's repeated
passages.

**Tempo fix: SPT 171 -> 168.** Both WAVs drifted steadily against the
simulation (0.29s over 17.5s = 1.6%), and that equals the 20.38s/20.05s loop
ratio. So the per-sample rate is right and the per-tick event cost is the
slack. At 168 the loop is 20.03s. Pitch is unaffected.

**Dead end worth recording:** the first comparison said the in-game audio
did not match the prototype (11% then 30% agreement). Two causes:
- `scratchpad/mix3/semi/mix3_semi.wav` is a STALE capture from before the
  variable-overlap fix. The one sent is `mix3/mix3_semi.wav`; their md5s
  differ.
- Log-band spectrogram correlation and dominant-pitch agreement both fail
  on three equal-level square waves: the control offset scored the same as
  the best one.

Compare recordings against a simulation of the data that produced them, and
check which file is which before believing a mismatch.

## Filming the ORIGINAL -- harness/zx_film.lua (built for T0115/T0116)

zx_warp.lua logs positions; for "what does this ANIMATE like" questions,
use zx_film.lua instead. It loads the tape, warps like zx_warp, presses
keys on a schedule (`KEYS="ENTER:0-6,X:40-90"`) and snapshots every SNAP
frames.

`ACTOR="51,76,96,120" ACTOR_OFF=12` finds that actor's 16-byte movingdata
record in RAM by its four orig* fields, which never change at runtime. It
then logs the live x/y/frame/delay/delaycounter/var1 every LOGEVERY frames.
That log settled the portcullis in one run, after three runs of guessing
from pictures. Room 51's gate record is at $A824 in the 48K tape build.

Gotchas:
- The lever message box, like every windowrou, waits for a key. Schedule
  a dismiss press after the throw, or the film is 1000 frames of a paused
  game.
- The throw only registered on a LATER ENTER press, not the first, and
  not at a consistent one between runs. Press several times, and check
  var1 in the RAM log rather than assuming.
- A 3-frame SPACE tap does not jump (the original samples keys once per
  ~3-frame tick). Hold it about 10 frames.
- The original's main-loop tick is ~3 frames, close to this port's 15
  passes/sec, so a delay/tick count copies 1:1 to passes.

## T0115 -- the portcullis: closed at rest, OPENS from below, slams, reopens

Playtest: "when you first actuate the lever, it grows out of the floor, and
stays closed; out of the room and back in, it animates closing again and
does not open."

**Two previous readings were both wrong.** T0068 had a hopping 8x8 block.
T0102 read `printmoving` without `rubprintmoving` as "leaves a trail", and
built the trail with an OR blit, plus a "filled" latch that made the whole
column solid.

The source settles it, and the real game confirms it:
- **Plot mode 0 overwrites.** Colour 7 has bit 3 clear, so frmplot=0.
  doplottype patches a NOP between `ld a,(iy+0)` and `ld (hl),a`. Mode 1
  is XOR, 2 is OR.
- **Frame 120's bottom two rows are blank** ($db,$b6,$db,$92,$db,$92,0,0).
  Overwriting 2px higher puts the blank rows on the old bottom edge, so
  rising ERASES upward and the gate opens. Falling closes it.
- **resetportcullis draws it at every 2px step from y=96 to its current
  y** on room entry: a closed lattice column at rest.
- **Timing, from the RAM log.** After the throw it rises 2px per 2 ticks
  (delay 2) to 96. It then slams back to 136 at 2px per tick (delay 0) and
  rises again at 2px per 4 ticks (delay 4), forever. delayrou runs a mover
  every delay-th tick, every tick for 0.

**Port** (gameplay.asm update_portcullis/draw_gate, room36.asm
build_solid_actors):
- **Movement:** the literal mechanism. v1 is -2/+2, offset 6 is the
  delay, and up_dc is the delay counter; ticks map to passes.
- **Drawing:** direct byte writes down the gate's framebuffer column
  (8px sprite, byte-aligned x=176):
  - Per buffer, it remembers the y last drawn there.
  - Rising, it draws every 2px step in between (skipping one leaves two
    stale rows). Falling, one draw at y covers it.
  - If the damage rect touches the column, it redraws the whole column:
    sprite rows 0/1 alternating from 96 to y-1, then the sprite at y.
    Row for row, that is what the top-down reset draw leaves.
- **Collision:** gate_col_hdr pinned at y=96, height rewritten each pass
  to y-96+6. Closed blocks, raised lets Dizzy under.
- **Dead code:** T0102's latch and PORT_SPEED are gone. The ROU_PORTCULLIS
  test in actors.asm's da_clear path is unreachable now; harmless.

**Verified:**
- portcullis.lua: opens, shuts, and redraws correctly after a forced full
  redraw of both buffers mid-rise, which is the re-entry case.
- portcullis_block.lua closed: blocked at x=152, and the on-screen column
  is inked on every frame.
- portcullis_block.lua OPEN=1: walks under the gate into room 52.

**Test lesson, twice in one task: read only the ON-SCREEN buffer.**
- cur_buf==0 means A is displayed and B is the redraw target, which can
  be caught mid-repaint (cleared, not yet redrawn). Reading both buffers
  "failed" a correct gate that way.
- For a few frames after a room change the other buffer still holds the
  PREVIOUS room's picture: room 36's art turned up in the gate column at
  a=10..14.
- The lever throw only registers while Dizzy drops past the switch on
  arrival (respawn y=80), so any test step before the DOWN press has to
  fit in the first ~14 frames. Closed-at-rest is checked in
  portcullis_block.lua instead.

## T0116 -- the dragon's flames were mirrored, and its neck vanished mid-breath

Filmed side by side (zx_film.lua, and a port film via the breathsfx
teleport). Two real differences:
- **Flame puffs pointed right**, back at the dragon, so the outward-moving
  plume read as flying INTO the mouth. The original draws each puff with
  its tip leading left. Fix: aspr_112_mirror, frame 112 with each byte
  bit-reversed (flame collision still uses aspr_112's size).
- **The neck was not drawn during a breath.** The source skips printneck
  while breathing but never erases, so the last neck stays on screen. The
  port clears DRAGON_BOX every pass and left the head floating. Fix: draw
  the neck every pass; the swing is frozen during a breath, so it matches.

**The flame maths was already right** (first flame x 140 → 72, away from
the mouth), and so is the hazard as far as I could test. Walking right into
a forced breath, the port kills at x=84 (orig 21); the original, walking
right from x=10, dies at x=21-31. The playtest's "can walk past while it
spits" is **not reproduced**: filed as T0119, waiting on the exact move.

Room 54 runs at 5.0 passes/sec, before and after this change.

## T0114 -- lives as the original: 2 spare eggs, and game over returns to the title

X-ALL.TXT:

  shown and 3 lives in all, to the new-life jingle.

  spare life left, `quitted` does `jp titlescreen`.

The port had lives=3, decremented only on death (4 lives in all). At 0 it
showed its own "GAME OVER / PRESS SPACE" box, refilled lives and respawned.

**Port:**

  one-time boot work. It resets the stack (`lds #$0100`), sets lives=2,
  sets both buffers' last-x to 255 so the title gets fully repainted, then
  runs the usual actors_init/gameplay_init/load_room/redraw. It now also

### Two bugs on the way, both mine, both now guarded

1. **Fixed-size title_frags.** With the staging windows full, the packed
   title spilled into a third hole in the low region. But title_frags.asm
   (the gather table) is assembled in that same region, and stage_pack's
   raw pass had used the previous build's 2-entry table. The table grew 4
   bytes between passes, and the low block overlapped the hole by exactly
   4 bytes (memaudit caught it). mktitle now pads the table to 6 entries,
   and fails if a title ever needs more.
2. **MIX3_DP rounded DOWN into its own blob.** I changed the variable page
   from +$1000 to +$0C00 to save headroom, but `/256` floors. With
   MIX3_BUF=$EFBC the page was $FB, inside the blob, which ends at $FB0E.
   The mixer clears that page on entry, wiped its stream's tail, and
   mix3title failed (no wrap, SPACE polled every few seconds).
   - Now `(MIX3_BUF+TITLE_MUSIC_RAW+255)/256`, with an `ifgt` guard that
     the page starts past the blob.
   - mktitle emits TITLE_MUSIC_RAW, the unpacked size.
   - room36.asm falls back to 3072 when an older title_frags.asm lacks
     the symbol, because stage_pack's pass 1 runs before mktitle. A 4096
     fallback pushed the page onto $FF and tripped the other guard.

### The budget, after this task -- read before adding another room

| region | free |
|---|---|
| staging window A (framebuffer A) | 25 bytes |
| staging window B (framebuffer B) | 33 bytes |
| title's load-time hole space | 421 bytes spare |
| low data ($0100-$0DFF) | 0 |
| code+data ($0E00-$3FFF) | 0 (its spare now holds a title fragment) |
| gap1 ($5800) | 296 |
| gap2 ($7800) | 67 |

**The $8000+ scratch chain is the other ceiling.** Above IMAGE_END ($C5BC)
sit, in order:
- TITLE_LZ_BUF, 4096 (3913 used);
- TITLE_RAW_BUF, 6144;
- CUR_ROOM_CMASK, 384, plus $200 slack;
- the mixer blob, 2898;
- its variable page, which must stay below $FF00.

MIX3_DP is page $FC now, so **only about 500-750 bytes of raw room image
can still be added** before that guard fires. The next room needs memory
work first. Cheapest options, in order:
- trim the scratch slack: TITLE_LZ_BUF's gap to ~3.9KB, the cmask slack
  to $180;
- reuse TITLE_LZ_BUF's tail for the mixer instead of a separate area;
- only then, a third staging window or a second load.

## T0121 -- memory: ~4.2KB of duplicated art removed, scratch laid out by lifetime

Starting point, after T0120:
- staging windows A/B 25/33 bytes free, title hole space 421;
- above $8000, ~750 bytes of room-image growth left before the mixer's
  page hit $FF00.

Three changes, none of them to game logic.

**1. Scratch buffers laid out by lifetime** (room36.asm; zero code bytes,
because boot_code's region is full). The chain above IMAGE_END is now:
- TITLE_LZ_BUF, the gathered packed title + music (PERMANENT);
- BANNER_BUF (PERMANENT);
- ONE transient 6144-byte area (TITLE_RAW_BUF), used in turn by:
  - the unpacked title, until it is blitted;
  - the mixer blob and its DP page, while the title is up;
  - CUR_ROOM_CMASK, while a game runs.

None of those is ever alive at the same time as another. Game over now
re-unpacks from the kept packed stream: show_title_again moved up three
instructions to sit before the unpack. Before, the banner overwrote the
packed stream, so the UNPACKED image had to be kept (6144 more bytes).
Result: ~13.9KB → ~11.6KB, guarded by asm errors for page overlap, page
past the transient area, and chain past $FF00.

**2. One copy of the flame and water tiles** (roompack
`--shared-anim target/shared_anim_data.asm`). They were byte-identical in
every room: 12 copies of the flame set, 3 of the water.
- The first room writes a named section into the shared file; later rooms
  verify theirs is identical, and roompack fails if not.
- Room descriptors point at the global flame_table/water_table.
- **No per-room `equ` aliases.** Rooms 35/36 are assembled in the low
  region while an alias's value lands in the staged image, so
  stage_pack's symbol export defined them twice. room36.asm's fire-pit
  overlay uses flame_table directly (was r2_flame_table).

**3. The self-contained rooms reuse the shared sprite pool**
(`--shared-sprites-reuse-only`). Rooms 67/83/84/85/86/100/70 were fully
self-contained because the pool's overflow half lives in the r9800 block.
In reuse-only mode a room references frames the pool already holds and
emits only the new ones locally; it never grows the pool. They run after
every pool-feeding room in regen_art.sh, so the pool is complete.

**Found by a hash scan, not by reading.** Hashing every `fcb` block in the
generated room .asm files found 4185 duplicated bytes. After the change:
148.

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| raw $8000 image | 17852 | **13648** |
| packed blocks A+B | 6052+6111 | **4754+5893** |
| staging A / B free | 25 / 33 | **1390 / 251** |
| code+data free | 0 (held a title fragment) | **301** |
| title hole space spare | 421 | **2305** (title now needs 2 holes, not 3) |
| room-image headroom above $8000 | ~750 | **7263** |

**Verified:**
- harness/framedump.lua, before (T0120 binary) vs after, all 16 built
  rooms: **byte-identical framebuffers**.
- lzverify: 13648 bytes exact.
- mix3title (vars page $D6), gameover, and newrooms, whose output matches
  T0120 line for line.
- The full suite is green, and rate is unchanged.

**What's left to spend.** Load-time space is now the tighter of the two
ceilings: ~2.3KB of hole space plus the staging windows' spare. Rooms have
packed at 60-80% of raw, so that is roughly two or three average rooms.
The next levers, if needed:
- Better compression. The LZSS here is 4096-window, 3-18 byte matches,
  and the dithered art packs to ~76%, so an entropy stage or a longer
  window would help. It needs a new 6809 decoder in the full low region.
- A second load file. That changes distribution: a user decision.
