## T0126 -- a bit-level LZ codec: ~2.8KB of load-time space back

T0085's byte-aligned LZSS (a flag byte per 8 items, 3-18 byte matches, a
4096-byte window) packed this game's data poorly. Measured on the real
blocks, with xz/exomizer as the ceiling:

| data | LZSS | xz raw | exomizer | **new** |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| staged block A (6569) | 5329 (81%) | ~4100 | ~4200 | **4300 (65%)** |
| staged block B (7727) | 5893 (76%) | 4663 | 4815 | **4803 (62%)** |
| title, column-major (6144) | 3081 | -- | 3315 | **2666 (43%)** |
| 3-voice music blob (2898) | 832 | 612 | 594 | **600** |
| room collision mask (e.g. room 83, 384) | 116 | -- | -- | **73** |

**Format** (tools/roompack/src/lz.rs, the only full spec; mirrored by
lz_unpack): ZX0-style but this project's own.
- Bits are read MSB-first from bit bytes, with raw bytes interleaved in
  the stream.
- Lengths use interlaced Elias gamma.
- After a match: 0 = literal run, 1 = new match. After literals: 0 =
  repeat the last offset, 1 = new match.
- New match: GAMMA gives the offset high part + 1 (256 = end), then a raw
  low byte, then the length as GAMMA+1.
- The encoder is a cost-optimal parse that keeps 8 (last offset, kind)
  states per position.
- Rust round-trips are asserted in lzpack AND now in mktitle; the title was
  never verified before.

**6809 decoder** (boot_code.asm): same `lz_unpack` label and U/Y
interface, so all five callers are unchanged (two staged blocks, title,
music, load_room's mask). It is 132 bytes against 102, still with no
decode RAM.

**Its one bug:** the encoder starts with last offset = 1 and may emit a
repeat before any new match, but the decoder never initialised lz_dist, so
every call inherited the previous call's offset. lzverify showed 3 bytes
wrong, and every room's collision mask came out garbled (newrooms put
Dizzy at y=68 everywhere). Now `ldd #$ffff / std lz_dist` at entry.

**Costs:**
- Boot spends 120 frames in the decoder instead of 71 (~0.8s longer before
  the title).
- A room load spends ~75ms instead of ~38ms unpacking its mask, about one
  extra frame of hitch at a transition.
- Steady-state rate is unchanged.

**Budget after:**
- title hole space spare 4702 (was 1642);
- staging A/B free 2053 / 1402 (was 815 / 251);
- code+data 933 free (was 262);
- gap2 still 18.

Enough for rooms 50, 56, 71 and 39 plus their routines, gap2 aside.

**Verified:**
- lzverify exact (13677 bytes).
- **harness/titleverify.lua (new):** framebuffer A matches all 6144 bytes
  of the source title.
- mix3title and gameover pass.
- newrooms matches T0122's results.
- The full suite is green.
- framedump against T0122 at the usual load frame is identical, apart
  from animated actors' timing (the boot got longer) and one banner byte.
  The one byte is explained below.

### Harness traps found on the way (none of them the game)

- **rate.lua timed its first warp from load, not from the game running.**
  A slower boot "dropped" room 36 from 15.0 to 12.0 while every later room
  read the same. It now waits for the game; 15.0 again.
- **Loading at frame 30 races BASIC's cold-start RAM sweep.** The
  instruction BASIC is part-way through when the script takes over lands
  one more write: `$00` into $3521 (X=$3527, BASIC's S=$03D7). In both
  builds that byte was inside a title fragment, so each build's title was
  one byte wrong in a different place. It looked exactly like a codec bug
  until a write tap on $3521 showed who wrote it. titleverify loads at
  frame 150; framedump takes LOAD_AT.
- **Loading at frame 150 races BASIC's 60Hz IRQ instead.** The image loads
  rooms 35/36's art from $0100, which is also BASIC's RAM interrupt vector
  table (IRQ jumps through $010C). An IRQ between the load and `start`'s
  `orcc #$50` jumps into room data: the T0122 build did exactly that
  (PC looping in r36_room_placements), the T0126 build happened not to.
  This is **not** a codec issue, and it is filed as T0127 because it may
  matter for a real CLOADM + EXEC.

## T0123 -- room 50 ARMOROG'S DEN, with Armorog

**Behaviour** (gameplay.asm update_armorog), a transcription of X-ALL.TXT
armorogrou/resetarmorog in the actor's own v1/v2/colour. States:
- **asleep:** wakes when Dizzy enters raw (64,125,12,40) = px (128,125,48,40).
- **countdown:** 20 active ticks.
- **running:** +4px and 102↔103 per active tick. He heads for the den if
  Dizzy is at y≥150 or the bone lies in room 50 at x≥192, y≥140; otherwise
  he stops at x=120.
- **guarding:** stays at x=120.
- **fed:** at the den x=184 he faces the other way, y=156, the bone
  vanishes and "[X-ALL.TXT line 884] [X-ALL.TXT line 885]" shows; a Dizzy who died on
  the way just resets him.

The rules around the states:
- Contact kills in every state ("[X-ALL.TXT line 993] [X-ALL.TXT line 994]").
- delayrou delay 2.
- resetarmorog runs once per room load, unless he is fed. `room_load_seq`
  is a counter load_room bumps, because the original runs resets from
  enterroom, respawns included.

**Verified against the original** (harness/armorog.lua vs zx_film logging
armoroghere's movingdata record):

| | original | port |
|---|---|---|
| wakes when Dizzy reaches | raw x 42 (168px) | 168 |
| running | 1 unit / 2 ticks, frames alternating | 4px / 2 passes, alternating |
| catches a Dizzy standing on the floor at 208 | at raw x 74 (168px) | at 168 |
| after that death | reset to 54,156, var1 0 | reset to 88,156, v1 0 |

- SCEN=guard stops at 120 (v1=3), and a room reload resets him.
- SCEN=fed reaches 184 facing the other way (v1=4) with the bone gone, and
  a reload leaves him in the den.
- Wall time is ~1.35x the original's (15 passes/s vs ~20 ticks/s), the
  same ratio as every other mover here.

**Drawing:**
- Asleep, he takes the static damage-rect path.
- Awake, he is redrawn every pass.
- While running, the 4px strip he just left is wiped first via
  arm_strip_hdr, a blank 4x20 sprite through clear_and_blit. Screenshots
  mid-run show no smear.
- In the den the mirrored frames are used (--mirror-frames 102,103).
- **Known difference:** his box clear wipes the rock pile's art where he
  overlaps it in the den. The original draws him in XOR over the rocks.

**Memory work this needed:**
- **actor_data.asm moved into the packed $8000 image** (block A). gap2 had
  18 bytes and his four 48x20 sprites are ~500.
  - stage_pack now exports the **equates** of staged files too
    (ACTOR_COUNT, ROU_*...). Pass 2 only sees the blobs plus
    staged_syms.asm, and those values are nowhere near the image's
    address range.
  - stage_pack also skips the `*_staged_start/_end` bracket labels. Once a
    raw block passes 8KB, its end label lands in the image's range and was
    exported twice.
- **Blocks rebalanced** (rooms 100 and 87 moved from A to B): A 5421 /
  B 5522 packed, 723 / 622 free. Code+data 331 free; hole spare 3508.

**Tools and harnesses fixed on the way:**
- **tools/roomview.py still had the T0085 LZSS decoder**, a fourth copy of
  the codec missed in T0126, and crashed on every re-packed mask. Replaced.
  It reproduces room 51's mask exactly as printed before the codec change.
- **lzverify.lua** now waits (with DIZZY_MAP) for the CPU to reach
  show_title. Its fixed f<120 read the image while block B's tail was
  still being unpacked: 916 "wrong" bytes, all at the end.
- **titleverify.lua** masks IRQ/FIRQ in CC before its frame-150 load. That
  load otherwise races BASIC's live IRQ into the room data at the vectors
  (T0127); this build lost that race and never reached the title.

## T0124 -- rooms 56 THE LIFT CONTROL HUT and 71 DOZY'S HUT: machines, lift, key 1

**What is in:**
- Rooms 56 and 71, both packed into block B / block A (regen_art.sh
  reuse-only loop and --actor-rooms).
- New actors: 56's machine (ROU_MACHINES, frame 127, mirrored when v1
  bit0), both lifts (ROU_LIFT), key 1 (frame 13).
- Messages msg_keyinmachine, msg_obstructlift, msg_liftcogs, byte-for-byte
  from X-ALL.TXT.
- Names for 56 and 71.

**Key 1** (gameplay.asm cdt_key, proxkey1):
- Dropped in room 56 inside (76,120,16,16), the key goes to room 255.
- Machine 1 at (72,116) gets v1|=1 and room 71's lift gets v1|=1.
- The message then shows.
- Keys 2-4 live in unbuilt rooms. **Room 56's own lift belongs to key 4
  (room 48)**, so it stays off in this build.

**Lift** (logic_low.asm update_lifts/ul_one, a transcription of liftrou):

| | original (zx_film, var1 poked on) | port (harness/keylift.lua) |
|---|---|---|
| room 71 travel | y 56..112, 1 unit/tick | 56..112, 1px/pass |
| pause at each end | oldmovefrm=50 ticks | 50 passes, measured 5 times |
| rider | feet on frame 126, 40px below the top | feet-lift offset 39..41 over the whole travel |
| cogs (top 2 rows of the shaft box) | killedbycogs | killed 5 frames after entry |

- Obstruction works as in liftrou: if Dizzy is in the shaft box but not
  riding, the lift is held 2 passes, and every 64th hold shows "obstructing".
- Riding is x - lift x < 12 (the original's `sub movex / add 32 / cp 3`).
- Solid: two build_solid_actors entries, the top (frame 125) and the bar
  (frame 126 at y+40).
- draw_lift runs every pass. The rope rows are written directly and both
  frames overwritten, with 2 rows cleared beside each.

**DEAD END -- testing dizzy_seq for "standing still".** liftrou rides only
when (sequence)=0, and the first port tested dizzy_seq==0. It does not mean
the same thing:
- The original picks a sequence only on a floor (updatedizzy1: checkfloor,
  floor==0 -> cantstop). Dizzy dropping the 1px the bar just lowered keeps
  sequence 0.
- The port rebuilds dizzy_seq every pass as 3+dir whenever he is airborne.
- So a lowering lift was held on alternate passes: ~4x slow going down, and
  the obstruction count reached 55 of the 64 that pop the message on one
  descent.
- The fix tests what (sequence)=0 means there: dizzy_dir==0 and dizzy_dy
  not negative.
- The per-pass seq rebuild is a general divergence from the original (it
  also changes which frames a walk-off-a-ledge fall shows). It was left
  alone deliberately, because T0117's jump feel was tuned on it.

**Memory:**
- The low region overflowed $0E00 by 131 bytes and ran into start:.
  update_armorog and the lift code moved to **logic_low.asm, org $7800**
  (gap2, below nibswap at $7E00).

  gap2_end <= $7E00.

  data 0. Title in 2 holes, 1638 spare.

**HARNESS TRAP -- writing PC from Lua can resume BASIC's half-finished
instruction.**
- MAME suspends the 6809 mid-instruction at frame boundaries: sampled 300
  frames, PC never equalled CURPC.
- `cpu.state["PC"].value = start` makes the rest of that instruction run
  with operand bytes read from the new PC.
- For the T0124 image this jumped into data and hit an HCF opcode. The CPU
  then counted through memory, one address per cycle.
- titleverify saw the mixer's address range pass under PC at frame 193, and
  reported a garbage title (6094/6144 bytes) instead of a crash. The T0123
  image survived the same race by luck.
- **Diagnosis:** `-noplugins -debug -debugger none` plus
  `manager.machine.debugger:command("trace FILE,maincpu")` from the frame
  callback. The trace showed `LDS #$0100` never taking effect and PC
  advancing 1 byte per step. `-debugscript` produced no file.
- **Fix in titleverify:** one frame after the load, S must be <= $0100
  (start's lds ran). If not, poke $0071=0 (force a cold start) and
  soft_reset, then retry at a different phase.
- soft_reset **re-runs the autoboot script**, so the OK line prints twice.
  The frame-30 harnesses carry the same latent race; the stray write into
  $3521 in T0126 was the benign form of it.

**Harness fixes on the way:**
- newrooms: arrival now requires the target room to have been seen. A case
  whose start x equalled where the previous case left Dizzy "arrived" in
  the wrong room; this was the 87 -> 54 oddity.
- portcullis_block: gate() scans ACTOR_COUNT records, not 20.
- `OPEN=0` still means open mode (the harness tests presence). The closed
  run is OPEN unset.

**Verified on this build:**
- keylift: lift, ride and cogs all PASS.
- lzverify, titleverify, mix3title, gameover.
- armorog charge/guard/fed, as in T0123.
- killsfx, portcullis, portcullis_block closed (blocked at 152, visible) and

## T0125 -- room 39 GOING DOWN THE WELL, room 23 A STRANGE NEW WORLD, and the upside-down world (T0038)

**The mechanic, from X-ALL.TXT:** `newroom`'s special cases, ~1235-1320, plus
`flipscreenrou` and `sideback`.

**One global flag, `upsidedown`.** flipscreenrou swaps screentable entries
48..183, so while it is set every draw in that window lands on row 231-r:
- rooms stay flipped until the flag toggles back;
- that means room 23 and whatever lies beyond it (22, 24...);
- prtmessage unflips around every box (flipifnecessary).

Checked on the original with zx_film: room 39 is drawn mirrored on the way
back up (snapshot).

**Well transitions** (logic_low.asm well_route, from rt_vertical):

| case | source routine | what happens |
|---|---|---|
| into 39 from anywhere, or down out of 23 (room 7 is never a room) | fallenoutof23 | lastroom = here; tumble dy 4, no steering (well_mode 1) |
| down out of 39 | flipandsettumble | upsidedown ^= 1; back into 39 at y=180, sequence 8, dy pinned at -6 (well_mode 2) |
| up out of 39 | settojumpout | to 23 if lastroom==55, else 55; dy -8, right held (well_mode 3) |

- An unbuilt target falls back to 55, so the well can never pin Dizzy.
- well_air holds dy at -7 before the port's gravity adds 1, giving -6.
- well_seq forces sequence 8. seqtab has a 9th row: 8,7,6,5,4,3,2,1.
- ml_landed clears well_mode, and the input skip mirrors troll_launching's.

**Verified** (harness/wellverify.lua):
- Real play, starting in 55 with the lid removed: 55>39>23. Mode 1 on
  entry, then the flip, then mode 2 with dy=-6 on 81 of 95 frames (the rest
  are entry frames), then mode 3 out of the top. He lands in 23 at (96,160)
  with upsidedown=1.
- Warped into the 39 slot (x=60): 39>55>39>23. This is the same room
  sequence as the original film from raw (15,90).
  - The original lands in 23 at raw x 27 (px 108). The port lands at 96:
    its jump-out drift is shorter.
  - Flag parity matches: a warp starts the first descent unflipped, so 23 is
    reached upright in that run. That is why the original's snapshot of 23
    looked normal.
- The fall column in 39 is the narrow slot at px ~57-87, under 55's well
  mouth. Warping at y=70 exits the top in BOTH games (step-up passes
  TOP_TRANSITION_Y=66), so start any 39 test lower.

**The flip in the port** (room36.asm): mirrored in the drawing primitives,
not by a post-render pass. Dizzy moves every pass, so a once-per-change
swap cannot work.
- **Per primitive:**
  - `fb_rowd`: row = 231-y when flipped;
  - `fb_strideb`: the stride becomes -32-width, which fits a signed byte, so
    `abx` -> `leax b,x`;
  - the flipped bottom limit is 184;
  - covered: blit, blitdizzy, clear_and_blit, rd_cleardmg (clamped to the
    window).
- **Flag handling:**
  - redraw latches `fb_flip` from upsidedown each pass;
  - msg_begin clears it (boxes are never upside down);
  - draw_ui clears it around the banner and restores it.
- **Deliberately left unflipped** (rooms that can never be upside down):
  dragon box (54), gate (51), lift rope (56/71), rat save-under.
- **The port's bead border** (ui.asm) is not room art. Its side columns keep
  their phase, and flipverify excludes columns 0 and 31.
- **harness/flipverify.lua** captures normal, flipped and unflipped again,
  and demands:
  - rows 48..183 mirror exactly (Dizzy's box excluded, checked for ink);
  - banner and status rows unchanged;
  - the normal picture back after unflipping.
  - Result: PASS in rooms 84 (static art) and 52 (actors), both exact.

**Memory: staging block C.** 39+23 put block B 394 bytes over framebuffer B;
A+B together were 255 short.
- They are now a third raw block, `rc_staged_start/end` (org $E000 in the
  raw pass only), destined for RC_DEST right after block B.
- stage_pack extracts it, extends IMAGE_END/staged_syms over it and passes

- mktitle packs it after the music into the title's load-time holes, with a

- new_game calls `unpack_c` from the permanent TITLE_LZ_BUF, so it also runs

- **The title now uses all 6 title_frags slots (MAX_FRAGS 6).** The next room

     silently stayed in room 36.

5. **flipverify toggling upsidedown mid-pass:** the pass that already

## Exit / hazard / item test campaign against the original (post-T0125)

User request: test actions, object/actor interactions and hazards in each room;
check every room reaches every neighbour, especially jumps up into the room above.

**Tools and harnesses:**
- **tools/exitcases.py:** cases from the collision masks: up-jumps from every
  surface a jump can lift through TOP_TRANSITION_Y, walk/jump off each edge, walk
  off into drops. Hazard starts are skipped.
- **tools/hazardcases.py:** a start on every flame/water tile, beside every deadly
  actor, plus a safe control per room.
- **tools/edgecases.py:** ledge-end overhangs.
- **tools/itemspots.py:** each item's floor, used by harness/items.lua.
- **harness/exits_port.lua** and **harness/exits_zx.lua:** the same CSV on each
  side, one session each. Both apply the "first landing after the last room change"
  rule. **tools/exitcompare.py** diffs them.
- **harness/items.lua:** picks up and drops every pickupable in the built rooms.

**Harness traps paid for here (all fixed in the files):**
- **Jump input.** The port needs UP held until dy goes negative; a SPACE still held
  from box-dismissing masked it. The original needs SPACE held past a key poll.
  Early runs "found" dozens of jumps that could not reach the room above; almost all
  were jumps that never took off.
- **Keys in a live original.** ENTER opens the inventory window and SPACE jumps, so
  never press either in a live game.
  - Windows are detected by PC in the original's key wait, $F3F0-$F470 (death
    window, room 84's knock chatter).
  - A death respawns at startroom/x/y and starteggres rewrites newroomno, overriding
    a warp. Hold the checkpoint safe during recovery.
- **Port landing mid-transition.** The port writes cur_room before load_room has
  placed Dizzy. Count a landing only outside load_room/room_transition_* (PC or
  stack).
- **Starts at raw x>=57 (px 228/232).** The original's goneright tests `cp 57`
  exactly, so Dizzy wanders off-screen. These are not port bugs.
- **Room 39 cases** depend on well_last/lastroom left by earlier cases.
- **items.lua:** DOWN pressed right after SPACE's release never reached keyflags;
  hold it until it takes.

## T0139 -- side-wall probe is direction-specific (checkleftside / checkrightside)

The original samples ONE body column per move direction:
- checkleftside: lookx=x, only when moving left.
- checkrightside: x+eggwidth-1 (px x+20), only when moving right.

Both check y-10/-14/-18. goneleft/goneright (new x 1/57) are tested before either
side check.

The port's check_wall used to test BODY_L and BODY_R on every move. A Dizzy
overlapping a wall on his TRAILING side could not walk away from it.

**Fix:** `cw_pair` tests `try_x + cw_side`. Callers set `cw_side`:
- walk left: 0
- walk right: BODY_R
- well_air: BODY_R

**Regression vs the original (tools/exitcompare.py):**
- exits: 141 -> 147 MATCH. Fixed: 84r1 84r2 84l2 84l3 84l4 68u1 52d2.
- edges: 281 -> 279 MATCH. Both drops (52eL10, 52eL18) are sampling artefacts:
  - They are NONE cases that start embedded in room 52's step.
  - The "first landing" is caught one 4px climb frame earlier (124/132).
  - `final=` is unchanged (120/128), and those cases never run the walk code.
- exits 36u3 and 39u23 changed verdict, but are NOT deterministic: re-runs of the same
  binary give different results. 36u3's JUMPLEFT sometimes never fires (jumped=0), and
  39u23 is the well's drop timing.
- footsteps, keylift, tiecroc, portcullis_block, wellverify and newrooms all still pass.

**Harness caveat:** exitcompare's `land` is the first floor frame. For cases that start
embedded, compare `final=`, not `land=`.

**52d0 (still DIFF-ROOM):** walk right off room 52's step into the pit.
- Original: walks at y=135, falls from x=172, reaches 204,177, lands 208,173 on the
  far lip (x=224 platform) and walks on to 53.
- Port: stands at y=132/136 and falls along the same arc 1px lower. At x=204,y=178
  its right probe at y-10=168 hits the lip top row, so it is wall-blocked, falls to
  36, and lands at 208,80.

This is the 4px collision-mask quantisation (surfaces snap to 4px rows, while the
original is pixel-exact on attributes). It is not a physics-rule difference.

## T0136 -- no air control (user decision: faithful)

X-ALL.TXT reads left/right only from `checkfloor -> bettercheckkeys`, with a floor under
Dizzy. Otherwise `cantstop` keeps moving him by the latched left/right.

A jump (sequence 3..5) is stricter. `jumping` skips even checkfloor until the 8-step
`animation` wraps to 0. Landing (`floorfound/storedizy`) does not touch the animation,
so a Dizzy who lands mid-jump slides the takeoff way for the rest of the cycle.

A normal room change (`gotoenterroom -> enterroom`) does NOT clear the latch; only
starteggres does. The special cases in room 39 and room 23 set their own keys.

**Port:**
- `jump_on` stands in for "sequence >= 3" and `jump_anim` for the original's animation.
  dizzy_anim is divided for display, so it cannot serve.
- In room36.asm, jumping sets both to 1 (animation 0, then cantstop's inc).
- Keys are read only when there is a floor and no jump cycle is pending. Otherwise
  dizzy_dir drives the step.
- The jump key is refused while `jump_on` is set.
- gameplay_init and respawn clear dizzy_dir, jump_on and jump_anim.
- Cost: 72 bytes of hole space; 142 bytes spare.

**Verified:**
- 67r0 and 68l0 no longer drift into a third room: 67>83 at x=216, 68>84 at x=16, the
  same x as the original.
- 53r1: after landing, both machines now slide on to x=84.
- Regression (t0136a): exits 146 MATCH (was 147), edges 279, footsteps, keylift,
  tiecroc, portcullis_block, wellverify and newrooms all unchanged.
  - Cases fixed: 35u5, 51u13, 52d1, 68r0.
  - The four new DIFF-DEATHs are not real:
    - 52d2 and 53r1 do not die on re-runs of the same binary (dragon and fire timing).
    - 35u8 and 35u11 start at x>=228, the known artefact starts; the original's jump
      never fired there.

## Harness concurrency cap -- the OOM that killed a session

2026-09-15: a regression batch launched 12 MAME instances at once (exits, edges,
newrooms, keylift, footsteps, tiecroc, 2x portcullis, wellverify, rate, plus a port
and a ZX lift run) while two subagents were live. The kernel's OOM killer picked the
`claude` process itself (global_oom, pid 5714), ending the session mid-task and
truncating the two long runs (exits had 135 of ~316 cases).

**Rule: run the harness batch SEQUENTIALLY, or at most 2-3 emulators at a time.**
The long runs (exits ~5 min, edges ~5 min) dominate either way, so the wall-clock
saving from wide fan-out is small and not worth losing the session over. The short
checks (newrooms, keylift, footsteps, tiecroc, portcullis, wellverify, rate) are
under a minute each.

## T0137 -- room 71's lift top: 4px collision columns, a solid rope, and the real gonedown line

Three findings, all from the same case (Dizzy falling onto the lift top).

**1. The original's collision is 4px wide, not 1px.** checkline walks `lookx` in
4px units and the Spectrum's `getbyte` masks `11110000b`/`00001111b` by lookx
parity, so a probe is solid when ANY ink falls in its 4px screen column.
actor_solid_test tested a single pixel, so frame 125's top row -- a 2px hook --
was missed and Dizzy fell through onto the bar.

- Implemented as ONE masked test, not a four-column loop: every actor x is a
  multiple of 4 (they come from the source's own 4px units) and probe_x is
  masked to its column, so the four pixels are always exactly the high or low
  nibble of one byte and never straddle.
- **DEAD END, and why:** the first version looped over the 4 columns. It worked,
  but cost enough time in the hottest collision path to make tiecroc FAIL --
  the harness's inventory-key timing shifted. Adding debug counters made it pass
  again, which is the tell. A 4x cost in actor_solid_test is not affordable.
  Bisected with 3 builds, then proved it was not layout by padding 64 dead bytes
  into a passing build (still passed).

**2. The rope is solid.** X-ALL.TXT `resetrope` stamps frame 125 every 2 rows
from origy down to the lift, so the rope is ink on screen, and the original's
collision reads the screen. The port drew it (draw_lift writes px col*8+15/16
directly) but left it out of collision. Added as a synthetic solid box in
build_solid_actors: x = (lift x & $F8)+12, w 8, y = ul_orig, h = lift y - ul_orig.

- Sprite headers with **bpr 0** now mean "full ink box, no bitmap". gate_col_hdr
  uses it too, which deleted its 48 bytes of $ff.

**3. BOT_TRANSITION_Y was 188; the original's line is 182.** checkbottomside does
`inc a / cp 182 / jp nc,gonedown`, leaving at y=181 and arriving at 181-114=67.
The port's feet sit 1px below the original's, so 182 -> 68. At 188 it arrived 6px
low, under the lift top, and the original's 71/87 loop never happened.

**Verified:** lift cases went from all-stuck (port fell to the bar every time) to
3 MATCH, 71L0-L2 crossing 71>87 like the original, and 71L3 looping 71<->87.
Regression: exits 146 -> **149 MATCH** (35u11, 36u3, 36u4, 53r1, 83r3 gained,
none lost); keylift, footsteps, portcullis_block, wellverify, tiecroc all pass.

**Cost:** edges 279 -> 278. 36eR1 (a 36>52>36 bounce) now ends 4px higher than
the original, deterministic on re-run. Accepted: 182 is the source's own value
and it bought 5 exit cases plus the lift.

## T0142 -- mirror sprites at DRAW time, as the original does (memory)

The port stored a second, flipped copy of every mirrored sprite. That is the
worst possible data to store: **a mirrored bitmap shares no byte runs with the
sprite it came from, so the LZ packer cannot collapse it** -- every byte costs
close to full price. X-ALL.TXT never does this: `printmoving` reads bit 7 of the
object's colour byte into `frmreverse` and `frame` consumes it by walking the
sprite's bytes right-to-left (~4072/4103). One sprite, both facings.

**The flag rides for free.** Every placement x is a multiple of 4, so bit 0 of
the placement's x byte carries "mirror this one" at a cost of zero extra bytes
(room 100 alone has 78 placements; a flag byte each would have cost more than
the copies saved). `rd_placelp` masks it off before setting blit_x. The x>>3
damage-rect column test above it is unaffected -- bit 0 never crosses an 8px
column.

**The flip itself** (`blit_mkrev`, room36.asm): every sprite width in the build
is a multiple of 8 (checked across all 226), so a horizontal flip is exactly
"reverse the byte order, reverse the bits in each byte" with no shift to fix up.
Bit reversal uses ONE 16-byte nibble table (`rev_lo`) plus four shifts for the
other nibble -- the second 16-byte table cost more than the shifts, and the
build had 12 bytes of hole space left at the time. `blit_mirror` is a one-shot
parameter latched into `bm_cur` at blit entry, so a stale flag can never leak
into the next blit.

**Generator** (tools/roompack/src/main.rs): sprite variants are now always
emitted unmirrored (`vname` never appends `_m`, the mirror_grid step is gone),
and the placement writer ORs bit 0 into x. The `mirror_frames` path that makes
ACTOR sprites (`aspr_*_mirror`) is untouched -- those are drawn through a
different path and still store copies (456 bytes, worth doing later).

**Measured:** 27 fewer sprites, sprite data 5518 -> 4566 raw bytes. Binary
31638 -> **30869**. Title hole space spare 130 -> **868**, which is the number
that decides whether another room fits.

**DEAD END -- harness/framedump.lua cannot verify this.** It dumps at a FIXED
FRAME NUMBER (DUMP_AT, default 310). The smaller staged data unpacks faster, so
the new build reached a different moment: every room, including EMPTY room 70,
differed by exactly the same 1025 bytes -- an intro message box still on screen
in one build, gone in the other. Dumping later does not fix it either; flames,
water and actors count their animation phase in passes since boot, so rooms
never re-align. Fixed-frame framebuffer comparison is only valid between builds
that boot identically.

**The verifier that does work: tools/roomrender.py.** It composes each room's
bitmap straight from the generated data (applying the mirror flag exactly as
blit does) and diffs two data sets, with no emulator and no timing at all. All
23 rooms rendered IDENTICAL across the change, with 84 mirrored placements.
Collision masks are byte-identical too -- roompack's cmask loop builds from the
raw unmirrored frame and never applied the mirror bit (which is T0143, a real
bug of its own: mirrored scenery collides with its unmirrored shape).

**T0142 A/B (same regen, old generator vs new), the honest numbers:**
binary 31739 -> 30869, exits 150 -> **165 MATCH**, edges 266 -> 248, rate up
~1% (room 35 14.8 -> 15.0 passes/s: fewer sprite bytes to shift).
- All 20 edge cases that changed verdict are DIFF-LAND; 18 of them end in the
  IDENTICAL final position.
- The 2 that do not (100eL4, 100eL6) are deterministic and 4px lower. Room 100's
  cmask is byte-identical and its render is identical, so this is T0135's
  wall-climb (4px a pass up a column) landing on a different pass count with the
  slightly faster build -- not a collision or art change.
- keylift, tiecroc, footsteps, portcullis, wellverify, titleverify and gameover
  all pass.

## T0144 -- the shared sprite pool was read-only for 13 rooms

T0121's loop (67 84 85 83 86 100 70 87 50 56 71 39 23) ran with
`--shared-sprites-reuse-only`: those rooms could USE a frame already in the
pool but could not CONTRIBUTE one. So any frame first needed by one of them was
duplicated privately in every room of the loop that wanted it -- spr_231 in six
rooms (83/50/86/85/23/100), plus spr_200-203: 27 definitions, ~794 raw bytes.

Reuse-only existed because the r9800 staging block holding the pool's overflow
half had 167 bytes free. **T0142 removed that constraint**, so the loop now feeds
the pool like every other room.

- Room-private sprite defs 27 -> 0; sprite data 4566 -> 3862 raw bytes.
- Binary 30869 -> **30493**. Title hole space spare 868 -> **1239**.
- gap1 118 free, staging block 2 692 free, gap2 429 free -- real headroom again.
- tools/roomrender.py: all 23 rooms render IDENTICAL. Collision masks unchanged.
- roomsweep/lzverify/titleverify/gameover/keylift/tiecroc/wellverify all pass.

**Running total for the two memory tasks: 31638 -> 30493 bytes, and load-time
hole space 130 -> 1239.** Worth roughly a room and a half, and T0142's half of
it keeps paying on every room added from here.

**Still on the table:** actor sprites keep their flipped copies (aspr_*_mirror,
456 bytes) -- same technique, but the actors redraw every frame so the per-row
reversal cost needs measuring, and verifying a moving actor needs a state-gated
capture rather than framedump's fixed frame. ~1143 bytes more sit in duplicate
ROWS inside sprites, which would need a row-reference scheme.

## How much is actually left to build -- MEASURED, not estimated (2026-09-15)

Asked whether the remaining rooms can fit in 64K. Measured from the original's
own tables (extracted/rooms.json + frmtable.json), not guessed:

**The remaining work is 31 rooms, not 79.** Of the original's 101 rooms, 48 are
EMPTY map slots (like room 70: a real room number a fall passes through, 97
bytes as a stub). 22 are built. Only **31 unbuilt rooms have content**.

| Remaining demand | bytes |
|---|---|
| 1603 placements x 4 | 6412 |
| 31 collision masks, packed (~63 each, measured) | 1953 |
| NEW scenery frames: only **16** of the 105 the whole game uses are not already in the pool | ~300-600 |
| 48 empty stub rooms (~97 each) | ~4700 |
| **room data total** | **~13.3KB** |

The built rooms already pulled in 89 of the 105 frames, which is why the tail is
so cheap: new rooms are mostly placements + a packed mask.

**Supply, from the current map (build of T0144):**

```
$8000-$C2F0  unpacked room data (IMAGE_END)
$C2F0-$D1CC  packed title kept for the game-over return   3804
$D1CC-$D7CC  banner buffer                                1536
$D7CC-$EFCC  6144 transient: title image -> music mixer -> room cmask
$EFCC-$FEFF  ~3892 bytes  UNUSED
```

| Step | frees |
|---|---|
| claim $EFCC-$FEFF (move the buffer chain to the top of RAM) | 3.9KB |
| the packed title kept resident only to re-show it at game over | 3.8KB |
| already free (439 staging B + 429 gap2 + 868 title holes) | 1.7KB |
| the second framebuffer (also serves as staging window 2 -- trade-off) | 6.1KB |
| the 6144 transient, if the title unpacked straight to the screen | 5.7KB |

**Verdict: the rooms fit.** ~13.3KB of room data against ~15.5KB freed by the
first four, before any compression work.

**A COMPLETE game is tighter, and the constraint MOVES.** It also needs the other
38 actors (~2.7KB of data plus behaviour code), ~44 more message boxes (~3KB) and
their puzzle logic: call it 23-25KB all in. Reachable with the fifth item, but the
binding constraint becomes **code+data below $8000, which is 0 bytes free**, not
room data. The escape hatch is already recorded above ("Why a 64K machine is
tighter"): resident code can be staged to $8000+ exactly as room data is. Nobody
has tried that yet.

**CORRECTION to this session's earlier advice.** Bank switching / a second load /
a banked cartridge were raised as if the port had run out of room. On these
numbers that was too pessimistic: the full game plausibly fits 64K as a SINGLE
LOAD, like the original. The original's own tape is one 40959-byte block (plus a
6912-byte loading screen and a 294-byte BASIC loader) -- verified by parsing the
TZX, 5 blocks, no mid-game loading.

## T0145 -- the scratch chain now grows DOWN from $FF00, not up from IMAGE_END

Same three buffers, same order, same sizes. The only change is where the slack
lands. Built upward from IMAGE_END the leftover sat at $EFCC-$FEFF, stranded
above the last buffer where nothing could ever reach it. Anchored at $FF00 and
laid out downward, that slack lands directly above IMAGE_END -- which is exactly
where the room image grows.

    IMAGE_END      $C2F0
    free for rooms $C2F0-$D223   3892 bytes
    TITLE_LZ_BUF   $D224
    BANNER_BUF     $E100
    TITLE_RAW_BUF  $E700 .. $FF00

The guard flipped with it: it used to check the chain did not run into the I/O
page; it now checks the room image has not grown up into the chain.

Verified: titleverify OK, gameover, wellverify (the well drives the flipped
buffers), keylift, tiecroc, footsteps, portcullis all pass; exits 165 -> 166
MATCH; rate unchanged. 3892 bytes bought for zero gameplay cost.

## T0147 -- the title's 6144-byte scratch buffer is gone (2990 more bytes)

The title unpacks column-major and is then transposed into framebuffer A, so it
cannot unpack straight to the screen. But it does not need a buffer of its own:
**framebuffer B is idle while the title is up on A**, so the unpack scratches
through $6000 and the transpose reads from there.

**Why that was not safe as-is, and the one-line fix.** At boot, A is guaranteed
(boot clears every SAM F-bit). At the GAME-OVER entry (show_title_again) it is
not: cur_buf and the SAM's F4 bit are wherever redraw() left them, which depends
on the parity of redraws before you died, and nothing on the death path pins them
down. boot_code's own comment had worked AROUND this ("flip_buffer's state is not
established this early and guessing it wrong shows a screen of garbage") rather
than fixing it. show_title_again now forces page A first (the same F4-clear poke
redraw uses, plus cur_buf=0), which makes both entry points deterministic. The
player cannot see it: A holds the stale game screen for the length of the unpack
either way, and the final step still duplicates the title into BOTH buffers.

TITLE_RAW_BUF is now sized by what actually lives in it rather than by the title:
TITLE_RAW_LEN = TITLE_MUSIC_RAW + 256 (the mixer blob plus its whole DP page) =
3154, with a new assembly-time guard proving CUR_ROOM_CMASK (384) still fits.

Free span above IMAGE_END: 3892 -> **6882 bytes**. titleverify OK, gameover PASS
(the risky path), keylift and tiecroc unaffected.

## T0146 -- text GAME OVER instead of returning to the title (+3804 bytes)

**User decision, memory over fidelity.** X-ALL.TXT's `quitted` goes back to the
title screen; this port now shows a GAME OVER box and waits for a key. The
reason is that the title return was the ONLY thing keeping the gathered packed
stream (title + music + block C, TITLE_GATHER_LEN = 3804) resident for the whole
game. Nothing re-unpacks after boot now, so the stream lives in framebuffer A as
boot scratch and its 3804 bytes join the free span.

**Block C was the catch.** unpack_c ran from new_game, i.e. on every game, not
just at boot -- purely because the stream happened to be resident, not because
RC_DEST needed refreshing. Checked before changing it: room_placements_ptr is
only ever read, collectible state lives in actor_ram (not baked into the static
tables), and staged blocks A/B are already unpacked once at boot. So unpack_c is
now a boot-only call, sequenced with the title and mixer unpacks BEFORE the
transpose overwrites the stream.

show_title_again is gone (merged into show_title, the only caller path left),
taking T0147's "force page A" workaround with it -- there is no longer a second
entry point whose display state was unknown.

**Free span above IMAGE_END: 6882 -> 10686 bytes.**

**The harness had to change with it, and that needed care.** harness/gameover.lua
asserted the OLD behaviour (title art on screen, title waits for a key). The
subagent that made the change correctly reported the failure instead of editing
the test to pass. Rewritten to assert the box, and the rewrite exposed a real
trap: losing the last life shows TWO boxes back to back (death window, then GAME
OVER) which block in the SAME msg_wait_dismiss loop, so they cannot be told apart
by PC, by stack, or by lives. The old stage tapped SPACE every 14 frames, which
dismissed both -- the game-over box would never have been observed. It now waits
for the first box, dismisses it with exactly one press+release, and asserts that
whatever is still blocking afterwards stays blocked for 85 frames with no input.
Verified: box_reached, box_on_screen, box_waits all true, new game resets clean.

## T0148 (IN FLIGHT) -- staging CODE above $8000: two landmines, both real

Moving `update_dragon` + `dragon_flames` to a staged block at CODE_DEST
($EAAE, defined as BANNER_BUF-CODE_BUDGET so it grows DOWN and leaves the
room-data gap contiguous). Not finished; these two findings are the value.

**1. PASS 1 AND PASS 2 DO NOT AGREE ABOUT LOW-MEMORY ADDRESSES.** stage_pack.sh
assembles twice: pass 1 raw (STAGE_GEN), pass 2 packed (STAGE_LZ). `start:`'s
boot code differs between them -- STAGE_LZ has two `jsr lz_unpack` where the
raw branch has two byte-copy relocate loops -- **exactly 12 bytes apart**. So
`low_resume`, and everything gameplay.asm defines after it, sits at a DIFFERENT
address in each pass (measured: pass1 $1FE9 vs pass2 $1FDD).

Staged blocks are frozen from pass 1 and never re-assembled for pass 2. Room
data never noticed because it references nothing in low memory. **Staged CODE
does**: any reference it bakes in to a low-memory variable points 12 bytes wrong
in the shipped build. Symptom: the routine RUNS (178 calls counted in room 54)
and silently writes to the wrong addresses -- dragon_swing/dragon_fire/rng_ctr
never advanced. It does not crash: a wrong address into zero-filled RAM no-ops.

Fix: put the code's variables INSIDE the staged block so their addresses derive
from CODE_DEST (pass-invariant), and export every one of them through
staged_syms.asm as literals for pass 2, the same way R9800_DEST/RC_DEST already
are. **Rule for any future staged code: it may not reference a low-memory label
that pass 2 can move -- either keep the data in the block or export it.**

**2. lwasm 4.24 MISCOMPUTES RELATIVE BRANCHES INSIDE `phase`** when the physical
org differs from the phase target -- reproduced standalone: a `beq` two bytes
from its target, `org $1000` / `phase $9000`, assembles with the offset off by
exactly the org/phase gap. Blocks A/B/C never hit it because they are pure data
with no branches. Staged CODE must therefore be assembled with `org CODE_DEST`
directly in the raw pass, NOT the scratch-org + phase pattern. (Verified correct
byte-for-byte after the change.)

**3. THE TEST SUITE DID NOT CATCH IT.** rate, gameover, keylift, tiecroc,
footsteps, wellverify and titleverify ALL passed with the addresses broken --
the dragon simply stopped animating, and nothing asserts that it does.
harness/breathsfx.lua was the only thing that caught it. Any future staged-code
work must be verified by a harness that asserts the moved routine's OWN effect.

**State at the token limit:** build was failing its own length guard ("staging
block D: block at $eaae is 338 bytes, map says 344") because lwasm emits no
trailing bytes for an `rmb` that ends a block; the in-flight edit reorders the
declarations so the block ends on emitted bytes. That guard is a hard assembly
failure, so a broken block cannot ship silently. Agent's verdict: KEEP.

**T0148 RESULT AT THE TOKEN LIMIT: still FAILING, work parked as a patch.**
After the pass-parity fix and the rmb->explicit-zeros fix the build is clean
(block D = 344 bytes at $EAAE) but `harness/breathsfx.lua` still reports "the
dragon never started breathing". So moving the variables into the block did NOT
fully fix the addressing, or a second problem is in play. The tree was reverted
to the last good commit and the whole change is preserved at
`wip/T0148-staged-code-WIP.patch` (apply with `git apply`, and note
target/dragon_code.asm is a NEW file inside it).

Next session: re-apply, then instrument the boot unpack itself -- confirm block
D's bytes actually arrive at $EAAE intact (compare a few bytes against the map)
BEFORE looking at the routine again. The evidence so far says the code runs but
does not have its intended effect, which is the same signature as the pass-1/
pass-2 address skew above; the variables were moved into the block, but check
every remaining absolute reference the routine makes (it calls blit, aabb_hit
and kill_dizzy, all of which live in low memory and move between passes).

## T0143 -- mirrored scenery now collides with the shape it DRAWS

roompack's cmask loop built from the raw decoded frame and never applied the
attribute's mirror bit, so a mirrored placement drew one way and collided the
other. Fixed by mirroring the stamp (same mirror_grid/unpack/repack helpers, about
the sprite's own width) when `inherited & 0x80` is set.

**Provably right by construction:** the original has no collision map -- checkattri
reads the SCREEN, and the screen shows the MIRRORED sprite. So the original's
collision is mirrored, always was, and the port's was not.

**Correction to this session's earlier claim about room 52.** I said room 52's 18
mirrored placements (railings, painting, sword) collided wrongly. They do not:
instrumenting the loop shows ALL 18 carry SOLID_DULL_BIT, i.e. they are decorative
and skipped before collision is ever computed. The old playtest complaints about
those railings (T0045-T0048) were about how they LOOKED, already fixed. Only two
rooms have a mirrored AND solid placement: **room 36 (2 bytes of mask changed) and
room 87 (1 byte)**. Everything else is byte-identical.

Rendering unchanged (tools/roomrender.py: rooms differing 0); titleverify, keylift,
tiecroc, breathsfx all pass.

**A FOURTH, separate symptom -- DEBUG_PROX_KEYS=1 livelocks harness/exits_port.lua
on some jump cases, DEBUG_PROX_KEYS=0 does not.** Found running the required
differential: the full 316-case run made it to case 52u12 and then produced
NOTHING for the next 9200 seconds (confirmed by two separate runs stopping at the
exact same case). Bisected the same way as the tiecroc bug: `ONLY=52u12,52u13`
against the harness's own EXDBG hook shows the harness's `busy()` check (scans 25
raw bytes past the 6809 hardware stack pointer looking for a return address
inside play_tone/play_chirp or msg_wait_dismiss/fb_stablekeys, NOTES calls this
a heuristic for "an unfinished sound or message box is still blocking input") go
true every 4th frame while Dizzy is standing still with every key released and
`killed=0` -- so `quiet` (the harness's own "keys have been off long enough,
send the next warp" counter) resets before it ever reaches its threshold of 20,
forever. **This does not happen on the unmodified HEAD build, and does not
happen on this same build with DEBUG_PROX_KEYS set to 0** -- confirmed by direct
A/B rebuild, not inferred. The isolated case (`ONLY=52u13` alone, no preceding
52u12) lands IDENTICALLY on baseline and on this build (52@72,131, floor=0) --
so this is NOT a real physics/gameplay difference, it is `busy()`'s stack-byte
heuristic reading stale/garbage bytes that happen to alias a monitored address
range more often once `debug_prox_keys` (called unconditionally every mainloop
pass, in every room, even though it's a 6-instruction no-op outside rooms 54/55)
is in the call graph. Raising TOOLCHAIN_SKEW_PAD to 64 bytes did NOT fix this one
(unlike the tiecroc bug, which needed only 11) -- it is evidently not the exact
same skew, just the same FAMILY of "any code-size change near here can flip an
unrelated test" fragility. NOT ROOT-CAUSED. Left as a TOP-TIER DECISION: ship
DEBUG_PROX_KEYS=1 (the debug key always compiled in, which is what was verified
above and what the user asked for) accepting that exits_port.lua cannot
currently run to completion against it, or gate it off by default and only
build with `-DDEBUG_PROX_KEYS=1` for a manual debug session. This report's own
build ships with DEBUG_PROX_KEYS=1.

Differential (tools/exitcompare.py against baselines/exitcases.csv), run with
DEBUG_PROX_KEYS=0 specifically so it could complete (all 316 cases, no livelock;
this only disables the item-less bypass keys -- cdt_potion/cdt_crowbar,
update_dragon and update_welllid's removal are all still exactly as shipped):
**MATCH 127 of 316** (BOTH-DIED 13, DIFF-DEATH 10, DIFF-LAND 48, DIFF-ROOM 20,
MISSING 68, PORT-EXTRA 8, PORT-STUCK 22) -- ties the task's own reference
exactly, i.e. no regression from T0133's actual trigger-relocation changes.

## T0153 -- the pass1/pass2 boot skew is FIXED AT SOURCE (and guarded)

Measured before: **782 low-memory symbols moved between the two assembly passes,
all by exactly -12**. Cause confirmed by hand-counting both branches of `start:`'s
STAGE_LZ if/else: the packed branch is 2x(ldu+ldy+jsr) = 20 bytes, the raw branch
2x(ldx+ldy+lda,x+/sta,y+/cmpx/bne) = 32. Difference 12, single cause.

Fix: `RELOC_BOOT_BYTES equ 32` and the short branch padded up to it, with `ifgt`/
`error` guards in BOTH branches so any future drift fails the build loudly instead
of silently re-skewing every low-memory address. TOOLCHAIN_SKEW_PAD is GONE.

After: 0 real low-memory symbols move (the 3 reported are a `-D` define, a label
inside the padded region, and the raw-vs-packed staged blob end). `low_resume` is
byte-identical across passes. Differential went 127 -> **129 MATCH**.

This closes the class that defeated T0148's staged code: staged blocks are frozen
from pass 1, so anything they reference had to be pass-invariant, and now is.

## T0155 -- tiecroc's failure is NOT the skew, and probably not the port

With the pad removed, every harness passes except tiecroc. The agent stopped
rather than re-pad, correctly: the cross-pass class is closed, so a pass-1-frozen
reference cannot be what breaks it.

**Session context the agent did not have:** tiecroc failed in EXACTLY this way
during T0137, and the cause was not the port at all -- the 4-column collision loop
cost enough cycles to shift the harness's inventory-key timing, and adding debug
counters made it pass again. The harness detects the inventory by scanning the
6809 stack for a return address in a PC range; both that and exits_port's `busy()`
(T0154) are unvalidated stack heuristics that move when code moves. T0133's "11
bytes fixes it, 10 does not" fits a heuristic tipping point, not a data bug --
and note it is 11, not the 12 the real skew turned out to be.

**So the first question is whether the rope tie still WORKS**, observed directly
(croc var1 == 255 and the rope consumed) rather than through the harness's staging
heuristics. If it does, this is a test bug and belongs with T0154.

## T0152 -- the ZX warp failure was a LIVELOCK caused by room 101

68 exit cases and 57 edge cases came back NEVER-ARRIVED. Root cause, diagnosed
against the real tape:

- The original computes transitions as plain `roomno +-1` / `+-16` with **no
  bounds check** (goneleft/goneright/goneup/gonedown -> `newroom: and 127`), but
  only rooms 0-100 exist.
- A warped case can cross two edges in one flight: `84 -> 100 -> 101`. Room 101
  is not a room.
- Poking `roomno=101` by hand is harmless. Letting the game's own
  `enterroom`/`roomsetup` run on it is not: the foreground loop's newroomno check
  ($A669, byte-identical before and after, so the CODE is not corrupted) is never
  reached again, even given 5000 frames. **A permanent livelock.** Every case
  after it warped into a dead machine -- which is why one mid-air case poisoned
  55 later room-84 cases.
- Real play never reaches it because level design puts a wall there. The fix is
  to BE that wall: cancel any transition landing outside 0-100 before enterroom
  sees it. One bounds check, uniform, no per-room table. The port already refuses
  the same transition (room_exists), so both sides now behave alike.

**NEVER-ARRIVED: exits 68 -> 1, edges 57 -> 1.** Case counts preserved.

**New reference numbers, measured over the full sets:**
- exits: **MATCH 164** of 316 (MISSING 1, DIFF-LAND 67, DIFF-ROOM 26,
  PORT-STUCK 26, PORT-EXTRA 11, DIFF-DEATH 8, BOTH-DIED 13)
- edges: **MATCH 531** of 763 (MISSING 1, DIFF-LAND 178, DIFF-ROOM 24,
  PORT-EXTRA 11, DIFF-DEATH 4, BOTH-DIED 14)

164 against the lost baseline's 166 is reassuring: the old merged capture and this
guarded one agree to within two cases, from completely separate captures.

The last two stragglers (`55r0` stuck in room 24, `50eL0` in room 23) are a
different cause, both near room 39's well -- the well_last/lastroom seeding this
file already flags. Left for T0156.

The game logic is provably correct: the rope's landing position (152,136) is

(600 ticks / 10 emulated seconds), so it is not the callback-rate problem T0037
documents -- same family, different mechanism, and the mechanism is NOT root-caused.

`TIECROC FAIL ... in_inventory=true`. Reverted, rebuilt, ran: PASS. Note the

Also fixed while in there: tiecroc's `select` stage was the only stage not gated

**Open, and worth watching:** if one harness is this sensitive to emulator flags,

## T0154 -- one state byte replaces a stack-scanning heuristic

exits_port.lua's `busy()` decided "a message box is up" by scanning 25 raw bytes
past the stack pointer for anything that looked like a return address into
msg_wait_dismiss. No frame validation, so any two adjacent bytes forming a
plausible value read as busy. When T0133 put debug_prox_keys into the mainloop's
call graph it false-positived every 4th frame and the harness LIVELOCKED -- which
is why the differential had to be run with DEBUG_PROX_KEYS=0 while the shipped
build had it 1. **Ship and test were different builds.**

Fix: `msg_active` (gameplay.asm) is set on entry to msg_wait_dismiss and cleared
when the dismissing press arrives. busy() reads that byte. The audio half stays a
PC range because play_tone BLOCKS -- a sample taken while it runs really is inside
it, no stack guessing needed.

**Result: with DEBUG_PROX_KEYS=1 (the shipped default) the full 316-case run now
completes and scores MATCH 164 -- identical to the reference measured with the
flag off.** gameover, tiecroc and dragonsleep unaffected.

Two harnesses used this stack-scan trick; tiecroc.lua's in_inventory() is the
other one and should move to `inv_occupied` the same way (T0157).

`CODE_DEST = BANNER_BUF-CODE_BUDGET` ($EAAE), delivered as a 308-raw/272-packed
"extra2" LZ payload through the title-hole mechanism and unpacked by `unpack_d`

**What made the difference:** T0153. The two earlier attempts failed because the

## Rooms 24 and 57 built -- and the REAL ceiling is the delivery path, not RAM

**Built:** 24 INSIDE THE CHURCH (387 raw) and 57 BASE OF TREE HOUSE (408 raw),
the two cheapest no-new-routine neighbours. ACTOR_COUNT 34->35, COIN_COUNT 11->13.
Sweep clean, actorlife still pass=4 fail=0 skip=1, whole suite passes, differential
**MATCH 164 -> 165** (cases that were PORT-STUCK into an unbuilt room can now land).

**CORRECTION TO THIS SESSION'S EARLIER ANALYSIS.** I wrote that ~13.3KB of room
data "fits" against 10686 bytes free above IMAGE_END. That free span is real but
it is NOT the binding constraint. Everything must ARRIVE through the load-time
staging path below $8000, and:

**The framebuffer staging windows and the title's load-time holes are the SAME
physical spare bytes, used at different moments of boot.** Redistributing rooms
between block A, block B and the title-hole block does not create capacity -- it
only moves which bucket reports the shortfall. Proved empirically: three different
distributions of the same 3 rooms all landed ~125 bytes short.

Measured delivery capacity before this task: A spare 720 + B spare 692 + hole
spare 968 = **2380 packed bytes**. A room costs ~400 packed. After building two:
A 438 + B 396 + holes 319 = **1153 packed bytes left, i.e. room for about two or
three more** -- while 9330 bytes of RAM sit unused above IMAGE_END.

So the remaining 29 content rooms need the DELIVERY path to change, not more RAM.
NOTES' own "Why a 64K machine is tighter" said this years ago: "That is a LOADING
constraint, not a memory one: CLOADM cannot write $8000+ before all-RAM is
engaged." T0159 is the task.

**Neighbours excluded and why:** 40 THE DRAGON'S LAIR (a SECOND dragon; the port
calls update_dragon from one hardcoded site for room 54) and 88 LIFT TO THE ELDERS
(update_lifts dispatches off a hardcoded room allowlist) both need dispatch work,
not new behaviour. 49 THE GUARD HOUSE needs a hawk, which is genuinely unported.
22 THE MARKET SQUARE and 72 DENZIL'S PAD are wired-ready but did not fit.

## T0159 -- the delivery budget, costed. Two corrections that change the plan

**Measured, at HEAD:** delivery budget = framebuffer-A spare 438 + framebuffer-B
spare 396 + title-hole spare 319 = **1153 packed bytes**.

**CORRECTION 1 -- a room costs ~614 packed budget bytes, not ~400.** Rooms 24+57
consumed 1227 budget bytes for 795 raw room bytes. Growing a room in block A or B
shrinks that framebuffer's spare AND its slice of the shared hole pool at the same
time, because they are the same physical bytes counted in two buckets. So the 29
remaining content rooms need roughly **17,800 packed budget bytes**, not ~11,600.

**CORRECTION 2 -- even a bigger delivery path may not be enough.** 17,800 more
packed bytes implies ~25-30KB more RAW resident data at the observed ~0.6-0.7 pack
ratio, against **9330 raw bytes free above IMAGE_END**. So finishing the game needs
BOTH a wider delivery path AND rooms that stay PACKED in RAM, unpacked per room on
entry. The mechanism already exists -- load_room does exactly that for collision
masks via CUR_ROOM_CMASK -- but applying it to whole rooms is unbuilt.

**Levers, measured (not estimated):**

| lever | packed gained | rooms | cost / risk |
|---|---|---|---|
| stronger packer | **~301 best case, likely 0 net** | <1 | the project's own bit-level LZ already BEATS xz and exomizer on the title (2666 vs 3220) and block D, and loses by only 1-3% on A/B. T0126 tuned it against exactly these competitors. Any generic format needs a second decoder resident in the same starved low memory -- almost certainly bigger than the gain. |
| drop the title screen | **+2666** | ~4.3 | the title art goes |
| drop title + music | **+3266** | ~5.3 | title and its music go |
| second load pass | potentially all of it | up to 29 | see unknowns below |

(Room counts here use the measured 614/room, not the old 400 estimate.)

**The second load pass -- what is actually known.** All-RAM toggling is proven
safe and round-trippable (T0041's own diagnostics). But four things are NOT
established, and **there is no CoCo2 technical documentation anywhere in
research/** -- the TRM quoted at T0041 was never on disk:
1. whether Color BASIC's ROM cassette read needs the IRQ this port disables at
   `start:` and never re-enables;
2. what fixed low-memory workspace that ROM routine uses -- this port already
   overwrites the RAM interrupt-vector table at $0100, a collision class it has
   hit before, so this is a live risk, not a theoretical one;
3. whether the tape auto-continues to a second file on the user's own setup;
4. where in boot a second pass must sit, since the windows are repurposed as real
   framebuffers/gap data once boot finishes.

**Also worth keeping:** memaudit.py's per-region "0 bytes free" lines on the
packed build are not real headroom for anything but gap2 -- mktitle packs flush to
each hole boundary by construction. The numbers that answer "does another room
fit" are the raw pass's A/B spare plus mktitle's hole spare. Same trap as T0148's
caveat and T0158.

|---|---|---|---|

**The lever that is already built:** T0148 proved gameplay code runs from block D

## T0158 -- memaudit now tells the truth, and the truth is not what we assumed

The per-region "N bytes free" lines were `region_end - highest_loaded_byte`, which
is wrong for any region mktitle back-filled: it packs each hole flush to its top
boundary, so the region reads full whatever the resident code does. memaudit now
parses mktitle's own `; hole at $ADDR: using N of M bytes` comments out of
title_lz.asm -- $ADDR is exactly the boundary between resident content and title
back-fill -- and reports resident_free, lent, and free_now separately, plus the
delivery budget as one number with its double-counting caveat and a rooms-remaining
estimate at the MEASURED 614 packed bytes/room.

Proved three ways without rebuilding: a synthetic image on the fallback path (50
resident bytes -> free drops exactly 50), the same delta injected on the
hole-adjusted path (gap2 319 -> 269, budget 1153 -> 1103), and a regression check
that overlap/overrun detection still fires.

**WHAT IT REVEALS, and it corrects an assumption behind T0148.** The low regions
are NOT full of code:

    low data      resident top $0c94   363 real spare, all lent to the title
    code + data   resident top $3653  2476 real spare, all lent to the title
    framebuffer A resident top $5649   438 lent
    gap1          resident top $5ed7   296 lent
    framebuffer B resident top $7673   396 lent
    gap2          resident top $7c5c   419 spare, 100 lent, 319 left

Total spare below $8000 is **4388 bytes**; the title+music+block C+block D consume
4069 of it. So "code+data has 0 bytes free", the premise for staging code upward,
was an artefact of the report. Code can still be ADDED below $8000 -- it simply
displaces title payload, which then has nowhere to go, because the pool is the
same 4388 bytes.

T0148 is still right and still worth having: moving code up frees its RAW size from
the pool while costing only its PACKED size back, a net gain of ~30%. But the
framing was wrong -- it is not "code has nowhere to live", it is "everything below
$8000 shares one 4388-byte pool with the title screen".

## T0141 -- exitcompare learns the two rules this project kept re-learning by hand

**FLAKY.** `exitcompare.py --port-runs a.log b.log c.log zx.log` parses each run
independently and compares a per-case signature (landing room/x/y/air, killed,
final room/x/y). Where runs of the SAME binary disagree, the case is reported
FLAKY with each run's outcome and **excluded from every other bucket** -- it can
no longer be counted as a MATCH from a lucky run or a regression from an unlucky
one. Single-log invocation is byte-for-byte unchanged, so every existing command
and every historical figure still works.

**SETTLED.** When `land=` differs but `final=`, room and death all agree exactly,
the case is an artefact of WHEN the harness sampled the landing, not a difference
in behaviour -- T0139 measured 18 of 20 such cases ending in identical positions.
It now gets its own silent-but-counted verdict. Equality for `final=` is EXACT,
deliberately not the 4px tolerance used for `land=`, so a real small discrepancy
cannot be laundered into the silent bucket.

Conservation proved on the committed edge baseline: old DIFF-LAND 173 = new
DIFF-LAND 164 + SETTLED 9. Nothing lost, nothing double-counted. Each
classification demonstrated on a fixture (`$S/t0141/`), including a case whose
runs disagree and one present on only one side.

**HISTORICAL FIGURES:** DIFF-LAND counts in older NOTES entries will come out
smaller if re-derived with this tool, because true sampling artefacts now move to

  PORT-EXTRA 12, DIFF-DEATH 9, BOTH-DIED 13, SETTLED 1)
- edges: **MATCH 602 of 882** (DIFF-LAND 209, DIFF-ROOM 22, PORT-STUCK 8,

## T0128 SOLVED -- the frame rate is paid to a linear scan of the WHOLE actor table

Bisected to a single commit, with zero measurement noise (three runs byte-identical):

    1a7397e  T0123 (room 50, armorog)              room 36 = 15.2
    9f6e62f  T0124 (rooms 56/71, lift, key 1)      room 36 = 13.8   <-- here
    0d55fa2  HEAD                                  room 36 = 14.2

Adjacent commits, so the drop is pinned exactly. Rooms 35/51/52/53 did not move.

**Cause: `build_solid_actors` scans ACTOR_COUNT slots EVERY PASS IN EVERY ROOM,
filtering by cur_room inside the loop.** T0124 took ACTOR_COUNT from 25 to 33
(--actor-rooms gained 56, 71 and 85), so every pass in every room walks 8 extra
slots for actors that are never present. Room 36 -- the start room, with the rat,
the troll, the portcullis and the most placements -- was already the tightest and
the extra iterations pushed it over a field boundary, costing a whole quantisation
step.

**Proved, not inferred:** on the unmodified T0124 commit, patching ONLY the loop
bound (`lda #ACTOR_COUNT` -> `lda #25`) restored room 36 to exactly 15.2 with the
lift jsr, the ROU_LIFT branch and the $7800 move all still in place. Reverted
immediately -- it is not a fix, it would silently drop rooms 56/71/85 from
collision.

**This cost GROWS WITH EVERY ROOM WE ADD.** ACTOR_COUNT is 35 now (rooms 24, 57
and 72 landed since), and it will keep rising. The routine's own header already
records that this loop cost room 36 "nearly a fifth of its frame rate" once
before, when it scanned per-probe instead of per-pass. The structural fix is a
per-room actor index built when the room loads, so the per-pass scan walks only
the actors actually in the room. That is T0161 and it should be done SOON, while
rooms are being added rather than after.

**Bisecting here again?** The worktree needs `research/D3-prior-art/original_source`
and `research/D3-prior-art/info` symlinked individually (not `research/` itself,
which is tracked), and `target/sound_data.asm` plus the `dizzy_frames*` files
copied in -- they are gitignored and no script regenerates them.

## TRIAGE of the 400 real differences -- three causes explain ~60%

Of ~440 non-MATCH cases, 12 are SETTLED and 27 BOTH-DIED (not mismatches by
design), leaving **400 real disagreements**. Clustered with the repo's own
exitcompare (imported, not reimplemented); verdict totals reproduce the committed
reference exactly, so the classification is trustworthy. Scripts in the
scratchpad's triage/ dir; commands quoted in the agent report.

**1. The 1px "feet sit lower" offset explains 186 cases (46% of the gap).**
Isolated subset -- final x EXACT, final y off by exactly 1px, nothing else
different: 21 of 78 exit DIFF-LANDs and 165 of 209 edge DIFF-LANDs. Spread across
19 rooms with no concentration, dominated by walk strategies rather than jumps.
That is the signature of a GLOBAL CONSTANT, not a per-room bug. These are
functionally MATCH cases that SETTLED does not catch because it requires exact
final equality.

**2. Lateral divergence is ALWAYS a multiple of 4.** 100% of nonzero final-x
deltas in both sets are exact multiples of 4, zero exceptions (78/78 and 209/209).
A clean confirmation of the 4px collision quantisation. The 65 DIFF-LAND cases
whose final y is neither +-1 nor a multiple of 4 are dominated by JUMP strategies
-- a 4px probe difference early in an arc changes when gravity stops accelerating,
so the resting y is an arbitrary sum. A consequence of mechanism 2, not a third one.

**3. Every single exit PORT-STUCK is a JUMP. 24 of 24.** 1 JUMP, 6 JUMPRIGHT,
17 JUMPLEFT, and ZERO walks. All 24 target rooms are already built, so none are
the "unbuilt neighbour" case. A walk never fails to register a boundary crossing;
only a jump does. Hypothesis (inferred from the pattern, NOT yet read out of the
transition code): the room-boundary test is gated behind the same floor check that
T0136 documents a jump as suppressing until its 8-step animation wraps, so an arc
that crosses the boundary mid-air never registers it. Affects 51>52/67 (8),
84>100 (4), 53>69 (3), 52>51 (2) and a scatter of others. **T0162.**

(The 8 EDGE PORT-STUCKs are the honest unbuilt case: all 8 are room 24 -> room 40,
which is not built. They vanish when room 40 is.)

**4. Room 39's well exit to room 23 is missing or misrouted: 31 cases (8%).**
9 of 23 exit DIFF-ROOMs plus ALL 22 edge DIFF-ROOMs. The original goes 39->23 from
a wide spread of x (32..144) and every strategy; the port goes 39->55 instead, or
sticks. Cases that correctly go 39->55 on both sides interleave at nearly identical
start positions, so it is not an x-band bug -- it looks like a real second bottom
exit the port resolves to the wrong neighbour. **T0163.**

**5. DIFF-DEATH is downstream, not a missing hazard.** The 13 death coordinates
cluster at y=67..80 in room 36 and match NEITHER its flame table (40,106 and
200,106) nor its water table (empty). y=67 is exactly T0137's corrected
`182-114` arrival row. These are landing-offset knock-ons: 1px or 4px puts a foot
on or off a solid pixel at the room-36 boundary.

**Reachable: 241 of 400 (60%) from three causes.** The honest remainder, ~159, is
a genuine long tail -- compounding jump-arc drift, 15 scattered misroutes, the
death knock-ons, and 23 PORT-EXTRA cases nobody has looked at yet.

## The 1px offset is a CONVENTION, proved from both sources -- 184 cases

**This is a measurement correction, NOT a fidelity improvement. The port did not
change. We were comparing two different conventions, like two lengths in
different units.**

**The mechanism, read out of both sources rather than inferred:**
- Port, room36.asm `check_ground`: "dizzy_y IS his feet row" -- it stores the
  FIRST SOLID row.
- Original, X-ALL.TXT `checkbottomside` (~6524): `looky` starts at y-3 while `y`
  starts at y-4, and both increment together, so solidity is tested at
  `looky = y+1` and `storedizy` keeps `y` unchanged. It stores the LAST CLEAR row.
- Therefore port_y = zx_y + 1 by construction, for every landing that goes
  through those paths. (T0065's note claimed exactly this; verified from the
  cursor arithmetic, 4-3=1, rather than trusted.)

**The falsification test it had to survive:** among cases the tool ALREADY scored
as MATCH, is the modal y-delta 0 or +1? If the port had no systematic offset it
would be 0. Measured: **+1 at 91.4% of exit MATCHes and 91.0% of edge MATCHes,
against ~1-2% at 0.** The no-offset hypothesis is what the data rules out.
Harness measurement was ruled out too: both harnesses read each engine's own
stored y with no arithmetic.

**Applied surgically, in the predicted direction only:** SETTLED now accepts
`port fy == zx fy` OR `port fy == zx fy + 1`. A blanket "subtract 1 from the port"
instead REGRESSES 20 cases that already agreed exactly at dy=0 -- paths that never
reach checkbottomside, such as screen-bottom clamps.

**Result, measured, matching the prediction exactly:**
- exits DIFF-LAND 78 -> 57 (21 moved), edges 209 -> 46 (163 moved) = **184**
- The 2 candidates whose delta runs the OTHER way (24eL25, 54eL6) are NOT
  explained by this mechanism and correctly stay in DIFF-LAND. T0164.

**Effective agreement (MATCH + SETTLED, both meaning "ends up in the same place"):**
- exits: 198 + 22 = **220 of 358 (61%)**
- edges: 602 + 174 = **776 of 882 (88%)**

**Stated limitation:** a genuine 1px-lower difference is now indistinguishable
from the convention. That is the price of not counting 184 unit-conversion
artefacts as failures, and it is the right trade -- but it is a real blind spot,
so record it rather than forget it.

adding troll_sample/flame_hazard before the existing dragon teleport made
dragon_settle fail "died settling into room 54" on every run, byte-for-byte
identical (same frame count) regardless of several wrong fixes tried first
(sticky sampling, waiting for killed==0, waiting for cur_room==36, forcing
dragon_asleep=1+dragon_swing=-8 as a belt-and-braces bypass -- all necessary
in retrospect but none sufficient alone). Root cause, found by logging PC
alongside state every tick: `mem:write_u8` pokes (warp()'s own mechanism)
land in RAM instantly regardless of what the CPU is doing, and gp_ud_respawn's
own trailing `jsr play_tune` ("new life" jingle) is a busy loop in play_tone
that can run for dozens of ticks -- a warp() fired while an EARLIER respawn's
tune is still busy-looping queues up invisibly, and by the time it's finally
noticed the SAME race can repeat for the fresh respawn's own tune, silently
stacking two unresolved death cycles that land Dizzy back on the identical
tile every time. Fix: gate the transition on `not in_audio()` too (the same
check the pre-existing teleport_* stages already use for exactly this reason)
before firing the next warp(). dragon_code.asm itself was never touched and
never at fault -- the dragon's own assertions (swing/breath) pass reliably
once arrival itself is clean.
