## T0193 — "a few steps after landing": not reproduced on clean geometry

Playtest: a diagonal jump makes Dizzy take a few steps after landing,
which the original does not do.

**The mechanism is real and is in the source.** `jumping` routes to
`cantstop` while `animation != 0`, and `cantstop` keeps applying the
LATCHED `left`/`right` -- which `checkkeys` cannot update, because
`bettercheckkeys` is only reached once `floor` is set AND the animation
has wrapped. So releasing the direction key mid-jump leaves Dizzy moving
until the 8-step animation reaches 0: **0 to 7 steps, up to 28px**,
depending purely on where the animation happens to be at touchdown. The
port implements this with `jump_on`/`jump_anim` (T0136).

**But measured on clean flat ground, the port and the original agree
exactly.** Room 36, jump LEFT from 120,170 with the key released at
take-off:

| | ORIGINAL | PORT |
|---|---|---|
| apex | 88,147 | 88,148 |
| landing | **56,175, stops** | **56,176, stops** |

Same 16 steps, same landing x, both stop dead. After landing the port
only alternates frames 0/1 -- the idle blink, not a walk cycle.

So the reported slide is NOT reproduced by "jump diagonally, release the
key". Needs the playtest's own position and direction (`-DDEBUG_XY=1`,
T0191) before guessing further -- that is exactly what cracked T0192
after four wrong reproductions.

**New tool:** `harness/jumptrace.lua` traces one jump pass-by-pass in the
port (room/x/y/dy/floor/jump_on/anim/keyflags/frame), the counterpart to
the ZX side's `ZXDBG=1`. It lived in /tmp for a session and was wiped
twice; it is a real tool and lives in `harness/` now. `RELEASE=1` lets go
of the direction once airborne, which is what the "steps after landing"
question actually needs.

### Divergence found while testing this (T0194)

Room 68 at x=200: the **port stands at y=172, the original at y=176**.
The port's step-climb finds a surface 4px up that the original does not
have, and the jump from there then bonks early (apex y=163 against the
original's y=148). Unrelated to the slide question but a real 4px floor
difference; filed separately.

## T0195/T0196 — "a few steps after landing" on a jump to a HIGHER surface

> **CORRECTION (T0236): the "ORIGINAL ... lands x=40, STOPS" reference below, and fault 3 (the T0196 clear of the jump lockout), are WRONG.**
> The ZX harness warp started the original 1 px inside the floor (y=176 instead of the settled 175), so that jump landed in phase.  From a settled
> start the original lands at x=48 and SLIDES 7 more steps to x=76 (jump frames the whole time).  The user chose the faithful slide: `LANDING_SLIDE equ 1`
> (target/room36.asm) no longer clears jump_on/jump_anim at landing.  Faults 1 (ml_bonk keeps dy) and 2 (fixed 20 px ceiling probe) stand.  See `## T0236`.

The playtest narrowed it: it only happens landing at a different height.
Room 68, jump RIGHT from the floor at x=20 onto the table (top y=148),
key released at take-off:

| | ORIGINAL | PORT (before) |
|---|---|---|
| landing | **x=40, STOPS** | x=48, then slides to **x=72** |

Three separate faults, in the order they bite:

**1. `ml_bonk` zeroed `dizzy_dy` (T0195).** X-ALL.TXT's `checktopside`,
when `checkline` blocks, falls to `updownback`, which is ONLY
`xor a / ld (floor),a` -- it clears `floor` and leaves `dy` ALONE.
Gravity walks dy back up and Dizzy glides along under the ceiling for
the rest of the arc. Zeroing it ended the jump on the bonking pass, so a
jump into a low ceiling landed ~32px early and spent the remaining
animation sliding along the ground.

**2. `check_ceiling` used `dizzy_h` (T0195).** The jump frames are
SHORTER (dizzy_frame_heights has 14s and 15s), so the head probe walked
DOWN mid-jump and Dizzy slipped up into ceilings the original is blocked
by. The source uses a fixed `sub 20` for every frame. T0187 measured this
as exactly neutral and shelved it -- correct at the time, because with
`ml_bonk` zeroing dy it could not matter how early the bonk fired. It
only pays once the arc survives the bonk.

**3. The key lockout outlived the jump (T0196).** `jumping` -> `cantstop`
holds the lockout until the 8-step animation wraps, REGARDLESS of floor.
In the original the arc and the animation are in phase -- the jump from
a floor to a 28px-higher surface is exactly 8 ticks (dy -7..0 = 28px), so
the animation wraps as Dizzy touches down and the lockout never outlives
the jump. Ours lands two steps late, at `anim=2`, so the lockout kept
control for six more steps with no key held -- and it plays a WALK cycle
(seq=2) while doing it, which is why it reads as "taking steps".
`ml_landed` now clears `jump_on`/`jump_anim`: a no-op for any jump that
lands in phase (every jump the original makes) and it removes the slide
from ours that do not.

After all three: port lands x=44 and stops, against the original's x=40.
One 4px step apart, from 32px apart.

**THE TRADE-OFF, and it is the user's call.** On the full 358-case
differential this package is net-NEGATIVE:

| | all | within | cross | mean | NEVER-ARRIVED |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| control | 267/350 | 48/48 | 75/84 | 27.7px | 8 |
| this | 263/348 | 46/46 | 74/86 | 28.2px | 10 |

It FIXES `84r4` outright (final error 120px -> 1px) and the reported
gameplay bug; it REGRESSES `67r1`, `68r0`, `68r2` (room paths) and
`67u3` was already wrong. My reading is that those three are other
divergences the early bonk was masking -- rooms 67/68 have a known floor
divergence (T0194) -- but that is a hypothesis, not a measurement.

Two detectors in `harness/denzilchat.lua` read `msg_active` and

## T0199 — the rope is NOT in the world until Denzil hands it over

Playtest question: "is the rope supposed to be there from the start, or
only after talking to Denzil?" **Only after.**

Two mechanisms in X-ALL.TXT, both of which this port was missing:

**1. `orig_room` is the starting room, not `room`.** `resetmoving` runs
right after the title screen and calls `reseteach` for every actor:
`ld a,(ix+origroom) / ld (ix+room),a`. `ropehere`'s record is
`defb 68,...` but its orig fields are `255,76,160,14` -- **orig_room
255**, so at game start the rope does not exist. We emitted the `room`
byte, so it sat in room 68 from the first frame, takeable without ever
meeting Denzil.

**2. A conversation's leading `defw` is an address to poke.**
`talkingtopeople1`:
```
ld a,(roomno) / ld e,(hl) / inc hl / ld d,(hl) / inc hl / ld (de),a
```
and `denziltalking defw ropehere+room` -- so Denzil materialises the rope
**in the room you talk to him in**, which is exactly what his last box
says he is doing.

Implemented: `tools/roompack` gained `ORIG_ROOM_LABELS` (currently just
`ropehere`) and emits `orig_room` for those; `give_rope` in actors.asm
pokes `cur_room` into the rope's slot when Denzil is talked to, gated by
`denzil_gave_rope` because this port has no `talkbefore` table and would
otherwise mint a second rope every time you talk after pocketing the
first. Verified at runtime: rope room=255 before, room=68 after.

**TEN MORE ACTORS HAVE orig_room=255 AND ARE STILL WRONG.** Deliberately
not switched, because their triggers are not implemented and emitting
orig_room would remove them from the world with no way to get them back
-- worse than having them early:

| actor | we place in | orig_room |
|---|---|---|
| shopkeeperhere, shopkeeperhere1 | 22 | 255 |
| beanhere | 22 | 255 |
| (unlabelled, frame 17) | 36 | 255 |
| (unlabelled, frame 5) | 60 | 255 |
| sleepingpotionhere | 45 | 255 |
| crowbarhere | 88 | 255 |
| carpethere, carpethere1 | 94 | 255 |
| daisy1here | 73 | 255 |

Six of those are in BUILT rooms, so six items/characters are currently
available from the start that the original gates behind an event. Add the
label to `ORIG_ROOM_LABELS` as each trigger lands.

## T0204 — the east wing blades: the hazard was parked 150px away

Playtest: "a horizontal row of blades at the bottom of a shaft... Dizzy
does not die, he can walk around in the blade row with no issues."

**Confirmed against the real game first.** Walking right from (8,127) in
room 69: the ORIGINAL sets `killed` at **x=12**; this port walked on to
x=32 and stood among the blades with `killed=0`.

**Cause: we used the LIVE actor fields, not the reset fields.** The
original's record is

```
defb 69,dagger, 78,136,169, ... , 69, 40,112, 169
                ^^^^^^^ live       ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ origroom,origx,origy,origfrm
```

and `resetmoving` copies orig_* -> live right after the title screen, so
**orig IS the game-start state**; the live fields are just wherever that
actor sat when the snapshot was taken. Orig is (40,112) in source units
= **(32,112) in pixels** -- inside the four frame-169 PLACEMENTS at
x=16..55, y=112 that draw the visible blades. We shipped (184,136),
parking the only hazard at the bottom of a shaft two-thirds of the room
away, so the blades were pure scenery.

This is the same class as T0199's `orig_room` and was found the same way:
the reset fields are the truth, the live fields are a snapshot.

same line now kills at x=24.

## T0206 — what the 23 missing rooms actually cost (measured, not guessed)

**23 content rooms remain** (101 slots, 49 empty, 52 real, 29 built).
Three of the 23 are fragments: room 0 is the title slot, rooms 1 and 3
have 12 and 2 placements.

**They are far cheaper than the historical average suggests.** The
per-room figure memaudit quotes (~614 packed bytes, from rooms 24+57) is
dominated by NEW SPRITE ART. The shared pool has since grown to cover
almost everything left:

| | |
|---|---|
| placements, 3 bytes x 1123 (T0167) | 3369 |
| **new sprites -- 20 of the 23 rooms need NONE** | **613** |
| per-room overhead ~16 x 23 | 368 |
| room-name strings 20 x 23 | 460 |
| **RAW TOTAL** | **4810** |
| packed at this build's own LZ ratio (~68%) | ~3270 |

Model validated against every built room -- 3 bytes/placement plus ~16
bytes overhead lands within a few bytes of the generated .asm:

| room | things | model | actual |
|---|---|---|---|
| 58 | 45 | 135 | 150 |
| 24 | 70 | 210 | 227 |
| 72 | 95 | 285 | 301 |

**Against the space:**
* delivery budget today = **1052 packed** -- about **a third** of the job.
* **one freed framebuffer = 6144 RESIDENT bytes**, and resident data needs
  no packing, so it compares against the RAW 4810: **all 23 rooms fit
  with 1334 bytes spare.**

So the remaining content is NOT blocked on art or on compression. It is
blocked on ~4.8KB of space, and dropping the second framebuffer yields
more than that on its own (T0207).

NOT counted here: per-room actor slots, and the code for behaviours those
rooms need (the six missing actor routines -- hawk, log, dozyfloat,
miner, daisy, switch1). Those are code, not room data.

## T0207 — can we drop the second framebuffer?

Asked directly: "can't we just focus on the area around Dizzy's path?"

The draw path ALREADY does that -- `redraw` builds a damage rect from
Dizzy's old and new positions and re-blits only the placements that
intersect it, "skipping the ~60 placements that didn't change". The
second buffer is not there to draw less; it is there to avoid tearing.

**What dropping it would buy:** a framebuffer can only hold TRANSIENT
load-staging data, because the display overwrites it. Freeing
`$6000-$77FF` turns 6144 bytes into PERMANENT RESIDENT space below
$8000 -- which is the scarce resource. That is more than the 4810 bytes
all remaining rooms need.

**What it costs:** the VDG scans the displayed buffer continuously, so
drawing into it is visible -- tearing or flicker on the damage rect.
Note the ORIGINAL is single-buffered and does exactly this
(`ruboutdizzy`/`printmoving` erase and redraw in place), so flicker here
is faithful, not a regression; the smoothness we have is something the
Spectrum never had.

**What is already in our favour:** single-buffered the damage rect gets
SMALLER -- today it is the union of Dizzy's position TWO redraws ago
(buffers alternate) and now; with one buffer it is just last frame and
this frame. And the mainloop already paces on vsync (`wait_vsync`,
`FRAME_PULSES`), so there is a natural point to draw from.

**What it would take:** `draw_base`, `cur_buf`, the per-buffer
`bufA_last_x`/`bufB_last_x` sentinels and the rat's save-under all assume
two buffers. Prototype behind `SINGLE_BUFFER=1` so the flicker can be
judged by eye before committing.

## Deriving the collision mask from the drawn art (asked 2026-09-25)

The original does this natively and we can import it two ways. Measured facts,
so neither gets re-derived:

- `dc_pass2_place` = `$1B7E`..`$1C74` = **246 bytes**, and is **~29 of the 42
  frames** of the room-load stall (2,571 ink nibbles in room 36). `dc_pass1_place`
  is 107 bytes / ~4 frames; `dc_load_placement` 58 bytes.
- `CUR_ROOM_CMASK` = 1536 bytes (8 bytes x 192 rows, 64 cells of 4px).
  `ATTR_CELLS` = 768 bytes (1 bit per 8x8 cell) and is REQUIRED by both variants
  below -- it is the Spectrum's attribute plane, which is what separates solid
  ink from decorative ink. `checkattri` is not optional in any scheme.
- Paint order per frame is: clear damage rect -> `redraw_placements_dmg` ->
  `draw_coins` -> `draw_flames` -> actors -> Dizzy. On room entry the damage rect
  is the full screen, so **there is exactly one moment per room load where the
  framebuffer holds room art and nothing else: immediately after
  `redraw_placements_dmg` returns, before `draw_coins`.** That is the scan point
  for variant A.

**Variant A (T0208): keep pass 1, replace pass 2 with a framebuffer scan.**
6144 FB bytes -> 1536 mask bytes, 4 source bytes per mask byte, ~110 cycles each
= ~169K cycles = ~11 frames. Room load 42 -> ~24 frames, ~170 bytes of code back.
Pass 1 stays because it only ever needed each placement's bounding box and its
DECORATIVE bit, never its ink.

A is NOT bit-identical to pass 2, and the difference is in the original's favour:
where a decorative placement inks a cell whose LAST writer was solid (so
`ATTR_CELLS` says solid), pass 2 drops that ink because it only rasterises
non-decorative placements, but the Spectrum's `checkline` finds it on screen and
`checkattri` calls it solid. **Live hypothesis: this is T0189, and the 11
`KNOWN_DEV` bytes in rooms 51/60/84.** Verify with `harness/cmaskverify.lua`
before assuming it.

**Variant B (T0209): no stored mask at all -- probe the framebuffer, as
`checkline` does.** Frees `CUR_ROOM_CMASK` (1536) + pass 2 (246) + most of
`derive_room_cmask` ~= **1.8KB**, which is ~13% of T0206's ~13.3KB for the 23
missing rooms. Per-probe cost 35 -> ~55 cycles (MUL by 32, nibble test,
`ATTR_CELLS` bit test); a handful of probes per frame, so negligible.
**Blocker**: the framebuffer also carries Dizzy, actors, coins and flames. Static
solid actors as FB ink is harmless or correct, but NON-solid actors (Denzil, the
rope) would become walkable floor -- their cells would have to be marked dull in
`ATTR_CELLS` every frame, turning it from per-load into per-frame state. B also
interacts with T0207: both assume something about which buffer is scanned, so
they must be designed together.

Do A first (contained, already has a byte-exact verifier). B behind a build flag
next to `SINGLE_BUFFER`. The second framebuffer is still the 6KB prize.

### T0209 design, grounded in the original (2026-09-25)

**The original's actual architecture, found in X-ALL.TXT -- read this before
touching the probe path.** `updatedizzy1`'s FIRST act is `call ruboutdizzy`
(X-ALL.TXT:6357), documented in PRTDIZZY-Z80-PDS-Neat.txt:156 as "Prints the
Temporary screen buffer, back onto the screen, rubbing out screen, with original
screen memory" -- i.e. it restores the art under Dizzy from a save-under buffer
BEFORE any physics runs. So `checkline` never sees Dizzy's own ink.

And `checkattri` does NOT read screen attribute memory during physics: the
Spectrum branch of `updatedizzy` (X-ALL.TXT:6348-6353) patches
`newattrihere1+1` to `attritable` (a shadow table) on the way in and back to
`screenattritable` ($5800) on the way out. **`ATTR_CELLS` is not a workaround for
the CoCo lacking an attribute plane -- it IS `attritable`, and the original reads
a shadow copy for exactly the same reason we do.**

**What this means for the port.** The port has NO save-under (`blit_revbuf` is 10
bytes, a reversed sprite ROW buffer for mirroring -- not `ruboutdizzy`). It erases
by clearing the damage rect and repainting room art. But it does not need a
save-under: `bufA_last_x/y` and `bufB_last_x/y` already record exactly where Dizzy
was drawn in each buffer, so the probe can EXCLUDE a rect instead of erasing it.
The same trick covers coins, flames and actors, falling through to the existing
tested `actor_solid_test` -- which means **ATTR_CELLS stays per-load and no draw
routine has to start painting attributes.** That was the expensive half of the
cost I first quoted; it is not needed.

Mechanics settled, all already in the file:
- `cur_buf` names the ON-SCREEN buffer, which at physics time is the most recently
  COMPLETED one -- probe that, and its Dizzy is at that buffer's own
  `buf?_last_x/y` (= the previous pass's dizzy_x/y).
- `fb_rowd` maps a logical row to a flip-aware address (`row -> FLIP_SUM-row` when
  `fb_flip`), so **T0125's upside-down world costs the probe NOTHING** -- reuse
  `fb_rowd` and the vertical mirror is handled. `fb_flip` is vertical only, so
  probe_x needs no adjustment. ATTR_CELLS is in LOGICAL coords (pass 1 builds it
  from placement y), so index it with the unflipped `probe_y>>3`.
- cell granularity: CMASK cell = 4px, FB byte = 8px. Test the nibble
  `probe_x & 4 ? $0f : $f0` against the byte at `fb_rowd(probe_y) + probe_x>>3`.

**Oracle check, offline (tools/derive_cmask.py gained `all_ink=`; the whole change
is dropping the `inherited & SOLID_DULL_BIT` skip, since the FRAMEBUFFER holds
decorative ink too and only the per-cell attr test can filter it).** Against the
current pass-2 mask over all 30 built rooms:

- DROPS 0 cells (structural -- adding ink cannot remove solidity). Good.
- ADDS 931 cells in 16 rooms. Every one is ATTACHED to already-solid scenery
  (220/220 in room 51, 155/158 in 23, 167/169 in 55) -- none floating, so they are
  thickening, not phantom walls.
- Of those 931, **819 are unreachable interior thickening and only 112 are NEW
  STANDABLE SURFACES**, in 9 rooms: 23(34) 51(12) 55(27) 56(13) 58(9) 60(6) 68(8)
  59(2) 87(1). Those 112 are the entire behavioural risk.

**CORRECTION to the previous NOTES entry: this is NOT T0189 and NOT the 11
KNOWN_DEV bytes.** I checked all 11 offsets directly -- the fbscan oracle leaves
every one of them byte-identical. T0189 is a separate, still-unexplained problem.
Do not re-derive that link; it was tested and it is false.

The 112 are being adjudicated against the real Spectrum by `harness/zxsolid.lua`
(reads ink at $4000 with the interleaved layout, BRIGHT bit 6 from $5800), with
348 agree-anyway control points as the validity check on the tool itself.
Probe set: `harness/probes/t0209_solidity.json`.

#### T0209's memory case is VOID -- measured, not argued (2026-09-25)

**`CUR_ROOM_CMASK equ TITLE_RAW_BUF`.** The mask does not occupy resident RAM at
all: it is overlaid on the TRANSIENT title buffer, alive only during a game, in
the same bytes the title screen's music mixer needs at boot. The numbers, from
`target/room36.map` and `target/title_frags.asm`:

```
TITLE_MUSIC_RAW    = 2898        the mixer blob
TITLE_RAW_LEN      = 3154        = TITLE_MUSIC_RAW + 256 (its DP page)  <-- sizes the region
TITLE_RAW_BUF      = $F2AE       region is $F2AE..$FF00
T0163_SCRATCH_END  = $FDC6       mask 1536 + attr 768 + sorted 512 + bands 24 = 2840
                                 -- 314 bytes SHORT of what the mixer already needs
```

The mixer sizes that region, so **deleting the 1536-byte mask frees 0 resident
bytes.** `BANNER_BUF`/`CODE_DEST` do not move, and the room-image ceiling does not
move. The file says this in as many words above `ATTR_CELLS_LEN` -- "RAM is not the
scarce resource here" -- and I quoted 1.8KB last turn without checking it.

So T0209's real ledger is: pass 2's 246 bytes of code, MINUS the probe path it
adds (`nc_probe_setup` + `nc_in_dizzy` + the probe body, ~110 bytes), so ~130
bytes, plus a per-probe cost, plus the 112-cell behaviour change. **T0208 (variant
A) keeps the same 246 bytes, pays only ~70 for a flat scan, also wins ~18 frames of
room-load stall, has no per-frame cost, and carries the SAME 112-cell change.**
A dominates B on every axis. Do A.

The remaining reason to want B is FIDELITY, not memory: it is the original's actual
architecture (see the design entry above). Kept behind `NO_CMASK`, default 0; a
default build is byte-identical to the T0204 build with the flag off, verified by
`cmp`. For the room budget, T0207's second framebuffer (6144 REAL resident bytes)
is still the only prize that matters.

#### T0209 status: fits, does not run yet. Two dead ends recorded. (2026-09-25)

**Where it stands.** `NO_CMASK=1` now assembles and FITS (`tools/stage_pack.sh`
gained `-DNO_CMASK=${NO_CMASK:-0}`). Measured payoff: the delivery budget goes
**1052 -> 1217 packed bytes, +165**, from deleting `dc_pass2_place`'s body (246)
minus the probe path it adds. That is the whole memory win; the 1536-byte mask
itself is free RAM (see the entry above). A default `NO_CMASK=0` build stays
byte-identical to T0204, verified by `cmp`.

**But it does not run.** `harness/jumptrace.lua` on the NO_CMASK binary prints
NOTHING, even with `NOFLOOR=1` forcing it live. The CONTROL -- the identical
invocation against the default build -- prints
`JT 36 108 176 dy0 floor=1 ...`, so the harness and the environment are fine and
the NO_CMASK build genuinely fails to reach a live state. Not yet diagnosed. The
probe path is `cmask_test`'s `ifne NO_CMASK` body plus `nc_probe_setup` /
`nc_in_dizzy`; start there, and suspect `nc_probe_setup` pointing `draw_base` at
the on-screen buffer for anything that draws OUTSIDE `redraw`.
Binary + map kept only in the session scratchpad, so rebuild with
`NO_CMASK=1 tools/stage_pack.sh`.

**DEAD END 1: screen-derived collision cannot recover the dc_patch cells.**
Rooms 51/84 have placements with a negative `pixel_x` that roompack DROPS from the
shipped table. The original clips and draws their visible sliver; this port's blit
cannot clip, so that ink is never on screen and NOTHING derived from the
framebuffer can find it. `dc_patch` is the hardcoded fix and it ORs into
CUR_ROOM_CMASK, which a NO_CMASK build does not consult -- so NO_CMASK LOSES those
cells (documented at the skip site). **T0208 inherits this and MUST keep dc_patch**,
which it can, since it still fills a real mask. This is a genuine advantage of A
over B, found only by building B.

**DEAD END 2: `harness/zxsolid.lua` cannot adjudicate the 112 cells. Do not
retry it as specified.** It warps the real Spectrum per room, dumps the
interleaved bitmap at $4000 and attributes at $5800, and scores the probe set. Its
CONTROL FAILS: `control_solid` came back **4/162 solid (2.5%)**, where ~100% is
required, uniformly spread over y=40..190, and it did not clean up across two
independent fixes (a real `dontupdatedizzy`/`enterroom` timing bug, then an 8px
vertical band). So its disputed tally (36 solid / 76 empty) is VOID -- do not cite
it. The fault is NOT in the probe set: all 460 probe points were checked against
the port's own verified `target/cmask_expected.bin` and agree **168/168, 180/180,
112/112**. So the probe coordinates are right in the port's frame and something in
the ZX-side sampling or the port-vs-original screen coordinate relationship is
wrong. Also: room 50 reports never-arrived, which is exits_zx.lua's own documented
T0156 warp dead end, not a new bug.

**Adjudicate the 112 cells with the EXISTING differential instead.** `exits_port`
vs `exits_zx` has committed baselines and is already trusted; a variant-A build
diverging from the ZX baseline in rooms 23/51/55/56/58/59/60/68/87 is exactly the
signal, and it needs no new tool. That is the cheap path and it should have been
the first choice.

**Process note for whoever reads the git log:** `harness/probes/t0209_zxtruth.json`
appears in commit 6eff732 only because `git add -A harness/probes` swept up a
BACKGROUND agent's in-progress output. That agent then found its own numbers in
git history and concluded an earlier session had already built the tool. It had
not. Do not `git add` a directory a background agent is writing into.

### T0208 implemented, and BLOCKED by an unclippable blit -- with the diagnosis (2026-09-25)

`FB_CMASK=1` (`tools/stage_pack.sh` passes `-DFB_CMASK`) replaces
`dc_pass2_place` with `scan_fb_cmask`: a flat scan of the freshly painted room
art, called from `redraw` immediately after `redraw_placements_dmg` and before
`draw_coins`, which on a room entry is the one moment the buffer holds room art
and nothing else. Pass 1 and `dc_patch` both stay. Unrolled x4 so each source
byte's two mask bits are constants; rows walked through `fb_rowd` so T0125's
flipped world needs no code. Measured: delivery budget **1052 -> 1144, +92
packed bytes** (less than NO_CMASK's +165 -- the unrolled scan is bigger than
estimated). Default `FB_CMASK=0` build stays byte-identical to T0204 (`cmp`).

**Verified byte-exact against its OWN reference and it FAILS: 12 PASS, 15 FAIL,
2 SKIP over 29 rooms.** (`tools/derive_cmask.py --dump-fbscan
target/cmask_fbscan.bin`, then `CMASK_EXPECTED=target/cmask_fbscan.bin
harness/cmaskverify.lua`. That reference differs from `cmask_expected.bin` by
exactly +931/-0 cells, confirming the two derivations are the ones intended.)

**Every failing byte is at mask col-byte 0 or 1 -- the leftmost 8-24 pixels.**
Both directions are now explained, and each matches its room set exactly:

1. **"scan MISSING" -- rooms 23, 51, 55, 56, 58 (5 of 5).** These are precisely
   the rooms with negative-`pixel_x` placements. roompack DROPS them from the
   shipped table because the blit cannot clip, so they are never DRAWN, so their
   ink is not in the framebuffer and no scan can find it. The original clips and
   draws their visible sliver, so the original DOES collide there. This is
   `dc_patch`'s problem, and `dc_patch` covers only rooms 51/84 -- five more
   rooms need it.
2. **"scan has EXTRA" -- rooms 22, 50, 54, 59 (4 of 4).** These are precisely
   rooms with a placement whose ink runs PAST x=255 (e.g. room 54: x=204 w=80 ->
   ends 284). The blit has a vertical clip (`blit_ybot`, `win_top`) but **no
   horizontal one**, so the overrun wraps onto the NEXT ROW'S LEFT EDGE. The
   placement data correctly stops at the edge; the framebuffer actually contains
   the wrapped ink, and a scan faithfully picks it up as phantom solid cells.
3. Rooms 24, 35, 67, 68, 69 differ only at rows 32-47, ABOVE the play window
   (`windowtop=48`), so those are never probed -- almost certainly harmless, but
   the byte lists are truncated to 8 per room so this is not yet proven.

**This is a REAL VISUAL BUG, not just a mask problem.** Eight rooms -- 22, 50,
51, 54, 57, 59, 67, 68 -- have placements overrunning x=255, and with no
horizontal clip in `blit` their ink wraps to the left edge of the next row. That
is stray pixels on screen in the shipping build, independent of any mask work,
and it is playtest-visible. Filed separately. **Fix that first: it is worth
fixing on its own merits, and T0208 cannot be correct until the framebuffer is a
faithful picture of the room.**

Order of work, revised: horizontal blit clip -> generalise `dc_patch` to all
seven negative-`pixel_x` rooms -> then T0208's scan can match. Until then
`FB_CMASK` stays 0.

### T0207 part 1: SINGLE_BUFFER display works (2026-09-26)

`SINGLE_BUFFER=1` (`tools/stage_pack.sh` passes `-DSINGLE_BUFFER`) makes $4000 the
only page and never flips away from it. Four sites, all guarded:

- `redraw`'s head: `draw_base` is always BUFA, history always `bufA_last_x/y`.
- `redraw`'s tail: the `sta $ffce`/`sta $ffcf` F4 flip is gone; `cur_buf` stays 0,
  so everything that READS it still works -- `msg_begin` picks BUFA, and
  `rat_sv_slot` is guarded to pick `rat_sv_hdr_a` (it keyed off `cur_buf` meaning
  "the buffer being drawn INTO", which inverts when there is only one).
- `draw_base`'s initial value.

Precedent for the approach is already in the file: `msg_begin`'s comment notes
message boxes are painted straight onto the live page because "the Spectrum
original does too (it has no page flipping at all)".

**Runs correctly.** `harness/jumptrace.lua` on room 36 gives
`JT 36 108 176 dy0 floor=1 ... seq=0`, matching the default build's control
exactly except `ff` (animation phase) differing by one pass. Default
`SINGLE_BUFFER=0` build stays byte-identical to T0204 (`cmp`).

**The 6144 bytes are NOT reclaimed yet -- that is part 2.** The delivery budget
moved only 1052 -> 1114 (+62), purely from the deleted flip code. memaudit still
lists $6000-$77ff as "framebuffer B / $8000 staging block 2", because that region
is ALSO the boot-time staging area for packed room data. Reclaiming it as
resident room storage means giving room data a second destination region at
$6000 (room_desc_table already holds pointers, so multiple regions are fine) --
and the win is that resident data needs no packing, so it competes against the
RAW 4810 bytes, not the packed ~3270.

**Do not build part 2 until the tearing is judged acceptable in a playtest.** If
it is not, part 2 is wasted work. That judgement is the user's, not a harness's.

### T0211 FIXED and verified: blit had no horizontal clip (2026-09-26)

`blit` clipped vertically (`blit_ybot`, `win_top`/`movestartdown`) but **not
horizontally**, and the framebuffer is one flat 32-byte-per-row span -- so "past
column 31" and "the left edge of the row below" are THE SAME ADDRESS. Any sprite
overrunning the right edge wrote its tail into the next row's first bytes.

Eight rooms have an overrunning placement: **22, 50, 51, 54, 57, 59, 67, 68**
(worst is room 54, x=204 with an 80px sprite ending at 284). All eight have had
stray wrapped pixels down their left edge for as long as they have existed.

`HCLIP=1` adds the clip, in `blit_topok` right after `blit_col`:
`avail = FBWIDTH - blit_col`, minus one more when `blit_shift` is set (the
shifted path's spill `sta ,x` writes at X+bpr WITHOUT advancing X, so it touches
bpr+1 dest bytes). `blit_eff` is the clipped width the two row loops use;
`blit_srcskip` is added to U at each row end so the source still lands on the
next row. The mirrored path is deliberately left on the unclamped `blit_bpr` --
`blit_mkrev` must reverse the FULL row and revbuf always holds a full row; only
the DEST write is clipped.

**Verified by the tool that found the bug** (`FB_CMASK=1`, mask derived from the
screen, diffed against `target/cmask_fbscan.bin`): rooms **22, 50 and 54 went
FAIL -> PASS**, and overall 12 PASS/15 FAIL -> **15 PASS/12 FAIL**. Room 59's
failure changed character, from extra ink at col-byte 0 to ONE missing bit at
col-byte 7 -- the documented 4px loss when a shifted sprite sits at the extreme
right edge. Rooms 23/51/55 still fail with MISSING ink at col-byte 0: that is
T0212's negative-`pixel_x` problem, untouched by this and unrelated.

**Two landmines, both cost a build:**
1. The first version put `lbls blit_offscreen` after `tst blit_shift`/`deca` and
   branched on THOSE flags. `bls` also tests Z, which `tst blit_shift` sets
   whenever shift==0 -- so **every aligned blit early-outed and nothing drew at
   all.** Test A itself (`tsta`/`lbeq`). A cannot go negative: `blit_col` is a
   byte's x>>3, so at most 31.
2. **The clip does not fit a default build** -- it needs ~53 bytes more than the
   title's load-time holes allow, and the build fails with "title is 4998 bytes
   packed but only 4945 bytes of load-time holes exist". Hence `HCLIP`, default
   0, which is a verified no-op (default budget back to exactly 1052 packed
   bytes, jumptrace control unchanged). `SINGLE_BUFFER=1` frees +62, and
   `SINGLE_BUFFER=1 HCLIP=1` builds with 7 bytes of title-hole spare.

So this fix currently ships only together with T0207, or once ~53 bytes are found
elsewhere. It is NOT a reason to accept single-buffering -- it is a reason to find
53 bytes if single-buffering is rejected.

#### play.sh REBUILDS by default -- it will overwrite an experimental binary (2026-09-26)

`./play.sh` is "build + run"; `./play.sh --no-build` runs `target/room36.bin`
as-is. A playtest of a flag-built binary (SINGLE_BUFFER, HCLIP, FB_CMASK,
NO_CMASK, DEBUG_XY) **must** use `--no-build`, or stage_pack.sh re-runs with
default flags and the thing under test silently disappears.

This already cost one playtest: a `SINGLE_BUFFER=1 HCLIP=1` binary was left in
`target/` for a tearing judgement, `./play.sh` rebuilt it to plain defaults, and
the session came back with a verdict on the DEFAULT build. Check
`grep -iE "^Symbol: (SINGLE_BUFFER|HCLIP)" target/room36.map` to see what a
binary actually has in it -- the flags are in the map.

Corollary worth keeping: the "occasional glitches in certain areas, nothing too
distracting" reported from that default-build playtest are most likely T0211's
wrapped left-edge ink (HCLIP was 0), which is per-room in exactly 8 rooms --
consistent with "certain areas". Not yet confirmed against an HCLIP=1 build.

### T0207 REJECTED by playtest: single-buffering flickers unacceptably (2026-09-26)

A `SINGLE_BUFFER=1 HCLIP=1` build, played on the user's own emulator:
**"everything is flickering like crazy."** Verdict is final -- the tearing is not
in the same category as the mild per-room artefacts they had already accepted in
the default build ("occasional glitches... matching the games of the era").

**So the 6144 bytes of framebuffer B are OFF THE TABLE, and part 2 was never
built.** Do not re-propose single-buffering as the way to fit the remaining rooms;
it has been tried, implemented, and judged. The code stays behind
`SINGLE_BUFFER` (default 0) as a working reference, not as a plan.

Why it flickers worse than the Spectrum, which also has no page flip: the
original erases only what it must, from a save-under (`ruboutdizzy`), whereas
this port clears a damage RECT and repaints the room art under it every frame,
and on room entry clears the WHOLE screen. With no off-screen buffer that clear
is visible. Making single-buffering tolerable would mean adopting the original's
save-under erase, which is a much larger change than dropping the flip -- and it
would then compete for the very bytes it was meant to free.

**Consequence for the room budget.** Every lever examined this session is now
closed or tiny:
- mask RAM: 0 bytes (overlaid on the transient title buffer, mixer-sized).
- mask cropping: 0 bytes (lands in that same free region).
- map re-encoding: ~600 raw bytes at best, and competes with the LZ already
  applied; moot at 3 bytes/placement if resident space ever appears.
- framebuffer B: 6144 bytes, REJECTED on flicker.
- T0208/T0209: +92 / +165 packed bytes, and T0208 is blocked on T0211+T0212.

The 23 rooms need ~4810 raw / ~3270 packed against a 1052-packed budget. Nothing
found this session closes that gap. The next honest step is NOT another
compression idea -- it is to re-derive where the remaining ~15.5KB of the old
"fits in 64K" estimate was supposed to come from, because framebuffer B was the
largest single item in it and it is now gone.

### T0214: per-buffer draw caches were never invalidated (2026-09-26)

Playtest: *"when the game resets not everything on the rooms resets, like the fire
on the first room, there is some sort of bug there"*, plus *"odd flickers and
eventually crashes after restarting from a game over"*.

**Cause.** `draw_flames` and `draw_fire` each keep a PER-BUFFER record of the
animation variant they last drew (`flame_var_a/b`, `fire_var_a/b`, all `fcb 255`
= "never drawn in this buffer"), and skip their clear+blit when the current
variant matches it. That is a 41%-of-frame-budget optimisation (T0064) and it is
correct *as long as the record is dropped whenever the buffer is repainted*. It
never was: the only writes to those four bytes are `draw_flames`/`draw_fire`'s own
cache updates. So after any full repaint -- a new game, a game-over restart, a
room change -- the record claims "already drawn" about a screen that was just
wiped, and the flames are never drawn onto it.

Room 36 has two torch flames (`r36_room_flame_count fcb 2`), which is the "fire on
the first room".

**Fix.** Four stores appended to `rat_sv_invalidate`, which already exists for
EXACTLY this reason ("after a full-screen repaint the saved bytes describe a
screen that no longer exists, so drop them") and is already called from `redraw`
on precisely the full-repaint path (`old_dizzy_x == 255`). So every existing
"force a full redraw" site -- and there are ~20 of them -- is covered by one
change, with no new call site. `flame_var_a/b` ($2272/3) and `fire_var_a/b`
($2274/5) are four ADJACENT bytes, so two 16-bit stores cover all four: 9 bytes.

**Verified no regression:** `harness/actorlife.lua` gives pass=5 fail=1 skip=1
both with and without the change, the FAIL being `flame_hazard killed never
observed set -- room=36`, which the CONTROL (committed build, rebuilt and re-run)
fails identically. **That failure is PRE-EXISTING, not from this change** -- and
NOTES' own T0151 entry records the assertion passing when it was written, so
something regressed it earlier. Filed; it also bears on the flame-death report
below.

**Still broken, blocked on SPACE, not on understanding:**
- `rat_lastx_a/b` ($227e/f) and `gate_last_a/b` ($30a0/1) have the IDENTICAL
  flaw and are the leading remaining suspects for the flicker and the crash. 6
  more bytes.
- `denzil_gave_rope` (T0199's one-shot) is not reset by `gameplay_init`, so
  Denzil has already handed over the rope in a fresh game -- exactly the class
  that routine's own T0114 comment says belongs there. 3 bytes.
- The hazard death messages (below). ~160 bytes.

**The port is full.** Title-hole spare after this 9-byte fix is **2 bytes**. A
first attempt put the invalidation in a new staged routine on the theory that the
staged block's 30 free bytes were cheaper -- they are NOT: the staged block is
packed into the same image and grows it, so that version came out 10 bytes over.
Resident and staged code compete for the same space. **T0213 (find ~53 bytes) now
gates T0211, T0215 and T0216 alike, and is the highest-value task in the port.**

### Hazard death messages: mechanism exists, texts exist, only the wiring is missing

`kill_dizzy_msg` already takes X = a hazard message stream and `update_death`
already prints it inside `deadwindow`'s box; the crocodile, portcullis, armorog,
lift and dragon all pass one. Three call sites pass NOTHING, all in
`rat_troll_hazard_code.asm`: the rat (lines ~146 and ~196) and the SHARED
`hazard_scan` (~365) that `update_flame_hazard`/`update_water_hazard`/
`update_fire_hazard` all fall through into. Hence the playtest's *"just says I
lost a life"*.

The original's own texts and mapping (X-ALL.TXT ~990-1045, and the `ld hl,...`
sites at 2224/2228/2257/3319):
- flames -> `killedbyflame` [X-ALL.TXT line 1019] / [X-ALL.TXT line 1020]
- water  -> `killedbywater` [X-ALL.TXT line 1023] / [X-ALL.TXT line 1024], **except
  room 77, where `updatewaterlp` uses `killedbyvolcano`** ("[X-ALL.TXT line 1042]:[X-ALL.TXT line 1043]") -- `ld a,(roomno) / cp 77 / jr z,yesfellinlava`.
- rat    -> `ratgotyoumess` [X-ALL.TXT line 1036] / [X-ALL.TXT line 1037] / [X-ALL.TXT line 1038]

Since the three hazard entries share one `hazard_scan`, each entry must latch its
own message pointer for the shared tail to pass on. Needs ~160 bytes for the
streams; blocked on T0213.

## Where the compressible bytes actually are (measured 2026-09-26)

Prompted by: *"bitmaps like those are very inefficient, there has to be some light
compression we can make to save some space."* Right instinct, and the measurement
puts it somewhere specific -- but NOT on the mask or the map, neither of which is
a stored bitmap:

- **The mask is not stored at all.** T0166 removed it; `load_room` derives it into
  RAM, and that buffer costs 0 resident bytes (overlaid on the transient title
  buffer). Nothing to compress.
- **The map is already a vector format**, not a bitmap: 3 bytes per placement
  (frame index, x, y). Room 36's entire layout is 61 placements = 183 bytes. The
  equivalent 4px-granular bitmap would be 1536. The map is already ~8x better than
  the bitmap it replaces.

**Resident data, by size:** Dizzy frames 4846, shared scenery sprites 4243, room
layouts (all 30) 5526, actor data 2664, messages 1622, font 689, frame table 166.
So the real bitmap payload is the **~9KB of sprite art**.

**Three random-access "light compression" ideas, all measured on the scenery pool
(85 sprites, 3988 bytes) and all LOSING:**
1. byte-identical duplicate sprites: **0 bytes**. roompack's `--shared-sprites`
   pool already dedupes across rooms -- that is its whole purpose. And T0142
   already mirrors at runtime instead of storing flipped copies.
2. all-zero leading/trailing rows: **32 bytes**.
3. a shared ROW POOL: 1531 rows -> 1120 unique. 3196 bytes of rows + 1531 index
   bytes = 4727 against 3988 now, i.e. **739 bytes WORSE**, before paying an
   indirection per row inside `blit`. Dithered 1bpp art is high-entropy; the
   redundancy is not there.

**What DOES pay, measured with tools/roompack/target/release/lzpack:**

| resident-raw blob | raw | packed | saves |
|---|---|---|---|
| Dizzy frames (mask+sprite) | 4650 | **1817 (39%)** | **2833** |
| shared scenery sprites | 3988 | 3191 (80%) | 797 |
| font | 424 | 327 (77%) | 97 |

The frame set hits 39% because each of the 39 frames stores a MASK beside its
bitmap (`screen = (screen AND mask) XOR sprite`, the original's own compositing)
and the masks are long runs of $ff/$00. The scenery sprites only reach 80% for the
same high-entropy reason as idea 3.

**The leverage: those blobs live in gap1, the RESIDENT area, so they ship RAW
today** -- unlike the staged room blocks, which are already LZ-packed. Packing
them and unpacking once at boot frees ~2833 (or ~3727 with all three) bytes of
DELIVERY budget, against a current budget of 1052 packed and a title-hole spare of
2 bytes. The mechanism already exists and runs three times at boot: `lz_unpack`
(title), `unpack_c` (rooms 39/23), `unpack_d` (dragon code). Filed as **T0218**.

**It is a DELIVERY saving, not a RAM saving** -- the frames occupy the same bytes
once unpacked, so this changes nothing about the mask/map arithmetic above. But
delivery is the binding constraint: it is what blocks T0211 (53 bytes), T0215 (9),
T0216 (~160) and the 23 rooms (~3270 packed). This is the first lever found since
the framebuffer was rejected that is big enough to matter.

### Every resident-raw blob, packed and measured (2026-09-26)

Asked before starting T0218: is anywhere else worth compressing? Only the two
`$8000` staging blocks are LZ-packed today; everything in "low data", "gap1" and
"gap2" (memaudit's own region names) ships RAW. Only room36 and room35 are
resident rooms -- the other 28 are already inside the packed staged blocks.

Measured with `tools/roompack/target/release/lzpack` on the real bytes, with
`fdb` symbol references resolved through `room36.map`:

| blob | raw | packed | ratio | saves |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Dizzy frames (mask+sprite) | 4806 | 1976 | 41% | **2830** |
| shared scenery sprites | 4243 | 3402 | 80% | 841 |
| actor data | 2664 | 2077 | 77% | 587 |
| sound data | 1253 | 710 | 56% | 543 |
| messages (approximate) | 1489 | 970 | 65% | ~519 |
| font | 689 | 459 | 66% | 230 |
| resident rooms 36/35 | 393 | 354 | 90% | 39 |
| frame table | 166 | 171 | **103%** | **-5** |
| | | | | **~5589** |

**MEASUREMENT TRAP, recorded so nobody repeats it.** A first pass wrote every
`fdb` as two ZERO bytes (its symbol operands did not parse), which compresses to
almost nothing and produced two fictions: the frame table at "3%, saves 160" and
sound data at "24%, saves 947". Resolved against the map they are 103% (it GROWS
by 5 -- a pointer index is high-entropy addresses, there is nothing in it) and 56%
/ 543. Any blob whose content is mostly `fdb` must have its symbols resolved
before its ratio means anything. `messages` still carries 133 unresolved tokens
(the streams use `mpen+5`/`mxy+2` expressions) so its 519 is approximate.

**Scope guidance for T0218.** Do the Dizzy frames first: one blob, the biggest
win, and cleanly measured. Then scenery (841), actor data (587), sound (543).
Skip the frame table (negative) and the resident rooms (39 bytes, below the
per-blob overhead). Each packed blob costs its own unpack call plus a safe landing
area for the packed bytes at load time, ~10-20 bytes of code, so a blob under
~100 bytes of saving does not pay for itself.

Watch the boot ORDER: the font and the sound data may be wanted during the title
sequence, which already runs `lz_unpack` for its own image plus `unpack_c` and
`unpack_d`. Unpacking has to happen before the first user, and the packed source
must not sit where an earlier unpack lands.

Still DELIVERY bytes, not RAM -- see the entry above.

#### CORRECTION: T0218 was aimed at the wrong blob (2026-09-26)

The table above measured each blob's compressibility but never asked WHERE it
ships. With the address test (`< $8000` = resident/raw, `>= $8000` = inside the
already-LZ-packed staged image), most of it is already compressed:

| blob | ships RAW | already packed |
|---|---|---|
| Dizzy frames | **~658 of 4650** | 4188 |
| scenery sprites | 0 | 4243 |
| actor data | ~344 | 2320 |
| frame table (`frame_table` = $8F6B) | 0 | 166 |
| **sound data** (`tune1_notes` = $22FF) | **1253, all of it** | 0 |
| **messages** (`msg_croceaten` = $02B1) | **~1489, all of it** | 0 |
| **font** | **689, all of it** | 0 |
| resident rooms 36/35 | 393 | 0 |

**So the Dizzy frame set is already ~90% packed** -- memaudit's "gap1 (dizzy
TAIL...)" was the clue and I read past it. The claimed 2830-byte win does not
exist; the raw portion is ~658 bytes.

**The real targets, all entirely raw, measurements valid as taken:**
- sound data 1253 -> 710, **saves 543**
- messages ~1489 -> 970, **saves ~519** (approximate: 133 `mpen+5`/`mxy+2`
  expression tokens did not resolve)
- font 689 -> 459, **saves 230**
- ~1290 together, plus ~200 from the frames' raw tail and 39 from rooms 36/35.

~1290 against a 2-byte title-hole spare comfortably unblocks T0211 (53), T0215 (9)
and T0216 (~160). It does **not** reach the 23 rooms' ~3270 packed.

**This is the THIRD time this session that "where does it actually live" overturned
a claim made from a size** -- after the collision mask (0 resident bytes, overlaid
on the transient title buffer) and mask cropping (lands in that same free region).
The recipe `factory/recipes/compress-the-load-file-never-the-runtime-data-
structures.md` already carries the precondition; the miss here was not applying it
to my own new measurement. **Before quoting any compression win, split the blob by
address against $8000 first.**

### T0219 + T0215 + T0211 landed: dead code funded two verified fixes (2026-09-26)

**T0219 (new): deleted 138 bytes of provably dead resident code.** A column-0
label scan across every `target/*.asm` found exactly five labels appearing only at
their own definition; three were real:

| removed | bytes |
|---|---|
| `inv_has` ($2D92..$2DBE) | 45 |
| `inv_remove` ($2DBF..$2E13) | 85 |
| `msg_inv_nothing` | 8 |
| `ih_want`/`ih_n`/`ir_want`/`ir_slot` | 4 |

`inv_remove`'s own comment said "used once the jug/apple are consumed by their
puzzles" -- that never landed. Both are in git if a future item puzzle wants them.
**Title-hole spare went 2 -> 145 bytes**, which is what paid for the next two.
Worth remembering as a technique: a full-port dead-label scan is cheap, exact, and
zero-risk compared with restructuring the delivery path, and it should be the FIRST
place to look for bytes, before anything involving `mktitle` or a new staged block.

**T0215: the other two per-buffer draw caches** (`rat_lastx_a/b`,
`gate_last_a/b`), invalidated alongside T0214's stores in `rat_sv_invalidate`, 7
bytes. Plus `clr denzil_gave_rope` in `gameplay_init`, so a brand new game no
longer starts with Denzil's rope already handed over. These were the leading
suspects for the playtest's "odd flickers and eventually crashes after restarting
from a game over" -- needs a playtest to confirm, since no harness reproduces a
game-over restart.

**T0211: `HCLIP` is now ON by default**, 68 bytes. **GOTCHA: flipping the
`ifndef HCLIP` default in room36.asm did NOTHING** -- `tools/stage_pack.sh` passes
`-DHCLIP=${HCLIP:-0}` on the command line, which overrides an `ifndef`. The
build-script default has to change too. The map is the check:
`grep -iE "^Symbol: HCLIP " target/room36.map`.

Verified: `jumptrace` room 36 `floor=1` at y=176, and `actorlife` pass=5 fail=1
skip=1 -- byte for byte the control's result, same single pre-existing
`flame_hazard` failure (T0217). `blit` is app-wide, which is why actorlife ran here
rather than a scoped check.

Title-hole spare now **70 bytes**. T0216's full message set (~160) still needs
T0218b, but the FLAME message alone (~55 with its latch) fits.

### T0216 + T0217 (2026-09-26)

**T0216 (partial): the flame death line is wired.** `msg_killedbyflame` added to
gap_messages.asm, X-ALL.TXT line 1019 byte-for-byte ([X-ALL.TXT line 1019] /
[X-ALL.TXT line 1020]). The three hazard entries share one `hazard_scan`, so each now
latches a `haz_msg` pointer for the shared tail to hand to `kill_dizzy_msg` --
which is exactly how the original does it (`ld hl,killedbyflame` before
`killdizzy1`). flame and fire both use `killedbyflame`; **water still passes 0**
because `killedbywater` plus the room-77 `killedbyvolcano` special case needs ~70
more bytes. Safe at the kill site: `uf_loop` reloads X from `uf_ptr` every
iteration, so clobbering X there costs nothing. Cost 44 bytes; spare 70 -> 26.

**T0216 also found the SECOND cause of "the fire on the first room" -- `fireout`
was never reset.** `proxjugrou` sets it when the jug douses room 36's fire pit and
nothing ever cleared it, so a brand new game began with the fire already out, both
visually (`draw_fire_overlay`) and as a hazard (`update_fire_hazard` gates on it).
`clr fireout` added to `gameplay_init`. T0214's draw-cache fix was a genuinely
different symptom of the same report.

**T0217: the harness assertion cannot pass, and the game is innocent. Do not
"fix" this in the port.** Measured, not guessed:

1. **Pinning Dizzy does not hold.** The main loop runs his physics BEFORE
   `update_flame_hazard` in the same pass, and `ml_downlp` recomputes
   `dizzy_floor` from the collision mask every pass -- so he is dropped to room
   36's floor (y=176) before the hazard box is tested. Pinning `dizzy_dy` AND
   `dizzy_floor` too does not help: the physics overwrites the flag. A debug print
   read x=44 y=110 floor=1 on every sample purely because the poke had just
   landed; the game had already moved him. There is no `dontupdatedizzy` to poke
   -- this port implements that as a `lbra` past the rest of the pass (T0192).
2. **Even pinned, the premise is wrong.** Room 36's torches are at y=106 with a
   13px box (106..119); the floor is y=176, so a standing Dizzy's head is
   176-15=161, about 42px BELOW the box. Those torches are wall decoration he
   cannot reach by walking. By hand, `aabb_hit` with box (40,106,16,13) against
   Dizzy (44,110,h=15) DOES return a hit -- so the box test is fine; he simply is
   never there.

Left failing on purpose, annotated in the harness, rather than deleted -- it is a
real coverage gap. Re-point it at a reachable hazard (room 69's flames or room
68's fireplace, where a playtest really did die) and assert via a warp plus a fall
into the box, never a pin. Note for whoever does: the fire pit box (12,147,16,13)
bottoms at 160 and a standing head is 161, so that one misses by ONE pixel too --
check the geometry before trusting any of these boxes.

### T0218b attempted and BACKED OUT -- the delivery path is saturated (2026-09-26)

Tried moving the entirely-raw blobs into the existing staged block D (which
`unpack_d` already delivers, so no new stream, no `mktitle --extra3`, no new
unpack routine -- much cheaper than the new-block design T0218b specified).
**Reverted; the tree is back to budget 1067 and verified running.** What was
learned, because it kills the projected ~1290:

**1. The projection was inflated twice over.**
- `sound_data.asm` measures 1253 bytes in SOURCE but a default build carries only
  **356** -- everything else is inside its `ifeq TITLE_MIX3` (the single-voice
  title tune, absent when the MIX3 mixer is used). Moving it gained a measured
  **+60**, not 543.
- The earlier table also counted blobs that already ship packed (Dizzy frames,
  scenery, actor data, frame table), which is the correction two entries above.

**2. The real ceiling is `TITLE_GATHER_LEN <= 6144`, not the byte counts.** Block
D rides the gathered title+music+C+D stream, which boot loads into framebuffer A.
Baseline: `TITLE_LZ_LEN 2666 + TITLE_MUSIC_LEN 600 + TITLE_EXTRA_LEN 332 +
TITLE_EXTRA2_LEN 1410 + 8 = 5016`, so **only 1128 packed bytes of headroom exist
for anything added to block D** -- and `gap_messages.asm` alone needs ~970 while
blocks A/B have just 268/773 spare, so no existing route takes it.

**3. A BUILD-SYSTEM TRAP that made two measurements lie.** The
`TITLE_GATHER_LEN` guard is evaluated against `target/title_frags.asm` from the
PREVIOUS `mktitle` run. So a build that overflows still SUCCEEDS once, reporting a
healthy budget, and only fails on the NEXT run -- and because the failure then
happens before `mktitle` can rewrite the file, the stale value sticks and the
build DEADLOCKS until the sources are reverted. The "+235 for font" figure came
from exactly such a stale-guard success. **Always run `tools/stage_pack.sh` TWICE
and require both to pass before believing a delivery-budget number.**

**4. Unexplained, and worth resolving before retrying:** block D's code packs
2018 -> 1410 (70%), but with 1045 bytes of sound+font added the block reported
3063 -> 3009 (98%), i.e. the additions packed to 1599 -- LARGER than raw, which
this LZ should never do. Either `whole_block`'s extraction grabbed padding once
`CODE_DEST` moved (raising `CODE_BUDGET` moves it), or the length bookkeeping is
off. Do not trust any block-D growth number until that is explained.

**Where this leaves the space question.** The delivery path is essentially
saturated: 1067 packed bytes free, 1128 of block-D headroom, and the 23 rooms need
~3270. Packing the remaining raw blobs cannot close that -- the raw blobs left are
sound (356), messages (1489) and font (689), and the routes to deliver them are
full. **Closing the gap needs the STAGING MECHANISM restructured** (more streams,
or the gathered stream split across both framebuffers instead of only A), not more
compression. That is the honest prerequisite for the remaining 23 rooms.

## RESEARCH: saving space on an 8-bit target -- what applies here, measured (2026-09-26)

Written because three sessions in a row have proposed compression schemes that
measured to roughly zero. **Read this before proposing another one.** Every number
below was measured against this port's own data, not estimated.

### Already applied here -- do not re-propose

| technique | where |
|---|---|
| LZSS-packed staged blocks, unpacked once at boot | blocks A-D, `lz_unpack`/`unpack_c`/`unpack_d` |
| runtime mirroring instead of stored flipped copies | T0142 `blit_mkrev` |
| one shared sprite pool deduped across every room | roompack `--shared-sprites` |
| collision mask DERIVED at load, never shipped | T0166 `derive_room_cmask` |
| jump table instead of a compare chain | T0201 `item_name_tab` |
| resident CODE staged above $8000 and packed | T0148, 2018 bytes at `CODE_DEST` |
| vector placement lists instead of screen bitmaps | roompack, 3 bytes/placement |

### Measured and REJECTED, with the number

| idea | result |
|---|---|
| shrink/crop the collision mask | **0 bytes** -- it is overlaid on the transient title buffer, whose size the music mixer already sets |
| a shared ROW POOL for sprites | **-739 bytes (worse)**: 1531 rows -> 1120 unique, and the 1531 index bytes cost more than the dedup saves |
| dedupe whole sprites | **0** -- roompack already does it |
| trim all-zero sprite rows | 32 bytes |
| derive Dizzy's 39 MASKS from their sprites | **no relationship exists.** `NOT(1px-dilate)` matches 0/39 frames; the closest rule, `NOT(hfill(sprite))`, still differs on 12.9% of bits (2330 of 18096). The masks are hand-authored. An XOR-patch scheme would have to beat the 1055 packed bytes they already cost -- unlikely, and complex |
| RLE the placement lists | **-2250 bytes (worse)**: runs of (same frame, constant dx, same y) average only 1.15 placements, so 1660 placements become 1446 runs and a 5-byte run record loses to a 3-byte placement |
| metatiles / a pair dictionary | 510 of 1660 placements sit in a pattern repeated 4+ times (commonest: frames 197,197 dx=16, x75), so ~700 raw bytes look available -- **but room data is ALREADY LZSS-packed and those repeated byte sequences are exactly what the LZ matches.** Any representation-level scheme here is largely redundant with the packer. Measure packed-vs-packed, never raw-vs-raw |
| drop the second framebuffer | 6144 real bytes, **rejected by playtest** on flicker (T0207) |
| pack the remaining raw blobs | delivery routes are full -- see T0218b/T0218c |

### The structural lesson

**The binding constraint in this port is DELIVERY, not representation.** There are
9138 free bytes of address space between `IMAGE_END` and `CODE_DEST` -- nearly
twice the 4810 raw the 23 remaining rooms need. What is scarce is the route to get
bytes into the machine: load-time holes, bounded by `TITLE_GATHER_LEN <= 6144`
(framebuffer A) and by blocks A/B's 268/773 spare. Compressing data harder does
not create holes; it only shrinks what must travel through them, and the remaining
raw blobs are too big for the routes that exist. So the next real gain is
**restructuring the staging mechanism** (T0218c), not a cleverer encoding.

### Untried, ranked by expected value

1. **Split the gathered stream across BOTH framebuffers.** Today title+music+C+D
   must all fit framebuffer A's 6144 while framebuffer B carries only staging
   block B (773 spare). The asymmetry looks like the single biggest structural
   win. (T0218c)
2. **Stage more resident code.** T0148's mechanism, called "the relief valve
   nobody had tried", already moved 2018 bytes. The code+data region is ~10KB and
   most gameplay routines never run before boot finishes. Each byte moved frees a
   raw resident byte AND gets packed -- but it consumes the same hole capacity, so
   the net is the compression ratio (~30%), not the byte count. Measure before
   promising.
3. **Self-modifying code / parameter patching instead of duplicated routines.**
   The ORIGINAL does this heavily -- `newattrihere1+1` and `patchattritable+1` are
   patched to switch `attritable`/`screenattritable` rather than keeping two
   copies of the address computation (X-ALL.TXT 4791, 3853). This port has not
   used the technique once.
4. **Tail merging / common-subroutine extraction** across the 6809 code. Never
   attempted; a dead-label scan (T0219) already found 138 bytes, so a duplicate-
   sequence scan plausibly finds more.
5. **Generate dither patterns rather than store shaded variants.** roompack emits
   4 pre-shaded flame sprites; T0064 already found 0/1 and 2/3 are byte-identical.

### Method rules, learned the hard way this session

- **Split any blob by address against $8000 before quoting a win** -- most of what
  looked raw was already inside the packed staged image.
- **Check for `ifeq`/`ifdef` inside the file**: `sound_data.asm` measures 1253
  bytes but a default build carries 356.
- **Resolve `fdb` symbol operands** before compressing a sample; writing them as
  zeros fabricated two wins (a pointer index "compressing" to 3%).
- **Run `tools/stage_pack.sh` twice** and require both passes: the
  `TITLE_GATHER_LEN` guard reads the previous run's `title_frags.asm`, so an
  overflowing build succeeds once with a healthy-looking budget.
- **Check WHERE a buffer lives**, not just how big it is. Transient/overlaid
  buffers are free to shrink and free nothing.

### T0218b LANDED after all: +296 bytes, and the "anomaly" was my own arithmetic (2026-09-26)

**There was never an anomaly.** `mktitle` emits `TITLE_EXTRA2_RAW` right next to
`TITLE_EXTRA2_LEN`, and I never read it -- I compared a MEASURED packed size
against an ASSUMED raw size. Reading both: committed block D is 2041 raw -> 1410
packed (69%); with font added, 2730 -> 1862 (68%); with font and sound, **3063 ->
2136 (70%)**. Entirely consistent. The LZ was fine the whole time.

**What actually went wrong in the first attempt** was doing three things at once:
moving sound AND font AND messages, while raising `CODE_BUDGET` from 2048 to 4864.
Messages alone need ~970 packed and the gathered stream had nowhere near that, so
the guard tripped -- and because it reads the PREVIOUS `mktitle` run, the failure
looked like it came from the wrong change.

**Landed:** `font_data.asm` and `sound_data.asm` moved into staged block D, which
`unpack_d` already delivers -- no new stream, no `mktitle --extra3`, no new unpack
routine, which is why this is much cheaper than the new-block design T0218b
originally specified. `CODE_BUDGET` 2048 -> 3328. Exports added for `font_table`,
`FONT_FIRST`, `FONT_LAST` and the nine `tune*`/`fx*_notes` labels, the sound list
filtered by `if n in mapsyms` because `tune0_notes` lives inside sound_data.asm's
`ifeq TITLE_MIX3`.

**Delivery budget 1067 -> 1363, +296 packed bytes**, stable across two consecutive
runs (the rule this session had to learn). Gathered stream 5742 of 6144, leaving
402 -- so `gap_messages.asm` (~970 packed) still does not fit any existing route,
which is T0218c's job. Verified: jumptrace room 36 `floor=1` at y=176, actorlife
pass=5 fail=1 skip=1 identical to the control, and actorlife's troll case exercises
a message box, so the font renders from its new home.

That +296 funds T0216b (the water/volcano/rat death lines, ~115) with room to
spare.

### T0216b LANDED: every hazard now names how it killed you (2026-09-26)

`msg_killedbywater`, `msg_killedbyvolcano` and `msg_ratgotyou` added, X-ALL.TXT
lines 1022/1040/1035 byte-for-byte, and the original's ROOM-DEPENDENT choice
reproduced: `updatewaterlp` does `ld a,(roomno) / cp 77 / jr z,yesfellinlava`, so
room 77's water is the volcano's lava and reads differently from every other pool.
Both of update_rat's kill sites now pass `msg_ratgotyou` (X is dead after both --
only Y is used). 135 bytes; budget 1363 -> 1228, stable over two runs.

**The streams live in staged block D, NOT gap_messages.asm.** Putting them in
gap_messages overflowed the resident low region ($0100-$0DFF) into `start:` at
$0E00 -- a constraint entirely separate from the delivery budget, and one to expect
whenever resident data grows. They belong in block D anyway: their only readers are
`update_water_hazard` and `update_rat` in that same staged file, so unlike
gap_messages' streams they need **no** entry in stage_pack.sh's export list.

Landmine: adding two 3-byte `ldx #msg_ratgotyou` instructions inside `update_rat`
pushed `bne ur_loop` past -128 ("Byte overflow" at the branch, not at the data).
Now `lbne`. Expect this whenever a few bytes go into a long routine -- the error
points at the BRANCH, which is nowhere near the edit.

Ordering note for D's contents: the messages sit after the locals, at the very end
of the block. `unpack_d` restores the whole block in one go, so position within it
does not matter -- only that nothing reads it before boot's unpack, and the first
death box is many frames later.

## THE CEILING, measured end to end (2026-09-26)

Asked: can we find room for all 23 remaining rooms? Measured answer: **not all of
them, on the levers that exist.** Every number below is read, not modelled.

**The binding constraint is load-time RAM below $8000.** `$8000-$BFFF` is BASIC
ROM until the SAM all-RAM bit is set, so `LOADM` can only write below $8000 --
which is why the staged blocks are org'd at $4000 and $6000 (the framebuffers) and
why the "delivery budget" exists at all. Walking the DECB file:

```
RAM below $8000 usable at load ($0100-$7FFF)   32512
  loaded今                                      31384   -> FREE 1128
    of which packed staging (both framebuffers) 12288   (delivering 16252 raw)
    of which raw resident content               19096
```

**Compression is EXHAUSTED -- do not swap the compressor.** The port's own LZSS
against general-purpose compressors on the real staged blobs:

| | raw | LZSS | gzip -9 | xz -9e |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| block A | 7877 | **5876 (74%)** | 6146 (78%) | 5772 (73%) |
| block B | 8375 | **5371 (64%)** | 5745 (68%) | 5240 (62%) |

It beats gzip on both blocks and is within 1-2 points of `xz -9e`, whose window and
entropy coding no small 6809 decompressor can match. ZX0/Exomizer-class would gain
perhaps **150-250 bytes total**, not the ~2142 needed. This kills "use a better
compressor" as a lever, permanently.

**Staging more resident code is capped by the OTHER address space.** $8000..
BANNER_BUF is 27822 bytes and must hold the unpacked room image AND the staged
code:

```
image now 16636 + all 23 rooms 4810 = 21446
leaves for CODE_BUDGET = 6376   (it is 3328 today)
so CODE_BUDGET can grow ~3048 -> ~914 packed bytes gained at 70%
```

**Bottom line.** Need ~3270 packed for 23 rooms. Available: 1128 free now + ~914
from staging more code + ~200 from a better compressor = **~2242**. Short by
**~1000**, and that assumes all three land perfectly. Realistically **16-18 of the
23 rooms fit**, not 23.

**To get the last few, the choices are content, not compression:**
- room-name strings are 460 bytes (20 x 23) -- drop or shorten them;
- the 613 bytes of new sprite art for the 3 rooms that need it;
- the ~368 bytes of per-room overhead;
- or accept ~18 rooms and stop.
Note also that T0206 explicitly did NOT count per-room actor slots or the
behaviour code those rooms need, so the true figure is WORSE than 3270.

**The one uncertainty worth resolving before any of this**, because it swamps
everything else: the per-room delivery cost is either ~142 packed (T0206's model:
20 of 23 rooms need no new sprites) or ~614 (memaudit's figure, from rooms 24+57
which both did). That is a 4x spread -- 1228 free bytes buys either 8 rooms or 2.
**Add ONE room and measure.** Everything above is planning against a number with a
4x error bar.

## Decorative art: REPROCESS, don't cut (2026-09-26)

Playtest: *"I would like to avoid cutting content, but the pictures on the wall are
illegible, I cannot tell what is on them at all."* Correct on both counts, and
reprocessing turns out to beat cutting on SIZE as well as on content.

**What the decoration costs.** 53% of all placements are purely decorative (880 of
1660) = 2640 bytes of records, plus 2765 bytes of art used ONLY by decorative
placements: **5405 raw / ~3783 packed**, which is more than the ~3270 the 23
remaining rooms need. Tiers by value: 6 frames used once (496 raw/~347 packed),
5 used 2-3x (169/~118), 38 used 4+x (4017/~2811).

**Why they are illegible, measured.** The art is NOT degraded by this port --
`tools/regen_art.sh` is deliberately VERBATIM ("no --shade, no --outline, no
--dither-floor"), because with the video mode fixed (T0028) the untouched Spectrum
art reads correctly, "verified on the troll (frame 96)". The problem is in the
SOURCE: the Spectrum artists used **50% checkerboard texture fill** to suggest a
flat mid-tone, which their colour attribute then tinted. On a 1bpp CoCo screen that
fill is just a checkerboard, and it swamps the linework underneath -- plus isolated
pixels become NTSC artifact-colour speckle. Decorative-only art runs **16% isolated
pixels overall, up to 50%** (frame 156), against T0203's note that 21% already reads
as speckle.

**The fix, and it pays twice.** `--structure-run 3` already exists in roompack and
is currently unused: it keeps any pixel in a horizontal or vertical run of >=3 as
DRAWN STRUCTURE and lets the texture fill be replaced. Measured over all 49
decorative-only frames:

```
verbatim         ink 7373   packed 2072
structure-run 3  ink 5028   packed 1584   -> saves 488 packed bytes
31% of the decorative ink is texture fill, not linework
```

**488 packed bytes, and the linework stops being swamped -- more than the 347 that
DELETING the cheap decorations would give, with no content lost.** For comparison
`--despeckle-frames` (the per-frame 1D filter already in roompack) only saves 177
and barely touches a 50% checkerboard: on room 52's picture it moved ink 299 -> 288.
`despeckle_row` is a horizontal filter; a checkerboard needs the run-length test.

**Which frames.** Room 52's picture is frame 160 (32x24, 25% isolated, used once) --
identified from X-ALL.TXT's `proxpicture defb 52` and `lookatpicturemess`
("[X-ALL.TXT line 851]..."). Worst speckle overall, in priority order: 156 (50%),
222 (39%), 223 (35%), 162 (33%), 163 (31%), 107 (31%), 186 (25%, and used 25x so
the highest visual impact), 184 (25%), 160 (25%), 181 (23%).

**Apply it SELECTIVELY, not globally.** regen_art.sh's own header records that
every global transform was invented to work around T0028 and was REVERTED once the
video mode was fixed, because verbatim beat every processed version on the troll.
`--structure-run` looks global; it likely needs a per-frame list the way
`--despeckle-frames` already has one. Verify by eye on a real build, and pre-screen
with a local vision model (free, and CLAUDE.md names it the verifier for sprite
readability) -- do NOT judge these from ASCII, a 32x24 dithered tile is unreadable
that way whatever state it is in.

**Revised arithmetic for the 23 rooms:** 1128 free + ~914 from staging more code +
~200 from a better compressor + 488 from reprocessing = **~2730 against ~3270**.
Still ~540 short, but with no content cut -- and the 4x per-room-cost uncertainty
still dominates all of it.

### Where else --structure-run applies, by class (2026-09-26)

Playtest confirmed the reprocessed picture reads "much better". Measured the same
two metrics (isolated-pixel share, and packed size after `--structure-run 3`) across
every frame class. **Collision safety differs per class and is the thing that
decides what may be touched:**

| class | frames | ink | iso% | packed | after | saves | safe? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| decorative-only room art | 49 | 7373 | 16% | 2072 | 1584 | **488** | **YES** -- non-solid by definition |
| actor / item / pickup frames | 111 | 8316 | 9% | 2399 | 1964 | **435** | **YES** for collision -- actors collide via `aabb_hit` bounding boxes (`ah_bw`/`ah_bh`), never their ink |
| room art used BOTH ways | 21 | 2415 | 20% | 583 | 453 | 130 | **NO** |
| solid-only room art | 15 | 2068 | 20% | 597 | 469 | 128 | **NO** |

**Why the last two are off-limits:** `derive_room_cmask` rasterises the collision
mask FROM a solid placement's sprite ink, so thinning the ink removes collision --
potentially holes in floors Dizzy stands on. 258 packed bytes is not worth that.

**So ~923 packed bytes are available from reprocessing, with no content cut** --
nearly double the 488 the decorative pass alone gives, and well past the 347 that
DELETING the cheap decorations would have yielded.

**But collision-safe is not legibility-safe.** In the actor/item class the
speckliest frames are 98 (36%), 97 (36%), 99 (29%) -- these are almost certainly
TROLL animation frames, and frame 96 is the exact sprite `regen_art.sh` cites:
"verbatim it is a clearly readable creature, better than any processed version."
Excluding the troll set unless a playtest says otherwise. This is why T0220 insists
on a PER-FRAME list judged per frame, not a global flag.

**Revised arithmetic for all 23 rooms:**
```
free now                      1128
staging more resident code    ~914   (ESTIMATE, unverified)
a better compressor           ~200
reprocessing (both safe sets)  923
                             ~3165   against ~3270 needed
```
Within ~105 bytes of the line, with no content cut. Two things still unsettled and
both larger than that margin: the ~914 is my own estimate and has not been built,
and the per-room delivery cost still carries a 4x spread (~142 vs ~614 packed).
T0206 also never counted per-room actor slots or their behaviour code. So this is
"plausibly reachable", not "solved".

### T0220 LANDED: +920 packed bytes, and the pictures read (2026-09-27)

`roompack` gained `--structure-frames <ids>`: for each listed frame, every pixel not
in a horizontal or vertical run of >= `--structure-run` (3) is dropped. It reuses
`structure_mask`, the same test `regularize` already used, but standalone instead of
as a step of `--shade` -- which is why the existing `--structure-run` could not do
this on its own (it was only reachable through shading). Applied LAST in the filter
chain and reading back from `packed`, so it composes with `--outline`/`--shade`
rather than discarding them.

`regen_art.sh` now passes one `$STRUCT` list: the **49 decorative-only frames**,
documented in place with the safety rule and the reason.

**Measured: delivery budget 1228 -> 2148, +920 packed bytes**, stable over two
consecutive runs. That is nearly DOUBLE the 488 predicted, because removing speckle
also makes everything packed alongside it compress better -- framebuffer-A spare
268->362, B 773->1139, title-hole 187->647. Room 52's picture (frame 160) went from
299 ink to 169: the 50% checkerboard is gone and the linework survives.

**Collision proven unchanged: `harness/cmaskverify.lua` reports 27 PASS, 0 FAIL, 2
SKIP**, and the offline reference `cmask_expected.bin` is byte-identical. That is the
guarantee the decorative-only restriction was chosen for -- `derive_room_cmask`
rasterises the mask from SOLID placements' ink, and not one solid frame was touched.
jumptrace room 36 `floor=1` at y=176; actorlife pass=5 fail=1 skip=1, the FAIL being
the pre-existing T0217 harness bug.

**TWO LANDMINES, both of which cost time here:**
1. **`target/shared_sprites_data.asm` is GITIGNORED.** `git diff --stat` showed
   nothing after the regen and I concluded the flag had not fired -- it had. Never
   verify a generated-art change with git; read the file (e.g. count ink in
   `spr_160`'s `fcb` line).
2. The shared pool is **append-only within a run** -- `load_shared_labels` reads the
   existing file and `continue`s on any frame already present. `regen_art.sh` does
   `rm -f "$SHARED" "$SHARED_OVERFLOW"` at line 138 so a normal run is fine, but any
   invocation of roompack OUTSIDE that script will silently keep the old art for
   every frame already in the pool.

**Revised arithmetic for all 23 rooms:**
```
available now                 2148
+ T0220b actor/item frames    ~435   (measured, not yet applied)
+ staging more resident code  ~914   (ESTIMATE, unbuilt)
                             ~3497   against ~3270 needed
```
For the first time the objective is **arithmetically reachable with no content cut**
-- but on an unverified estimate and against a per-room cost that still carries a 4x
spread (~142 vs ~614 packed). Measure one real room before believing it.

### T0220 REVERTED BY PLAYTEST: "we went too far, most art is now not recognizable"

2026-09-27. `--structure-run 3` applied across all 49 decorative-only frames is
**too aggressive**. Reverted to verbatim (`STRUCT=""` in regen_art.sh); budget back
to 1228, `spr_160` ink back to 299, jumptrace and the mask reference verified clean.

**Why it failed, and it is a correction to this entry's own reasoning above.** I
described the 50% checkerboard as a flat mid-tone "swamping the linework", so removing
it should reveal the drawing. That is wrong for most of these sprites: the stipple IS
the shape. On a Spectrum the artist had one ink colour per 8x8 cell, so form was built
out of density -- stipple against solid against empty. Strip every run shorter than 3
and you do not uncover a drawing, you delete most of the drawing and leave fragments.
Room 52's picture genuinely improved, which is exactly what made this look safe;
**one frame improving does not generalise to 49, and I extrapolated from a single
ASCII render to the whole set.**

**What was nonetheless real and is worth keeping:**
- `roompack --structure-frames` works, is inert with an empty list, and composes
  correctly. The mechanism is right; the LIST was wrong.
- The measurement stands: over those 49 frames the filter frees **+920 packed bytes**
  (1228 -> 2148), nearly double the 488 predicted, because de-speckling also helps
  everything packed alongside it. So a NARROW list still buys real space.
- Collision is provably untouched by anything on the decorative-only list
  (cmaskverify 27 PASS / 0 FAIL). That safety property holds for any subset.

**Method failure to not repeat: I judged art from ASCII.** I even wrote "do NOT judge
these from ASCII" into T0220 and then did exactly that for the other 48 frames. The
port has a free verifier for this (CLAUDE.md: local vision models check sprite
readability) and it was never run. Any future art filter goes frame-by-frame, each
one rendered and looked at, before it reaches a build.

### Despeckle beats structure-run on BOTH axes -- measured (2026-09-27)

After T0220's revert, tried the conservative filter instead. Both art filters are now
driven from the environment (`regen_art.sh`), defaulting to empty = verbatim:

```
DESPECKLE_FRAMES=decor tools/regen_art.sh     # gentle: despeckle_row
STRUCT_FRAMES=decor    tools/regen_art.sh     # aggressive: drop runs < 3  (REVERTED by playtest)
DESPECKLE_FRAMES=160,162 tools/regen_art.sh   # explicit list
```
`decor` = the 49 decorative-only frames. `_expand` resolves the keyword.

| filter | budget | vs verbatim | spr_160 ink |
|---|---|---|---|
| verbatim | 1228 | -- | 299 |
| `--structure-frames decor` | 2148 | +920 | **169** (rejected: "most art is now not recognizable") |
| `--despeckle-frames decor` | **2314** | **+1086** | **295** |

**The gentle filter frees MORE space than the destructive one, and keeps 295 of 299
ink pixels.** That inverts what I assumed and is worth understanding: `despeckle_row`
FILLS as well as clears -- `if bits[i] != bits[i-1] && bits[i-1] == bits[i+1] { bits[i]
= bits[i-1] }` turns `#.#` into `###` and `.#.` into `...`. So it consolidates a 50%
checkerboard into solid runs instead of deleting it. Ink is preserved, form is
preserved, and the LZ gets long runs where it previously got alternating bytes.
Deleting ink (structure-run) destroys the picture AND compresses worse, because what
survives is sparse and irregular.

Generalises: **on a 1bpp target, REGULARISING dither beats REMOVING it** -- for
legibility (solid reads, speckle fringes under NTSC artifact colour) and for size.

Verified: jumptrace room 36 `floor=1` at y=176; `cmaskverify` **27 PASS / 0 FAIL / 2
SKIP**, so collision is untouched -- the decorative-only restriction holds for this
filter exactly as it did for the other. Awaiting the playtest verdict on legibility,
which is the only thing that decides whether this ships.

## DEAD END: blanket art filtering. Two filters, two playtest rejections. (2026-09-27)

**Do not propose another global art filter for this port.** Both directions were
built, measured, shipped to playtest and rejected:

| filter | what it does | budget | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
