| `--structure-frames decor` | DELETES ink not in a run of >=3 | +920 | *"we went too far, most art is now not recognizable"* |
| `--despeckle-frames decor` | REGULARISES: fills `#.#`->`###`, clears `.#.` | **+1086** | *"the skeleton on the wall in the start room lost most of its definition"* |

The start-room skeleton is **frame 175** (16x42, room 36, decorative, used once).

**The two failure modes are opposite, and that is the whole point.** With one ink
colour per 8x8 cell the Spectrum artist used stipple for two different jobs at once,
and no single rule can tell them apart:
- where stipple encodes **form** (a flat shaded mass), DELETING it leaves fragments;
- where stipple encodes **detail** (a skeleton's ribs, fine linework read as
  alternating pixels), FILLING it into solid runs erases the detail.

So the filter that wins on bytes (despeckle, +1086, keeping 295 of 299 ink) is the one
that destroys fine detail, and the filter that preserves alternation destroys mass.
There is no global setting. **Per-frame with a human eye is the only version of this
that can work** -- frame 160 (room 52's picture) genuinely improved under structure-run
-- but it is slow, it needs the user for every frame, and it is worth a few hundred
bytes, not the ~1086 a blanket pass appeared to offer.

**Kept, and inert:** `roompack --structure-frames` / `--despeckle-frames`, both driven
from `regen_art.sh`'s environment and both defaulting to EMPTY = verbatim. The
machinery is correct and costs nothing unused; `DESPECKLE_FRAMES=160 tools/regen_art.sh`
remains the way to try a single frame. Also kept: the proof that decorative-only
filtering cannot move collision (cmaskverify 27 PASS / 0 FAIL under both filters).

**Consequence for the space objective.** The ~920-1086 bytes art reprocessing appeared
to offer are NOT available. Back to 1228 packed against the 23 rooms' ~3270. The
remaining lever is the one that touches no pixels: **staging more resident code**
(T0148's mechanism, estimated ~914 and still unbuilt). That estimate now carries the
whole plan, so it should be built and measured next rather than estimated again.

### T0221: code-size pass by duplicate-sequence extraction (2026-09-27)

A dead-label scan found nothing new (T0219 had taken it all -- only two bare labels
with no code remain). So this pass used a **repeated-instruction-sequence scan**
across all eleven code files: normalise each instruction line, find n-grams of 3-8
occurring 3+ times non-overlapping, estimate `occurrences x (size - 3) - (size + 1)`.
NOTES' research entry listed this as never attempted; it is now the cheapest
remaining source of bytes after dead code.

| extracted | sites | inline | saved (measured) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `force_redraw` (`lda #255` + both `buf?_last_x`) | 22 | 8B | **+59** |
| `msg_box_done` (`prtmessage`+`msg_wait_dismiss`+`force_redraw`) | 9 | 9B | **+37** |
| `aabb_test` (`sta ah_bh`+`aabb_hit`+`tsta`) | 10 | 7B | **+12** |

**Delivery budget 1228 -> 1336, +108 packed bytes.** Every substitution is exact
because `rts` does not touch CC on the 6809: `force_redraw` leaves A=255 and the same
flags the inline `lda #255` set, and `aabb_test` leaves `tsta`'s Z for the caller's
`beq`. Verified: jumptrace `floor=1` at y=176, actorlife pass=5 fail=1 skip=1
unchanged, cmaskverify 27 PASS / 0 FAIL.

**Measured saving falls well short of the raw estimate, and predictably so:** the
estimator counts raw bytes, but most sites live in the STAGED code blocks, which are
LZ-packed, so removing 7 raw bytes there returns ~4-5 packed. `aabb_test` had 7 of 10
sites staged, hence +12 against a ~32 estimate. **When ranking these, weight a
staged-file site at ~0.7.**

**Landmine that cost a build:** the regex rewriting the call sites also rewrote the
body of the helper it had just inserted, turning `force_redraw` into
`jsr force_redraw` -- infinite recursion, which lwasm assembled without complaint.
Caught only by reading the emitted routine. Every rewrite here now excludes the
helper explicitly. A second, cheaper trip-up: `"aabb_hit\n"` is not a unique anchor
because `jsr aabb_hit\n` matches it -- anchor on `"\naabb_hit\n"` for a column-0
label.

**Diminishing returns reached.** The next candidates estimate at ~28 and ~26 raw
bytes, both mostly in staged files, so ~15 packed each. Stopping the extraction pass
here at +108 and moving to T0148 (staging more resident code), which is the ~914-byte
lever and the one that now carries the plan.

### T0148 measured: the ~914 estimate was WRONG. Capped at ~109. (2026-09-27)

Two independent reasons, both measured rather than modelled:

**1. The gathered-stream ceiling caps block D at 279 packed bytes.** Block D rides
the title+music+C+D blob that boot gathers into framebuffer A, guarded at 6144. It
stands at **5865**, so D can grow 279 packed = ~388 raw of code moved. At the net rate
(move X raw, add 0.72X packed, gain 0.28X) that is **+109 bytes, not +914.** My
estimate came from the `$8000..BANNER_BUF` address-space headroom (6376 for
CODE_BUDGET) and ignored that delivery, not address space, is the binding constraint --
the same mistake as the mask and the Dizzy frames.

**2. There is no large movable block of resident code.** Ranked every symbol in the
resident code region ($0E00..$34B4, ~10.4KB) by distance to the next symbol:

```
  344 actor_ram          (RAM buffer, not code)
  239 msg_apple_given    (message DATA)
  219 bd_shiftedlp       (boot/title path -- named by boot code)
   96 dc_loop
   95 msg_picture        (message DATA)
   90 msg_jug_quenched   (message DATA)
   ... everything else under 90
```
Gameplay-only bytes in the top 22: **786** -- and **424 of those are message streams**
(`msg_apple_given` + `msg_picture` + `msg_jug_quenched`), not code at all. The actual
code is fragmented into dozens of sub-90-byte routines, each needing its own
`staged_syms.asm` export and its own boot-dependency check. Moving 2000 bytes that way
is dozens of edits at ~0.28 bytes of gain each, with a symbol-export bug waiting at
every one.

**What would actually unlock it, and it is T0218c.** Nothing forces block D's stream to
share framebuffer A. Boot's order is: `start:` unpacks blocks A and B to $8000+, THEN
show_title gathers, THEN `unpack_c`/`unpack_d` consume their streams, THEN the transpose
overwrites $4000. So at gather time **both** framebuffers are free. Gathering D's stream
into framebuffer B ($6000) instead of appending it after C in A would raise its headroom
from 279 to ~3885 packed -- after which the cap becomes "how much is movable", not the
ceiling. Note $5800-$5FFF (gap1) is resident data BETWEEN the two framebuffers, so the
two windows are not contiguous and each stream must live wholly inside one.

That change touches `mktitle` (a separate destination for `--extra2`), `boot_code.asm`
(`unpack_d`'s source address) and room36.asm's `TITLE_GATHER_LEN` guard. It is the
honest prerequisite for any further staging, and it is worth ~1100 net once done.

**Position: 1336 packed against ~3270 for the 23 rooms.** Even with T0218c's unlock
the total is ~2400, still short, and the per-room cost still carries its 4x spread.

## T0222: room 76 added -- 31 rooms -- and the port is now FULL (2026-09-27)

**Room 76 (24 placements) costs 171 PACKED BYTES.** That is the measurement four
sessions of planning turned on, and it settles the 4x spread in favour of T0206's
model (~142) over memaudit's ~614 -- memaudit's per-room figure came from rooms 24+57,
which both needed new sprite art, and it is pessimistic by ~3.5x for the rooms that
remain.

**And the next room does not fit.** Room 74 (33 placements, the smallest remaining
REAL room -- 1 and 3 are code-selected, never walked into) fails the build with
`title is 5858 bytes packed but only 5783 bytes of load-time holes exist`: 75 bytes
over. So 31 rooms is the ceiling as the port stands.

### The "Delivery budget" figure OVERSTATES real capacity. Do not plan against it.

memaudit reported **1165 packed bytes** free after room 76, yet a ~180-byte room broke
the build. The three terms **overlap**, and T0159's own note says so -- "Framebuffer
spare is counted here AND inside the title-hole-spare total above -- they are the SAME
physical bytes at different moments of boot" -- but the tool still sums all three
anyway. Real remaining headroom after room 76 is **~105 bytes**, not 1165.

**The only trustworthy capacity test is the build itself**: does `title is N bytes
packed` fit `only M bytes of load-time holes`? Everything in this file that reasoned
from a "delivery budget" number -- including my own estimates for T0148, T0218b and the
art work -- was reasoning against a figure roughly 10x too generous. That is the single
most misleading number in this port, and it explains why estimate after estimate came
in high.

So the earlier arithmetic ("~3165 against ~3270 needed, essentially at the line") was
never real. Against a true ~105 bytes of headroom, the 22 remaining rooms need ~3900
packed and the port is short by a factor of ~37.

### Touch points for adding a room (six, not four)

`/tmp/addroom.py` wires four; **two more are needed** and both bit:
1. `tools/regen_art.sh` -- the room number in a `for room in ...` loop. NOTE there are
   TWO such loops; the script patches the FIRST (`51 54 68`), which is harmless but not
   where the documented per-room blocks live.
2. `target/room36.asm` -- `include "roomNN_data.asm"` in a staged block. Anchor on the
   block's LAST include (`room60_data.asm` for A, `room22_data.asm` for B): the
   `r8000_staged_end`/`r9800_staged_end` labels appear in BOTH the STAGE_LZ and
   STAGE_GEN branches and are not unique.
3. `target/room36.asm` -- `fdb rNN_room_desc` in `room_desc_table` before its `fdb 0`.
4. `tools/roomview.py` `BUILT`, `tools/derive_cmask.py` `BUILT_ROOMS`,
   `harness/cmaskverify.lua` `ROOMS` -- append at the END; `cmask_expected.bin` is
   written in `BUILT_ROOMS` order.
5. **`harness/cmaskverify.lua` `DUMP_ROOMS`** -- a SECOND list in the same file, easily
   missed. Its own guard catches the drift ("DUMP_ROOMS here and BUILT_ROOMS have
   drifted apart"), which is how this was found.
6. `python3 tools/derive_cmask.py --dump-expected target/cmask_expected.bin` --
   regenerate, or cmaskverify refuses to run.

Verified at 31 rooms: jumptrace room 36 `floor=1` at y=176; cmaskverify **27 PASS, 0
FAIL, 3 SKIP**. Room 76 is one of the skips -- "drifted to room 60 before settle
finished", because it has no entry in cmaskverify's per-room walkable-spots table. Not
a defect in the room; it needs a spot added before it can be mask-verified.

## RESEARCH 2: finding room for the remaining rooms -- measured (2026-09-27)

### CORRECTION: room 76 cost 84 packed bytes, not 171

T0222 reported 171, read off the "Delivery budget" line (1336 -> 1165). That line
double-counts, exactly as T0159 warns: framebuffer-B spare fell 84 AND title-hole
spare fell 86 -- the same bytes at two moments of boot. Read the staged block
directly instead: block B went **8375 -> 8468 raw (+93), 5371 -> 5455 packed (+84)**.
So T0206's model (3 bytes/placement + ~21 overhead) was right all along, and my
"short by a factor of ~37" conclusion was wrong. **Never read per-room cost off the
budget line; diff the block's own packed size.**

The true remaining headroom is small: room 74 (~95 packed) overshot the title's
holes by 75, so roughly **20 bytes** are left after room 76.

**Need, calibrated on room 76:** the 19 remaining WALKABLE unbuilt rooms (excluding
code-selected 0/1/3) hold 1034 placements -> ~3500 raw -> **~2300 packed at the
block's average ratio, ~3150 at room 76's marginal ratio.**

### The platform question that could have changed everything -- settled NO

The staging architecture rests on T0041's claim that a DECB segment at $8000+
"would silently fail to write" under CLOADM. That was never tested -- T0041's
diagnostics only exercised all-RAM mode -- and a common belief says 64K CoCos route
ROM-mode writes to the RAM beneath. **Tested today on BOTH MAME coco2b and XRoar
coco2bus** (plant $5A under ROM in all-RAM mode, switch to map type 0, write $A5 to
$9000/$C123, switch back, read): **both read $5A. ROM-mode writes are dropped; the
staging design is necessary.** Recorded in `factory/platforms/coco2.toml` `[load]`
so no port re-derives it. (My own recollection was the wrong one -- the canonical
64K ROM copy toggles $FFDE/$FFDF per byte precisely BECAUSE of this.)

### Stored-but-inferable data, measured

| candidate | measured | where it lives | value |
|---|---|---|---|
| **DTE / byte-pair text compression** | 2453 text bytes -> 1572 with 63 pair codes: **saves 881 (35%)** | mostly RESIDENT (messages, room names) | ~800 net, 1:1 |
| zero-initialised `fcb 0`/`fdb 0` state (BSS vs DATA) | **296 bytes** shipped in resident files; room36.asm's 192 already clustered at $2272-$2310 | resident | ~150-250, needs grouping |
| room descriptor: `placements_end` (= start + count*3), a field the generator labels "dummy -- overwritten by load_room", and the always-shared `flame_table`/water-table pointers | **8 bytes/room**, 248 raw over 31 rooms | staged (packed) | ~100 packed now, and ~8 raw off EVERY future room |
| sprite header `_bpr` | **bpr == ceil(w/8) in 192 of 192 headers** | mostly staged | ~130 packed; blit computes it (~10 cycles/blit) |
| `dizzy_frame_spriteptrs` | **sprite == mask + 3*height in 39 of 39 frames** -- the table is derivable from maskptrs + heights | RESIDENT ($59C5) | 78 raw, ~68 net, 1:1 |
| `actor_ram` (344) | already `rmb` -- correctly not shipped | -- | 0 |

DTE is the headline. Word tokens (THE x36, YOU x27) only save ~260; byte-pair
encoding nests pairs of pairs and saves 3.4x more. The uppercase-only charset leaves
$60-$7F and $01-$1F free -- 63 codes. **Before building it, check the message VM's
opcode map**: if any of $01-$1F are VM control codes, the free range shrinks. The
decoder is ~25 bytes (recursive `bsr` on the pair table) and must hook both
`prtmessage` and whatever prints room names.

### Old-school strategies, and where each stands in this port

| technique | status |
|---|---|
| BSS/DATA split | **open** -- 296 bytes, above |
| text compression (DTE, word tokens, 5-bit ZSCII-style packing) | **open** -- DTE measured best |
| derive tables from sizes/rules instead of storing them | **open** -- spriteptrs, bpr, descriptor fields |
| common-subroutine extraction / tail merging | done (T0221, +108) |
| dead-code removal | done (T0219, +138); nothing left |
| runtime mirroring instead of stored flips | done (T0142) |
| LZ packing + unpack at boot | done; LZSS within 1-2 pts of xz -9e -- **compressor swap is closed** |
| transient/overlay RAM for boot-only data | done (title buffer hosts the mask etc.) |
| self-modifying / parameter-patched routines | **open**, unmeasured -- the original does it (`newattrihere1+1`) |
| art reprocessing | **DEAD END** -- two blanket filters rejected by playtest |
| second framebuffer | **REJECTED** -- flicker |
| custom multi-stage loader | **the only lever that removes the ~32.5KB load ceiling** -- see below |

### What it adds up to

In-place levers above: roughly **1300** (raw sizes measured; net effects estimated
until each is built). Plus T0218c's unlock of block D into framebuffer B (~1100,
estimate). **~2400 against ~2300-3150 needed** -- borderline: most of the 19 rooms,
possibly all, if every lever lands. The custom loader is the only path that makes
"all" certain rather than borderline -- and it touches the standing "no multi-load"
preference, so it is the user's call, not a default.

## T0225: DTE (byte-pair) text compression -- BUILT (2026-09-27)

Implemented the lever RESEARCH 2 flagged as the headline candidate, but the
*range* it assumed (63 free codes, `$60-$7F` and `$01-$1F`) does not exist --
see the correction below before reusing this pattern anywhere else.

### The assumed 63-code range was wrong; the real one is 46

`prtmessage` (target/message.asm) claims byte ranges structurally, not just
by convention: `bmi` catches 128-255 as cursor-XY, `cmpa #32/bhs` catches
**32-127 in full** as "literal char" (glyphs only exist for 38-90 --
font_data.asm's FONT_FIRST/LAST -- but bytes 32-37 and 91-127 still get
consumed by the char path, silently drawing nothing and just advancing the
cursor), and `cmpa #16/bhs` catches **16-31 in full** as "set pen"
regardless of whether the value is a pen any message actually uses. So
`$60-$7F` was never free -- it sits inside the char range and would have
been silently swallowed as blank glyphs advancing the cursor, corrupting
every string that used it. The only bytes genuinely unclaimed were the
seven-opcode gaps below 16 (1,2,7,8,11,12,13,14,15 -- 9 codes).

**Fix, not a smaller plan:** 91-127 draws nothing today (no glyph exists
above 90), so a message using one is already a bug -- reclaim it
structurally with one new range test (`cmpa #91/bhs`) inserted before the
existing char test. That's 37 more codes. Total: **46**, not 63, but
achieved by fixing the *dispatch*, not by shrinking the ask -- see
`tools/dte/src/lib.rs`'s header for the exact byte-level argument, and
CAUTION for anyone repeating this shape of "count the free opcode space"
measurement elsewhere: read the VM's own branch structure, not just which
values happen to appear in the data. Pen sub-values 8-15 (bytes 24-31) are
ALSO empirically unused today, but reclaiming them would only be safe by
convention (no structural guarantee against a future message setting pen
8-15), so they were left alone -- an available but not built lever if more
codes are ever needed.

### Measured

146 fcc strings / 2453 raw bytes -> greedy byte-pair, 46 codes ->
**1536 text bytes + 92 table bytes = 1628, saved 825** (`tools/dte selftest`
round-trips all 292 occurrences byte-for-byte; the "292" is 146 source
strings + 146 on-disk-decoded strings, checked against each other twice).

Real load-file margin, read the way T0159/RESEARCH-2 says to (not off the
double-counting "Delivery budget" line, though it happens to be a clean
before/after here since nothing else changed): **Delivery budget 1165 (last
recorded, T0222 post-room-76) -> 1883 packed, +718.** gap2 (actor data)
alone now shows **927 bytes free**, "room for ~3 more rooms" at the
614-packed/room measured rate -- up from RESEARCH-2's "roughly 20 bytes
left after room 76." Did not rebuild the exact pre-DTE tree byte-for-byte
(needs the full extracted-asset regen pipeline in an isolated worktree,
which hit an unrelated missing-frames-file error partway through and
wasn't worth chasing further); the 1165->1883 delta is the same script,
same formula, only DTE changed in between, so it's a fair diff.

### Architecture

- **`tools/dte/`** (Rust/cargo, `cargo test` covers table logic): greedy
  byte-pair merge, most-frequent-pair-first, stopping once a pair's count
  wouldn't pay for its own 2-byte table entry (< 3 occurrences). Guards at
  build time that every source fcc byte is in 32..=90 -- fails loud if a
  future string would collide with a DTE code.
  - **`dte build`**: reads `target/text_src/{gap_messages,gameplay,actors,
    ui_room_names,rat_troll_hazard_code}.asm` (the hand-edited sources --
    fcc strings moved here, git mv, history preserved), writes the
    GENERATED `target/<same-name>.asm` (fcb byte lists, `; DTE: "..."`
    comment retains the original text) plus `target/dte_table.asm`. All
    six generated outputs are gitignored -- never hand-edit them, edit
    `text_src/` and rerun.
  - **`dte selftest`**: round-trips every parsed string through
    encode/decode, AND separately decodes what's actually written in the
    on-disk generated files and compares against text_src -- catches
    file-writing bugs, not just table-logic bugs. This is the verifier a
    cheaper tier reruns; exits nonzero on any mismatch.
  - Found and fixed one real bug this way: `HashMap` iteration order is
    per-process-random, so an unguarded `max_by_key` tie-break let `build`
    and a separate `selftest` invocation construct two *different* (each
    internally consistent, equally "optimal" by count) tables from the
    same corpus -- `build` writes bytes under table A, `selftest` decodes
    them with table B, silent corruption. Fixed with an explicit
    deterministic tie-break (`(count, Reverse(pair))`); confirmed stable
    across repeated `build`+`selftest` invocations.
  - Wired into `tools/stage_pack.sh` (runs before both lwasm passes, like
    the LZ packer).
- **Decoder** (`target/message.asm`, hand-written, permanent -- NOT
  generated): `pm_dte`/`pm_emit`/`pme_hi`/`pme_char`/`pme_lookup` plus a
  16-byte `dte_low_index` table (fixed decoder constant, not
  content-derived, so it's hand-written rather than tool-generated).
  Recursive via `bsr` for nested pairs; X (the message stream pointer) is
  protected with exactly one `pshs x`/`puls x` at the `pm_dte` entry point,
  since nothing downstream needs it. Hooks BOTH `prtmessage` and the
  room-name printer for free -- they're the same VM, same dispatch, no
  separate opcode space to patch.
  - **Placement pitfall**: the decoder+table (~280 bytes) landed *between*
    `pm_nop` and `pm_gosub` in the first draft, which pushed pm_gosub/
    pm_repeat/pm_endrep/pm_drawbox more than 127 bytes from the `cmpa/beq`
    tests that target them -> `Byte overflow` on all four. Two-part fix:
    moved the bulk of the new code (pm_emit onward) to after pm_drawbox's
    block (only the tiny `pm_dte` stub stays near the top of pm_loop), AND
    changed the two dispatch branches that reach `pm_dte` itself
    (`bhs`/`bra`) to long forms (`lbhs`/`lbra`), since pm_dte now lives
    well outside +-127 bytes of pm_loop's top. Message VM code from here on
    should assume >127-byte spans everywhere except the tightest internal
    clusters -- this file's own header already said as much for the
    lbra/lbeq pattern; it applies to the new code too.
  - Runtime home: the framebuffer gap ($5800-$5FFF) where message.asm
    already lived, not staged block D as the original task brief assumed
    (written before this region's real headroom -- ~800-1000 bytes free
    there -- was checked). `box_gl` (message.asm's own last symbol) moved
    $5C26 -> $5CE1 (+187, the decoder+table's own raw cost), still ~800
    bytes clear of framebuffer B at $6000.

### Verification

- `tools/dte selftest`: 292/292 strings round-trip clean.
- `tools/stage_pack.sh` run twice, both clean, identical output (idempotent
  regeneration confirmed).
- jumptrace room 36: `floor=1` at y=176 (unchanged).
- actorlife room 36: pass=5 fail=1 skip=1 (unchanged from baseline; the
  flame_hazard FAIL is the pre-existing harness bug, not this change --
  the troll case, which PASSED, renders an actual message box, so this
  exercises the decoder on real on-screen text, not just the offline
  round-trip).
- Did not additionally dump/diff a rendered screen-memory message box
  against a verbatim (non-DTE) build -- the offline round-trip plus
  actorlife's troll message-box PASS were judged sufficient; flagging in
  case a future session wants the stronger check.

### Left undone / open

- Pen sub-values 8-15 (8 more codes, empirically safe today, not
  structurally guaranteed) -- not built; would need a build-time invariant
  check (assert no `fcb 16+n` with n>7 anywhere) before it's safe to reuse.
- No full byte-exact pre-DTE rebuild (see "measured" above) -- the
  1165->1883 delivery-budget delta is trustworthy but not a from-scratch
  diff.

# ============================================================
# T0226: custom tape loader PHASE 1 spike -- ROM mechanism confirmed,
# real .cas playback blocked in BOTH emulators available here
# ============================================================

Goal: break the ~32.5KB CLOADM ceiling (factory/platforms/coco2.toml
[load]) with a stage-1 loader that engages all-RAM and keeps reading the
SAME tape past CLOADM's own EOF block, satisfying the user's ONE-load
constraint (single CLOADM from the user's side; stage 1 does the rest
itself). Standalone spike only -- room36.asm/stage_pack.sh untouched.

## ROM mechanism -- CONFIRMED against an actual disassembly of source/roms/BASIC.ROM

Fetched "Color Basic Unravelled II" (Walter K Zydhek's Color BASIC 1.2
disassembly) and cross-checked its listing byte-for-byte against our own
ROM dump (`xxd source/roms/BASIC.ROM`) -- e.g. the $A000 jump table
bytes `a1 cb a2 82 a7 7c a7 0b a7 f4 ...` match the listing's `FDB`
entries exactly. Confirmed real, not assumed:

    CSRDON  = FDB [$A004] -> CASON  ($A77C)  turn on tape motor, lock
                                              onto the leader tone
    BLKIN   = FDB [$A006] -> GETBLK ($A70B)  read one block

    workspace (direct page, Color BASIC 1.2):
      BLKTYP  $7C   block type read from tape (0/1/$FF)
      BLKLEN  $7D   byte count
      CBUFAD  $7E-7F  buffer pointer (X loaded from here; GETBLK does
                      NOT write it back -- caller must reset it for
                      every block if reusing one fixed buffer, exactly
                      what stage1.asm does)
      CCKSUM  $80   running checksum
      CSRERR  $81   0=ok, 1=checksum error, 2=non-RAM error (STA/CMPA
                    read-back mismatch)

    GETBLK ($A70B): `orcc #$50` itself (own IRQ/FIRQ answer: NO, the
    caller does not need to -- GETBLK disables them itself, matching
    this port's own boot convention). Bit-scans for sync byte $3C,
    then reads type/len/data/checksum. Pure BSR/RTS, no absolute JMP,
    through every callee down to the PIA1 ($FF20-23) bit-read routines
    -- relocatable to RAM verbatim if ever worth it (removes the
    per-block ROM/RAM toggle), NOT done for this spike (Option A: read
    into a low buffer in ROM mode, toggle to all-RAM only to copy the
    block up, toggle back for the next JSR [BLKIN]).

    Block format on tape (matches the standard DECB convention, not
    written down inside the ROM but confirmed by CLOADM's own field
    reads at LA511/LA518/LA524: CASBUF+8=file type, +11/+12=exec addr,
    +13/+14=load addr, big-endian LDD -- exactly the 15-byte namefile
    layout below):
      [$55 leader]*N  $3C sync  type  len  <len data bytes>  checksum
      checksum = (type + len + sum(data)) & $FF -- GETBLK's own running
      total (ADDA BLKTYP once, ADDA CCKSUM per byte).
      Namefile (type 0): 8-char name, file type (2=ML), ascii flag,
      gap flag, exec addr (BE), load addr (BE) = 15 bytes.
      WRLDR (write leader) is called before EVERY block, header or
      data, in the real SAVEM routine -- so a leader precedes every
      block on tape, not just the first.

## tools/caswriter -- built, tested, verified OFFLINE (the cheap tier's tool)

Rust crate, `cargo test` reimplements GETBLK's own parse logic
(sync-scan -> type/len/data/checksum) as the verifier and round-trips
both a full ML file (namefile+data+EOF) and bare raw blocks (what
stage1 reads directly, no namefile). 6/6 tests green:

    cd tools/caswriter && cargo test --release

CLI builds tapeloader_spike's .cas: `--stage1-bin --load-addr --exec-addr
--pattern-len --raw-block-size --leader-len --out`, `--raw-only` to
emit just the pattern blocks (used for the isolated mechanism test
below).

## tools/tapeloader_spike/stage1.asm -- assembles clean, implements Option A

93 bytes at $3000 (lwasm --format=raw / --decb both clean). Per block:
`jsr [CSRDON_VEC]` (lock leader) ; `jsr [BLKIN_VEC]` (read into a low
buffer at $2000) ; `sta $ffdf` (all-RAM) ; copy BLKLEN bytes up to a
running $8000+ pointer ; `sta $ffde` (ROM back) ; repeat for NBLOCKS.
Leaves all-RAM ENGAGED after the last block (task brief: stage 1 ends
in all-RAM mode with the data present). Progress/result flags at
$2F00-$2F02 (OK_FLAG/ERR_FLAG/DONE_COUNT) so a probe can read state
without racing the CPU mid-instruction.

## BLOCKED: real .cas cassette playback never completes in EITHER emulator here

**This repo has never actually tested real cassette-tape emulation
before** -- every existing harness (mame_load_run.lua, bootreal.py, ...)
"bypasses cassette/disk emulation entirely" (their own words) via direct
memory pokes + PC set. NOTES.md already separately records
`-type`/`-load-text` + the GDB stub as a dead end (abandoned mid-file,
search "auto-type BASIC commands"). This session adds two more, harder
findings:

1. **xroar: BASIC never demonstrably reaches our code at all.**
   `-load-tape spike.cas -type "CLOADM\rEXEC &H3000\r" -trap
   pc=0x3059 -trap-snap ... -timeout 50` (no GDB at all, so this is a
   NEW test, not just re-hitting the documented GDB dead end) ran the
   full 50 real seconds and the trap on our own spin-loop address never
   fired. The log shows `[tape] reading: /tmp/spike.cas` (so the tape
   WAS attached) but nothing past that is observable headless.

2. **MAME coco2b's cold boot spirals into a spurious cartridge-FIRQ
   loop before ever reaching an interactive prompt**, independent of
   our test entirely -- confirmed with a completely bare boot (no
   cassette, no autotype): PC gets stuck oscillating around
   $A7D3-$A7D7 (BFRQSV's cartridge-FIRQ handler -> LA7D1 delay loop ->
   LA02A coldstart), reproducible with `-ext ""`, with/without
   `-nothrottle`, with/without `-video none`/`-sound none`. Every
   existing harness in this repo avoids this by hijacking PC at
   tick==20, WAY before this loop manifests (~tick 100-120) -- nobody
   had let a coco2b boot run this long unassisted before. **New,
   durable finding, unrelated to tape:** MAME coco2b in this sandbox
   cannot reach BASIC's "OK" prompt on its own; don't trust any future
   MAME coco2b test that lets the boot run past ~1.5 real/emulated
   seconds without a PC override.

3. **Isolated core-mechanism test (bypasses both problems above):**
   loaded stage1 directly via Lua `mem:write_u8` + `cpu.state["PC"]`
   at tick==20 (same technique as mame_load_run.lua, before MAME's FIRQ
   loop starts), `-cass /tmp/spike_raw.cas` (raw pattern blocks only,
   no namefile). **Real progress**: PC genuinely moves through CASON's
   own bit-timing loop ($A765-$A7BB, the LO-HI/HI-LO transition waits
   and period-timer compares) for the full 49-second run -- this is
   GETBLK/CASON actually processing real toggling bits from the
   emulated cassette, not stuck static. But `DONE_COUNT` never leaves
   0: CASON's 96-consecutive-good-transitions tone lock (`CMPA #-96` at
   $A790) never completes, so it keeps resetting (`LA7BA: CLR CPULWD`)
   and retrying forever. **Root cause not yet found**: most likely
   caswriter's raw leader/data bytes don't decode to a 1200/2400Hz FSK
   waveform matching CASON's period-timer constants (CMPMID=18,
   CMP0=24, CMP1=10 direct-page copies of the ROM table at $A10D) as
   closely as a REAL recorded/dumped CoCo cassette would -- xroar and
   MAME both have mature, long-proven .cas decoders for real dumps, so
   the likelier fault is in this session's understanding of exactly
   what byte-for-byte content a `.cas` file needs (possibly NOT a
   literal 1:1 logical-byte-per-tape-byte stream the way this session
   assumed, despite that assumption matching CLOADM's own field
   offsets when checked against the disassembly). Same xroar isolated
   test (`-run stage1_decb.bin -load-tape spike_raw.cas`) got as far as
   setting the motor-on PIA1 CRA bit ($FF21=$3C, bit3 set) but showed
   NO comparable "is it actually reading transitions" evidence -- worth
   re-checking with PC sampling the way the MAME test did, next
   session.

**Next step, narrowed and cheap to start**: before touching stage1.asm
again, verify caswriter's byte stream against ANY known-good CoCo .cas
dump (none present in this repo -- would need to find one, e.g. a
public-domain CoCo type-in listing's cassette dump, or hand-derive the
exact bit/byte timing xroar's or MAME's decoder expects from their
source, since neither ships source docs on this machine). Until that's
resolved, PHASE 1's software mechanism (ROM vectors, workspace, the
all-RAM toggle dance, the block-copy loop) is believed correct by
inspection and by GETBLK/CASON genuinely running against real tape
signal in MAME, but is NOT yet proven to deliver a full, correct block.

**Phase 2: not started** (correctly gated on Phase 1 fully working,
per the task brief).

Artifacts, all standalone (nothing in target/ or stage_pack.sh touched):
  tools/caswriter/            -- .cas writer + offline verifier (green)
  tools/tapeloader_spike/stage1.asm -- the spike loader (assembles clean)

# ============================================================
# T0227: caswriter checksum bug found by reference diff -- PHASE 1 spike
# now PROVEN end-to-end in XRoar
# ============================================================

Coordinator-directed follow-up to T0226: generate a KNOWN-GOOD .cas with
XRoar's own encoder and diff byte-for-byte against caswriter's output,
rather than guessing further.

## The reference

    xroar -machine coco2bus -rompath source/roms -bas BASIC.ROM \
      -extbas EXTBASIC.ROM -tape-write /tmp/ref.cas \
      -type 'FOR I=0 TO 15:POKE &H3000+I,I:NEXT<CR>CSAVEM"REF",&H3000,&H300F,&H3000<CR>' \
      -timeout 20

Produced a real 559-byte .cas (namefile "REF", one 16-byte data block
0x00..0x0F, EOF). `xxd`+hand-decode confirmed the block layout this
session already had right (leader of $55s, sync $3C, type, len, 15/16
data bytes, checksum, matching CLOADM's own CASBUF+8/+11/+13 field
reads) -- **except the checksum**. Real namefile checksum is $EE;
caswriter produced $DF. Real data-block checksum is $89; caswriter
produced $79. Both off by exactly the block's own length byte.

## The bug and fix

`checksum()` only summed `block_type + data bytes`, dropping the length
byte GETBLK's own disassembly actually adds (`A71B STA BLKTYP; A71F STA
BLKLEN; A721 ADDA BLKTYP` -- i.e. the running total starts as
`len + type`, not just `type`). caswriter's own `parse_blocks()`
reimplementation used the same wrong formula, so this session's earlier
round-trip tests were self-consistently green while producing a byte
stream a real CoCo would reject. Fixed in tools/caswriter/src/lib.rs:
`checksum(block_type, len, data)`. Added two new tests: one pins the
exact $EE/$89 reference values, one does a full byte-for-byte compare of
caswriter's namefile/data/EOF blocks (sync..checksum, leader excluded)
against the bytes extracted from /tmp/ref.cas. `cargo test --release`:
8/8 green.

## End-to-end retry in XRoar: SUCCESS

Rebuilt spike.cas with the fixed checksum. `-trap pc=0x3059
-trap-snap` (spin: is the stage1 label spike ends in) fired within well
under a second of unthrottled emulated time -- unlike the PRE-FIX
attempt, which ran the full 50s timeout without ever reaching it. This
by itself doesn't distinguish success from an error abort (stage1's
error path also branches to `spin`), so memory still needed checking.

**Reloading the trap-snap .sna crashes XRoar** (`XKeysymToKeycode`
SIGSEGV inside a headless/Xvfb-adjacent environment, happens even with
`-ui null` appended after load -- an XRoar snapshot/keyboard-replay bug
under this display setup, unrelated to our own code; not chased
further, out of scope). Worked around it instead: the earlier
documented "`-type`+GDB is a dead end" (NOTES.md, "auto-type BASIC
commands") turns out to be specifically about connecting GDB EARLY,
while `-type`'s tape-timing-sensitive typing/loading is still in
flight -- `gdb_run.py`'s `Target()` halts the CPU the instant a client
connects, and that halt corrupts whatever real-time-sensitive state the
tape read is mid-way through. **Connecting late, after the whole
CLOADM+EXEC+stage1 sequence has already finished and the CPU is idling
in stage1's own harmless `spin: bra spin` loop, works fine** -- this is
a NEW, reusable, narrower version of that old finding, not a
contradiction of it.

    OK_FLAG=1  ERR_FLAG=0  DONE_COUNT=41
    $8000..$9FFF: all 8192 bytes match the expected 0..255 counter
    pattern, byte-for-byte.

**This is the real proof PHASE 1 set out for**: a single CLOADM from
BASIC loads stage1 below $8000 (ROM-writable region), EXEC hands it
control, and stage1 -- entirely on its own, no further BASIC
involvement, same tape, same "one load" from the user's side -- reads
41 more raw blocks via the real ROM's CSRDON/BLKIN vectors and lands
all 8192 of their bytes correctly above $8000 by toggling the SAM's
all-RAM bit per block. Confirmed in XRoar, the user's own emulator.

Load time: this run completes in well under 1 second of XRoar's own
`-no-ratelimit`+fast-tape-loading emulated time -- XRoar accelerates
recognized ROM cassette-read loops the same way for any program, ours
included, so this is not a real-hardware timing measurement. A rough
real-hardware estimate: ~13.6KB of physical tape bytes (8192 payload +
41 blocks x ~133 bytes of leader/framing overhead) at Color BASIC's
standard ~1500 baud is on the order of 70-75 real seconds -- not
measured on real hardware or with `-no-tape-fast`, flagged as an
estimate only.

## MAME coco2b: still does not tone-lock, now ISOLATED to MAME/environment, not caswriter

Re-ran the isolated core-mechanism test (T0226) against BOTH the
fixed spike_raw.cas AND XRoar's own known-good /tmp/ref.cas (attached
directly via `-cass`, no caswriter involved at all). **Neither
completes a single block** -- CASON's tone-lock loop ($A765-$A7BB)
runs for the full 49s test both times, DONE_COUNT stays 0. Since this
reproduces on a file XRoar itself wrote and can read back, **the
blocker is conclusively in MAME's own cassette-read emulation (or how
this sandbox drives it), not in caswriter's output or the ROM
mechanism**. Combined with the already-recorded spurious cartridge-FIRQ
cold-boot loop (T0226), MAME is not a productive path for this feature
in this sandbox; XRoar is proven and is the user's own playtest
emulator anyway (see MEMORY.md "Playtests on their own emulator").

## Status

PHASE 1: DONE. Mechanism proven end-to-end in XRoar with real ROM
cassette I/O, real all-RAM toggling, real tape-timing (fast-loaded).
PHASE 2 (integrate into stage_pack.sh/room36.asm/play.sh): NOT STARTED,
per the coordinator's explicit instruction this round. Next session can
go straight to Phase 2 planning from here.

# ============================================================
# T0228: PHASE 2 -- ONE-tape-image integration, first cut PROVEN
# ============================================================

Goal: ship as ONE tape image (target/room36.cas), ONE CLOADM(+EXEC)
from the user's side, with real headroom for more rooms as the payoff.
This round: prove the mechanism with the tape-only region EMPTY, so the
tape build is behaviourally IDENTICAL to today's -run build -- the
demonstration move (put a real room in the new region, show the margin
grow) is next round, per the coordinator's own scope guard.

## Design decision: stage1 does ALL the loading, CLOADM only loads stage1

Real Color BASIC CLOADM only supports ONE CONTIGUOUS destination range
per file (confirmed from the disassembly, T0226: LA533 "store new start
addr, ONE BLOCK HIGHER" -- CBUFAD auto-increments by the block's own
length, it cannot skip to a different address mid-file). But
target/room36.bin is NOT one contiguous range: it is 19 separate DECB
blocks with small gaps between them (title-screen holes, T0092/T0159) --
real CLOADM cannot reproduce that layout at all.

So CLOADM's job here is reduced to loading a TINY bootstrap
(target/tape_stage1.asm, 392 bytes) at a computed address, EXEC'd
immediately. Stage1 then reads the REST of the tape itself as a stream
of (dest addr, chunk) segments -- one caswriter now derives directly
from room36.bin's own DECB blocks (tools/caswriter's new `parse_decb`),
so this is NOT hand-maintained and cannot go stale independently of the
real build. Segments below $8000 are written DIRECTLY via CBUFAD (no
buffer needed -- exactly what plain CLOADM already relies on); segments
at $8000+ (none yet -- that is next round's demonstration) go through
the proven low-buffer + all-RAM-toggle dance from T0226/T0227. A
sentinel segment (dest=$FFFF) carries the real game's exec address
($0E00, `start`); stage1 jumps there directly -- no return to BASIC.

## Workspace placement (the brief's constraint 2)

The load image now runs $0100..LOAD_END ($7A61 as of this build --
tools/tape_pack.sh computes it fresh every run, does NOT hardcode it).
start: does not touch $7E00 (nibswap, room36.asm's own T0052 note)
until AFTER stage1 hands off control. So [LOAD_END, $7E00) -- 927 bytes
in this build -- is the one gap guaranteed free while stage1 runs, and
is where stage1's OWN code AND its hdr_buf/stagebuf scratch both live
(392 bytes used, 535 spare) -- NOT $2000, which the standalone spike
used and which the real load image now fully occupies.
tools/tape_pack.sh asserts at least 64 bytes of gap exist before even
assembling stage1, and again that stage1's own assembled end doesn't
run into $7E00 -- fails loudly rather than silently corrupting nibswap
if a future room addition ever closes this gap.

No stack setup needed (same as the proven spike): stage1 runs on
whatever S BASIC's EXEC left it as; start: sets its own `lds #$0100`
immediately on entry, unchanged.

## New tools

- `tools/caswriter`: added `parse_decb` (reads any `lwasm --decb` image
  into its (addr,data) segments + exec addr) and `write_segment_stream`
  (chunks each segment to <=255 bytes, writes header+data block pairs,
  terminated by the $FFFF/exec-addr sentinel) -- both covered by new
  tests reimplementing tape_stage1.asm's OWN reader as the oracle
  (`segment_stream_round_trips_a_chunked_decb_image` etc). New binary
  `tools/caswriter/src/bin/tapepack.rs` builds the actual .cas from a
  stage1 binary + a DECB image + optional `--extra-segment addr:file`
  (empty this round). `cargo test --release`: 10/10 green.
- `target/tape_stage1.asm`: the real loader, generalising
  tools/tapeloader_spike's proven mechanism to N segments instead of 1,
  with direct (unbuffered) writes for addr<$8000.
- `tools/tape_pack.sh`: runs tools/stage_pack.sh (room36.bin/.map
  UNCHANGED, still built exactly as today), computes LOAD_END, asserts
  the workspace gap, assembles stage1 at the right address, builds
  target/room36.cas via `tapepack`. `[--extra-segment ADDR:FILE ...]`
  is the hook for next round's demonstration.
- `play.sh --tape`: builds (via tape_pack.sh) and boots
  target/room36.cas with `-load-tape ... -type "CLOADM<CR>EXEC<CR>"`
  instead of `-run target/room36.bin`. Default (`-run`) behaviour is
  byte-for-byte unchanged; `--no-build --tape` re-runs the already-built
  .cas without rebuilding, matching `--no-build`'s existing contract.

## Verified

- **room36.bin (the -run/-load_decb path) is UNTOUCHED**: `tools/tape_pack.sh`
  never edits room36.asm or stage_pack.sh, only reads their output.
  `harness/bootreal.py target/room36.bin` still PASSES (CRA=$b4, 8/8

- **target/room36.cas boots the SAME game, for real, in XRoar**: using
  the T0227 late-GDB-connect technique (connect only after CLOADM+

  early still breaks tape-timing-sensitive work, same finding as

    - PIA0 CRA = $B4 (bootreal.py's own DDR-select-bit check, PASS)
    - TITLE_RAW_BUF ($F2AE) is populated with real (non-zero) tune
      bytes -- proves the EXISTING $8000+ relocate/unpack mechanism
      (T0041, untouched by this work) ran correctly on top of what
      stage1 loaded
    - cur_room=36, dizzy_x=0, dizzy_y=0 -- **identical** to the same
      three reads taken from a plain `-run target/room36.bin` boot in
      the same session (these are the pre-title-dismiss zeroed values,
      not a bug -- new_game hasn't run yet on EITHER path at this
      point, confirmed by running both side by side)
- **Real-hardware load-time estimate**: target/room36.cas is 66558

  own per-chunk leader overhead, see "known inefficiency" below). At

## Known inefficiency, not chased this round

tape_stage1 calls CSRDON (CASON's full ~96-transition tone lock) before
EVERY header AND every data block -- 262 blocks for today's 30644
bytes, each with its own ~128-byte leader (T0226 found the REAL SAVEM
routine does the same, calling WRLDR before every block, so this
matches stock behaviour, just applied at a finer 255-byte grain than
strictly necessary). The real ROM's own CLOADM avoids re-locking
between blocks of the SAME file (GETBLK's own $3C bit-scan is enough
once CASON has locked once) -- tape_stage1 could do the same (call
CSRDON ONCE, then GETBLK repeatedly, only re-locking after a genuine
gap), which would cut the ~35KB of leader overhead dramatically. Left
as a follow-on: this round is about proving the mechanism and the
headroom win, not tape efficiency, and a slow-but-correct load is a
strictly better starting point than a fast-but-wrong one.

(or wherever), move one existing staged room block into it, and report
the holes-sum-minus-title-stream-needed margin before/after (NOT the
double-counted "Delivery budget" line, per the brief) -- the mechanism
to do this is already in place (`--extra-segment`, the addr>=$8000
staged-copy path in tape_stage1.asm), untested with real (non-empty)
content.

# ============================================================
# T0229: PART A -- real load-time fix (66558 -> 33282 bytes)
# ============================================================

The .cas was 66558 bytes against a 30744-byte raw image (2.16x) because
tape_stage1 called CSRDON (CASON's full ~96-transition tone lock)
before EVERY one of 262 blocks, each with its own ~128-byte leader.
Real Color BASIC CLOADM does NOT do this: the disassembly (T0226,
LA52B/LA52E) shows CASON is called ONCE per file, then the read loop
calls GETBLK alone for every subsequent block -- GETBLK's own $3C
bit-scan is enough to find the next block without re-locking tone.

**Confirmed the real inter-block gap directly**, not assumed: generated
a second real reference with xroar's own encoder
(`CSAVEM"REF",&H3000,&H3257,&H3000`, a 600-byte range, which CSAVEM
itself splits into 255+255+90-byte data blocks) and measured the exact
byte count between blocks. The namefile block gets a full ~234-byte
leader; every block after that -- data block 2, data block 3, EOF --
has **exactly 2 bytes** of $55 before its sync, not a fresh leader.

**Fix**: `tools/caswriter` gained `INTER_BLOCK_GAP = 2` (documented with
the measurement above); `write_ml_file` and `write_segment_stream` now
give a full leader ONLY to the very first block they emit, and
`INTER_BLOCK_GAP` to everything after. `target/tape_stage1.asm` now
calls `jsr [CSRDON_VEC]` exactly ONCE, before the loop, matching the
write side. New test `only_the_first_block_gets_a_full_leader` pins
this exactly (walks the stream sequentially like GETBLK does, asserts
leader length is the full value for block 0 and exactly
`INTER_BLOCK_GAP` for every block after). `cargo test --release`:
11/11 green. Also confirmed max block size is 255 throughout (already
true since the previous round's tapepack default).

**Result**: target/room36.cas is now 33282 bytes against 30744 raw --
**8.3% overhead**, comfortably inside the ~15% target (down from 116%
overhead before this fix).

**Re-verified identical boot** (same checks as T0228, late-GDB-connect):
PIA0 CRA=$B4, TITLE_RAW_BUF populated, cur_room=36/dizzy_x=0/dizzy_y=0
-- unchanged.

**Real-hardware load-time**: attempted direct measurement with
`-no-tape-fast` (no `-no-ratelimit`, i.e. real 6809-clock-equivalent
timing) twice, with 250s and then 510s budgets -- **neither run
completed**: the trap on `start` ($0E00) never fired, `-timeout` killed
the process both times. This is itself the honest, useful data point:
naive Kansas-City-standard math (33282 bytes x 8 bits / 1500 baud) gives
~178s, but the REAL emulated load takes longer than 510s -- more than
2.8x the naive estimate. Not chased further this round (each attempt
costs 250-500+ real seconds; a third, longer attempt was judged not
worth the time against the session budget) -- worth knowing for a
future round: either CASON's tone-lock phase costs much more real time
under `-no-tape-fast` than the bulk data-rate math accounts for, or
something about the `-type` CLOADM/EXEC interaction adds real delay
before the tape read even starts. **Report the range honestly: ~178s
theoretical minimum, empirically MORE than 510s (>8.5 minutes)** -- do
not quote the theoretical number alone as if it were measured.

# ============================================================
# T0229: PART B -- analysed, NOT attempted this round (large, per scope guard)
# ============================================================

Goal: move one existing room's staged data (or a whole staged block)
out of framebuffer packing into the tape-only region, and show the
REAL margin -- (sum of tools/title_holes.py's hole sizes) minus
(TITLE_LZ_LEN+TITLE_MUSIC_LEN+TITLE_EXTRA_LEN+TITLE_EXTRA2_LEN from
target/title_frags.asm), NOT the double-counting "Delivery budget"
line -- grow.

**The real margin today, computed correctly (not just quoted)**:

    holes (tools/title_holes.py, this build):
      732 + 3130 + 267 + 798 + 689 + 1135 = 6751
    title streams actually consumed (target/title_frags.asm):
      TITLE_LZ_LEN 2666 + TITLE_MUSIC_LEN 600 + TITLE_EXTRA_LEN 332
      + TITLE_EXTRA2_LEN 2226 = 5824
    REAL MARGIN = 6751 - 5824 = 927

This matches mktitle's own "927 bytes of hole space spare" and
stage_pack.sh's "927 bytes free gap2" lines exactly -- the 927 number
was already correct and already visible; the "1883 packed bytes"
Delivery-budget line is the one that double-counts (framebuffer spare
IS one of the six holes, not a separate pool -- see T0159).

## Why moving a room out of A/B is NOT a small change

Blocks A and B are the ONLY framebuffer-staged (packed) blocks -- C and
D are already delivered via the title's load-time holes, not via a
framebuffer, so they're not eligible "move it to tape instead" targets
(they'd gain nothing; they don't compete for framebuffer space today).

A and B are each a SINGLE packed LZ stream covering MULTIPLE rooms'
combined raw data (7877 and 8468 raw bytes respectively -- more than
one room's worth each). The packed stream decompresses as ONE
contiguous run starting at a fixed address ($8000 for A, R9800_DEST for
B); every room's placements inside it are addressed relative to where
lz_unpack puts the FIRST byte. Removing ONE room's bytes from the
MIDDLE of that stream would shift every room after it in the same
block by however many bytes were removed -- there is no way to excise a
single room without either re-deriving every subsequent room's absolute
addresses, or leaving a deliberate "hole" inside the packed stream
(defeating the point, since LZ packing already assumes a contiguous
input).

**The only clean cut is a WHOLE staged block** (matches the brief's own
"or the whole of one staged block if cleaner"), delivering it raw,
already-unpacked, directly to its own known resident address
(`R9800_DEST` for block B, computed and exported by stage_pack.sh
already) via `--extra-segment`. That is a real, coded design, but it
requires touching the CORE, deliberately fragile build pipeline in
THREE places, not one:

1. **room36.asm's STAGE_LZ conditional** (`RELOC_BOOT_BYTES`, ~line
   670): remove the second `jsr lz_unpack` (block B, R9800_DEST) from
   the STAGE_LZ branch (bytes already resident via tape, courtesy of
   tape_stage1's own all-RAM-toggle segment write -- BEFORE `start:`
   even runs). The `else` branch (STAGE_GEN pass 1, raw) would need the
   SAME removal for a different reason (block B's bytes shouldn't stage
   into the $6000 framebuffer window during the raw pass either, if
   it's not going to be packed from there at all). **Both branches
   carry a byte-count parity guard specifically added (T0153) because a
   past session got bitten by exactly this class of drift** -- this
   change touches precisely the code that guard exists to protect.

2. **stage_pack.sh's packing/hole computation**: block B's raw bytes
   (`/tmp/stage_b.bin`) currently feed `lzpack` -> `target/staged_b_lz.asm`
   -> the $6000 framebuffer window; removing that leaves framebuffer
   B's ENTIRE 6144-byte window free (not just its small "spare"), which
   `tools/title_holes.py` needs to report as a MUCH bigger hole (today
   it only credits the small unused REMAINDER of the packed size, not
   the whole window) -- a real change to that script's own hole
   arithmetic, which every other hole depends on being right (its own
   header note: "the assembler guard fails loudly if this script's
   holes turn out wrong", i.e. it is trusted to be exact).

3. **tools/tape_pack.sh**: add the `--extra-segment R9800_DEST:stage_b.bin`
   wiring, sourced from stage_pack.sh's own intermediate
   `/tmp/stage_b.bin` (already produced, unchanged) -- this part alone
   IS small; it's (1) and (2) that carry the real risk.

Given this touches the same guarded, historically fragile code paths
the project's own NOTES repeatedly flag (T0153's parity guard exists
BECAUSE of a prior multi-session bug in this exact area; T0107 and
T0148 are two more examples of subtle bugs in this same pipeline), and
given the round's own scope guard ("stop after A if B turns out large,
and report"), **this was analysed but NOT attempted this round**. The
mechanism to deliver it once room36.asm/stage_pack.sh are adjusted
already exists and needs no further design (`--extra-segment`, the
addr>=$8000 staged-copy path in tape_stage1.asm, both already coded and
proven in Part A/T0228) -- what remains is the two guarded,
higher-risk edits above, which deserve their own dedicated round with a
full room36.asm/stage_pack.sh rebuild-and-diff safety net (byte-compare
target/room36.bin before/after on every unrelated room, not just a
smoke boot) rather than being folded into an already-long round.

**Next round, concretely**: (1) remove block B's `jsr lz_unpack` +
matching `else`-branch raw-stage skip in room36.asm, re-deriving
RELOC_BOOT_BYTES for both branches; (2) teach tools/title_holes.py that
block B's framebuffer window is now a full 6144-byte hole rather than
its packed remainder; (3) wire `--extra-segment` in tools/tape_pack.sh;
(4) rebuild, recompute the margin with the formula above, verify it
grew by roughly (6144 - previous packed-B-in-window-size); (5) verify a
room actually stored in former-block-B still loads correctly (late-GDB
room warp or a walk-in, per the brief) in the TAPE build specifically
-- and decide + state clearly whether target/room36.bin (the -run
build) keeps carrying block B the OLD way (framebuffer-staged, as
today) or is retired in favour of the tape build for anything that
depends on this room, since -run has no tape-only delivery mechanism at
all.

# ============================================================
# T0230: TAPE-ONLY MEMORY REGION -- proven end-to-end with real
# content (rooms 74/75), separate from room36.bin (the -run build)
# ============================================================

Goal (proving step for a later full memory-map reorganisation): put NEW
rooms into a TAPE-ONLY region above $8000 that the tape loader
(target/tape_stage1.asm, T0228/T0229) delivers directly at final
address -- no framebuffer staging, no LZ block A/B, no title-hole
gather. Rooms 74 (THE GIANT BEANSTALK, 58+16) and 75 (COMPLEX CLOUD
ROUTE, 59+16) -- the smallest walkable unbuilt rooms, both chaining off
already-built neighbours -- prove it with real content.

## Design

Discovered that [IMAGE_END, CODE_DEST) -- the span between the packed
room image (blocks A/B/C) and the staged resident code block (block D)
-- is ALREADY a real, final $8000+ address range that room36.asm
computes but never uses (there's a guard that just checks it doesn't
overflow). Both ends are derived, not hardcoded, and identical in
either STAGE_LZ pass (see room36.asm's own comments on why). That made
this a small, additive change:

- **room36.asm**: new `TAPE_ROOMS` flag (default 0, same `ifndef`
  pattern as `STAGE_LZ`). A new block, unconditional on STAGE_LZ but
  gated on TAPE_ROOMS, `org`s DIRECTLY at IMAGE_END (no `phase` needed
  -- IMAGE_END is already the real final address, same reasoning as
  block D's `org CODE_DEST`) and includes room74_data.asm/
  room75_data.asm. Two guards: `tape_room_staged_end` must not pass
  CODE_DEST, and must start EXACTLY at IMAGE_END. room_desc_table
  gets `r74_room_desc`/`r75_room_desc` appended, also gated on
  TAPE_ROOMS. Did NOT touch RELOC_BOOT_BYTES or anything inside the
  STAGE_LZ if/else's boot-relocate branches -- this block lives
  entirely after that code resolves.
- **tools/regen_art.sh**: rooms 74/75 generated self-contained (no
  `--shared-sprites` -- neither has any actor/pickup placements, both
  pure beanstalk/cloud-platform scenery, checked against
  extracted/rooms.json's `things` list before deciding), same
  reasoning as rooms 52/53/67/84/85's own self-contained choice
  (plenty of headroom up here, dedup buys nothing).
- **tools/tape_pack.sh**: ONE extra `lwasm` pass after
  tools/stage_pack.sh, reusing every artifact it just generated
  (staged_syms.asm, image_end_lz.asm, title_frags.asm, title_lz.asm)
  with `-DTAPE_ROOMS=1` added -- produces target/room36_tape.bin/.map,
  which is room36.bin PLUS the new block (verified: below IMAGE_END,
  both images carry the same block count and exactly +4 bytes, the
  two new room_desc_table `fdb` entries -- not byte-identical, because
  that 4-byte growth in resident code re-addresses everything after
  it, which is expected, not drift). `--decb` for the `.cas` build now
  points at room36_tape.bin instead of room36.bin -- no
  `--extra-segment` wiring needed at all: tape_stage1.asm's existing
  addr>=$8000 staged-copy path already treats ANY DECB block up there
  the same way, whichever image it came from.

## Which build carries what

- **target/room36.bin** (`tools/stage_pack.sh`, unchanged, TAPE_ROOMS
  defaults to 0): exactly today's 31-room game. Verified BYTE-FOR-BYTE
  identical to the pre-T0230 build (rebuilt room36.asm at HEAD in a
  scratch copy, ran the identical stage_pack.sh, `cmp` clean). Rooms
  74/75 do not exist in this build at all -- absent from
  room_desc_table, not merely unreachable.
- **target/room36_tape.bin** (`tools/tape_pack.sh`, TAPE_ROOMS=1): the
  DECB image harnesses load directly (see harness/jumptrace.lua's new
  `load_decb`, below). Carries rooms 74/75 at $C159..$C424, in
  addition to everything room36.bin has (re-addressed by +4 bytes from
  IMAGE_END downward, see above).
- **target/room36.cas** (`tools/tape_pack.sh`): the real tape image --
  ONE CLOADM+EXEC from the user's side, built from room36_tape.bin.
  34046 bytes (up from T0229's 33282 for the empty-region proof, +764
  for rooms 74/75's own segment framing).

## Harness: loading an image with $8000+ content

`harness/jumptrace.lua`'s `load_decb` now pokes `$FFDF` (all-RAM) once,
before writing the FIRST DECB block whose address is >=$8000, and
simply leaves it engaged -- this is not a harness-only shortcut, it
matches the REAL tape path exactly (tape_stage1.asm's own header:
"Leaves all-RAM ENGAGED after the last block"), and room36.asm's
`start:` re-asserts `sta $ffdf` itself as its very first instruction
regardless (T0153-guarded boot code, unmodified), so entering already
all-RAM is the same state a real tape boot hands off in. Verified no
clobber: the new region sits strictly inside [IMAGE_END, CODE_DEST),
which `start:`'s own relocate loop (blocks A/B only) and the title/
scratch chain (BANNER_BUF and everything above it, all >= CODE_DEST)
never touch.

Scoped to jumptrace.lua only this round (what T0230's own verification
needed) -- the pattern is documented inline as reusable if another
harness needs it later. Did NOT wire rooms 74/75 into
tools/derive_cmask.py's BUILT_ROOMS / harness/cmaskverify.lua's
ROOMS/DUMP_ROOMS (touch points 4-6 of T0222's six) -- those lists are
about masks for rooms 74/75 in the same "PASS" sense as the 27 already
verified, which needs either a shared BUILT_ROOMS across both builds
(the -run build doesn't have these rooms) or a second list; left
undone, see below.

- No attempt to push rooms 74/75 through the shared sprite pool (they
  were made self-contained) -- moot at 7050 bytes still free; would
  only matter once this region is much fuller.

# T0231 (RESOLVED) -- title-on-game-over for the tape build: root cause
# found and fixed (2026-09-27)
#
# UPDATE, same day, after a top-tier diagnosis: root cause found and
# fixed. tools/tape_pack.sh used to build the tape image with ONE extra
# STAGE_LZ=1 lwasm pass that REUSED the packed staged blocks (A/B/C/D,
# title) and target/staged_syms.asm produced by tools/stage_pack.sh's
# -run build. Those staged blocks (dragon/croc/rat/troll/armorog code,
# sound_data.asm's tune tables) reference a handful of RESIDENT globals
# BY NAME (lives, killed, kill_dizzy_msg, actor_ram, cur_room, dizzy_x/
# y/floor, force_redraw, keyflags, play_breath, troll_bribed) -- those
# names get resolved to ABSOLUTE ADDRESSES and BAKED into the raw bytes
# during PASS 1 (the RAW/STAGE_GEN measurement pass), then LZ-packed;
# pass 2 never re-assembles those files, it only unpacks the same bytes
# at CODE_DEST (T0148's own rule: staged code may not reference a
# low-memory label that pass 2 can move). Phase 1's resident changes
# (show_title_resident et al, gated on TAPE_ROOMS) shift EVERY resident
# symbol's address once TAPE_ROOMS=1 (confirmed: kill_dizzy_msg $2B89
# in room36.map vs $2B8D in room36_tape.map; lives $2299 vs $229D;
# killed $2EFE vs $2F08) -- but the reused staged blocks had been baked
# against the -RUN build's addresses, so in the tape build they called/
# read stale addresses. Symptom (found via MAME single-frame tracing,
# not guesswork): forcing lives=0/killed=1 on room36_tape.bin left the
# CPU spinning in play_tone/pt_step/pts_phase (the shared tune player)
# for 8900+ frames instead of ~80, because a staged routine's baked
# reference resolved somewhere it shouldn't have. T0230's own +4-byte
# room_desc_table growth had the exact same latent bug -- just never
# exercised, because nothing in that round poked lives/killed on the
# tape build.
#
# THE FIX, permanent rule: **never reuse one build's staged artifacts
# in another build.** tools/stage_pack.sh is now a COMPLETE, INDEPENDENT
# pipeline per value of TAPE_ROOMS -- run once with TAPE_ROOMS=0
# (-run build) and once with TAPE_ROOMS=1 (tape build), writing
# "_tape"-suffixed artifacts for the latter (staged_syms_tape.asm,
# image_end_lz_tape.asm, staged_a_lz_tape.asm/staged_b_lz_tape.asm,
# title_lz_tape.asm, title_frags_tape.asm) so the two runs cannot
# collide on disk, and room36.asm/boot_code.asm `include` whichever set
# TAPE_ROOMS selects. tools/tape_pack.sh now runs `TAPE_ROOMS=0
# tools/stage_pack.sh` then `TAPE_ROOMS=1 tools/stage_pack.sh` instead
# of its own extra reusing lwasm pass. tools/title_holes.py takes a
# path-prefix argument for the same reason (holes are measured from the
# RAW pass, which now differs by TAPE_ROOMS). memaudit.py (which only
# understands the ordinary boot-time load path, not the tape-only
# region's separate delivery mechanism) is now scoped to the -run build
# only -- T0230 never ran it against room36_tape.bin either, for the
# same reason.
#
# GUARD added (tools/stage_pack.sh, runs for BOTH builds): after each
# build, parse the RAW pass's map and this build's own final map, and
# assert the curated list of resident globals staged code references by
# name resolve IDENTICALLY in both -- this is exactly the class of bug
# above, caught the moment pass 1 and pass 2 (of the SAME build) ever
# disagree again, not just across builds. `bootstrap seed files`
# (target/*_tape.asm) were copied once from the non-suffixed originals
# to get the first-ever tape build past the same chicken-and-egg
# bootstrap the -run build already has (title_frags.asm etc. are
# checked into git for exactly this reason) -- committed alongside this
# fix.
#
# tools/tape_pack.sh's own cross-build sanity check (below IMAGE_END,
# room36_tape.bin vs room36.bin) used to assert an EXACT byte delta;
# now that packing is independent per build, the packed size of blocks
# A-D can legitimately differ by a few bytes between builds (different
# baked-in addresses compress slightly differently), so this is now a
# looser bound (block count must match; delta must be a small positive
# number) rather than an exact constant.
#
# VERIFIED after the fix:
# - `tools/stage_pack.sh` (TAPE_ROOMS=0, default): room36.bin is
#   BYTE-FOR-BYTE IDENTICAL to a from-HEAD rebuild (same cmp method as
#   before the fix). The new staged-code resident-symbol guard passes
#   (12 names checked). `harness/bootreal.py target/room36.bin`: PASS.
#   `harness/jumptrace.lua` (room 36, no movement): floor=1 as before.
#   `harness/cmaskverify.lua`: **27 PASS, 0 FAIL, 3 SKIP** -- identical
#   to the T0222/T0230 baseline.
# - `tools/tape_pack.sh` (both stage_pack.sh runs + the tape-only region
#   + tape_stage1 + room36.cas): assembles clean, run TWICE in a row.
#   The new guard passes for the tape build too (12 names, pass 1 and
#   this build's own final map agree).
# - `harness/gameover_tape.lua` against target/room36_tape.bin/.map:
#   **GAMEOVER_TAPE PASS (rounds=1)** -- both the first AND a forced
#   SECOND game-over cycle show `title_frame_match=true(bad=0)` (the
#   redrawn framebuffer matches the source title image exactly),
#   `reset=true` (fresh lives=2/coins=0/inv0=0 after SPACE), and
#   `machine=true` (DP=0, stack back near $0100) -- no state leak across
#   repeated title entries, which is what the user's own historical
#   "flicker/crashes after restarting" report (pre-T0146) would have
#   caught.
# - `harness/jumptrace.lua` on target/room36_tape.bin, no movement:
#   room 74 lands on floor=1 at y=176, room 75 at floor=1 at y=160 --
#   unchanged from T0230's own findings.
#
# Files changed for the fix: tools/stage_pack.sh (parametrized by
# TAPE_ROOMS/SUF/OUT_BIN/OUT_MAP, the new guard), tools/tape_pack.sh
# (two independent stage_pack.sh calls, looser cross-build sanity
# check), tools/title_holes.py (path-prefix argument), target/room36.asm
# and target/boot_code.asm (conditional `if TAPE_ROOMS` includes for
# every artifact that now has a "_tape" twin).

## Goal (PHASE 1 of a two-phase brief, PHASE 2 -- 17 more rooms -- not
started, see "Scope note" at the end)

X-ALL.TXT's `quitted` does `jp titlescreen`; T0146 replaced that with a
text GAME OVER box, specifically because the packed title+music stream
(TITLE_LZ_BUF) had to stay resident the whole game to make a second
`show_title` possible, and freeing it bought 3804 bytes. T0230's
tape-only region ([IMAGE_END, CODE_DEST), gated on TAPE_ROOMS) makes
that trade unnecessary for the TAPE build specifically: keep a SECOND,
independent resident copy of the packed title-image+music stream up
there, and restore the real title-on-game-over for TAPE_ROOMS=1 only.
The -run build keeps T0146's box, byte-for-byte, unchanged.

## What's built

- **tools/roompack/src/bin/mktitle.rs**: new `--resident-out PATH` flag,
  always emitted (harmless for the -run build, which never includes the
  file) -- packed title-image + packed music, concatenated as ONE
  contiguous blob (no hole-splitting), i.e. `packed[..title_len+music_len]`
  from the SAME `packed` vector the existing hole-splitter already builds,
  captured before `--extra`/`--extra2` (block C/D, deliberately NOT
  included -- see below) are appended. Writes `TITLE_RESIDENT_LZ`
  (label) / `TITLE_RESIDENT_LEN` (equ).
- **tools/stage_pack.sh**: mktitle's call now always passes
  `--resident-out target/title_resident_lz.asm`.
- **target/room36.asm**: TAPE_ROOMS block now `include`s
  `title_resident_lz.asm` FIRST (before rooms 74/75), so it never moves
  as more rooms are appended. Uses 3266 bytes (TITLE_LZ_LEN 2666 +
  TITLE_MUSIC_LEN 600) of the tape-only region.
- **target/boot_code.asm**: `show_title`'s body now has a new label,
  `ti_transpose`, placed right after the title+music `lz_unpack` calls
  and the `unpack_c`/`unpack_d` calls -- i.e. AFTER block C/D unpack, at
  the start of the column-major transpose. A new routine,
  `show_title_resident` (TAPE_ROOMS only), copies the resident blob into
  `TITLE_LZ_BUF` (exactly where the boot gather loop would have left
  it), redoes the SAME two `lz_unpack` calls (title, then music) show_title
  itself does, and `jmp`s straight to `ti_transpose` -- deliberately
  skipping `unpack_c`/`unpack_d`: those are boot-once (RC_DEST/CODE_DEST
  already hold live resident data/code by the time a game-over can
  happen) and must not run again mid-game.
- **target/text_src/gameplay.asm** (regenerate with `tools/dte build`,
  NEVER hand-edit `target/gameplay.asm`): `gp_ud_gameover` gets a new
  `if TAPE_ROOMS` branch, first: `jsr show_title_resident / jmp
  new_game`. Falls through to T0146's unchanged `msg_gameover` path
  otherwise (both are ASSEMBLED in the tape build -- the old path is
  dead code there, harmless, see the byte-accounting note below).
- **tools/tape_pack.sh**: the below-IMAGE_END sanity check originally
  asserted an exact +60-byte delta (T0230's `room_desc_table` entries
  (4) + the `if TAPE_ROOMS` branch in `gp_ud_gameover`/
  `show_title_resident` (56), confirmed by hand via a parsed before/
  after `cmp` of the two images' DECB blocks). **Superseded by the
  staged-artifact-reuse fix below**: once each build packs its staged
  blocks independently, that byte count is no longer a fixed constant
  (see the ROOT CAUSE section) -- now a loose bound (same block count,
  small positive delta), measured at +64 bytes after the fix.
- **harness/gameover_tape.lua** (new): gameover.lua's own scenario
  adapted for `target/room36_tape.bin` (T0230's all-RAM-aware
  `load_decb`), extended to run the WHOLE cycle TWICE (catch state
  leaks across repeated title entries, the user's own historical
  "flicker/crashes after restarting" report) and to assert the box goes
  STRAIGHT to the title (no second msg_gameover box, unlike the -run
  build). **PASS after the staged-artifact-reuse fix below -- see
  "Verified" and the ROOT CAUSE section.**

## Verified

1. **room36.bin (the -run build) is BYTE-FOR-BYTE UNCHANGED.** `cmp`
   against a fresh HEAD rebuild in an isolated `git worktree add
   --detach` (source/extracted/research symlinked in, gitignored
   `target/*_data.asm` etc. copied from the main tree since they don't
   depend on this change) -- clean, twice (once before starting, once
   at the end after all edits). `tools/stage_pack.sh` run twice in a
   row also produces an identical `room36.bin`.
2. **The tape build assembles cleanly** (`tools/tape_pack.sh`, run
   twice in a row): 19 DECB blocks below IMAGE_END both sides (now +64
   bytes vs room36.bin, not the +60 first measured -- see the ROOT
   CAUSE section: once each build packs its staged blocks
   independently, the packed size can differ by a few bytes even for
   equivalent content, so this check is a loose bound now, not an exact
   constant); tape-only region $C159..$DFAE (7765 bytes), title-resident
   blob + rooms 74/75 use 3981 bytes (3266 + 715), 3784 bytes free.
3. **`tools/roompack/mktitle`'s round-trip assert already covers the
   resident blob** (it's a slice of the SAME `packed` vector that
   `roompack::lz::unpack(&packed) == cm` already checks for the title
   half; the music half has its own existing assert). Not re-verified
   as its own standalone round-trip -- would be cheap to add if this
   session's bug turns out to be somewhere else entirely.

## Historical: the bug hunt before the fix (kept for the trail)

This subsection is the RECORD of how the bug above was found -- kept
because the reasoning (what was ruled out, and why the leading
hypothesis was a red herring) is exactly what a future similar bug will
need, not because it is still open. **Resolved, see the ROOT CAUSE
section above.**

Forcing game-over on `target/room36_tape.bin` (MAME, `harness/jumptrace`
-style all-RAM-aware `load_decb`, boot past the title, poke `lives=0`
`killed=1` directly -- gameover.lua's own proven method) does **not**
cleanly reach `show_title_resident`'s title. Instead:

- A **clean, isolated pre-Phase-1 tape build** (T0230 HEAD, rebuilt in
  the same worktree with the SAME poke) reaches the (old, `msg_gameover`)
  box in **~60 frames**, exactly like the -run build. The bug is new
  this round.
- After Phase 1's changes, the SAME poke on `target/room36_tape.bin`
  takes **~9000 frames (150 real seconds)** to reach anything resembling
  a message box (measured with a robust `in_death_box()` check --
  PC or a stack return address inside
  `[msg_wait_dismiss,fb_stablekeys)` -- 78 frames on the -run build,
  8911 on the tape build, same poke, same frame).
- Fine-grained tracing (PC/Y/S every frame) during the hang shows the
  CPU genuinely executing `play_tone`/`pt_wave`/`pt_delaylp` (all
  unmodified, shared code used by every sound effect) with **Y cycling
  repeatedly through `tune1_notes`'s own 89-byte span** ($EA6E-$EAC7,
  the "new life" jingle `gp_ud_respawn`/`new_game` play) -- not
  `tune2_notes` (the death tune) as the code path would suggest. A
  stack walk during the hang resolves a return address to
  `gp_ud_respawn+0x39` (right after `jsr play_tune` there), meaning
  `lda lives / beq gp_ud_gameover` did NOT branch even though the very
  same frame's read-back (via the SAME symbol table) confirms
  `lives=0` was written and observed as 0 immediately after the poke.
- **Ruled out** (each independently confirmed, see this session's
  scratch probes, not kept): the tune tables (`tune1_notes`/`tune2_notes`)
  are byte-identical between the -run and tape builds, including a real
  `$0000` terminator; `CODE_DEST`/`update_dragon`/`tune2_notes`/
  `tune1_notes` all resolve to the IDENTICAL absolute address in both
  builds' own `.map`s; the compiled `ldd #tune1_notes` bytes (`cc ea
  6e`) and the compiled `lda lives`/`beq` bytes (`b6 22 9d` / `27 06`)
  are exactly what the source says and exactly match the -run build's
  equivalent instructions; no natural (hazard-triggered) death happens
  in the 400 idle frames before the poke in either build; IRQs are
  masked (`orcc #$50`) so this cannot be async corruption. The evidence
  is consistent with `gp_ud_respawn` genuinely running with `lives`
  read as nonzero DESPITE the poke reading back as 0 one frame earlier
  -- not yet explained.
- **Leading, unconfirmed hypothesis**: `show_title_resident`'s own
  `lz_unpack` of the music blob writes into `MIX3_BUF` = `TITLE_RAW_BUF`
  = `CUR_ROOM_CMASK` (T0147's designed-safe aliasing, but ONLY proven
  safe for the BOOT-time call, where "nothing reads the mask between
  boot and the first new_game" -- see T0147's own header). Called
  MID-GAME instead (from `gp_ud_gameover`, after a room has already been
  played), that mask is the LIVE current-room collision data, and
  whatever runs between the `jsr show_title_resident` returning and
  `new_game` reloading it fresh has not been audited this round for
  whether it reads the mask/`ROOM_PLACE_SORTED`/`ATTR_CELLS` in that
  window. Not confirmed: the stack evidence above shows `gp_ud_respawn`
  running, which is a DIFFERENT code path that doesn't call
  `show_title_resident` at all, so this may be a red herring -- or a
  LATER cycle's corruption from an EARLIER `show_title_resident` call
  feeding back into a subsequent `new_game`/`load_room`. Needs a
  session with room to single-step (MAME's own debugger console, not
  scripted probes) rather than more probe-script iterations, which is
  what consumed this round's budget without resolving it.

## What's built

- **tools/regen_art.sh**: rooms 74/75 (T0230) re-generated against the
  shared sprite pool via `--shared-sprites-reuse-only` (see T0232's own
  commit) instead of self-contained. The REMAINING walkable rooms --
  63,91,92,45,48,49,94,89,41,73,88,93,40,46,31,47 (smallest/most-
  connected first, per the brief) -- generated the same way: reuse-only
  against the pool, no `--frame-table`, no `--actors`/`--actor-rooms`.
  **Room 77 (THE ACTIVE VOLCANO) is NOT built**: roompack's water-tile
  emitter panics unconditionally ("water tiles at differing y-phases
  need per-tile variants") because its lava tiles don't share one y%4
  phase -- a pre-existing limitation (every water room built before now
  happened to be single-phase), not something this round introduced or
  fixed. Tried dropping `--colour-water-blue` first (the panic isn't
  gated on that flag); would need roompack's water-animation emitter
  taught to support per-tile phase variants, a separate tool change.
- **No actor wiring, by design**: extracted/actors.json has real actor
  entries for several of these rooms (see the table below) -- none are
  wired into `--actor-rooms`. Doing so would grow `actor_data.asm`,
  RESIDENT low memory shared by BOTH builds (same coupling class as
  `shared_sprites_data.asm`, T0231/T0232's own finding) -- the -run
  build's byte-identity to HEAD is the hard constraint, and there is no
  way to grow a table both builds share without touching both. Every
  actor-shaped placement in these rooms therefore renders as ordinary
  static scenery (visible, correctly positioned, but inert: no
  movement, no pickup, no trigger).
- **target/room36.asm**'s TAPE_ROOMS block gained the 16 rooms' own
  `include`s, appended after rooms 74/75 (which stay first, per T0231's
  own placement note).
- **tools/derive_cmask.py / harness/cmaskverify.lua**: both gained a
  `CMASK_TAPE=1` switch (env var) that selects the tape-only region's
  own room list (`TAPE_BUILT_ROOMS`/`TAPE_ROOMS_LIST`: the 18 rooms
  above, in the same order both files use so the flat
  `--dump-expected` blob and the Lua slice-by-position agree) and their

  room), instead of the -run build's BUILT_ROOMS/ROOMS/POS. `harness/
  cmaskverify.lua`'s `load_decb` is now the all-RAM-aware version
  (T0230's own pattern, copied from harness/jumptrace.lua) so it can
  load a DECB image with $8000+ content.
