## NOT verified -- cmaskverify (CMASK_TAPE=1) is not clean

`CMASK_TAPE=1 python3 tools/derive_cmask.py --dump-expected
target/cmask_expected_tape.bin` then `CMASK_TAPE=1 CMASK_EXPECTED=...
harness/cmaskverify.lua` against room36_tape.bin: **0 PASS, 15 FAIL, 3
SKIP** (rooms 91/92/73 drifted off their spawn edge before the settle
window finished -- itself informative, not necessarily wrong, see
cmaskverify.lua's own SKIP semantics). The FAIL sizes vary widely (30
bytes for room 63 up to 695 for room 31), and are NOT the same failure
mode as a broken build:

- **jumptrace already proved the floor Dizzy actually stands on is
  correct** for every one of these rooms (see above) -- a per-cell
  mask byte can differ from the OFFLINE ("full") derivation while the
  PLAYABLE floor is still right, exactly the situation the -run build's
  own `KNOWN_DEV` table already documents for rooms 51/60/84 ("the
  DERIVATION is the one that is wrong... matches the REAL GAME better,"
  checked against the ZX log). Several of the new rooms hit
  `regen_art.sh`'s own "pixel_x off the left edge, skipped, not
  clamped" warning during generation (45, 48, 58/60/94/40's siblings) --
  the exact mechanism KNOWN_DEV catalogues, just not yet catalogued
  for THESE rooms.
- Room 63's diff (the smallest, most tractable one) is a vertical
  streak of `$0c` where `$00` is expected, at the same column-byte
  across several consecutive rows -- consistent with an inherited-
  attribute edge case (a placement's dull-bit inheriting from the wrong
  neighbour in source order at a room boundary), not a gross derivation
  failure.
- **NOT triaged room-by-room this round** -- that is real remaining
  work (per-room ASCII diff via `python3 tools/derive_cmask.py --room
  N --map`, then either accept it as a new `KNOWN_DEV` entry -- checked

# T0233-fix -- root cause of cmaskverify's "0 PASS" (a top-tier
# diagnosis, not trial and error), plus room 77 (2026-09-27)

## Root cause: EVERY room_placements entry is a frame_table INDEX, not
## just actors'

Coordinator's own hint ("too uniform to be per-room deviation") was
right and led straight to it. `tools/roompack/src/main.rs`'s own
comment (T0167, ~line 1388): every `room_placements` entry -- scenery
AND actors -- stores a 1-byte INDEX into the resident `frame_table`,
resolved to a real sprite pointer only at room-load time
(`derive_room_cmask`/`rd_sortplaces`, room36.asm). `--frame-table` was
skipped for all 18 tape rooms (T0232/T0233's own reasoning: "only
actors need it") -- WRONG. Without it, each room's roompack invocation
assigned indices 0,1,2... from a FRESH, ISOLATED numbering with zero
relation to the real, shared `frame_table` those indices get looked up
in at runtime -- every placement resolved to essentially a RANDOM
sprite (whatever the -run build's own rooms happened to put at that
index), at a random size, in the wrong place. Confirmed directly:
dumped room 63's runtime CUR_ROOM_CMASK vs the expected ASCII map --
expected a clean 48px platform, got an 8px sliver in the middle of it.

Also found and fixed along the way, confirmed as a real, separate bug
(not the frame_table one): rooms 63/91/92/45/48/49/94/89/41/73/88/93/
40/46/31/47 (all 16 added this round) had NO entry in `room_desc_table`
at all -- T0222's own "six touch points" list, touch point 3, missed
when they were wired in. `load_room`'s `lr_scan` never matched their
room numbers, hit `lr_unknown`, and silently left the PREVIOUS room's
placements/mask in place -- meaning the earlier round's own "jumptrace
floor=1, all 16 rooms PASS" claim was **reading room 36's stale
geometry at each room's own spawn x**, not the new rooms' real floor.
Both bugs were present simultaneously; fixing the room_desc_table one
alone still left 0 PASS (verified: re-ran cmaskverify after that fix
alone, still 0/18), which is what forced the frame_table diagnosis.

Control run per the brief's own instruction (c): CMASK_TAPE=1's harness
mechanism (all-RAM load_decb, CM_LEN, CUR_ROOM_CMASK addressing) tested
against room 36 (which exists identically in both builds) via BOTH
target/room36.bin and target/room36_tape.bin -- **PASS both times**,
before either bug was found. Confirms the mechanism itself was never
broken; both bugs were specific to the new rooms' own data/wiring.

## The fix

- **tools/regen_art.sh**: a tape-only frame table
  (`target/frame_table_data_tape.asm`) seeded as an EXACT COPY of the
  -run build's own `target/frame_table_data.asm` (so every index the
  -run build's rooms already assigned keeps resolving identically),
  then every one of the 18 (now 19, see below) tape rooms is regenerated
  through `--frame-table` pointing at this copy, in the SAME single
  loop (order matters: `--frame-table` accumulates state across calls
  within one script run). Growing the ORIGINAL frame_table_data.asm
  would change block A/B's raw bytes for BOTH builds (T0231's own
  coupling class); this file only exists inside the tape build's own
  independent pass.
- **target/room36.asm**: `if TAPE_ROOMS` conditional include of
  `frame_table_data_tape.asm` instead of `frame_table_data.asm` (same
  pattern as staged_syms.asm et al), plus the missing 16 `fdb
  rNN_room_desc` entries in `room_desc_table` (touch point 3).

## Room 77 (THE ACTIVE VOLCANO) -- built

`tools/roompack`'s water-tile emitter used to panic unconditionally
("water tiles at differing y-phases need per-tile variants") whenever
a room's water/lava tiles didn't all share one y%4 phase -- room 77's
lava has two (4 tiles at phase 0, 2 at phase 3). Fixed (`tools/
roompack/src/main.rs`): pick the phase covering the MOST tiles (mode),
matching the FLAMES code's own already-accepted `phase=0` hardcode
immediately above it in the same file ("we deliberately ignore
per-tile y here"). **Not** "true" per-tile variants: `draw_water`
(room36.asm) draws every water tile in a room from ONE shared bitmap
set with ONE shared counter already ("a synchronized ripple instead of
a staggered one", its own comment) -- there is no per-tile selection
at runtime to feed even if multiple variants were emitted, and adding
one would mean rewriting draw_water's own dispatch, which risks
regressing every already-working water room. Flagged here in case a
future round wants true per-tile animation; not attempted.

Room 77 wired in exactly like the other 18 (reuse-only pool,
`--frame-table` against the tape table, no actors, `room_desc_table`
entry, TAPE_ROOMS include). Verified:
- **Floor landing**: jumptrace, no movement, lands floor=1 at y=128.
- **killedbyvolcano, not killedbywater**: forced a fall onto one of
  room 77's lava tiles (respawn_room=77, x=120 above a y=168 water
  tile) -- `killed` counts down (a real hazard trigger, not a poke),
  `death_msg` latches to a real message pointer, and the 16 bytes read
  back from that exact address at runtime are `146,88,15,125,1,114,82,
  78,84,145,96,66,89,13,72,79` -- byte-for-byte `msg_killedbyvolcano`'s
  own source bytes ([X-ALL.TXT line 1019] / [X-ALL.TXT line 1042] DTE codes),
  confirming `update_water_hazard`'s `cmpa #77` branch fired, not the
  ordinary `msg_killedbywater` path.

Three rooms have small residual diffs, all the SAME negative-pixel_x-

# T0234 -- tape-resident actor table: safe pickupables wired, reset on
# game over (a real bug, fixed), lift + key4 deliberately deferred
# (2026-09-30)

## Design: a SECOND, independent actor table, not a shared one

`target/actor_data_tape.asm` (roompack `--actors ... --actor-suffix
_tape --actor-no-coins --actor-exclude-routines lift --actor-reuse-
sprites target/actor_data.asm --actor-template`), entirely separate
from `actor_data.asm`/`actor_ram` -- growing the SHARED table would
break the -run build's byte-identity to HEAD (T0233's own reasoning for
leaving `--actor-rooms` out of the tape rooms' own generation
entirely). `target/room36.bin` stays byte-for-byte identical to HEAD
throughout this round (`cmp`, checked after every rebuild).

roompack gained four flags for this, all opt-in/additive (the -run
build's own regen_art.sh call passes none of them, and `actor_data.asm`
came out byte-identical to a pre-change baseline):
- `--actor-suffix STR`: suffixes `ACTOR_STRIDE`/`ACTOR_COUNT`/
  `actor_init`/`ACTOR_SPR_N`/`actor_spr_tab`; skips re-emitting `ROU_*`
  (the dense routine-id space is shared and already defined by the
  first table).
- `--actor-no-coins`: skips `COIN_STRIDE`/`COIN_COUNT`/`coin_init` --
  coins are a separate, unrelated mechanic (CoinRec's own doc comment:
  "not an actor"), out of scope this round, and 3 of the 6 wired-room
  actors' rooms have coin entries that would otherwise collide.
- `--actor-exclude-routines lift`: drops room 88's lift entry.
  `draw_actors`' dispatch special-cases `ROU_LIFT` unconditionally
  (`jsr draw_lift`, which reads per-room bounds from `ul_bounds`/
  `logic_low.asm`) -- an inert lift entry with no `ul_bounds` case for
  its room would still run that dispatch and likely misdraw, unlike a
  genuinely un-special-cased routine (dragon/log/hawk/dozyfloat/daisy1/
  etc, which fall through to ordinary static rendering safely --
  confirmed by reading every special-cased branch in `draw_actors`, not
  assumed).
- `--actor-reuse-sprites FILE`: skips re-emitting `aspr_<frame>_*` for
  frames FILE already defines. Room 40's second dragon (dragonhere1)
  shares frame 109 with room 54's dragon in the -run build's own
  table -- without this, `lwasm` correctly refused ("Multiply defined
  symbol").
- `--actor-template` (this round's fix, see below): also emits a
  pristine, never-mutated copy of the same records under
  `actor_init{suffix}_template`.

## Shared-code changes (target/text_src/actors.asm, gameplay.asm --
## the DTE SOURCES; stage_pack.sh's own generated copies are
## gitignored, never hand-edit those)

All gated `if TAPE_ROOMS` -- zero bytes, zero behaviour change for the
-run build:
- `draw_actors_tape`: a second entry point that jumps straight into
  `draw_actors`' own `da_loop` body with `Y=#actor_init_tape`,
  `count=ACTOR_COUNT_tape`. Zero duplication -- every branch in that
  loop already reads Y/ACTOR_STRIDE generically, nothing in it is
  base-table-specific. Called from room36.asm's mainloop right after
  `jsr draw_actors`.
- `actor_sprite`'s linear scan: falls back to `actor_spr_tab_tape`
  before giving up (`as_none2`, its own terminator so the fallback
  can't loop into itself). Needed because tape-only sprite frames
  (4/10/12/15/21/204 etc) aren't in the base `actor_spr_tab` at all.
- `try_pickup`: after the base-table scan's own `tp_next` tail runs
  out, a gated second pass re-enters the SAME `tp_loop` body with
  `Y=#actor_init_tape`, `count=ACTOR_COUNT_tape`, `B` (slot index)
  starting at 100 instead of 0 -- `tp_take` (unchanged, shared) then
  stores `tp_slot` as 101..112 for a tape item vs 1..43 for a base one.
  A new gated 1-byte flag `tp_scan_phase` stops the second pass
  re-triggering itself once IT also exhausts (the same "two passes
  through one shared loop" shape as `draw_actors_tape`, applied where
  the loop ALSO needs to terminate cleanly rather than just return).
- `drop_to_world` (actors.asm) and `check_drop_trigger` (gameplay.asm):
  both branch on `drop_slot > 100` to recompute the record address
  against `actor_init_tape` instead of `actor_ram` -- both already did
  raw index arithmetic straight off `drop_slot`'s numeric value, so a
  naive shared index would have silently mis-addressed a dropped tape
  item into the wrong table. Two `beq`s had to become `TAPE_ROOMS`-
  conditional `lbeq` (`if/else`, so the -run build keeps the original
  1-byte-shorter `beq`) -- the inserted code pushed the branch target
  out of an 8-bit branch's reach in the tape build only; `lwasm`
  caught both as "Byte overflow", not a silent miscompile.

POTION` already had `cdt_potion` wired and waiting, room 54 built), 73
(an unnamed window item fr204), 88 (crowbarhere fr4 -- `FRAME_CROWBAR`

**Excluded, with reasons (not silently dropped):**

## Bug found and fixed: tape actors never reset after a game over

Reported by the user directly: non-resetting tape rooms after a game
over is a real bug, not an acceptable limitation. Root cause: `actor_
init_tape` has no separate ROM master to restore from (T0230's own
"delivered raw, no relocation" design -- the assembled `fcb` bytes ARE
the live record, unlike `actor_data.asm`/`actor_ram`'s ROM-copied-to-
RAM-at-boot pattern) -- a picked-up/moved item stayed changed for the
rest of the tape session, including across `new_game`.

Fixed with `--actor-template` (roompack, above): a pristine second
copy, `actor_init_tape_template`, and a new `reset_tape_actors`
routine (actors.asm, same shape as the existing `actors_init`) that
copies it back over `actor_init_tape`, called from `new_game`
immediately after `jsr actors_init`, gated `if TAPE_ROOMS`.

**Verified end-to-end** (`harness/tape_actor_reset.lua`, new): pick up
crowbarhere (room 88) via the real `try_pickup` path -- room byte ->
255 -- then force a death at 0 lives (`gameover_tape.lua`'s own
`force_death` shape: `lives=0`, `killed=1`), ride the REAL death
sequence (msg_deadwindow, the death tune -- both take real time, ~120
frames, discovered the hard way: the harness's first few attempts
mistook the tune for a hang) through to the title, press SPACE for a
genuinely new game, then read `actor_init_tape`'s crowbarhere slot
directly: **room byte = 88 again (RESTORED)**. Two harness gotchas hit
and fixed along the way, both about NOT skipping steps the real game
requires: (1) `tp_take` opens `show_inventory` on every successful
pickup (actors.asm's own comment, "entered on EVERY successful
pickup") -- its input loop blocks the mainloop (`update_death` never
runs) until dismissed; the harness must press SPACE once (cursor
defaults to EXIT) before forcing the death. (2) room 88 also has
doughere (a person, frame 36, 24px wide) immediately next to
crowbarhere -- warping to `crowbarhere`'s own x-8 (items.lua's usual
formula) overlaps BOTH boxes and `try_pickup`'s tape pass hits doughere
FIRST (earlier table slot), opening Denzil's generic chatter instead
(the ALREADY-SHIPPED "wrong text for a non-Denzil person" simplification,
not a new bug -- see the pickupable note above) -- fixed by standing at
doughere's own right edge (x=64, excluded by `actor_hit`'s own `>=`
boundary) while still overlapping crowbarhere (x=64..80).

# T0235 -- per-room LZ pack, TAPE build only: 182 -> 752 bytes free in the
# tape-only region (2026-09-30)

## Design

Each room's own placements+flames+water (the SOURCE-order table
`load_room` reads, room36.asm) can be LZ-packed with the same codec as
the title screen (`tools/roompack::lz`, mirrored by `lz_unpack`,
target/boot_code.asm). `tools/roompack` gained `--pack-room-data`:

- Collects the exact raw bytes [placements 3B/entry][flames 2B/entry]
  [water 2B/entry] that would otherwise ship as three raw tables, packs
  them, and **only uses the packed form if it is smaller than raw**
  (room 77: 94 raw -> 98 packed -- LZ's own per-token overhead loses on
  tiny rooms; roompack decides per room and falls back to the ORIGINAL
  raw emission automatically, logging "declined" to stderr). No per-room
  exclusion list needed anywhere else.
- When packing wins: emits one `rNN_room_packed` blob, an assemble-time
  guard (`rNN_ROOM_RAW_LEN equ n` / `ifgt ...-ROOM_UNPACK_BUF_LEN
  error`), and changes the room_desc record's shape: `room_placements_
  ptr` points at the blob, `room_placements_end` ships as the sentinel
  `0` (never a valid ROM address) so `load_room` can tell a packed room
  from a raw one without a separate flag byte anywhere. `flame_tab_ptr`/
  `water_tab_ptr` are untouched -- those always pointed at the SHARED
  `flame_table`/`water_table` animation bitmaps, never per-room data.
- `target/room36.asm`: `ROOM_UNPACK_BUF_LEN equ 315` (max raw size
  across every room that packs, room 31) is defined right next to
  `RELOC_BOOT_BYTES`, near the TOP of the file -- NOT next to
  `ROOM_UNPACK_BUF`'s own address (which has to live inside the
  tape-only region, near the end) -- because the 28 base rooms' own
  `ifgt` guards are assembled far EARLIER in the file (staged block A/B/
  C, org $4000/$6000/$E000) and `ifgt` needs the constant resolvable at
  the point it's read, not a forward reference the way an ordinary
  operand can be. `ROOM_UNPACK_BUF` itself is a `fill 0,LEN` (NOT `rmb`
  -- T0172's own reasoning, right above the unrelated boot-relocation
  branch this deliberately never touches: `rmb` here would split the
  tape image into two DECB segments). `load_room`, right after the
  existing `lr_copy` block-copy, gated `if TAPE_ROOMS`: tests
  `room_placements_end` for the sentinel; if packed, `jsr lz_unpack`
  (U=blob, Y=#ROOM_UNPACK_BUF) then recomputes `room_placements_ptr/
  end`, `room_flames_ptr`, `room_water_ptr` from the counts `lr_copy`
  already copied (`*3`/`*2` via `mul`), all BEFORE `derive_room_cmask`/
  `rd_sortplaces` run -- same ordering constraint the raw path already
  had.
- Confirmed: touches neither `RELOC_BOOT_BYTES` nor the `STAGE_LZ` boot
  branch -- `load_room` runs at gameplay time, a wholly separate call
  site from boot relocation. The brief's own flagged concern didn't
  apply.

## PHASE 1 (19 tape-only rooms, checkpoint measured and reported
## mid-round) -- net NEGATIVE alone

3056 raw -> 2749 packed (307 saved) across the 19 tape-only rooms
(74,75,63,91,92,45,48,49,94,89,41,73,88,93,40,46,31,47,77) --far short
of the offline 50-room estimate's pro-rated share, because most of
these rooms are small (room 77 alone: 94->98, LZ losing outright).
ROOM_UNPACK_BUF_LEN (max of these 19) = 315. Net: 182 bytes free (T0234
baseline) -> 174 -- **an 8-byte regression**, reported to the
coordinator rather than committed or extended further per the brief's
own "measure and report before going further" checkpoint.

## PHASE 2 (28 base rooms, TAPE-only duplicate) -- net POSITIVE

Coordinator's decision: extend to the 31 base rooms (room2 excluded --
no room_desc_table entry, load_room can never load it; room35/room36
excluded -- they live in the LOW $0100 region, not the staged $8000+
blocks this mechanism targets, so packing them would not move
IMAGE_END at all). 28 rooms in scope: block A (org $4000) 52,53,69,67,
84,85,83,86,70,50,71,57,72,58,59,60; block B (org $6000) 51,54,68,55,
100,87,56,24,22,76; block C (org $E000) 39,23.

**A tape-only duplicate file per room** (`roomNN_data_tape.asm`),
generated by a SECOND `regen_art.sh` invocation per room --
`--shared-sprites-reuse-only` (every sprite these rooms use is ALREADY
in the pool from their own FIRST, -run-build generation earlier in the
same script; growing it a second time here would double-count budget
against framebuffer windows already sized against the first pass),
`--frame-table "$FRAME_TABLE_TAPE"` (a lookup, not a growth -- confirmed
frame_table_data_tape.asm's own byte count does not change across this
loop), `--pack-room-data`. `target/room36.asm`'s block A/B/C raw-pass
includes (`else` branch of `if STAGE_LZ`) wrapped `if TAPE_ROOMS /
include roomNN_data_tape.asm / else / include roomNN_data.asm / endif`
per room -- same pattern as `frame_table_data_tape.asm`/
`actor_data_tape.asm` (T0233-fix/T0234). The -run build's own
`roomNN_data.asm` includes are completely untouched.

Why this grows the tape-only region: shrinking these rooms' RAW
(uncompressed, pass-1/STAGE_GEN) size moves `IMAGE_END` DOWN (`IMAGE_END
equ RC_DEST+(rc_staged_end-rc_staged_start)`, all computed from RAW
block sizes) -- the tape-only room region starts at `org IMAGE_END` and
runs up to `CODE_DEST`, so a smaller `IMAGE_END` is a BIGGER region,
independent of `STAGE_LZ`'s own separate bulk-compression pass over
whatever ends up in those blocks (which still runs, on the now-smaller
raw image, for -run-build-style delivery efficiency -- unrelated to
this region's own size).

Result: 22 of 28 rooms packed (6 declined -- LZ losing outright, same
class as room 77): 4153 raw -> 3588 packed (**565 saved**) across the
packed 22. `ROOM_UNPACK_BUF_LEN` unchanged at 315 (room 31, from phase
1, stays the max across both phases -- checked directly, not assumed).

**Combined net**: `target/room36_tape.map`, `CODE_DEST=$DFAE`,
`tape_room_staged_end` moved from `$DF00` (phase 1) to `$DCBE` (phase
2) -- **752 bytes free**, up from the T0234 baseline of 182 (net **+570
bytes**), close to the coordinator's own ~+800 estimate (the 6 declined
rooms and phase 1's own -8 are the gap).

## Room-load frames added -- NOT reliably measured

Tried an ad-hoc adaptation of `harness/cmasktime.lua` (PC-sampling
between `load_room`/`room_desc_table`) driven by a mid-game `killed=1`
warp (the same mechanism `cmaskverify.lua`'s own `warp()` uses) instead
of cmasktime's initial-boot-only load. Two attempts both produced
IDENTICAL sample counts across different rooms regardless of whether
they were packed, raw, or in the -run build entirely (42/300 samples
every time at one delay, 0/300 at another) -- a red flag that the
warp/boot-detection timing in the ad-hoc script, not the real load cost,
was what got measured (most likely: the fixed frame delay before
warping does not reliably land past this build's own boot+title
sequence, unlike `cmaskverify.lua`'s own robust settle-based detection).
Not trusted, not reported as a real number -- see "Check the data
before calling it expensive" (memory). Left as a genuinely open task
for whoever wants the precise figure: reuse `cmaskverify.lua`'s own
settle/warp sequencing (not a fixed frame count) with a PC-range sample
accumulator plumbed in.

**Analytical estimate only** (not measured): the added code per packed
room is one `jsr lz_unpack` over at most `ROOM_UNPACK_BUF_LEN` (315)
bytes plus ~10 instructions of pointer/count arithmetic. `derive_room_
cmask`/`rd_sortplaces` (unchanged, already the dominant, multi-frame
cost per T0163's own cmasktime.lua measurement of room 36) are O(placement
count x cell tests); `lz_unpack`'s own cost is O(unpacked bytes) at a
cheap bit-level decode. For 315 bytes this should be a small fraction
of derive_room_cmask's own already-paid cost, not a second visible
stall -- but this is reasoning, not a measurement, and should be
labelled as such until someone re-runs the harness properly.

## Daisy's ending (daisyrou1, room 73, daisy1here, frame 35, ROU_DAISY1)

Priority order was pre-decided by the coordinator (not this round's own
call): (1) the coins==30 trigger + coins<30 nag, REQUIRED; (2)
completedgame + completion tune, tune reused ONLY if already in sound
data; (3) what happens after a win (REQUIRED if (1) is in); (4) the
heart demo visual, LOWEST priority, cut if it doesn't fit. Stop before
free bytes would drop below 64.

**Ported (1) and (3)**: `update_daisy1` (actors.asm, gated `if
TAPE_ROOMS`) scans `actor_init_tape` for a `ROU_DAISY1` entry in
`cur_room` and calls `actor_hit` (the same AABB test `try_pickup`'s
pickupable scan already uses -- `collidewithdizzy16`'s real equivalent
here). On a hit: `coins<30` shows `msg_notgotallcoins` (4-box
`msg_chatter` run, X-ALL.TXT's own `notgotallcoins`, byte-for-byte,
game carries on exactly as before -- no state change, matching
`chatter`'s own `jp windowrou1`); `coins==30` sets `completedgame=1` and
shows `msg_gotallcoins` (5-box run, X-ALL.TXT's own `gotallcoins`,
byte-for-byte, including its own closing-credits box -- [X-ALL.TXT line 787]/"THE OLIVER TWINS" -- carried over verbatim, not trimmed).
`room36.asm`'s mainloop reads `completedgame` itself right after
calling `update_daisy1` and, if set, runs `show_title_resident`/`jmp
new_game` -- X-ALL.TXT's own mainloop check (`ld a,(completedgame)/and
a/jr nz,quitted`, line 1357), the SAME title-return path
`update_death`'s own game-over tail already uses. `new_game` clears
`completedgame` (X-ALL.TXT `resetlives`' own `ld (completedgame),a`
with a=0).

Deliberately NOT gated on X-ALL.TXT's own `sequence` flag
(`doendmessages`' `ld a,(sequence)/and a/ret nz`): this port implements
no cross-routine "a cutscene is running" state machine anywhere
(checked: zero hits for "sequence" as such a flag in `target/text_src`)
-- there is only this one routine that would ever need it, so there is
nothing to gate against. `completedgame` itself already stops a second
touch from re-running the win path.

**Real behaviour, confirmed against X-ALL.TXT, not a bug**:
`update_daisy1` retriggers every mainloop pass while Dizzy stays in
contact with daisy1here -- there is no "already shown, don't ask again"
latch in the original either (`chatter`'s own tail is `jp windowrou1`,
a plain return to ordinary play, still standing on her). Confirmed via
`harness/tape_daisy_ending.lua`'s own design, below.

**The DTE trap (a real, systemic finding, not specific to this
change)**: the two message tables were first written into
`target/text_src/gameplay.asm` like every other message table in this
port. Doing that changed `room36.bin` (the -run build) even though
every new byte was wrapped `if TAPE_ROOMS` -- confirmed directly:
rebuilding TAPE_ROOMS=0 changed `msg_troll`'s own COMPRESSED bytes, with
its SOURCE `fcc` text completely untouched. Root cause: `tools/dte`
derives ONE shared codebook from the WHOLE corpus of its 5 fixed source
files (`gap_messages`/`gameplay`/`actors`/`ui_room_names`/
`rat_troll_hazard_code`.asm) with NO knowledge of `if TAPE_ROOMS` --
adding text there, even gated, shifts corpus frequency statistics
enough to reassign which bit-patterns encode which characters (same
code COUNT, 46, different assignments), changing the compressed bytes
of unrelated, already-shipped, UNGATED strings. **Rule for future
rounds**: any new TAPE_ROOMS-only message text goes in a plain,
hand-written, NOT-DTE-processed file (like `actor_data_tape.asm`/
`coin_data_tape.asm`), never into one of DTE's 5 fixed sources, even
inside an `if` block. Fixed here by moving the two tables into a new
`target/msg_data_tape.asm`, included from `room36.asm` gated
`TAPE_ROOMS`, at the cost of DTE's ~40% compression (measured:
~552 bytes uncompressed for both tables combined).

# T0237 -- BANNER_BUF eliminated for the TAPE build only: the real
# clobber found and fixed, 1536 bytes recovered (109 -> 1645 free)

Goal: remove BANNER_BUF (T0146's "floor of the chain", 1536 bytes) from
the tape-only memory map without ANY visible banner change, per T0092's
own rule -- measure with a real framebuffer capture, do not argue it
away. Built `harness/banner_writers.lua` to do exactly that: MAME write
taps on rows 0-47 of BOTH framebuffers ($4000-$45FF, $6000-$65FF),
mapping every writer PC to its enclosing symbol from the .map, run
across a real scenario (boot/title, gameplay redraws, three room warps,
a death, game over -> title -> new game). It also dumps rows 0-47 of
both buffers to named checkpoints for a byte-exact before/after diff
(STEP 3 below).

**Harness gotcha, worth remembering for any future write-tap script on
this target**: `install_write_tap` must be installed AFTER the tape
image's own `$FFDF` all-RAM switch, not before. Installed early, a tap
only ever sees the loader's OWN direct pokes into the fb A/B staging
blocks (one batch, one frozen PC) -- SAM remapping $4000-$7FFF to a
different underlying view silently detaches a tap bound to the
pre-switch view, and nothing from real CPU execution is ever seen again.
Fixed by calling `load_decb` first, then installing (and, to survive
any LATER remap too, re-installing every frame via `tap:remove()` +
re-`install_write_tap`, which is cheap and turned out to be necessary --
the first title paint remap-detached the tap a SECOND time).

## STEP 1 -- the writer list (measured, not guessed)

Only two kinds of writer ever touch rows 0-47 in this build:

- **Legitimate full-screen paints**: `ti_gcopy`/`ti_row`/`ti_dup`
  (boot's `show_title`) and `tr_copy`/`lz_cplp`/`lz_litlp`
  (`show_title_resident`, the tape build's game-over title replay).
  These write the CORRECT content directly; nothing needs to restore
  after them.
- **`draw_border`'s `bd_bandrow`/`bd_siderow`** (rows 40-47 only) --
  drawn unconditionally, unclipped, LAST in every single redraw pass
  (T0079's own header: "does not need its own clear"). Self-heals every
  frame regardless; not a clobber that needs handling.
- **The CLOBBER, found**: `rd_clrxloop` -- room36.asm's `rd_cleardmg`
  (redraw's own damage-rect clear). A buffer that has never been drawn
  into (`bufA_last_x`/`bufB_last_x` == 255, the "just force_redraw'd or
  never drawn" sentinel) gets a FULL-SCREEN damage rect (dmg_y0=0,
  dmg_y1=192), and the clamp-to-win_top code only ran when `fb_flip` was
  set (`tst fb_flip / beq rd_noclamp` skipped the whole clamp
  otherwise). Every room used in the scenario is unflipped, so EVERY
  room warp (and the very first draw after boot) cleared rows 0-47
  straight to black. NOTES' own earlier hypothesis (the banner-repaint
  section above, "clear_and_blit is the suspect... not a finding") was
  half right about the SHAPE of the bug (a clip missing on the unflipped
  path) but wrong about WHICH routine -- `clear_and_blit`'s own
  win_top/FLIP_YEND handling is fine; `rd_cleardmg`'s is not. Confirmed
  live: the writer list showed `rd_clrxloop` at rows 0..47 exactly when
  expected (every warp), and NOT at all after the fix below.
- **`draw_ui`'s own repaint** (`ui_bncol`, full 1536-byte copy from
  BANNER_BUF) and its text-slot clears (`ui_clr1`, room name) -- the
  CURRENT self-heal mechanism, confirmed present, and the thing being
  replaced.
- Message boxes (troll/daisy/death/inventory) never appeared at all --
  `blit`/`prtmessage` are clipped to `win_top`, which only `draw_ui`
  ever clears, so a message box CANNOT physically reach rows 0-47
  regardless of its own y. No restoration needed for boxes.

## STEP 2 -- implemented, TAPE_ROOMS only

1. **`room36.asm`, `rd_cleardmg`**: TAPE_ROOMS clamps `dmg_y0` to
   `win_top` UNCONDITIONALLY (both flipped and unflipped), instead of
   only when flipped. `dmg_y1` is still only clamped to `FLIP_YEND` when
   actually flipped -- the unflipped bottom bound (up to row 191) was
   never the problem, since `draw_border` repaints that band fresh every
   pass regardless. The `else` branch (the -run build) is the ORIGINAL
   code, byte-for-byte.
2. **`ui.asm`, `draw_ui`**: TAPE_ROOMS drops the 1536-byte BANNER_BUF
   repaint entirely. Instead it clears just the two small TEXT slots
   (lives, coins) before drawing new text into them, the same way the
   room-name slot already did. **Exact footprint, measured with
   `/tmp/probe_banner.lua`** (forced two different lives/coins values,
   diffed the resulting framebuffers): lives occupies rows 8-15, bytes
   7-8 only (2 max -- `lives` is never set above 2, room36.asm's
   `resetlives`); coins occupies rows 8-15, bytes 23-24 only (2 digits,
   coins never exceeds 30). **A first attempt cleared only row 8 (not
   all 8 rows of the glyph) and a padded byte range "for margin"** --
   the margin ate byte 6, part of the STATIC "DIZZY III" art immediately
   to the left, with nothing left to ever repaint it since there is no
   more periodic BANNER_BUF restore. Caught by STEP 3's own checkpoint
   diff (not by the write-tap list, which only shows WHERE a routine
   wrote, not whether it should have). **Margin is not "a little extra"
   once the periodic full restore is gone -- it is a permanent erasure.
   Measure the exact footprint, do not pad it.**
3. **`room36.asm`**: TAPE_ROOMS aliases `BANNER_BUF equ TITLE_RAW_BUF`
   (dead, but keeps the symbol defined) instead of reserving
   `BANNER_BYTES` below it; `CODE_DEST` rises by the same amount. The
   -run build's `BANNER_BUF equ TITLE_RAW_BUF-BANNER_BYTES` is
   unchanged.

Harness lessons (3 false failures this round, all harness not game):
1. stack_has() scanned 20-63 words from S, running past the stack top
   ($0100) into low-RAM variables; a resident layout shift put a variable
   word inside [msg_wait_dismiss,fb_stablekeys) -> "message wait" forever.
   Bounded to sp+i+1<$0100 in every harness that has the helper.
2. tape_item_pickup/tape_actor_reset hardcoded crowbarhere's tape slot
   (changed 4 times); they now parse target/actor_data_tape.asm by
   (room,frame).
3. actorlife.lua on the TAPE binary is phase-sensitive (SPACE mashing every
   14 frames): adding even a bare `jsr update_hawk` (3 bytes) flipped it from
   5/1/1 to 2/4/1 with killed=1 stuck in a death box, while every other
   warp/death harness (gameover_tape, tape_*, key3lift88, lift94) passes.
   The required check is actorlife on the -run build (identical to HEAD,
   5/1/1). Not chased (time-box).
   **CORRECTED (next session): NOT phase sensitivity -- a harness LOADER
   bug.** actorlife's load_decb wrote every DECB block with mem:write_u8
   while the SAM was still in ROM mode, so the tape image's $BF30-$E3D5
   block (the TAPE_ROOMS region: tape_code.asm, update_hawk, ...) was
   silently dropped. Before the hawk, nothing actorlife visited called
   into that region; `jsr update_hawk` from the main loop jumped into ROM.
   Fix = jumptrace's T0230 idiom (poke $FFDF before the first block at
   >=$8000), now applied to 36 harnesses' load_decb. With it, actorlife on
   room36_tape.bin = pass=5 fail=1 skip=1, same as -run. Rule: ANY harness
   run on a _tape binary must load all-RAM; a harness that lacks `allram`
   in load_decb is -run only. Left unpatched (old stage-3 diff tests, never
   run on tape): mame_{diff,idle_diff,walk_diff,jump_diff,physics}_test,
   mame_{dump,snapshot,frame_preview,load_run}.lua.

(port x = 176-4*wh: 152/128/104), rock.y=176, show `rockinwatermess`. The three rocks are the base-table
pickupables room 50 frame 138, room 35 frame 139, room 53 frame 136 (all carry `rockmess,proxrock`).
`addtowater` (2097): in room 48 the water is drawn at y = 168-waterheight and STRETCHED to 3 tiles 8 raw
(32 px) apart: x = 80,112,144 (each tile is a waterlist entry, so the drown box follows the drawn water).
`logrou` (2831): var1=(var1+1)&3, b=var1 (2 if 0), log.y = 162-waterheight+b, delay 4 (every 4th pass),
attr 2+8 (solid platform). Port y == ZX y for actors and room things.

**What raising the water ACHIEVES (measured in the port, harness/tape_log48.lua).** Room 48 is a river gap
between two cliffs (left cliff top y=112 with key 4, frame 13, tape actor at (32,96); right cliff top y=112,
where Dizzy arrives and the drop box is). The pit is water (kills), and the only thing in it is the log.
At waterheight 0 the log floats at y=163..165: Dizzy can land on it, but the left cliff face is a staircase of
4px steps (x=76,y~125 ... x=64,y=113 ... top 112) and a jump rises only ~28 px, so he cannot get off the log
onto the left cliff. Each rock lifts the log (and the water) 6 px. Jump-left tries from the log (3 start x x
tap/hold = 6 tries): 0 rocks 0/6, 1 rock 0/6, 2 rocks 2/6 (marginal, depends on landing x), 3 rocks 6/6.
So the puzzle is: push the three rocks into the river to float the log up to the left cliff, then take key 4
(which opens machine 4 in room 56, proxkey4 56). The harness proves it end to end: real carry+drop of each
rock, then Dizzy jumps from the log onto the ledge and picks key 4 up. NOT established: whether the
ORIGINAL's jump apex equals the port's (T0044 measured 32 on the flat; observed 28-32 here depending on the
log's bob phase), i.e. whether 2 rocks suffice in the ZX game; what else the left cliff leads to.

**Where the code is.** All in `target/tape_code.asm` (tape-only region) + `target/text_src_tape/msg_data_tape.asm`:
- `update_log48` (called every pass from room36.asm's mainloop, TAPE block): in room 48 sets
  y of the 3 `tide_list` tiles = 168-waterheight and repoints `room_water_ptr/room_water_count` at it (the
  shared room48_data.asm has ONE hidden tile at (80,184) and cannot change: it would change room36.bin),
  then advances/places the log. `draw_water` and `update_water_hazard` read those, so draw and drown box agree.
- `cdt_rock`: check_drop_trigger gets `cmpa #136 / lbhs cdt_rock` (frames 136/138/139; other >=136 frames
  fall out via cdt_done). Box test, room/x/y writes, waterheight+=6, `msg_rockinwater`.
- `tape_state_reset` (falls into dragon_reset) clears waterheight; reset_tape_actors now jumps to it.
  The rocks themselves are base-table records, restored by actors_init.
- Resident: actors.asm gets ROU_LOG in the two spots the hawk uses (always-redraw + rat save-under route).
  The log is 32x7, same as the rat, so RAT_SV_W/H already fit.
- The log needed NO new solidity code: its colour 10 has bit 6 clear, and build_solid_actors' tape pass
  already puts every non-dull tape actor into solid_list; the ground scan (STEP_UP lift + scan down) carries
  Dizzy with the bob.

**Costs (tape-only region, tools/tape_pack.sh).** 644 -> 405 free = 239 bytes. By part (symbol distances):
tide+water 54 (9 data, 42 code, 3 reset), log 47, rock drop 79 + message 45 (DTE) = 124; these sum to 225, the
other 14 bytes appear only in the region total (not located; probably alignment of what follows). Resident
(title-hole spare) 99 -> 81 = 18 bytes (three call/branch sites: update_log48 jsr, cdt_rock dispatch,
2 x ROU_LOG in actors.asm).

**Verified.** `harness/tape_log48.lua` (34 PASS / 0 FAIL): log bob 163..165 at 0, 157..159/151..153/145..147
after each rock; tiles at 168-wh; msg shown (msg_active=1) per rock; waterheight 6/12/18; rock at
(176-4*wh,176) in room 48; water band top row moves exactly 18 up in the framebuffer, zero changed bytes
outside the river columns; no ink more than 1 row above the log's current top in 120 samples per rock
count (mutation-tested: removing the ROU_LOG save-under hunk makes this FAIL with ~30 bad samples each);
game over -> waterheight 0 and rocks back in their own rooms. Also unchanged: cmask CMASK_TAPE=1 19/0/0,
tape_item_pickup, tape_actor_reset, key3lift88, gameover_tape.

**Gotchas / dead ends.**
- Dropping with the inventory UI: after the earlier death/warp the FIRST drop attempt of rock 3 consistently
  did nothing (inventory closed without selecting; inv still held the rock). Not investigated (inventory UI,
  not this change); the harness retries the open/select dance (up to 4 times) and logs "drop try N failed".
- A trail detector that demands one contiguous ink block over the log is wrong: frame 158 has a blank row 3.
  Use "no ink above the log's current top - 1".
- Routing the log through plain clear_and_blit (the default static-actor path) leaves trails; it must use the
  rat save-under route. The save-under region is 14 rows (RAT_SV_H, tape) from the log's y, which includes
  water pixels; harmless because restore runs before the water redraw.
- The rocks (y=176, 16 rows) are drawn over the bottom border (rows 184+); you see only their tops. Original
  has the same y; not compared pixel-wise with the ZX game.
- Water drawn before the log (draw order water -> actors), log ORed on top.
- build_solid_actors runs before update_log48 in a pass, so collision sees the log one pass behind the drawn
  position (<=1 px); not noticeable (STEP_UP absorbs it).
- Harness: the start x of a jump matters (cliff face is a staircase); a single hand-picked jump gives 0/1
  results by phase. Use attempt_set (6 tries) as the reachability measure.

## T0218 room 45 Dozy float

TAPE build only (`TAPE_ROOMS=1`); `target/room36.bin` stays byte-identical (cmp against the pre-task reference).

**Original mechanics (X-ALL.TXT).** Talking is `pickupablerou` (2302) -> frames 32..39 -> `talkingtopeople` (2374).
`talkbefore` (2294, 5 bytes, index frame-32) is a per-person talk COUNT: 0 -> set 1 and run the stream
(`notyolkfolk1`: `oldmovefrm/delay` = `dozytalking`, whose leading `defw sleepingpotionhere+room` is poked with
roomno = the potion materialises in the room you talk in, orig_room 255, same mechanism as T0199's rope); count>0 ->
`res 3 / inc`, DE=&count, jump to `oldmovex/oldmovey` = `dozyrou`. So: talk 1 = `dozytalking` (8 boxes: Dozy wakes,
Daisy eggnapped, [X-ALL.TXT line 641], ... [X-ALL.TXT line 659]), talks 2..4 = count 2..4 = `kickdozyagainmess`,
talk 5 = count 5 = `pushdozymess` + dozyhere.room=255 + dozyfloathere.var1=255, talk 6+ = nothing (`ret nc`).
`dozyfloatrou` runs EVERY pass (delay 0) and only while Dizzy is in room 45 (domoving): a=(var1-1)&3; if a==0 {x-=1 raw
(4 px); a=4}; var1=a; y = 139 + (a-1, with 3 -> 1) = 139 + {1,0, then repeating 1,2,1,0 }; ends (var1=0) when raw x < 28.
NB the bob is 1,2,1,0 by var1 4,3,2,1 (not 1,2,3,1). Float record: x raw 68 = px 144, y 139, frame 32 (24x28), colour
7+64+16+8 = 95. Colour bit 6 (dull) = the actor's screen attribute is not "bright", which is what the original's
attribute-based solidity tests (`checkattri` bit 6) treat as NOT solid; the log is colour 10 (bit 6 clear = solid).
Bit 3 is only the plot mode (`frmplotpatch`). So **the float is a picture, not a platform** (build_solid_actors' tape
pass already skips dull actors; verified nothing needed).

**What the port did before.** Measured on the pre-change tape binary: ANY talk to Dozy (and every one of 6) opened a
message box and changed nothing (frames 32..39 all went to Denzil's `msg_denzil` branch in tp_take: no count, no
potion, no push); the potion sat in room 45 from the start (its orig_room 255 was not honoured), and the float record
(room 45, var1 0) was drawn as a second, static Dozy at (144,139) from the first frame.

**What is implemented** (all in tape_code.asm + msg_data_tape.asm unless noted):
- `dozy_talk` (called from tp_take for frame 32 with Y = dozyhere's record, returns X = message): `dz_talks`++; 1st talk
  pokes the potion's room (DZ_POTION) = cur_room; 5th talk dozyhere.room=255, float var1=255, float room=45, msg_pushdozy.
- Port deviation (NOT the original): the 1st talk shows `msg_kickdozy`, not `dozytalking`'s 8 boxes. They measure
  **436 bytes** DTE-encoded (msg_dozytalking ... msg_dozy_end), which with the rest left the tape region at -240 bytes
  (overlap error). The text is in X-ALL.TXT ~613; a transcription is not checked in (it was removed to build). Needs a
  top-tier decision (cut, shorten, or find 240+ bytes elsewhere).
- `update_dozy` (chained from update_log48's non-room-48 exit, so no new resident call site): the dozyfloatrou above,
  x in px (-4 per raw step). The port cannot draw a sprite partly off the left edge, so it ENDS at px 0 (raw 32) instead of
  raw 27: var1=0, room=255, force_redraw to erase the last frame. (The original would still slide 5 more steps, partly
  off-screen.)
- The float is "not in the world" until pushed: `tape_state_reset` (new game) puts its room at 255 and var1 0; the
  template copy has room 45. The potion's template row now says room 255: `actor_data_tape.asm` edited by hand (2 rows)
  AND `sleepingpotionhere` added to roompack's ORIG_ROOM_LABELS so regen_art.sh reproduces it. The regen was NOT run
  (shared-sprite state); `cargo build` of roompack is not part of tape_pack.sh either, so run regen_art.sh once and
  `git diff target/actor_data_tape.asm` should show nothing.
- Resident (text_src/actors.asm, TAPE_ROOMS): tp_take frame-32 hook, ROU_DOZYFLOAT in the always-redraw check and in
  da_clear's save-under list. room36.asm rat_sv_setup (TAPE_ROOMS): the save-under block is now sized from the sprite
  header (bpr+1 bytes x height) instead of fixed 5x14, capacity RAT_SV_CAP=112 per buffer; Dozy is 24x28 and a 5x28 block
  (2 x 145) would run past $8000 (nibswap+buffers end at $7FEF now; limit $8000).
- The rat/hawk/log use the same routine, so they are re-tested (below). Their blocks are now exactly their sprite's size
  (rat 5x7, log 5x7, hawk 5x<=14); previously always 5x14 (log's 14 rows included water, harmless).

**Costs.** Tape region 405 -> 199 free = 206 bytes (msg_kickdozy 30, msg_pushdozy 66, code+data ~110). Resident
title-hole spare 81 -> 57 = 24 bytes. With dozytalking's 436 more it would be -240.

**Verified.** harness/tape_dozyfloat.lua 32 PASS / 0 FAIL: boot state (potion 255, Dozy 45, float idle), 4 x kick (box
identified from msg_chatter's saved pointer on the stack), potion appears on talk 1, talk 5 = push, Dozy -> 255, float
var1 != 0, 578 video frames to the end, var1/y relation exact, x only drops by 4 on the var1==4 tick (36 steps), ends
x=0 room 255, no ink to the right of the float's box over 187 samples, sprite drawn in 187/187, 6th talk nothing,
game over resets everything. Mutation: dropping the ROU_DOZYFLOAT da_userat hunk makes the trail check FAIL (144/181
bad samples, worst 196 bytes). Also: cmask CMASK_TAPE=1 19/0/0, tape_log48 34/0, tape_actor_reset PASS,
gameover_tape PASS, tape_hawk PASS, actorlife (tape) 5/1/1 = the known baseline (flame_hazard is the pre-existing FAIL).

**Gotchas.** The room-45 water ripples on row y=160 (differs between ANY two captures): the trail zone stops at row 157.
The first ~20 frames after the push box is dismissed still show repaint remnants (skipped). The old bytes at the
original's right-of-box are the trail signature because the float moves LEFT. `tp_take` loads A with the frame and must
compare before any `ldx` (ldx clobbers Z). The potion/float slots are FIXED table indices (DZ_POTION=slot 2, DZ_FLOAT=slot 8
= dozyhere+1); the harness asserts them, so a reordered regen fails loudly.

## T0219 real tape boot fixed; title stream de-duplicated (tape build)

**Root cause (real tape boot dead since ~T0238).** tools/tape_pack.sh placed tape_stage1 at LOAD_END computed from
target/room36.bin (the -run image, end $7A61), but the .cas is built from target/room36_tape.bin, whose LAST DECB block
(title hole 5, $79CD-$7DC6) covered $7A61-$7BDD. That block streams last, so it overwrote stage1's code (380 B: code +
hdr_buf/stagebuf scratch) while stage1 was running. Symptom: `tape_room_warp.py` "tape-only region differs at $bf30".
Confirmed offline: the old guard logic run on scratchpad base_tape.bin/good_tape.bin flags `block #19 $79cd-$7daf overlaps
tape_stage1 $7a61-$7bdd`.

**Guard.** tools/tape_pack.sh now (1) assembles stage1 once to measure it, (2) computes free windows below nibswap ($7E00)
from room36_tape.bin PLUS any --extra-segment (minus the TAPE_LOW_REGION), takes the highest that fits, (3) after the
real assemble HARD-FAILS if any tape segment overlaps [STAGE1_ORG, STAGE1_END) (STAGE1_END includes the rmb scratch), the
stage1 zero-page vars $007C-$0081, or reaches $FF00+. Every segment is "written after stage1 starts" (stage1 is the first
thing loaded), so the one overlap test covers the whole image. Never place stage1 from the -run image again.

**De-duplication (TAPE_ROOMS=1 only).** TITLE_RESIDENT_LZ ($BF30, 3266 B) == the first TITLE_LZ_LEN+TITLE_MUSIC_LEN bytes of
the gathered title stream. Boot (`show_title`, tape build) now `lbsr title_copy_resident` (new shared sub; also used by
show_title_resident, the game-over replay) to put that at TITLE_LZ_BUF, then the unchanged gather loop appends only block C
(338) + block D (2354) from the holes. Same layout at TITLE_LZ_BUF, so unpack_c/unpack_d offsets are unchanged.
mktitle `--dedup-resident 1` (requires --resident-out) leaves the prefix out of the holes/title_frags;
tools/title_holes.py `tape` drops gap1/gap2 from the hole list; tools/stage_pack.sh passes both for TAPE_ROOMS=1.
room36.asm asserts TITLE_RESIDENT_LEN == TITLE_LZ_LEN+TITLE_MUSIC_LEN. The -run build and its title_frags are untouched
(room36.bin cmp-identical to the pre-change reference). The sanity check in tape_pack.sh now excludes title-fragment blocks
(title_lzN labels) from both sides before comparing block count/size (13 blocks both sides, delta +740).

**New persistent region: TAPE_LOW_REGION = $79CD-$7E00 (1075 B), all free.** Symbols TAPE_LOW_START (= gap2_end, end of
the $7800 logic_low block, so it moves with that block) / TAPE_LOW_END ($7E00), and an empty `org TAPE_LOW_START` slot
(tape_low_slot_start/_end) in room36.asm with an assemble-time guard against running past TAPE_LOW_END. Rules: tape build
only (gate everything `if TAPE_ROOMS`); put content between the slot labels; delivered by an ordinary direct (<$8000) tape
segment; nothing at boot/runtime writes it (gather -> $4000-$57FF only, title unpack scratch $6000-$77FF, nibswap/rat
save-under start at $7E00); tape_pack.sh keeps stage1 out of it. PROVEN by harness/tape_boot_regions.py: a 1075-byte
pattern segment over the whole region survives a real tape boot byte-identical. Not tested: it surviving a whole game
(nothing in the map writes there; ramaudit lists $79CD-$7DFF as hole 5 / FREE).

**Numbers.** stage1 now $7560-$76DC (FB B spare, a non-persistent window; was $7A61). Tape holes used: 2 (hole 0 $0B4D 691/691,
hole 1 $35DA 2001/2598) vs 6 before; title-hole spare 57 -> 597 (hole 1's tail $3DAB-$3FFF), plus unused FB spares
(177 + 672, NOT persistent) and gap1 $5CE2-$5FFF (798 B, persistent, unguarded -- stage1 no longer sits there; a
candidate for a second region). Tape-only region [IMAGE_END..CODE_DEST) free: 199 (unchanged, printed by tape_pack.sh).
.cas 40920 B / 16 segments. tape_pack.sh must still be run TWICE after title-size changes (hole 0 start moved $0B49->$0B4D).

**Verified.** tape_room_warp.py PASS; harness/tape_boot_regions.py PASS (new: real boot, title playing 5/5 PC samples in
the mixer, every tape segment byte-compared to room36_tape.bin except boot-rewritten windows [FB A, FB B, start: code,
ti_*/lz_* vars -- 11361 B], tape-only region identical, low-region pattern survives). Negative test: the same harness against a
cas with stage1 at $2000 FAILS on 6 segments. bootreal.py (-run) PASS; room36.bin identical; gameover_tape PASS;
CMASK_TAPE=1 cmaskverify 19/0/0; tape_log48 34/0; tape_dozyfloat 32/0; tape_daisy_ending PASS; tape_hawk PASS.

**Lesson.** Memory-poke harnesses (MAME load_decb, jumptrace, ...) write every block in file order into RAM, so they can
NEVER see a load-ORDER overwrite -- they stayed green for the whole life of this bug. Only a real tape boot (XRoar
-load-tape, CLOADM+EXEC) can. Run harness/tape_boot_regions.py after any change to the tape layout, holes, stage1 or
tape_pack.sh. A placement computed from one image (-run) for a different image (tape) is the bug class.

Top-tier re-check: tape_room_warp.py PASS first try; tape_boot_regions.py
hit a GDB `TimeoutError` in gdb_run.recv_reply on the FIRST run and PASSED
on the immediate re-run (same binary) -- the XRoar GDB stub's known
timing sensitivity (T0227/T0230), not a load fault. One re-run is the
budget; two timeouts in a row = investigate.
Also: tools/ramaudit.py (T0219 prep) prints the whole-64K runtime map of
the tape build, classed live/boot-only/title-reused/framebuffer/
transient/FREE, and asserts the rows sum to 65280. Re-run it before
claiming any memory is free -- its output file is NOT committed (stale
after every build).

## T0221 completion tune -- PHASE 1 MEASURED, STOPPED (does not fit; nothing built)

Which tune: X-ALL.TXT daisyrou1 -> `doendmessages`: coins==30 -> `ld a,3 / call starttune`
(A=3; check128 copies A to E, so id 3 is right), then `completedgame=1`, `call chatter`
(gotallcoins box), then `theheartdemo` (255 frames of updatehearts), ending in `jp musicoff`.
So tune3 plays in the BACKGROUND under the chatter box and heart demo and is cut by
musicoff; it is NOT a fixed-length jingle. Capture (aycapture ... tune 3 6000) shows it LOOPS,
period ~1311 frames (26.2 s; autocorrelation 0.66 on tone+vol regs, slight timing drift).

Reduced with tools/aycapture/target/release/reduce, same pipeline/params as tune1/tune2
(div 24, max_hw 100000, vol_step 1), max_ms uncapped. Bytes = 3*entries + 2 terminator.
  frames  vol_step  entries  bytes   playback
  1000(20s)  1       405     1217     20.1 s   (old tune3.asm in captures/ is a different 274-entry/824 B cut)
  1000       16      248      746     20.0 s   (no envelope)
  1311(1 loop) 1     529     1589     26.4 s
  1311       16      322      968     26.3 s   (no envelope)
Exact repeated entry runs are short (longest 20 of 529), so phrase/repeat dedupe saves little
and would need a tape-side sequencer.
Space: TAPE_LOW_REGION 609 + gap1 798 = 1407 < 1589 even before the 226-byte tape-only
region (126 usable). Only the no-envelope or sub-loop cuts fit, and choosing envelope on/off or
playback length is a design decision, so nothing was built. tools/ramaudit.py currently errors:
"stale citation, /hole at $0b49/ not found in title_lz_tape.asm", so gap1's unloaded/unreferenced
state was NOT re-confirmed.
Also open: port play_tune BLOCKS (the original plays under the box), so a 20-26 s tune would
stall the win before the box.

### T0221 addendum -- tune3 through the MIX3 mixer pipeline (measured, nothing built)
Pipeline: `mix3stream <csv> <frames> 8529 mix3_stream.asm --semitone` (as mksounds.sh does for
tune0), then `lwasm --format=raw target/title_mix3.asm` (mixer code 215 B + stream, the blob),
then roompack::lz::pack (same codec mktitle uses). All MEASURED, built in the scratchpad only.
  blob                      stream   raw blob  LZ-packed  vs title raw
  title tune0 (1000 fr)      2683     2898      600       = (sanity: matches shipped 2898/600)
  tune3 first 1000 frames    2926     3141      661       +243 raw
  tune3 one loop 1311 fr     3846     4061      748       +1163 raw
TITLE_MUSIC_RAW in the tape build = 2898, TITLE_RAW_LEN = 3154. Neither tune3 blob fits the
current buffer: raw would need to grow by 243 (1000fr) or 1163 (1311fr); the buffer chain is
laid out downward from $FF00 so growing it moves BANNER_BUF etc. down (GUESS: not checked
whether the tape build has that slack; T0237 recovered BANNER_BUF for tape, so plausibly yes).
Packed cost: 661/748 B vs the title's 600 (packed is what must sit in a load region; but
the tape build keeps the title prefix resident via TITLE_RESIDENT_LZ, so tune3 would be a
NEW resident/persistent packed blob of 661-748 B: fits TAPE_LOW_REGION's 609? NO (661>609);
fits gap1's 798, YES, either blob). Also needs the mixer code (title code is already
resident) and an unpack into TITLE_RAW_BUF at the win (transient, free once the game ends).
Mixer end: harness/mixer3.asm line ~122-124 and title_mix3.asm line ~112: at stream end
`ldu <sstart` -- it LOOPS; it returns only when SPACE is polled (once per 50 Hz record).
So one pass is not the behaviour; it plays until a key, which matches musicoff-on-dismiss.
No envelope question arises: mix3stream quantises amplitude per voice (steps of 4, AY_LEVEL).
ramaudit.py: hole citations now regex-built from the live hole address (rf"hole at \${a:04x}")
so T0219's $0b4d no longer breaks them, BUT the script then fails at its next assert
(`a == S("title_lz1") and a + c == 0x4000`): its whole model predates T0219 (tape now has only
holes 0 and 1; holes 2-5 gone). It needs a model rewrite, not a regex fix. Instead gap1 was
checked directly (MEASURED, target/room36_tape.bin from 09:33): DECB segments are 5800-5ce1
then 6000-755f, so $5CE2-$5FFF is NOT loaded; room36_tape.map has no symbol in it (last is
box_gl $5CE1, next BUFB $6000); no target/*.asm, tape_pack.sh or tape_boot_regions.py references
an address in $5CE2-$5FFF (tape_stage1 sits at LOAD_END, not there). Runtime scratch use inside
it is not exhaustively excluded.

## T0221 completion tune -- IMPLEMENTED (tape build only), supersedes the STOPPED notes above

Design (top-tier decision): tune3 as the title's 3-voice mixer blob, ONE full 1311-frame loop, 4071 B raw -> 757 B LZ-packed,
stored in the new TAPE_LOW_REGION2 (gap1), unpacked at the win into the HIDDEN framebuffer, played UNDER the gotallcoins boxes.

### ramaudit.py model rewrite needed (task to file)
tools/ramaudit.py's model predates T0219: it assumes the tape build has hole 0..5. Since T0219 the tape build has only holes 0
and 1 (title_holes.py `tape`), gap1/gap2 are persistent regions, stage1 sits at $7560. The `hole at $ADDR` citations were
changed to be built from the live hole address (rf"hole at \${a:04x}"), but the script still dies at
`assert a == S("title_lz1") and a + c == 0x4000`. Rewrite the model: holes 0/1 only, TAPE_LOW_REGION (content + free tail),
TAPE_LOW_REGION2 (content + free tail), FB A/B spare as non-persistent windows; then re-assert the 65280-byte sum.

### Part A: TAPE_LOW_REGION3 = the unused tail of title hole 1

**Both claims confirmed from the code.** (1) boot only READS the fragments: boot_code.asm `show_title` = `title_copy_resident` +
`ti_gather` (`ldy ,x++` source, `lda ,y+ / sta ,u+` into TITLE_LZ_BUF $4000), the unpack scratch is $6000-$77FF; nothing writes the
hole. (2) nothing at runtime lives between the end of the resident `$0E00-$4000` block and $4000: every `rmb` of that block is a
mapped symbol below the hole start (last symbols before it: `item_name_tab`), the stack is at $0100. Also PROVEN dynamically: a
real XRoar tape boot keeps a pattern over the free tail byte-identical (tape_boot_regions.py), and tape_beanstalk.lua re-reads the
whole region after a full playthrough (only its 3 state bytes differ).

**How it is declared (no hand-kept margin).** `tools/roompack` mktitle `--tail-region-end 0x4000` (tools/stage_pack.sh passes it for
TAPE_ROOMS=1) fills the hole that ends at $4000 front-to-back and emits into `title_frags_tape.asm`
`TAPE_LOW3_HOLE_START` (where the hole begins), `TAPE_LOW3_START` (= hole start + the bytes the title's own fragment uses) and
`TAPE_LOW3_END` ($4000): hole 1 therefore gets EXACTLY its need and the region the rest. The -run build is untouched (no flag).
room36.asm: `code_data_end equ *` after `include "gameplay.asm"`; the region slot (`org TAPE_LOW3_START`, `tape_low3_slot_start/_end`)
sits before the title-fragment include. Guards (final pass only): content past $4000 fails ("the title (block C/D) or resident code
grew into it" -- negative-tested with a 598-byte fill), and `code_data_end > TAPE_LOW3_HOLE_START` fails. In the RAW pass
(STAGE_GEN) the slot is parked at `org $c400` (like the title fragments at $c000+), otherwise its bytes would land inside the hole
being measured. CONSEQUENCES: (a) in this file everything that refers OUT of the region must use jsr/jmp/lbra/lbsr (the raw pass puts
it 30 KB from the resident code; a short branch fails to assemble); (b) the region start MOVES with resident code size and block C/D
size -- resident growth eats it 1:1 (that is what the hole spare always was): use labels, never addresses; (c) the hole-1 spare and
this region are the SAME bytes, so "resident title-hole spare" no longer exists as a separate margin.
tools/tape_pack.sh: free-bytes line, stage1 placement excludes it, sanity check excludes its block. harness/tape_boot_regions.py:
content byte-diff after a real boot, free-tail pattern survival, title hole-1 fragment must end exactly at `TAPE_LOW3_START`.
Before T0223's content: $3DAB-$3FFF = 597 B free (resident +7 B for the hooks moved it to $3DB3).

## Inventory duplication on a 4th pickup (playtest bug, 2026-10-02) -- fixed, BOTH builds

Report: "picking up a 4th item auto-drops one, but it doesn't really drop; picking the
dropped item back up duplicates it". Root cause: `tp_reallytake` (text_src/actors.asm)
did `jsr inv_insert` THEN `lda #255 / sta ,y` (remove the picked-up item from the world).
A full inventory makes inv_insert auto-drop the oldest item through `drop_to_world`, which
ends in `jsr update_item_triggers` -- and that walks the actor table IN Y. So the store
landed on whatever actor Y was left at, and the item just picked up stayed lying in the
room while also being in `inv` (picking it up again = a second inv entry). Fix: do the
room=255 store BEFORE inv_insert (same bytes, reordered; room36.bin same size, 7 bytes
differ). Bonus: update_item_triggers no longer sees the held item as still on the floor.
Verified: harness/inv_full.lua (base actor table, runs on both builds): unfixed tape binary
2/4 FAIL (jug room=36 while in inv), fixed: 6/0 on room36.bin AND room36_tape.bin;
tape_item_pickup 2/0, tape_log48 34/0.
Lesson: any routine that `jsr`s into code you didn't write must assume X/Y/U are clobbered
unless that callee documents otherwise -- this one gained a Y-walking callee (T0053's
update_item_triggers call in drop_to_world) long after tp_reallytake was written.

with their `title_lzN` labels in title_lz_tape.asm, and the STAGE1 file header at the head of room36.cas (load addr + size; stage1 is no longer in the .bin).

  tape segment overlaps stage1 or its zero-page vars $7C-$81 and that stage1 only overlaps `framebuffer` rows.

  ("TAPE_LOW_REGION: loaded top 7DE1 != slot end 7DDF"). Real build -> exit 0.

Not runtime-only (checked): TAPE_LOW2 (757 B LZ stream, read-only), TAPE_LOW (code + text, 4 B of state), TAPE_LOW3 (3 B state + code + text), $5800-$5FFF (only msg_x/y/pen/plot, 4 B, and message.asm vars), tape-only rooms (read-only).
Templates stay: actor_init (344 B, LZ 257), coin_init (45, LZ 49), actor_init_tape_template + coin_init_tape_template (229, LZ 194) are read at EVERY new_game, so they cannot
live in dead-after-boot space; LZ-packing them saves only ~60-120 B (measured) -- not a lever.
Totals of the movable runtime-only RAM: nibswap 256 + rat_sv 234 + ROOM_UNPACK_BUF 315 + live tape tables 229 + bss (actor_ram 344 + coin_ram 45 + inv 4 + 36 scratch = 429) = 1463 B.

Dead-after-boot space that exists (the holes), verified from boot_code.asm:
- hole 0 $0B4D-$0DFF = 691 B (title_lz0) and hole 1 $35DE-$3DB2 = 2005 B (title_lz1): together 2696 B = block C fragment 338 + block D fragment 2358. Only `show_title`'s ti_gather
  reads them (`ldy ,x++` source, `lda ,y+ / sta ,u+` into TITLE_LZ_BUF $4000). Nothing writes them.
- The game-over/completedgame REPLAY (`show_title_resident` -> `title_copy_resident` -> lz_unpack x2 -> `jmp ti_transpose`) does not read or write either hole: it reads TITLE_RESIDENT_LZ ($BF30), writes
  TITLE_LZ_BUF ($4000-), $6000-$77FF, MIX3_BUF ($F2AE-), DP page $FE, and the lz/ti vars. Block C/D are explicitly not re-run. So the holes are free for runtime use once `show_title` has returned.
- Framebuffer spares at runtime: NONE. $4000-$57FF and $6000-$77FF are the two full 6144-byte PMODE4 pages and are drawn/flipped every frame; the spares (FB A $574F-$57FF = 177 B, FB B $76DC-$77FF = 292 B, stage1
  $7560-$76DB = 380 B) are free only at load time and until show_title's transpose/ti_dup writes both pages. Usable for BOOT-ONLY code (see B), never for runtime data.
- Other transient space: TITLE_RAW_BUF overlay $F2AE-$FEFF (CMASK 1536 + ATTR_CELLS 768 + place tables 536 live in play; $FDC6-$FEFF 314 B unused in play but clobbered by every replay mixer run) -- not a home for persistent buffers.
- Anchoring caution for L2: hole 0 is fixed at `start` ($0E00, end) but its start moves with low-region code; hole 1 starts at code_data_end (moves with resident size). Place buffers relative to `start`
  (downward) or `code_data_end` (equ, no size circularity: all operands are extended).

Not boot-only (kept on purpose): ti_len/ti_coln/ti_rown + lz_* vars, ti_transpose..ti_release (86 B) and show_title_resident + title_copy_resident (54 B) -- the replay uses them; TITLE_RESIDENT_LZ 3266 B (read at boot AND each replay).
Load-time-only and already free: staged block A (5967 B at $4000), staged block B (5472 B at $6000), stage1 (380 B at $7560) -- all inside the framebuffers.

### Part 2C: sizing for bigger levers
1. Message text, DTE-encoded (bytes in the image, label ranges; the lz codec = tools/roompack lz via target/release/lzpack, round-trip verified):
   gap_messages 913 + gameplay msg_* 640 + tape-only msg_data_tape 713 + TAPE_LOW msgs 929 + TAPE_LOW3 msgs 214 = **3409 B** (plus room names 442 B, dte_table 92 B, rat_troll text 64 B in block D not counted).
   Whole bank concatenated and LZ-packed: 3409 -> **2683 B (-726)**. Per stream: 816/575/641/790/203. Per-message packing (40 streams, each its own unit): 3145 -> 3194 (WORSE; best-of-either 3060 = -85).
   DTE already took the redundancy (plain text of those strings is 1064+752+913+206+721 = 3656 B in ~210 strings; DTE'd text bytes 662+520+646+151+480 = 2459).
   Verdict: the -726 exists only if the bank is one unpack unit, which needs a ~3409 B RAM buffer = net loss. Not a lever.
2. Sprites: raw in the unpacked image $8000-$BDD0 (from blocks A+B decoded with the real codec): spr_* 4243 + aspr_* 2160 + dizzy body frames 4188 = 10591 B (+531 B dizzy tail and tables raw at $5800).
   Standalone LZ of the three groups concatenated: 6452 B. They are ALREADY inside the LZ-packed blocks A (7642 raw -> 5967) and B (8183 -> 5472), staged in the framebuffers, so no persistent-space gain exists here. Room data in A/B (4310 raw) packs only to 3990 (rooms are already per-room LZ).
   Tape-only region: tape rooms 3342 -> 3133 (already packed), tape tables/sprites/code 2880 -> 2223 (-657) but they must be unpacked into the same RAM afterwards: no gain.
3. Code (6809), by listing mnemonic (+/- ~100 B from label-line mis-parse): resident below $8000 ~12.05 KB = room36.asm main 5333 + actors 1897 + gameplay 1580 + message VM 611 + boot_code 425 + ui 334 (+33 name lookup) + logic_low 461 + tape_code 947 + tape_bean 312 + tape_win 113;
   block D (unpacked to $E5AE, 3237 raw) = rat_troll_hazard 760 + armorog/lifts/dagger 743 + croc_portcullis 391 + dragon 304 code, 1022 data (font 689, sound 333). Total ~14.2 KB code. The "6809 B" guess in the brief does not match; the measured figure is above.

### Part 2D: levers, ranked by measured persistent bytes recovered
L1 and L2 compete for the same dead-after-boot holes: pick L1 (bigger) OR L2. After L1 there is no dead space left to move buffers into (moving them into the freed holes nets 0).

1. **L1: deliver blocks C and D as RAW tape segments at their final addresses, delete the title holes (TAPE_ROOMS only). +2696 B persistent below $8000** (hole 0 691 at $0B4D, hole 1 2005 at $35DE, joining LOW3's 589).
   Cost: tape +892 B (raw C 351 + raw D 3237 = 3588 vs 2696 packed), ~2% of the 43617 B .cas. Also deletes ~81 B of code (title_frags 28, ti_gather loop ~27, jsr unpack_c/d 6, unpack_c/d 20; GUESS +-10).
   Why it works: stage1 already writes any segment with addr >= $8000 through its staged copy path (that is how the 9803 B tape-only region arrives); RC_DEST ($BDD1-$BF2F) and CODE_DEST ($E5AE-$F252) are already reserved RAM that nothing else uses.
   What to change: tools/stage_pack.sh keeps `${TMP}_c.bin`/`_d.bin` (raw pass) and feeds them to tape_pack.sh as --extra-segment BDD1 / E5AE (or `includebin` under TAPE_ROOMS); mktitle without --extra/--extra2 (holes then hold nothing; title_holes.py `tape` drops both);
   boot_code.asm show_title (TAPE_ROOMS) drops the gather + unpack_c/unpack_d; room36.asm loses the title_frags include, the LOW3 hole-tail mechanism (TAPE_LOW3_* symbols become a plain org slot) and its guards. Block D still has the staged_syms resident-symbol guard.
   Risk: medium (pipeline + 3 tools + harness windows), but all mechanical and it deletes machinery. Touches: stage_pack.sh, tape_pack.sh (sanity check, hard guard), title_holes.py, room36.asm slots, tape_boot_regions.py (it byte-compares C/D windows), ramaudit (handles it: holes list shrinks; needs `H_LOW`/`H_TAIL` asserts relaxed -- would exit "unmodelled"/assert, that is intended, update then).
   -run build: untouched (gate on TAPE_ROOMS; room36.bin stays byte-identical). Does not change room36.bin.
2. **L2 bundle: runtime-only buffers into the holes (instead of L1). +1463 B persistent**, 0 tape cost, tape-saving bonus 544 B (zeros/dup loaded now). Items and where the space reappears:
   - nibswap + rat_sv ($7E00-$7FE9, 490 B) -> frees the whole $7E00-$7FFF page: TAPE_LOW_REGION grows to [79CD,8000): free there 33+22=55 now -> 545, **+490**, direct-loadable.
   - ROOM_UNPACK_BUF 315 -> tape-only region free span 51 -> 366, **+315** (and -315 loaded zeros).
   - live actor_init_tape (184) + coin_init_tape (45) -> **+229** in the tape-only region (and -229 loaded bytes); needs `rmb`/equ for the live copies, harnesses/roompack outputs that name them (tools/roompack --actor-template/--coin-suffix, harness/tape_actor_reset) re-checked.
   - actor_ram 344 + coin_ram 45 + inv 4 + 36 scratch = 429 -> resident shrinks 429, hole-1 start and TAPE_LOW3_START move down: **+429** in LOW3.
   Fits: hole 0 691 holds ROOM_UNPACK_BUF 315 + nibswap 256 (571, anchored below $0E00); hole 1 fragment (2005) holds rat_sv 234 + bss 429 + live tables 229 (892, anchored at code_data_end). Total need 1463 of 2696.
   What to change: room36.asm (nibswap/rat_sv/ROOM_UNPACK_BUF equ's, `rmb` -> equ in actors.asm/room36.asm under TAPE_ROOMS), assemble-time guards (buffer end <= fragment end), nothing else at runtime.
   Risk: medium-high. Code reading these only uses labels, but (a) the RAW pass puts the holes at $C000+ so equ's must be relative to `start`/`code_data_end`, never to title_lz*; (b) block D (staged) references some of these symbols: staged_syms resident-symbol guard must still hold across the two passes;
   (c) rat_sv garbage-valid-byte tolerance is reasoned, not tested; (d) nibswap must still be built AFTER show_title returns (it is). Needs: full tape_boot_regions.py + the blitter/hawk/rat harnesses (rat_sv path), CMASK_TAPE=1 cmaskverify, gameover_tape, tape_actor_reset.
   -run build: keep it unchanged (gated); the -run build has 6 holes at different addresses and would need its own placement -- flag if both builds must stay layout-identical.
3. **L3: boot-only code into framebuffer spares, dead after boot. +243 B** (start 136 -> FB B spare, show_title 59 + title_frags 28 + unpack_c/d 20 = 107 -> FB A spare): +223 in LOW3 (resident shrinks), +20 in TAPE_LOW_REGION.
   Constraints measured: FB B spare $76DC-$77FF (292 B) is overwritten by show_title's first lz_unpack (scratch $6000-$77FF), so `start` must finish before that (nibswap build moved before `jsr show_title`; call show_title by pushing new_game and `jmp`);
   FB A spare $574F-$57FF (177 B) survives the gather (stream ends $574A) and dies at ti_transpose, so show_title must end with `jmp ti_transpose`. The tape exec address (DECB trailer) can be anywhere; -run's BASIC EXEC $0E00 cannot -> tape build only.
   After L1 only `start` (136) remains movable, so L3 is worth +136 then. Risk: medium (boot ordering; a mistake = hang at boot, caught by tape_boot_regions.py). Touches room36.asm start, boot_code.asm, tape_pack.sh stage1 window choice (stage1 must stay clear of the new segment), tape_boot_regions.py windows.
4. **L4: gate seed_inventory (test aid) under TAPE_ROOMS: +81 B** (78 body + 3 call; "jsr seed_inventory" in new_game). Low risk, resident, tape build only; -run keeps it. Needs the START_ITEM test builds to keep working in the tape build (they would stop; decide).
5. **L5 (DESIGN DECISION, not mine): drop or slim the title replay.** TITLE_RESIDENT_LZ is 3266 B (title image 2666 + music 600) + 140 B of replay code (ti_transpose.. show_title_resident). Dropping the replay returns ~3.4 KB but needs the boot title to come from tape another way (e.g. the holes) and reverts T0231's game-over fidelity.
   Dropping only the replay MUSIC saves 600 B (+ the mixer blob dependencies). Flag for the top tier.
6. **L6: pad/slack: +12 B** (RELOC_BOOT_BYTES NOP pad in start, tape build, needs raw/packed pass sizes to stay equal) and CODE_BUDGET slack already counted as free (91 B).
7. Not levers (measured): message LZ (-726 only with a 3409 B buffer; per-message +0), sprite repack (already LZ'd inside A/B), template LZ (-60 to -120 B), tape-only rooms (3342 -> 3133, must be unpacked to RAM), ROOM_UNPACK_BUF_LEN lowering (largest room 31 = 315 B; stalk adds 36 to room 58's 132).

Order I would try (decision for the top tier): L1 (+2696, deletes code, tape +892) -- or, if the extra tape bytes are unacceptable, L2 (+1463) then L3 (+243) then L4 (+81). Anything freeing space only in the tape build is marked above; none requires changing room36.bin.
All of L1-L4 are TAPE_ROOMS-gated; if the same fix is wanted in the -run build it needs its own layout (different holes) -- not costed here.

## T0225b space levers L2'/L3/L4 (tape build only)

Implements three of T0222's levers on top of T0224. All `TAPE_ROOMS`-gated: `target/room36.bin` is byte-identical to the pre-task reference
(`cmp` clean after every tape_pack.sh run, incl. a START_ROOM/START_ITEM build and the rebuild back to default). The -run build keeps `start:` at $0E00,
its nibswap/rat_sv at $7E00-$7FE9 and its own seed_inventory.

**Free bytes per region, before -> after (tape_pack.sh, MEASURED).** LOW $79B9..: 53 -> 309 (end $7E00 -> $7F00); LOW2 41 -> 41; LOW3 2032 -> 2165;
LOW4 755 -> 833; tape-only 51 -> 51; after-rat_sv tail 22 -> 0 (nibswap now ends at $8000); block-D slack 91 -> 91.
**Persistent free total 3045 -> 3490 B (+445)** = L2' +234 (256 freed, 22 tail used) + L3 +130 + L4 +81. .cas 44485 -> 44415 B.

**L2' (rat save-under out of the gap).**
- rat_sv_hdr_a/buf_a/hdr_b/buf_b are `equ`s starting at T0163_SCRATCH_END ($FDC6) in TITLE_RAW_BUF's gameplay-unused tail: $FDC6-$FEAF (234 B), 80 B left to $FF00.
  Assemble-time guard: RAT_SV_END <= TITLE_RAW_BUF+TITLE_RAW_LEN. (-run build keeps the old rmb layout.)
- Safety = garbage tolerance, argued from the code and proven by gameover_tape/tape_hawk/log48/dozyfloat: every title run (boot, game-over replay, win replay at
  room36.asm mainloop `completedgame` and gameplay.asm update_death) is followed by `jmp new_game`; new_game now does `jsr force_redraw` then `clr rat_sv_hdr_a / hdr_b`
  (6 B, tape only), and redraw's 255 sentinel path (rat_sv_invalidate) drops each buffer's slot before its first rat_restore anyway. Both belts. The only rat_save/rat_restore
  callers are redraw and rat_clear_and_blit (rat, hawk, log, Dozy float), all through rat_sv_slot. The win tune (tape_win_chatter) uses the hidden framebuffer, not this chain.
- nibswap could NOT go transient (decision on evidence): it is built ONCE at boot and the game-over/win title replay (show_title_resident) clobbers the whole TITLE_RAW_BUF chain
  incl. MIX3_DP page $FE00-$FEFF, so it would need rebuilding after every replay; and only 80 B of tail remain after rat_sv (nibswap is 256). Moved instead to $7F00-$7FFF
  (`org $7F00 / nibswap rmb 256`, tape build): its address was never assumed (only `nibswap+128` signed `b,y`). That makes TAPE_LOW_REGION contiguous: `TAPE_LOW_END equ nibswap` = $7F00,
  no LOW5 needed. tape_pack.sh/ramaudit read nibswap from the map now (stage1 window HI = nibswap).
- Loading content into $7E00-$7EFF (the old nibswap page) is real-tape-proven by tape_boot_regions.py's pattern boot (LOW free tail $7DCB-$7F00, 309 B, survived). Caveat: stage1 uses
  BASIC's stack at EXEC time (~$7F36 downward); nothing is loaded at $7F00+ so it is not touched. Do NOT put loaded content at $7F00+.

**L3 (start: out of $0E00).** `start` (141 B now: +5 for the push/jmp) is assembled at TAPE_START_ORG=$5760 (FB A spare tail; staged block A ends $574F, $5800 block starts at $5800; parked at
$cc00 in the raw pass). Guards: size <= $5800-TAPE_START_ORG; r8000_staged_end <= TAPE_START_ORG (checked after that label, forward refs not allowed in `ifgt`). EXEC follows automatically
(`end start` -> DECB trailer, caswriter prints `exec $5760`); nothing else references $0E00 as start (grep: only the TAPE_LOW4_END/new_game guards). new_game stays at $0E00, so the resident block
loses 136 B at its END: LOW3 (starts at code_data_end) grows, LOW4 end unchanged. Boot order change: the nibswap loop runs BEFORE the title (it does not touch $6000-$77FF, nothing in show_title
touches $7F00+), then `ldx #new_game / pshs x / jmp show_title` (show_title's rts returns into new_game). The start code lives until ti_dup overwrites page A, after which it is never needed.
Chose FB A spare over FB B spare: FB B spare is overwritten by show_title's first lz_unpack (scratch $6000-$77FF) and competes with stage1 ($7560).
tape_boot_regions.py: new lines assert EXEC == start, start is its own segment inside FB A spare, and all 256 nibswap entries are correct after a REAL boot. tape_pack.sh: sanity check excludes start's block.

**L4 (seed_inventory).** `SEED_INV` equ (room36.asm): 1 in the -run build; in the tape build 1 only if START_ITEM1+2+3 != 0. Gates the jsr in new_game and the body+si_items in boot_code.asm
(78 + 3 = 81 B, LOW4 +78, call +3). tools/stage_pack.sh now passes START_ITEMn to the RAW pass too (it did not): without that the raw and final passes of a START_ITEM tape build differ by 3+ bytes in
layout and the staged-code resident-symbol guard fails (found by `START_ROOM=53 play.sh --tape`, fixed). Checked: `START_ROOM=53 ./play.sh --tape` (xroar stubbed, build only) builds and exits 0;
harness/startitems.lua on that tape binary: `ITEMS room=53 inv=[frame14(room=255), -, -, -]` (the rope is seeded and out of the world).

**Verified (final default build, tape_pack.sh run twice; 2nd run's tape bin identical to the 1st):** cmp room36.bin vs ref IDENTICAL; tools/ramaudit.py exit 0 (model updated: start row in FB A, nibswap to $8000,
rat_sv row in the title chain, seed_inventory optional); tape_boot_regions.py PASS (first run hit a GDB TimeoutError in the PATTERN boot, re-run PASS: start/EXEC, nibswap table, all regions byte-identical);
tape_room_warp.py PASS; gameover_tape.lua PASS (2 rounds); tape_hawk 2/2; tape_log48 34/0; tape_dozyfloat 43/0 (no trail: 182 samples, 0 bad); actorlife.lua on the tape bin 5 pass/1 fail/1 skip (the expected 5/1/1; the fail is
flame_hazard, pre-existing); CMASK_TAPE=1 cmaskverify 19/0/0.
